title: Platform and API Services Getting Started with Integrating Your Portkey APIs into Open WebUI
body:
If you are interested in integrating your personal Portkey API access into an existing Open WebUI setup, follow the instructions below.
Table of Contents
•	Introduction
•	Appropriate Use
•	Safety and Data Protection 
o	What You Should Know
•	Method 1: Admin Setup 
o	Step 1: Get Your Credentials
o	Step 2: Add Portkey to Open WebUI
o	Step 3: Verify Models Are Available
•	Method 2: User Setup (Direct Connection) 
o	Step 1: Get Your Credentials
o	Step 2: Add Portkey to Open WebUI
o	Step 3: Verify Models Are Available
•	Tips for Using Open WebUI with Portkey
•	Links
Introduction
Open WebUI is a self-hosted, web-based interface for interacting with AI models. It provides a familiar chat experience similar to ChatGPT or other commercial AI platforms, but runs on infrastructure you control. By connecting Open WebUI to Rutgers’ Portkey gateway, you can access multiple AI models (OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, and more) through a single chat interface while ensuring your data is protected under the university’s enterprise agreements.
This guide covers two methods for connecting Portkey to Open WebUI, depending on your level of access to the Open WebUI instance. Use only one of the two methods below - the Admin method if you manage the Open WebUI server, or the User method if you have a regular account on someone else’s instance.
Appropriate Use
Open WebUI with Portkey provides a conversational AI interface for a variety of tasks:
•	Writing and editing - Draft, revise, and proofread documents, emails, and reports.
•	Research and summarization - Summarize articles, explore topics, and synthesize information.
•	Brainstorming - Generate ideas for projects, presentations, and creative work.
•	Coding assistance - Write, debug, and explain code in multiple programming languages.
•	Teaching and learning - Create study materials, explain concepts, and generate practice questions.
•	Data analysis - Interpret data, draft reports, and explore analytical approaches.
As with all AI tools, always review AI-generated content for accuracy before using it in any official capacity.
Safety and Data Protection
When Open WebUI is connected to Rutgers’ Portkey gateway, all AI requests are routed through the university’s enterprise instance:
•	Your data is not used to train AI models. The enterprise agreements between Rutgers and the AI providers ensure your inputs and outputs are not used for model training.
•	API usage is tracked for accounting purposes through the Portkey dashboard.
What You Should Know
•	Do not enter protected health information (PHI), Social Security numbers, financial account numbers, or other highly sensitive data into Open WebUI or any AI tool.
•	Review AI-generated content carefully. AI models can produce plausible-sounding but incorrect information.
•	Protect your Portkey API key. Treat it like a password - do not share it or post it in documentation.
•	Be aware of academic integrity policies. Students should consult their instructors about acceptable use of AI tools in coursework.
Method 1: Admin Setup
Use this method if you are setting up an Open WebUI instance and have admin access. This configures Portkey as a server-wide connection available to all users on the instance.
Step 1: Get Your Credentials
1.	Sign in to the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area, within the Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account activated).
2.	Create your Portkey API key and save it.
Step 2: Add Portkey to Open WebUI
1.	Sign into your Open WebUI instance with an admin account.
2.	Go to Admin Panel > Settings > Connections.
3.	Under OpenAI API, click the + button to add a new connection.
4.	Fill in the following fields:
Field Values
Field	Value
Connection Type	External
URL	https://api.portkey.ai/v1
Auth	Bearer YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY
Prefix ID	portkey
Provider Type	OpenAI
API Type	Chat Completions
Model IDs	(leave empty)
Replace YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY with your actual Portkey API key.
1.	Next to the URL field, click the Verify icon. You should receive a “Successful Connection” message.
2.	Click Save.
Step 3: Verify Models Are Available
1.	Go to Admin Panel > Settings > Models.
2.	All of your Portkey models should appear with a portkey. prefix (e.g., portkey.gpt-4o, portkey.claude-sonnet-4-6).
If models appear in the list, the integration is configured correctly and users on your instance can now select Portkey models from the model dropdown in their chats.
Method 2: User Setup (Direct Connection)
Use this method if you have access to an Open WebUI instance but do not have admin access. This uses Open WebUI’s Direct Connections feature to add Portkey as a personal connection tied to your account.
Note: Direct Connections must be enabled by the server administrator. If the option is not available, contact your Open WebUI administrator to either enable Direct Connections or configure Portkey at the server level using the Admin method above.
Step 1: Get Your Credentials
1.	Sign in to the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area, within the Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account activated).
2.	Create your Portkey API key and save it.
Step 2: Add Portkey to Open WebUI
1.	Sign into your Open WebUI instance.
2.	Go to Settings > Connections.
3.	You will see “Manage Direct Connections”. Click the + button to add a new connection. 
o	If you do not see the + button, your Open WebUI server administrators have disabled the Direct Connections feature. Contact your administrator for assistance.
4.	Fill in the following fields:
Field Values
Field	Value
URL	https://api.portkey.ai/v1
Auth	Bearer YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY
Prefix ID	pk
Model IDs	(leave empty)
Replace YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY with your actual Portkey API key.
1.	Next to the URL field, click the Verify icon. You should receive a “Successful Connection” message.
2.	Click Save.
Step 3: Verify Models Are Available
When you open a new chat, click the model selector at the top. Your Portkey models should appear with a pk. prefix (e.g., pk.gpt-4o, pk.claude-sonnet-4-6).
If models appear in the selector, your personal Portkey connection is configured correctly.
Tips for Using Open WebUI with Portkey
•	Check which models are available. The models available through Rutgers’ Portkey instance may differ from public listings. Look at the model selector to see what is available with your Portkey prefix.
•	Use system prompts. Open WebUI allows you to set system prompts for conversations to customize the AI’s behavior and tone.
•	Try different models. One advantage of Portkey is access to multiple AI providers. Experiment with different models to find which works best for your specific task.
•	Review the Portkey dashboard. Visit app.portkey.ai to monitor your usage, view logs, and track costs.

title: Platform and API Services Getting Started with Portkey
body:
Portkey is an enterprise AI gateway that Rutgers provides to enable faculty, staff, and researchers to access multiple large language models (LLMs) - such as OpenAI’s GPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Meta’s Llama, and many others, through a single, unified API. Instead of managing separate accounts and API keys with each AI provider, you use Portkey as a secure intermediary that routes your requests to the appropriate model while providing centralized access control and data protection.
Portkey is designed for users who need programmatic access to AI models - researchers building AI-powered applications, developers integrating AI into workflows, faculty exploring AI in computational courses, and staff automating tasks with scripts or code. If you are looking for a conversational AI chat interface (rather than an API), consider using ChatGPT Edu, Microsoft Copilot, or Google Gemini instead.
Table of Contents
•	Who Is Portkey For?
•	How Portkey Works
•	Safety and Data Protection 
o	Enterprise-Level Protection
o	What You Should Know
o	Personal API Accounts vs. Rutgers Portkey
•	How to Get Started 
o	Request Access
o	Using Portkey APIs
•	Links
Who Is Portkey For?
•	Researchers who need API access to AI models for experiments, data analysis, or building research tools.
•	Developers building AI-powered applications, chatbots, agents, or automation workflows.
•	Faculty integrating AI APIs into coursework, labs, or computational projects.
•	Staff using scripts or code to automate tasks with AI assistance.
•	Anyone who needs to call AI models programmatically via cURL, Python, Node.js, or other programming languages.
How Portkey Works
Portkey sits between your application and the AI model providers. When you send a request through Portkey:
1.	Your application sends an API request to Portkey using your Portkey API key.
2.	Portkey authenticates your request, applies any configured routing rules, and forwards it to the appropriate AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).
3.	The AI provider processes the request and returns a response through Portkey back to your application.
4.	Portkey tracks the cost and applies any usage limits or access controls that have been set up by your administrator.
This architecture provides several key benefits:
•	Unified API - Access multiple AI providers through a single, consistent API interface. Switch between models without changing your application code.
•	Data protection - Requests routed through Rutgers’ Portkey instance are subject to the university’s enterprise data agreements. Your data is protected from being used to train AI models.
•	Cost tracking and monitoring - All API usage is recorded, providing visibility into costs and token usage.
•	Access control - Administrators can manage who has access, set usage limits, and configure routing rules.
•	Reliability - Portkey supports automatic fallbacks, retries, and load balancing across providers to keep your applications running smoothly.
Safety and Data Protection
Enterprise-Level Protection
When you use Portkey through Rutgers, your API requests are routed through the university’s enterprise Portkey instance. This provides important protections:
•	Your data is not used to train AI models. The enterprise agreements between Rutgers and the AI providers ensure your inputs and outputs are not used for model training.
•	Centralized security controls. Portkey administrators can enforce security policies, monitor usage, and respond to any issues that arise.
•	Compliance with university policies. Using Portkey helps ensure that your use of AI APIs aligns with Rutgers’ data classification and acceptable use policies.
What You Should Know
•	Do not send protected health information (PHI), Social Security numbers, financial account numbers, or other highly sensitive data through Portkey or any AI API.
•	Review AI-generated output carefully. AI model responses can contain errors, biased content, or fabricated information.
•	Follow university policies regarding data classification and acceptable use of AI tools.
•	Protect your Portkey API key. Treat it like a password - do not commit it to public code repositories, share it in emails, or post it in documentation.
Personal API Accounts vs. Rutgers Portkey
Feature Comparison
Feature	Personal AI API Account	Rutgers Portkey
Data used for model training	Varies by provider	No
Enterprise data protections	No	Yes
Centralized cost tracking	No	Yes
Access to multiple providers	Separate accounts needed	Single API key
Institutional support	No	Yes
How to Get Started
Request Access
To request access to Portkey please fill out the Portkey Workspace Request form.
Using Portkey APIs
Once your access is confirmed, refer to the following guides to start building:
•	How to Use Portkey APIs - Detailed instructions for using Portkey with cURL, Python, and other languages.
•	Getting Started with Integrating Your Portkey APIs into Open WebUI - Integrating Portkey into your own Open WebUI instance 
Links

•	AI at Rutgers - Office of Information Technology

title: Platform and API Services Getting Started with the Claude Code VS Code Extension
body:
The Claude Code extension for Visual Studio Code brings Anthropic’s AI-powered coding assistant directly into your editor. It provides the same capabilities as the terminal version of Claude Code - reading and editing files, running commands, debugging, refactoring, and interacting with Git - but within the familiar VS Code interface. By configuring the extension to use Rutgers’ Portkey gateway, all requests are routed through the university’s enterprise instance for data protection and usage tracking.
This guide covers how to set up the Claude Code VS Code extension with Portkey. If you prefer to use Claude Code in the terminal, see Getting Started with Claude Code (Terminal CLI) instead.
Table of Contents
•	Appropriate Use
•	Safety and Data Protection 
o	What You Should Know
•	Understanding Costs: Claude Code Is an Agentic System, Not a Chatbot 
o	What Claude Code Is Designed For
o	What Claude Code Is NOT Designed For
o	Monitoring Your Usage
•	Installation and Setup 
o	Step 1: Install the Extension
o	Step 2: Configure Portkey Environment Variables
o	Step 3: Open Claude Code
o	Step 4: Test Your Setup
•	Tips for Using Claude Code in VS Code
•	Known Limitations
•	Links
Appropriate Use
Claude Code in VS Code can assist with a wide range of development tasks:
•	Writing and editing code - Generate functions, classes, and files from natural language descriptions, all within your editor.
•	Debugging - Describe errors or unexpected behavior and get help identifying and fixing issues.
•	Refactoring - Improve code structure, update patterns, or reorganize files.
•	Code review - Get feedback on code quality, security, and best practices.
•	Exploring codebases - Ask Claude to explain unfamiliar code or trace how features work.
•	Git operations - Commit, branch, and manage version control conversationally.
As with all AI tools, always review code generated by Claude before running or deploying it. AI-generated code can contain bugs, security vulnerabilities, or incorrect logic.
Safety and Data Protection
When the Claude Code extension is configured to use Rutgers’ Portkey gateway, all API requests are routed through the university’s enterprise instance:
•	Your code and conversations are not used to train AI models.
•	API usage is tracked for accounting purposes through the Portkey dashboard.
What You Should Know
•	Do not use Claude Code on projects that contain highly sensitive data, such as PHI, Social Security numbers, or financial credentials.
•	Review all code changes before accepting them.
•	Protect your Portkey API key. The key will be stored in your VS Code settings file. Make sure this file is not committed to a public repository.
Understanding Costs: Claude Code Is an Agentic System, Not a Chatbot
The Claude Code extension is fundamentally different from conversational AI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, or Gemini. It is an agentic system - meaning it autonomously reads files, runs commands, searches your codebase, makes edits, and chains together multiple operations to complete a task. A single prompt can trigger dozens or even hundreds of API calls behind the scenes as Claude explores your project, plans an approach, and implements changes.
This means Claude Code can consume significant API credits very quickly. Every file it reads, every search it runs, and every response it generates costs tokens. A complex task that takes Claude several minutes of autonomous work can easily cost more in a single session than an entire day of conversational chatbot usage.
What Claude Code Is Designed For
Claude Code is purpose-built for complex, multi-step software development tasks where its agentic capabilities provide real value:
•	Implementing a new feature across multiple files in a codebase
•	Debugging a complex issue that requires reading and tracing code across many files
•	Refactoring an entire module or migrating a codebase to a new pattern
•	Setting up a project with build configuration, tests, and CI/CD pipelines
•	Reviewing a pull request and providing detailed, code-aware feedback
What Claude Code Is NOT Designed For
Do not use Claude Code for tasks that a simple chatbot can handle. These tasks waste significant resources because Claude Code’s agentic infrastructure activates regardless of how simple your question is:
•	General knowledge questions - “What is the weather today?” or “Explain the difference between TCP and UDP”
•	Simple code snippets - “Write me a quick Python script to convert CSV to JSON”
•	Learning and tutorials - “Explain how to get started with Python Flask”
•	Writing and editing - “Draft an email to my team about the upcoming meeting”
•	Brainstorming - “Give me ideas for my research project”
For these types of tasks, use ChatGPT Edu, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, or the Portkey APIs directly - they are far more cost-effective for conversational and single-turn tasks.
Monitoring Your Usage
Keep an eye on your API spending by checking the Portkey dashboard regularly. If you are unsure whether a task warrants using Claude Code, consider whether the task requires Claude to autonomously explore and modify your codebase. If it does not, use a less expensive tool.
Installation and Setup
Step 1: Install the Extension
1.	Open VS Code.
2.	Open the Extensions panel by pressing Ctrl+Shift+X (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+X (macOS).
3.	Search for “Claude Code for VS Code” - make sure the publisher says Anthropic.
4.	Click Install.
Step 2: Configure Portkey Environment Variables
1.	Open the Command Palette by pressing Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+P (macOS).
2.	Type “Open User Settings” and select Preferences: Open User Settings (not the JSON version).
3.	In the Search Settings box, type “claude code”.
4.	Scroll down to find Claude Code: Environment Variables and click “Edit in settings.json”.
5.	In the settings.json file, locate the claudeCode.environmentVariables section and configure it as follows:
"claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
    {
        "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://api.portkey.ai",
        "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY",
        "ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS": "x-portkey-api-key: YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY\nx-portkey-provider: @claude-models",
        "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
        "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "claude-opus-4-6",
        "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001"
    }
]
Replace both instances of YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY with your actual Portkey API key from the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area, within the Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account activated). You can also retrieve model providers and model names from this same card.
1.	Save the file (Ctrl+S or Cmd+S).
Configuration Explained
Setting explanations
Setting	Purpose
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL	Redirects Claude Code to send requests through Portkey instead of directly to Anthropic.
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN	Authenticates your requests with Portkey.
ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS	Passes your Portkey API key and specifies the @claude-models provider for routing.
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL	Specifies which Claude model to use for each tier.
Step 3: Open Claude Code
There are two ways to open Claude Code in VS Code:
•	Claude icon - If you have a file open, look for the Claude icon in the editor and click it to open the Claude Code panel.
•	Chat panel - Click the chat icon in the activity bar (left sidebar), then switch between “Chat” (GitHub Copilot) and “Claude Code” at the top of the panel.
Step 4: Test Your Setup
With a project folder open in VS Code, try a simple prompt in the Claude Code panel:
Explain the structure of this project
If Claude responds with an analysis of your project files, your Portkey integration is configured correctly.
Tips for Using Claude Code in VS Code
•	Open a project folder first. Claude Code works best when you have a project folder open in VS Code, giving it context about your codebase.
•	Use natural language. Describe what you want in plain language - Claude will figure out which files to read, edit, or create.
•	Review changes before accepting. Claude Code shows you diffs of proposed changes. Review them carefully before approving.
•	Combine with other VS Code features. You can use Claude Code alongside VS Code’s built-in debugger, terminal, source control, and other extensions.
•	Switch between Chat and Claude Code. If you also have GitHub Copilot, you can switch between the two in the chat panel depending on your needs.
Known Limitations
Since you are connecting through Portkey rather than signing into a Claude account with a Pro or Max subscription:
•	Remote Control is not available. Features requiring a direct Anthropic account connection will not work through Portkey.
•	Slack integration is not available. The Slack app requires a direct connection to an Anthropic account and cannot be used with Portkey.
•	Some account-specific features may be unavailable. Features tied to Anthropic subscription tiers may not be accessible when routing through a third-party API gateway.

title: Platform and API Services How to Use Portkey APIs
body:
Portkey provides a unified API gateway that allows you to access multiple AI models (OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, and more) through a single, consistent interface. This guide walks you through making API calls to Portkey using cURL and Python, the two most common methods for interacting with AI models programmatically.
Before following this guide, make sure you have a Portkey account and API key. If you have not set up your access yet, see Getting Started with Portkey at Rutgers first.
Table of Contents
•	Safety and Data Protection
•	Using Portkey with cURL 
o	Step 1: Get Your Credentials
o	Step 2: Make a Request
o	Switching Models
•	Using Portkey with Python 
o	Step 1: Set Up Your Project
o	Step 2: Install Dependencies
o	Step 3: Get Your Credentials
o	Step 4: Create a .env File
o	Step 5: Create Your Python Script
o	Step 6: Run It
o	Switching Models
o	Using System Messages
o	Multi-Turn Conversations
•	Tips for Working with Portkey APIs
•	Tips for Getting Started
•	Links
Safety and Data Protection
When using Portkey APIs through your Rutgers account, your requests are routed through the university’s enterprise Portkey instance. Your data is protected by enterprise agreements and is not used to train AI models.
•	Protect your API key. Never commit your Portkey API key to a public code repository, share it in emails, or hardcode it in scripts that others can access. Use environment variables or .env files instead.
•	Do not send highly sensitive data such as protected health information (PHI), Social Security numbers, or financial account numbers through any AI API.
•	Review AI-generated output carefully. Model responses can contain errors, biased content, or fabricated information.
Using Portkey with cURL
cURL is a command-line tool for making HTTP requests. It is available by default on macOS and Linux, and can be installed on Windows. This is the quickest way to test your Portkey access.
Step 1: Get Your Credentials
1.	Sign in to the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area, within the Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account activated).
2.	Create your Portkey API key and save it.
Step 2: Make a Request
Open your terminal and run the following command, replacing YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY with your actual API key:
curl https://api.portkey.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-portkey-api-key: YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-portkey-provider: @openai-prod" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." },
      { "role": "user", "content": "Hello!" }
    ]
  }'
You should receive a JSON response containing the model’s reply. The key fields in the response are:
•	choices[0].message.content - The model’s text response.
•	usage.prompt_tokens and usage.completion_tokens - Token counts for the request and response.
Switching Models
To use a different model or provider, change the x-portkey-provider header and the model field. For example, to use Anthropic’s Claude:
 curl https://api.portkey.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-portkey-api-key: YOUR_PORTKEY_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-portkey-provider: @claude-models" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Hello!" }
    ]
  }'
Using Portkey with Python
Python is the most popular language for working with AI APIs. The Portkey Python SDK provides a clean, familiar interface that is compatible with the OpenAI SDK pattern.
Step 1: Set Up Your Project
Create a project directory and a Python virtual environment:
mkdir myproject
cd myproject
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
On Windows, activate the virtual environment with:
.venv\Scripts\activate
Step 2: Install Dependencies
pip install portkey-ai python-dotenv
•	portkey-ai - The official Portkey Python SDK.
•	python-dotenv - Loads environment variables from a .env file so you don’t have to hardcode your API key.
Step 3: Get Your Credentials
1.	Sign in to the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area, within the Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account activated).
2.	Create your Portkey API key and save it.
Step 4: Create a .env File
In your project directory, create a file named .env with the following content:
PORTKEY_API_KEY=your-portkey-api-key
Replace your-portkey-api-key with your actual Portkey API key.
Important: If you are using Git, add .env to your .gitignore file to prevent accidentally committing your API key to a repository.
Step 5: Create Your Python Script
Create a file named test_portkey.py with the following content:
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from portkey_ai import Portkey
load_dotenv()
client = Portkey(
    api_key=os.environ["PORTKEY_API_KEY"],
    provider="@openai-prod"
)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
Step 6: Run It
python test_portkey.py
You should see the model’s response printed to your terminal.
Switching Models
To use a different model, change the provider parameter when creating the client and update the model in the API call. For example, to use Anthropic’s Claude:
client = Portkey(
    api_key=os.environ["PORTKEY_API_KEY"],
    provider="@claude-models"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
Using System Messages
System messages set the behavior and personality of the AI model. Add a system message as the first item in the messages list:
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful academic writing assistant. Respond in a clear, professional tone."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Help me write an abstract for a paper about renewable energy policy."}
    ],
)
Multi-Turn Conversations
To have a multi-turn conversation, include the full conversation history in the messages list:
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is photosynthesis?"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "What role does chlorophyll play in this process?"}
    ],
)
Tips for Working with Portkey APIs
•	Start simple. Get a basic request working before adding complexity like system messages, multi-turn conversations, or streaming.
•	Use environment variables. Never hardcode API keys in your scripts. Use .env files and python-dotenv, or set environment variables in your shell.
•	Check your API usage. After making requests, visit the Rutgers Account Tools Self-Service area and looking for your Portkey card (once you have a Portkey account) to view your usage.
•	Handle errors gracefully. Wrap API calls in try/except blocks to handle network errors, rate limits, and other issues.
•	Consult available models. The models and providers available through Rutgers’ Portkey instance may differ from public Portkey documentation. Check your dashboard for a current list.
Tips for Getting Started
•	Start with a simple test. Use the cURL example above to verify your access before building anything complex.
•	Use environment variables for your API key. Store your Portkey API key in an environment variable (e.g., PORTKEY_API_KEY) or a .env file rather than hardcoding it in your scripts.
•	Check which models are available. The models available through Rutgers’ Portkey instance may differ from what is shown in public Portkey documentation. Check your dashboard or contact your administrator for a current list.

title: Support ANCOR Clients: How to enable the WebReg drop registrations feature
body:
This article outlines how a client can DROP an existing registration via the MyAccount on our WebReg module. This option is enabled at the branch level and is not contingent upon other branches using it; however, once turned on, it applies to any/all course sections for your entire branch. You cannot apply it only to specific course sections.
If you are interested in utilizing the Drop feature, the ANCOR Helpdesk System Administrators must enable this for you. Please first review below, then email the help desk if interested, ancorhelp@rutgers.edu.
There are two (2) possible DROP methods that can be used:
Preferred Method: Change Status
This method changes the status of the Assignment to Did Not Complete-Dropped.  NOTE: Drops are not permitted beyond the start date. You must determine how many days before the start you will allow the client to drop. After that time, the DROP feature will automatically be disabled for that section. 
When this method is used, invoices and payments are not automatically adjusted or refunded. Invoice and payment adjustments must be performed manually. For a refresher on refunds and other adjustments: ANCOR Refunds
1.	When enabled, the client will log in to their account using their username and password, then navigate to My Account in the upper right and select Registrations from the drop-down menu.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	The client will then see a blue DROP hyperlink to the right of any eligible course on the Registrations page, where all of their assignments are displayed. Again, the client must be logged in to view this page.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	After selecting Drop, the client will review the Drop Registration page and confirm by clicking Drop again under OPTIONS.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	When a client drops a course, the status on the Registrations page will change to “Inactive.” In ANCOR, the client's Assignment status will be updated to "Did Not Complete – Dropped". 
5.	The client will receive a confirmation email from ANCORHelp@rutgers.edu with the subject line: "Drop confirmation via web registration".
6.	An email is also sent to your Branch Notification Email address from NoReply@Xenegrade with the same subject line/email content. 
Alternate Method: Delete
This method deletes the assignment entirely. No historical record of registration.
NOTE: This method can only be used if there are NO invoices and/or payments, NO Case Notes linked to the Assignment, and NO Attendance records.  
Drops are not permitted beyond the start date. You must determine how many days before the start date you want to allow the client to drop. After that time, the DROP feature will be disabled for that section.
1.	When enabled, the client will log in to their account using their username and password, then navigate to My Account in the upper right and select Registrations from the drop-down menu. 
2.	The client will then see a blue DROP hyperlink to the right of any eligible course on the Registrations page, where all of their assignments are displayed. Again, the client must be logged in to view this page. 
3.	After selecting Drop, the client will review the Drop Registration page and confirm by clicking Drop again under OPTIONS. The assignment will then be deleted from the client’s Registration Details page and from the ANCOR backend. 
4.	As with the Change Status method, the client will receive a confirmation email from ANCORHelp@docs with the subject line: “Drop confirmation via web registration.” An email is also sent to your Branch Notification email address from NoReply@Xenegrade with the same subject line/email content. 
REMINDER: If you are interested in this feature, the ANCOR Helpdesk System Administrators must enable this for you.  
Please email the ANCOR Helpdesk with the subject line "Enable Drop Feature". You must include:
•	Which method you would like to use. 
•	How many days before the start date of any course you wish to expire the DROP option.

title: Support ANCOR Courses: How to closeout a course section
body:
This article outlines the procedures for closing out a Course Section and updating clients' Assignment Status.
The following steps are required to close out a course section:
1.	Updating Course Section Status
2.	Updating Client Status/CEUs/Grades - Individually (per client)
3.	Updating Client Status/CEUs/Grades - Bulk (per course section)
To maintain accurate noncredit student records, the following procedures are required for all courses/programs and enrollment data managed in ANCOR.  
•	All course offerings must be closed upon completion; and,  
•	All learners must have an updated enrollment status for each course they participated in -- e.g., "Completed-Satisfactory." 
Only students with accurate, updated status will appear on Noncredit Transcripts. This remains the best practice for accurate student data management across CE, but it is now required for ANCOR users.
Updating Course Section Status
Following the end date of a course section, it is important that you properly update the Course Status to remove it from the catalog. It also provides you with an accurate historical record of courses that have been cancelled, completed, etc.
Course Status is updated at the Section level.  
1.	Navigate to the course section and then click EDIT on the Section panel.  
2.	For the Course Status field, select the status (ie, Completed); select other status when appropriate.  
3.	Click SAVE at the top of the Section panel to commit changes.

Error! Filename not specified.
Updating Client Status
You may update client status individually or in bulk for the entire course roster.
Individual Client Update
1.	Locate the client by clicking on Clients and searching by Name or Client ID#. 
2.	Click the pencil icon to Edit the client account.  
3.	Click the Assignments tab to view the client’s assignments.  
4.	Click the pencil icon to Edit next to the assignment to update.
5.	Change the Enrollment Status (select the appropriate status – ie. Completed-Satisfactory).  
6.	To add Grades or Credits, expand the Grade/Outcome panel and click EDIT. 
o	NOTE: credit types & credit values should already be added to the course section under More > Credits.

Error! Filename not specified.
7.	Enter Grades (as applicable).
8.	Earned Credits – enter number of credits for completed course (as applicable).
9.	Credit Type – use the drop-down menu to select a credit type already defined.
10.	Ensure that the Include on Transcript field is toggled to YES. 
11.	Click SAVE on each panel or SAVE ALL on the Assignment Information panel to save your changes.
Bulk Course Enrollment Status Update
CHANGE STATUS: This function allows you to change the Assignments Status and End Date for an entire course section.
1.	Click on the Tools button.

Before you can add custom questions, you must setup a Question Categories, if not already present and a Classification. This allows the questions to be visible during the registration checkout process.
Creating a Question Category
1.	View Question Categories from Main Menu > Selects N-Z > Question Category. 
2.	Confirm that a Question Category named WebReg already exists. If not, click the +New Question Category link to add a new Question Category and add WebReg.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Click Submit. A green banner prompt will display when complete.
Creating New Classifications
1.	Go to Main Menu > Selects > Classifications.  
2.	Click the +New Classification link in the blue toolbar to start a new record. 
3.	Enter a Classification. 
o	This will be the name displayed in the Client Classification record, so it should have some type of recognition for a user and be related to the question being asked during the check. Duplicate Classification names cannot exist. ?Names such as 'Parent' and 'Parent 1' can both exist. ?However, each will save as separate classifications under the Client Classification section.
o	The first four characters of the Classification should NOT be "Web-". ?This is a reserved classification prefix. 
4.	Classification Category field is optional. ?Entering a value may be helpful for reporting. Add a Classification Category by entering under Selects > Classification Categories. 
5.	Description is an optional field only visible to administrators. 
6.	Set Program Display to No. ?This field is not required or used in this case. 
7.	Set Web Display to Yes. ? ?If set to No, the question will not appear in the WebReg module. 
8.	Set the AutoOption to No. ?This field is not required or used in this case. 
9.	Save the Classification record by clicking +CREATE.
Custom Questions Overview
There are four types of Registration Questions. The difference between these four types lies in where replies are recorded and in the flexibility of the types of questions that can be asked. To specify the question type, the Classification Name entered during question setup must match an option from the reserved word-list provided.
Duplicate Classification names cannot exist.  Names such as Web-Contact and Web-Contact 1 can both exist. Both will save in the exact same location.
1.	Client Classifications Questions: 
o	The replies to these questions are recorded under the Client Profile tab, Classifications heading.
o	The name of the classification is recorded for the Client Classification, and the reply to the question is recorded in the Notes field.
o	These are the standard types of questions; no reserved words required.
2.	Client Info Questions: 
o	The replies for these questions?are recorded?directly into a specific existing field within the Client’s Info section and not in the Client Classification section.
o	The replies are preset to match the selected field.
o	Reserved word-list: 
	Web-Allergy:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Other panel.  Text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-BirthDate:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Formatted date reply as entered by the client.
	Web-CellPhone:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Address/Phone panel.  Formatted text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-CreditType:  This value will record in the Client's Assignment the Credit Type the client selected from the available Credit Types select list.  Can enforce credit type restriction based on Course Section Credit Types.
	Web-DominantLanguage:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Select list reply from Languages table.
	Web-Ethnicity:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Select list reply from Ethic table.
	Web-Gender:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Select list reply of M or F.
	Web-GradeCurrent:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Select list reply using list from -1 to 12 where -1 = pre-school, 0 = kindergarten and 1-12 = the year of school.
	Web-Guardian:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Info panel.  Text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-HomePhone:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Address/Phone panel.  Formatted text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-LicensePlate:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Other panel.  Text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-Medical:  This value will record in the Client’s Info »> » Other panel.  Text reply as entered by the client.
	Web-Nationality:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Select list reply from Countries table.
	Web-SocialSecurity:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Text reply as entered by the client.  Follows the format set in the Branch Profile.
	Web-SchoolCurrent:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Demographics panel.  Text reply as entered by the client or select reply as pre-entered by the user.
	Web-WorkPhone:  This value will record in the Client’s Info > Address/Phone panel.  Formatted text reply as entered by the client.
3.	Emergency Contact Question: 
o	This will allow up to two emergency contact records, with a minimum of one required. If any currently exist, the names will display for the client to review, but the client cannot see details or edit the existing contacts.
o	These questions are recorded in the Client Family section.
o	Reserved Word-list: 
	Web-Contact: This value will record in the Client’s Family tab. 
4.	Marketing Source Question: 
o	This feature will request the client to select a marketing source how they heard about the program and enter a marketing code if they have one. This feature differs from the same question asked in their profile. ?This feature records for all Assignments purchased from the WebReg module.
o	Reserved Word-list: 
	Web-HowHeard:  This value will record in the Client’s Assignment.
Setting Up Custom Questions
1.	Go to Admin/Security > Settings (gear icon) > Custom Questions.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click +NEW Custom Question to add.
3.	Question Settings: 
1.	Question Name: Title only visible to on the admin side.
2.	Question: ?Enter the question exactly as you want the question to display to the client including punctuation. ?Include instructions such as “Enter None if not relevant” for text boxes.
3.	Question Type: (use drop-down to choose type of answer requested) 
1.	Select: The Client will see a select list from the items added in the next field.
2.	Yes/No: The Client will see Yes and No radio buttons as the response to the question.
3.	File Upload: The Client will have a file upload option that records the file in the Client Documents area of the Client’s account record. (recommended to upload a PDF file)
4.	Text: The Client will see a text field to enter the reply. ?No formatting is enforced, so even dates will be entered as text.
5.	Checkbox: The client will see a single checkbox to check if they agree with or approve the question.
6.	Profile: Answers are stored on the Client’s Profile.
4.	Client Location: Only required for Client Info, Emergency Contact & Marketing Questions. 
5.	Select Options: ?Only required if the question type = Select. Type one selection (at a time) and click Tab to add each one.
6.	Question Description: Optional field, only visible to administrator.
7.	Question Required: Toggle Yes or No (client must answer the question if toggled to Yes).
8.	Question Frequency: Select how frequently the question should display.
9.	Question Order: When creating multiple questions, enter a numeric value to specify the order they will appear during the checkout process.
10.	Fee Group: Default = Regular. When used without Linked Sections, all clients of the desired Fee Group will see the question. If used in tandem with Linked Sections, only the Clients in the Fee Group and in the Linked Sections will see the question.
Linking Course Sections
1.	Go to the Course Section to link to the Custom Question. 
2.	To select a section, hover to the left of the Course ID and click the Checkbox. 
3.	Several links will appear above the section list. 
4.	Click the CLIENT QUESTIONS button.

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	A workflow will pop up: 
1.	Use the drop-down to select the Custom Question.
2.	Click Next to proceed.
3.	Review the Course Section and selected Question.
4.	Click the Confirm checkbox and click Submit.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	To view a list of Linked Course Sections: 
1.	Go to Admin/Security > Custom Questions.
2.	Hover your cursor to the left of the Custom Question and click the 'paper icon' - Sections.
3.	A list of linked Course Sections will be displayed. You may delete any sections by clicking the 'garbage bin icon' to the left of the Course Section.
Removing Course Section Links to Questions
Bulk Method
1.	Go to Admin/Security > Settings (gear icon) > Custom Questions
2.	Click the pencil icon to edit the custom question.
3.	Set the Delete All Linked Sections field to Yes.
4.	Click Save to update the record.
Single Course Section Method

InSight Report
This report can be used to pull a registration roster with replies to Custom Questions.

title: Support ANCOR Courses: How to create Canvas courses in ANCOR
body:
This article outlines the connection between ANCOR & Canvas and how to set up courses in ANCOR to push to Canvas to create the API connection.
Integration
ANCOR Branches must be assigned a Canvas subaccount before linking courses between systems. Contact the ANCOR Helpdesk to make a request. This builds the ANCOR to Canvas API connection.
Course Creation
ANCOR is the system driving the Canvas course shell creation – you must create the ANCOR course/section first and then Send to Canvas to create the Canvas course shell. All content can then be added on the Canvas side, while ANCOR then controls registration. 
1.	Courses are created in ANCOR with the following addition: 
1.	Go to Services > Courses > + NEW COURSE.
2.	In the Vendor field, select Canvas as the vendor. This is REQUIRED 
	NOTE: If you have an existing course in Canvas, see instructions for linking to ANCOR at the end of this guide.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Create course section(s) for each instance to be populated in Canvas as an online course offering.  You must create a new course section in ANCOR to generate a Canvas course shell. (Existing courses that you now want to create Canvas offerings for can be edited by simply updating the vendor to Canvas as well.) 
o	NOTE: If you are working with an existing ANCOR course section that already has registrants, please contact the ANCOR Helpdesk for assistance.
3.	Review to ensure ANCOR courses/sections are complete, with all requisite course information – i.e., section ID, status, start/end dates, instructor, and confirmation templates (see COMMUNICATIONS below).
4.	You are now ready to push the Course Section to Canvas.
5.	Go to Services > Courses > Sections > Section > Section Information > Actions.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	For each Section, you may elect to create an online course in Canvas via one of two methods: 
o	Send Unique Course/Section to Canvas – The ANCOR section will be pushed to Canvas as a separate Canvas course site, with no shared functionality (This should be your selection for INITIAL course creation or if it is a one-time program with no plans for multiple offerings, creating a new Canvas Course & Section each time).
o	Send Section under Course to Canvas – ANCOR sections listed under a single ANCOR course will be created as multi-sections within one (1) Canvas course site (This should be your selection if you offer course sections multiple times and will remain under the same Canvas Course).
The course in Canvas will be unpublished until all content is created in Canvas, and the instructor/Canvas admin elects to publish the course; however, students can still register if the course section is set to Offered in ANCOR.
NOTE: If future updates are made to a course section in ANCOR, admins can use the Update to Canvas option as well; however, only Course DATES will be updated. All other changes must be made manually on the Canvas site, including instructor changes.
Instructor Enrollment
1.	ANCOR admins must assign Staff to the ANCOR section (Staff > + NEW STAFF). Instructors must have a Canvas account and an ANCOR staff account with matching email addresses. 
2.	Once a course section is created and sent to Canvas, the ANCOR Staff will be enrolled in Canvas and receive a standard Canvas course invitation as an instructor only if: 
o	The ANCOR staff has a Canvas account; and,
o	The default email in Canvas matches their ANCOR Staff account email.
NOTE: The Branch Admin will receive an error in ANCOR if the instructor is not enrolled. Please read all pop-up messages carefully.
Student Enrollment
1.	Once a student registers via WebReg, ANCOR will automatically enroll the student in the Canvas course. 
2.	If a user has multiple emails in Canvas in their user profile, this reduces duplicate account creation, since ANCOR searches the Communication API rather than the User profile (which lists only a single default email). 
3.	If an ANCOR email address returns more than one Canvas user ID, ANCOR will associate the enrollment with the lowest Canvas User ID – i.e., the oldest account. 
o	This means that NetID users who are registered for ANCOR will log in with their NetID.
4.	If there is no email match, ANCOR will create a new user account.
5.	Once created, Canvas will send an “account creation” email message with instructions for users to log in, create a password, and/or add any other associated email addresses.
o	If a student adds an email address to their profile during the final steps of Canvas account creation AND that email address already exists in Canvas, then Canvas will automatically merge the accounts.
Communications
Each branch must have a Canvas Confirmation email template before launching registration. This communication is triggered automatically for web registrations and provides students with the necessary information to access their Canvas course(s). You only need to set it up once. Please contact the ANCOR Helpdesk for assistance.
1.	To confirm that the Canvas Confirmation email template exists or to modify it.
2.	Go to Tools (box icon) > Marketing Functions > Create Email Templates.
3.	The Template Name must be Canvas Confirmation to be automatically triggered at registration.

title: Support ANCOR Courses: How to create courses and sections
body:
This article outlines the steps to create a new Course and Section in ANCOR. You must create both a Course and Section to enable a WebReg link so clients can register for classes.
Before you create a course and/or section, you must confirm the following: 
•	Buildings, Facilities, Locations, Policies. If you need to add new information to these categories, do so by going to Main Menu > Selects > (Buildings, Facilities, Locations or Policies). Please review each one of these to ensure they are ready before creating a course.
•	Confirm your instructor(s) have a Staff account by going to Main Menu > Staff.
•	Sessions - A Session must be created before creating a new Course or a new Section. Main Menu > Selects N-Z > Sessions.
How to Create a New Course
1.	From the Main Menu, choose Services and click Courses.
2.	Click +New Course.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Enter a Course ID (user-defined – cannot be duplicated) and a Course Title. 
4.	Enter a brief course description for the course in the Description text box (Use the text editor in the top right corner of the text box, as needed).

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	If you are creating a CANVAS course, please also complete these two additional required steps: 
1.	Vendor: Select Canvas if this course will be linked to Canvas. Otherwise, leave it blank.
2.	Alt Course Title: Enter the course title here to display in Canvas. Otherwise, leave it blank.
6.	Click CREATE to save the new course. 
o	TIP: The CREATE button saves the course record and opens the course in view mode to continue editing. The CREATE AND ADD NEW button will save the course record and open a blank +New Course form to create an additional new course.
7.	You can add additional information to the new Course by clicking EDIT on the information panels.
8.	REQUIRED: Click Edit > Requirements and select Yes to Include on Transcript. 
o	(Important note: A Course can have unlimited Sections, but each Section must have a unique Section ID.)

How to Create a New Section
1.	Click the Sections tab. 
2.	Click +New Section. 
3.	Enter a unique Section ID (max. 15 characters). 
4.	Select a Session. 
5.	Select a Course Status. (Important note: The Course Status must be set to “Offered” to open registration.)
6.	Enter the Start and End Date. 
7.	Enter the Start and End Time. 
8.	Select Location. 
9.	Select Instructor 1 (required). (A secondary instructor may be added, but it is not required.) 
10.	Select Department. 
11.	Enter Total Scheduled Hours. 
o	TIP: To calculate Total Scheduled Hours, take the total amount of learning time and remove any planned/scheduled breaks. Please calculate the total course hours, not hours for each single class. Example: A class with 10 sessions, at 90 minutes each -> (1.5 hours x 10) = 15 Total Scheduled Hours.

o	Maximum Enrollment (registrations exceeding the Maximum will be waitlisted)

title: Support ANCOR Financial: How to create a Discount
body:
This article outlines how to create a discount used during the WebReg registration process to reduce course fees. 
1.	From the Main Menu, click Financial and select Discounts.
2.	Click +New.
3.	Select the discount Type from the drop-down: 
o	Promo Code: A single word or group of letters, up to 12 characters - Promo Codes are not case sensitive.
o	Early Registration:  
	Enter a positive number of days prior to the Start Date.
	Entering a value of zero allows a discount to be applied up to the start date.
	Course Section must have a Start Date to trigger the Early Registration discount.
o	Quantity: 
	Enter a positive number; courses required to trigger the discount.
	Include Members checkbox.
	NOTE: If registrations for the client's Members can be used toward qualifying for a Quantity discount, check the box for Include Members. Otherwise, the Members' registrations are ignored.
o	Corporate: 
	Restricted to members of Corporate Client.
	Must be a Member of a Corporate Client; Corp client not eligible.
	Must NOT be the first registrant.
	Client & Corporate Client must have the same Company listed.
4.	Enter a unique Title. 
o	The discount Title will appear on WebReg.
o	Do not include the word 'discount' in the title. "Discount" will be automatically applied at checkout.
5.	Enter either the exact Discount Amount or the Discount Percent to be calculated during checkout.
6.	Description: Optional.
7.	Enter the Promo Code that clients will enter during checkout? (Note: during checkout, clients must click the Recalculate button to apply the discount).
8.	Auto Add Admin: Used only in the admin portal.
9.	One Time Use: Toggle Yes to restrict use to one time.
10.	Enter Start Date for discount to begin (OPTIONAL).
11.	Enter End Date for Discount?(REQUIRED).
12.	Parameters to trigger Discount (TIP: Only set enough parameters that meet your criteria). 
o	Course: If ALL Sections qualify
o	Section: If only ONE section qualifies
o	Category: If ALL Sections of the Courses with this Category qualify
o	Session: If ALL Course Sections in the selected Session qualify
o	Program Group: If ALL Courses or Sections in the Program Group qualify
o	Fee Group: If valid only for the specified Fee Group
13.	Click CREATE to save.
Create a Course Category (Optional)
If utilizing Course Category as a criterion to trigger a discount, follow the steps below. This feature will group a particular set of courses and enable a discount code for course registrations.
1.	From the Main Menu, click Selects, then under Selects A-D,  click Course Categories.
2.	Click New Course Category.
3.	Create Course Category?.
4.	Enter the name for the Course Category?.
5.	Search Type is Course for courses?.
6.	Selections may also be Conferences, Products or Memberships?.
7.	Click OK to save the entry?.
8.	Next, tag courses to the Course Category.
9.	From the Main Menu, click Services > Courses.
10.	Utilize the search box to locate the appropriate course and click Search?.
11.	Locate the course and click the Paper icon to view the details.
12.	Click Edit to expand the Cataloging panel.
13.	Click the drop-down menu for Category and select the appropriate Course Category?.
14.	Click Save to save the entry.
15.	Repeat for all courses/sections you wish to apply the same discount.

title: Support ANCOR Financial: How to split an invoice
body:
This article will outline how to generate new invoices from an existing invoice that allow clients to pay in either installments or to split the original invoice by course.
There are two workflow methods to split your Invoice:  
•	Split by Course: This option allows an Admin to move all the line items and payments linked to a specific course assignment from one invoice to a new invoice or another invoice within the same client.  A message is added to the source and target invoice note sections when the split function is used.
•	Split by Invoice: This option allows an Admin to create up to 10 new invoices as an installment payment plan from one course code on an existing invoice.  The original invoice is not modified during this process; you must manually modify it after using this function. Each row entered creates a separate invoice for the same course code.
Invoice Lookup
1.	Begin by searching for the Invoice.
2.	Go to Clients and search for the client.  
3.	Click the kebab menu (three dots) and select Invoices.

Error! Filename not specified.
Split by Courses (Option 1)
This built-in workflow will guide you through the steps to move a registered course from the original invoice to a NEW or existing invoice, leaving all other courses registered on the original invoice.
1.	Select one of the course codes and then, under Select Target Invoice select New Invoice or using the drop-down menu, select another existing Invoice to move the course to.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click SPLIT BY COURSE to complete the process of splitting the invoice.   
3.	A NEW Invoice will be generated, moving all line items, fees, payments, and assignments.
Split by Invoice (Option 2)
This built-in workflow will allow you to create multiple invoices for an installment payment plan. You can create up to 10 new invoices as an installment plan and add a company or funding source for each new Invoice.
1.	Click SPLIT PAYMENTS to split the invoice.

title: Support ANCOR InSight: Transcripts
body:
This custom report allows the user to select a Transcript with either all client assignments as a Record of Registration or an Official Transcript displaying only completed coursework.
Uploading a Staff Digital Signature
It is the sole responsibility of each noncredit unit to ensure that the appropriate signature(s) are on file within the ANCOR system. Please review the steps outlined in the ANCOR STAFF: Uploading Digital Signatures to Staff Profiles article to ensure a signature has been uploaded properly prior to running a Transcript report.
Report Location
To find the reports, select InSight from the main menu toolbar on the left side of the screen. 
Note: If you do not see the menu links, click the three horizontal lines at the top left to expand the global menu. 
Error! Filename not specified. 
Error! Filename not specified.
Transcripts
1.	Scroll down to Local Reports and click the Credentialing dropdown.
2.	Then click Transcripts.
3.	Next, click to select either Record of Registration (unofficial) or Transcript (official) to open the report.
NOTE: There are TWO types of Transcript reports: 
•	Record of Registration (unofficial): (no seal, no signature) 
o	A Record of Registration is an unofficial comprehensive record of noncredit course activity, including all registrations and cancellations. It does not contain a signature nor does it constitute successful completion of all noncredit coursework. 
•	Noncredit Transcript (official): (digital signature required) 
o	All course offerings must be closed upon completion; and,
o	This report will ONLY display courses that have an enrollment status of Completed/Satisfactory.
o	Only students with accurate, updated status will appear on Noncredit Transcripts. 
Course, Section, and Assignment settings
Prior to running a Transcript report, the Course and Section's Include on Transcript field should be toggled to Yes. 
•	Course settings 
o	On the Requirements panel, toggle Include on Transcript to Yes
•	Section settings 
o	On the Schedule panel, toggle Include on Transcript to Yes
The client's Assignment Status for the courses listed on the transcript must be set to Completed prior to running the transcript report. 
Note: If these settings are not updated, the courses will not appear on the transcript. 
Running the Report
How to filter your report 
Record of Registration (unofficial)
1.	Click Client Last Name (s--) filter - Type the Client’s Last Name.
2.	Click Client First Name (s--) filter- Type the Client’s First Name.
3.	OPTIONAL: Click Client ID and enter the ID number for the specific client. (ie. RU363950000) This additional filter is useful for clients with common names.
4.	Click the blue Apply Filter button to the right of the Filter toolbar to refresh your results.
Noncredit Transcript (official)
1.	Click Signature Name (*required) filter to select a Staff signature.
2.	Click Client Last Name (s--) filter - Type the Client’s Last Name.
3.	Click Client First Name (s--) filter- Type the Client’s First Name.
4.	OPTIONAL: Click Client ID and enter the ID number for the specific client. (ie. RU363950000) This additional filter is useful for clients with common names.
5.	Click the blue Apply Filter button to the right of the Filter toolbar to refresh your results.

title: Support ANCOR Refunds: How to Process a refund in NelNet & ANCOR
body:
This article will outline all the steps required to properly and fully refund a client. In this multi-step process, you must first process the refund back to the client's original payment method in NelNet, then log in to ANCOR to record the refund. Please review the steps outlined below. Both steps must be completed to ensure the refund is properly processed.
STEP 1: Refund process in NelNet
Payments made by eCheck cannot be refunded through NelNet. A manual check request must be done. (see Addendum at the end of this article on how to process a Manual Check request) 
Refunds can only be processed within 180 days of the original transaction date. Any transaction older than 180 days cannot be processed through NelNet and must be issued through a manual check request. 
1.	Log in to NelNet using your individual credentials.
2.	Click the green QuikPay tile.
3.	Click Find Transaction from the side menu.
4.	Enter search criteria to locate the transaction and click Search. 
o	Confirmation number found on client receipt or in ANCOR.
o	Dollar amount of the transaction.
o	Date of transaction.

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	Click on the corresponding Confirmation # to review the details of a transaction.

Error! Filename not specified.
7.	Click Refund at the bottom of the page to begin processing a refund.
8.	Review transaction information, enter the refund amount at the bottom of the page, then click Continue. 
o	If processing a partial refund, enter the amount to refund.
9.	Click Refund to process. 
o	Note: partial refunds will allow additional refund(s) up to the balance amount in the future.
o	Transactions with multiple GL or project accounts cannot be refunded through NelNet and must be issued manually, typically as a paper check.

•	A refund will have a CR (credit) next to the transaction amount on the transactions list.

STEP 2: Recording the refund in ANCOR
NelNet QuikPay refunds do not automatically record in ANCOR; therefore, this is a manual process done in conjunction with the NelNet refund process.

title: Support ANCOR: How to create course bundles
body:
BUNDLES in ANCOR, allow you to group courses/products for purchase in various ways. If you have any questions or require assistance setting up a Bundle, please do not hesitate to contact the ANCOR Help Desk by emailing ancorhelp@rutgers.edu 
There are four different types of Bundles that can be created: 
•	Corequisite and Subrequisite Bundles: These are groups of courses that require clients to register for additional courses based on the courses already in their cart. 
•	Cross Selling Bundles: Cross Selling Bundles are groups of courses that suggest other courses on the course display page the client is viewing.
•	Products Link Bundles: Product Link Bundles are groups of products that are suggested for purchase based on the course display page the client is viewing, and allow the client to add the products to the cart at the same time as the course section.
•	Pricing Bundles: A set of courses that can be registered for simultaneously. Bundled pricing also allows each course to be priced differently from the individual courses. 
Create a Bundle
1.	Navigate and click on Services from the Main Menu. 
2.	Click Bundles from the drop-down.
3.	Click New Bundle.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Enter bundle information: 
o	Select Type: 
	Corequisite: Requires registration of all the courses in the bundle if any one of the courses in the bundle is added to the cart.
	Subrequisite: Requires registration of all the "Required" courses in the bundle if any one of the "Primary" courses in the bundle is added to the cart.
	Cross Selling: A list of suggested course titles appears at the bottom of the course details page when a client is viewing a course section.
	Product Links: A list of suggested product titles displays after the course section fees at the bottom of the course display page when a client is viewing the details of a course section.
	Pricing Bundles: An optional separate menu displays the Pricing Bundles list on the WebReg module. A client can select the course sections from the available list when viewing the bundle details. If one or more course sections are unavailable for registration, the bundle will display but cannot be purchased.
o	Title: Unique name for the bundle
o	Modules: WebReg (This field will always be set to WebReg. No action needed)
o	Start/End Date (Optional): These dates are optional and should be used only when creating a bundle with a specific active date range. Leave these dates blank if the bundle is always active.
o	Description: (Optional): Not visible to the client
o	Fee Group: (Only for Pricing Bundle) Default = Regular
Error! Filename not specified.
5.	Click Create to Save.
Editing/Customizing Bundle

Always/Other: Set the value of this field to Always if the suggestion should always display, regardless of the registration status of the course. Set the value of this field to Other if the suggestion should display only when the registration status of the course is not Registration Available.

body:
A user is asking for help with their PowerAutomate flows, what should I do?" "
Troubleshooting and Transferring Power Automate Flows
Since flows are tied to specific environments within the Power Platform, delegated admins cannot easily search for or manage flows created by other users. If a delegated admin receives a request involving an existing flow such as troubleshooting or transferring ownership they should first gather as much detail as possible from the requester. Useful information includes:
•	The user or group that currently owns the flow
•	The user or group that should receive ownership (if applicable)
•	The name or purpose of the flow
•	The environment where the flow may have been created (if known)
Not all users may know which environment the flow is in, so this detail is helpful but not always available.
Once this information is collected, email connect_support@oit.rutgers.edu for further assistance.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect Are OneDrive files subject to the same Rutgers e-discovery policy as is email?
body: Yes. Rutgers Connect/Office 365 usage also is covered by the University’s Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect Can files be shared across groups within Rutgers Connect?
body: Yes. All Office 365 services have a file sharing mechanism, including separate permission levels for individual folders and files.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect Can I use OneDrive as a backup server for my files?
body:
All data on Rutgers Connect itself (email, calendars, OneDrive) is automatically backed up by Microsoft, but you should not use OneDrive as your primary backup storage for your desktop files, for a number of reasons.
There is a transfer limit for downloading files, of any type, from OneDrive. You may not be able to retrieve files as rapidly as you were able to upload them to OneDrive. Avoid storing very large files on OneDrive until you are more familiar with how rapidly you can retrieve files.
All data stored on Rutgers Connect (including email and other files, whether business-related or personal) is subject to eDiscovery or Open Public Records Act (OPRA) requests, as are files and other data stored on work equipment (such as a Rutgers-provided laptop/desktop/mobile device). You should keep personal email and files off of all Rutgers equipment and services if you don’t want the personal files to be included in such requests.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect How many copies of Office 365 can I install with my Rutgers Connect account?
body:
Each Rutgers Connect license allows a user to install:
•	5 copies of Office 365 on your desktop (PC or Macs)
•	5 copies of Office 365 for your tablets (Windows, iPad, Android)
•	5 copies of Office 365 for your phones
After a platform's registration limit is reached, new registrations will automatically deactivate the oldest registration on the platform.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect What are the Security Features of Advanced Threat Protection (ATP)?
body:
Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) acts as a second layer of protection for attachments and links included in email messages for Rutgers Connect. ATP is composed of two components:
Attachment Scanning
All attachments that have never been seen by Rutgers Connect, including those attached to external and internal messages, will be thoroughly checked for possible malware by ATP. If ATP detects a malicious attachment, it will remove the attachment and deliver the email with a note regarding the removed attachment.
This scanning may delay the delivery of a message by a few seconds or minutes.
URL Scanning and Wrapping
ATP will scan and block all web addresses (URLs) arriving from outside Rutgers Connect that are known to contain malicious content, including malware and phishing sites. Links viewed in plain-text mail will be rewritten to link first to a safelinks.protection.outlook.com address and will likely be longer than the original URL. Non-harmful links will function normally when clicked, while links identified as harmful will redirect the user to a warning page.
The protections afforded by ATP also extend to Office 2016 ProPlus desktop applications. Harmful links found in Office documents will be protected by the same webpage-scanning and link-blocking technologies described above, adding a layer of protection to the desktop environment.
Additional information regarding Advanced Threat Protection for Rutgers Connect can be found on the Rutgers ATP news article.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect What is the difference between a Group and a Contact Group in Connect?
body:
A Group is a comprehensive way for multiple people to collaborate and organize their activities. Groups can be used to send email to every member of the group, but this is not the full extent of their functionality: they can have shared files through OneDrive, a list of tasks through Planner, a site, and much more. Additionally, Groups can be viewed and joined (if not private), and members can leave.
A Contact Group, however, is only visible to its creator and cannot be joined or left. It is simply a list of contacts in the creator’s address book. It is also known as a distribution list and is used only to send an email to every member.
For more on Groups, see Microsoft’s article on Groups. For more on Contact Groups, see Microsoft’s article on Contact Groups.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect What type of virus protection is available for Rutgers Connect?
body: Microsoft provides its own virus protection service which covers all data (email, files) stored on Rutgers Connect.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect Why am I unable to save an email directly to OneNote by emailing me@onenote.com?
body:
OneNote lets you save emails simply by emailing me@onenote.com (more information is available in Microsoft's "Email to OneNote" guide).
In order to use this feature, your primary email address in Connect (the address that appears when your name is searched in Connect and serves as your default “From” address) must exactly match your UPN (short for “User Principal Name” – the address that you use to log into Connect). If these addresses do not match, you will need to save the emails manually when you wish to add them to OneNote.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect Why do some of my groups not appear in OneDrive OWA?
body:
Groups do not appear in the list on the left-hand side of OneDrive OWA by default. To make a group appear:
1.	Go to the OneDrive web app and choose the group from the list of folders on the left-hand side.
2.	Select Go to site in the top right corner of the menu.
3.	On the site, you will see a star labeled Not following to the top-right; select it so that it changes to Following.
Afterward, the group will now appear in OneDrive OWA.

Background
Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) is a tool for network administration that enables the creation and enforcement of security policies. This allows for simplified management, and more dynamic allocation of access. Cisco ISE replaces the back-end RADIUS servers which previously supported RUWireless and ResNet. It also replaces the front-end Network Authentication Portal (NAP) used by OIT staff to view authentications, sessions, and manage bypassed endpoints. Cisco ISE uses your NetID and password to login, and will prompt your mobile device with a DUO push (you need to have a mobile device enabled with DUO to access ISE).
There is a 1:1 replacement of most parts of NAP within ISE and some new terminology used within ISE which will be referenced herein.
•	RADIUS Authentications displays authentication data, which was previously contained in the top of NAP (RUWireless_Secure Auth Data)
•	RADIUS Accounting displays session data, replacing the bottom table (RUWireless Login Data) in NAP.
•	Endpoints replaces bypassing devices (the MAB tool) and the bypass list.
Additionally, Cisco ISE replaces the preset expiration dates on bypassed endpoints and instead ages them out after 6 months of inactivity. Therefore, users who had devices in the spring and return in the fall will no longer need to contact the Help Desk.
