title: PlayPosit – Accommodations and Moderation for Learner Success
body:
Rutgers University is committed to ensuring equal access to information, programs, and activities through its technologies, web pages, services, and resources for all its constituencies. Please refer to Rutgers IT Accessibility: Course Accessibility Guidelines.
PlayPosit is a visual learning tool that allows instructors to build lessons into videos so that students can learn while viewing a video. The tool lets instructors use a library of videos from YouTube, TEDx, and other video-hosting websites, including Rutgers MediaSpace, powered by Kaltura. Instructors can add quizzes or text lessons to help facilitate learning during the course of a video. The goal of PlayPosit, is to have students learn at their own pace in a fully online setting. Video content may provide some challenges for your learners, depending on their needs. The scenarios below, with links to support articles, may help you provide accommodations for your learners.
What is the student experience using PlayPosit?
This article describes the Student Experience using PlayPosit 3.0. Instructors may search the Premade Bulb library for the bulb entitled “The PlayPosit Learner Experience” to share with your students in preparation for graded assignments.
How can I learn more about PlayPosit accessibility?
Please review the article on PlayPosit Accessibility that covers topics such as PlayPosit 3.0 VPATs, PlayPosit accessibility roadmap, player keyboard shortcuts, and equation editor accessibility tips.
How do I allow one student multiple attempts without making a new assignment?
Instructors may reset the learner attempt. Alternatively, the assignment can be configured to require a minimum completion score. Minimum completion scores will not sync to Canvas until the learner has met the requirement and should not be used with Broadcast assignments or interactions that require manual grading. Instructors may set individual interactions to allow multiple attempts for all users.
How do I allow one student the ability to rewind a video?
While there is no specific setting to allow for different learners to have different behaviors during the bulb assignment, instructors may opt to support learners by exporting a worksheet of the bulb interactions as a preview of the content to come in the video. This worksheet may be made available to students who request it or added as a PDF link in the Canvas assignment details. PlayPosit bulb settings may be edited to allow all learners the ability to rewind a bulb. 
How do I allow students to view the video after bulb attempts are complete?
Students can always view a read-only version of the video after attempts are complete as long as the Canvas assignment is accessible with no available date restrictions.

title: Respondus Lockdown Browser & Monitor - Screencastify error
body:
You may receive an error when opening Respondus Lockdown Browser that says you need to remove Screencastify from Google Chrome. Screencastify is a screen recording and editing tool available as a Google Chrome extension.
Removing Screencastify from Google Chrome
To remove Screencastify, follow the steps below.
1.	Open Google Chrome.
2.	Click the three dots on the upper right of the browser.
3.	Click Extensions.
4.	Scroll down and find Screencastify.
5.	Click Remove under Screencastify.
Once Screencastify is removed, close Google Chrome and open Respondus LockDown Browser to see if you can access the Rutgers Canvas homepage. If so, you should be able to access your Canvas Quiz accordingly.
Removing Screencastify from Microsoft Edge
To remove Screencastify, follow the steps below.
1.	Open Microsoft Edge.
2.	Click the Extension icon and choose Manage extensions.
3.	Scroll down and find Screencastify.
4.	Click Remove under Screencastify.
Once Screencastify is removed, close Microsoft Edge and open Respondus LockDown Browser to see if you can access the Rutgers Canvas homepage. If so, you should be able to access your Canvas Quiz accordingly.
Other Troubleshooting Options
If removing Screencastify from your list of extensions does not work and opening Respondus LockDown Browser still prompts you to remove it, it is possible that another profile in your Google Chrome browser also has it.
Please switch to any other profile associated with the Chrome browser. See Switching profiles within Google Chrome.
If you are unable to access these profiles (family member, colleague, friend, etc.), fully remove the profile to remove Screencastify from your Chrome browser. See Remove a profile in Google Chrome.
Once Screencastify is removed from all profiles or all other profiles have been deleted, please open Respondus LockDown Browser.
If you continue to receive the same error, complete the following actions:
1.	Remove any user data that is located with Chrome by following this file path:
o	PC: C:\Users\userid\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default
o	MAC: Users//Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default
2.	Uninstall Google Chrome, then reinstall Chrome.
If you are unable to remove the extension or completely uninstall it from Google Chrome, you will need to use another computer to take an exam or quiz that requires LockDown Browser. You can also reach out to the Canvas Help Desk for assistance.
Information in this guide can also be found in the Respondus article – Screencastify error.

title: Respondus LockDown Browser & Monitor – Getting Started for Instructors
body:
This document outlines the steps for instructors who would like to increase quiz or exam integrity by requiring LockDown Browser and the integrated Monitor for students to complete their assessment through Canvas Quizzes.
LockDown Browser is an application that must be downloaded. Providing a practice quiz before your assessment will help students identify technical issues. If your student has difficulties, you may need to make alternate accommodations. This tool does not restrict students from using other internet-enabled devices (tablets, smartphones, etc.) to search the web or a Canvas site.
Supplemental material can be found in Rutgers Canvas Commons by searching "Respondus Set-up".
Respondus LockDown Browser is only used in conjunction with Canvas Quizzes. It cannot be used with Canvas Assignments; however, both Classic Quizzes and New Quizzes support File Upload questions.
•	How do I create a File Upload quiz question in Classic Quizzes?
•	How do I create a File Upload assessment question using New Quizzes?
Table of Contents
•	Walk Through Instruction Video
•	Chromebook Extension Information
•	How to Enable LockDown Browser
•	How to Enable Respondus Monitor
Walk Through Instruction Video
 
Chromebook Extension Information
The Respondus LockDown Browser Extension is available for use with Chromebooks. While many security features are present, some features and behaviors are not available to students using Chromebooks. Known issues and limitations with the Chromebook Extension should inform your exam questions because these limitations may affect your students’ ability to complete your exam. These issues and limitations are:
•	LockDown Browser’s Calculator and Spreadsheet features aren’t currently supported.
•	The extended keyboard functions (for adding symbols and special characters) aren’t currently available.
•	LockDown Browser’s “Help Center” is currently unavailable, and there is no Live Chat support for students taking exams that require Respondus Monitor. The 
•	“Allow access to specific external web domains” option is currently not supported.
•	“Google Chrome OS can’t open this page” error will occur. Click Close on the error, and you should be able to proceed.
•	Exam feedback for “classic” quizzes is not yet compatible when viewed later. Feedback is viewable only in the same LockDown Browser session in which the exam was taken.
•	If a student is using a managed Chromebook that is configured and maintained by a school or organization, then the student may not have adequate permissions to install the Respondus LockDown Browser Extension. 
How to Enable LockDown Browser
1.	Access your Canvas course from the course dashboard or the Courses menu.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click LockDown Browser in your course navigation. If you do not see LockDown Browser in your course navigation, please enable it by managing your course navigation links. If this is the first time you are accessing LockDown browser, you will be asked to Authorize the application.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Review Video Tutorials, Getting Started, and Resources.
4.	For the desired Canvas quiz, click the drop-down menu next to the assessment name.
5.	Click Settings.
6.	Select the radio button labeled Require Respondus LockDown Browser for this exam to expand the options.  This radio button must be selected to turn on the LockDown Browser, preventing students from copying and pasting, printing, taking screenshots, accessing other programs, etc. LockDown Browser is required to use Monitor – you cannot use the Monitor feature without also using the LockDown Browser option.

Error! Filename not specified.
7.	Click to expand the Advanced Settings menu. 
1.	Require LockDown Browser to view post-exam feedback and results - If feedback and/or results are displayed after the exam, this option will require that LockDown Browser be used to view them.
2.	Lock students into the browser until the exam is completed – (Not Recommended). Typically, this box is checked only when LockDown Browser is used to proctor in-person exams. Checking this box can cause issues if, for example, the student’s internet connection is interrupted. They will remain locked in the browser until they forcibly restart their computer.
3.	Allow access to specific external web domains - This option can be used if, as part of the exam, the instructor has site(s) that they permit the students to access. This can be used to allow access to e-books or other approved online resources. For publisher materials, please test with a true student account (not just Student View).
4.	Enable Calculator on the toolbar - Use this option if a calculator is allowed or required during the exam. The students will not be able to start the calculator software included with their system, and the use of an external calculator will be flagged when the student looks away from the screen.
5.	Enable Printing from the toolbar – (Not Recommended)

     Error! Filename not specified.
8.	Click Save + Close.
How to Enable Respondus Monitor
     Error! Filename not specified.
1.	Select the radio button to Require Respondus Monitor for this exam if you would like this to be a video proctored exam. You can choose to have LockDown Browser record either the Webcam Only, both the Webcam and Screen, or Screen Only. 
2.	Select the radio button to Allow instructor live proctoring for this exam (via Zoom, Teams, etc) if you would like to utilize Live Proctoring for this Exam.  Further guidance on this can be found within the Live Proctoring section.
3.	In Startup Sequence, all options are enabled. Keep in mind that while completing these tasks does not count against the exam timer, they still take time to complete. If your exam is scheduled for one hour, it is useful to provide students with an earlier start time or a later end time to allow for these steps to be completed. 
o	Webcam Check – Requires the student to test their webcam before taking the exam. (This setting cannot be changed.)
o	Additional Instructions – You can enter additional instructions that will be displayed. 
o	Guidelines + Tips – The system displays helpful hints before the exam starts.
o	Student Photo – Requires the student to take a photo using their webcam
o	Show ID – Requires a student to take a picture of their ID. Many students are uneasy about providing state- or federally issued ID photos because they include additional private information. To avoid this concern, students should be informed in advance that they should use their Rutgers ID if you choose to require the submission of a photo ID.
o	Environment Check – The student will need to tilt/pan their webcam or laptop camera to show their working environment.
o	Facial Detection Check – The system will verify that it can detect a face using the webcam. (This setting cannot be changed.)
4.	Click Preview to demo the student experience.
5.	Where appropriate, Edit Text to provide more guidance for your students.
6.	Expand Facial Detection Options to ensure students remain in view of the webcam. 
o	Prevent students from starting the exam if face cannot be detected during startup sequence. Keeping this feature enabled is recommended.
o	Notify students during the exam if face cannot be detected. Keeping this feature enabled is also recommended so students are alerted if their face leaves the screen for any reason (e.g., the camera is covered or the student's hair or clothing obscures their face).
7.	Expand the option for Advanced Settings. Instructors may choose to use any of the settings below.  
1.	Allow use of an iPad for this exam - This enables the iPad Edition of LockDown Browser to be used with exams (download from the App Store). Because proctoring flags are based on webcam video, it's recommended that students be provided with instructions for using the iPad (e.g., position it vertically, place it on a stand, use an external keyboard). Note that screen recordings aren't available for iPad users. Also, the Excel option below cannot be selected at the same time as this option.  
2.	Allow switching to MS Excel during the Exam – This option requires the desktop version of the selected application to be installed on the student's computer, and is only available when Screen Recordings is selected above. Students using an iPad or Chromebook will not be permitted to access the test. Also, the proctored lab option cannot be selected at the same time as this option.  
3.	Allow this exam to additionally be delivered in a proctored lab – Students will have the option to use a web camera or to take the exam in a proctored computer lab. Instructors must share the password only with the exam proctor. See How does the optional setting in Respondus Monitor work?
4.	Enable "Show Your Work" step at the end of the exam – When checked, students must use their webcams to take photos of their worksheets and scratch paper. See Using the “Show Your Work” feature in Respondus Monitor. Expand Advanced Settings and check all that apply. 
8.	Second Camera 
o	Enable this option to require students to use two cameras during the exam: their primary webcam plus a mobile device camera. Students will scan a QR code with their mobile device to set up the second camera view. Click "Explain" to preview what students will see during setup.
9.	Click Save + Close
10.	To verify that Respondus Lockdown Browser and/or Monitor are enabled, you will see the following changes in your course: 
o	The Respondus Dashboard indicates whether Lockdown Browser & Monitor are required, only Lockdown Browser is required, or only Monitor is required.
o	Your Canvas Quiz name is changed and appended with “- Requires Respondus LockDown Browser” or “- Requires Respondus LockDown Browser + Webcam.” In this example, there is no name change when Lockdown Browser is not required (A), Requires Respondus LockDown Browser + Webcam (B) is added with LockDown and Monitor enabled, or Requires Respondus LockDown Browser (C) is added with only Lockdown Browser.

     Error! Filename not specified.

Note: Do not delete appended name changes, or Lockdown Browser will not recognize the exam.
11.	Your Canvas quiz settings are updated to reflect your Lockdown Browser/Monitor settings. 

     Error! Filename not specified.

In this example, Respondus Lockdown Browser and Monitor (Web camera required) are required to take the assessment. Lockdown Browser is required to view the answers.

title: Respondus LockDown Browser & Monitor – Getting Started for Students
body:
LockDown Browser is a browser that blocks access to other internet resources during quizzes and exams in Canvas. It prevents you from printing, copying, going to another URL, or accessing other applications during an assessment. If a quiz or exam requires LockDown Browser to be used, you will not be able to take the quiz or exam with a standard web browser.
LockDown Browser should only be used for taking Canvas Quizzes. It should not be used in other areas of Canvas.
Table of Contents

o	I am using a Chromebook but the App Store is locked. How do I unlock the App Store?
o	When I launch Lockdown Browser, why am I asked to turn off a browser plug-in?
o	Should I turn off my antivirus software to take a quiz with Lockdown Browser?
o	I am stuck on step 8a; the Webcam check. How do I get passed it?
Duo Two-Step Login with LockDown Browser
To authenticate with Duo when using the LockDown Browser, you will need to have an external device registered with Duo, such as a phone, tablet, or hardware token. The device must be set up to allow authentication through either the Verified Duo Push, Call, or SMS Passcode option.
Note: Touch ID authentication will not work in the LockDown Browser. If your Duo account is set to default to Touch ID, the LockDown Browser will automatically close. If this occurs, you must either remove the Touch ID authentication method from your Duo account or add a new device to Duo.
See Adding, removing, and renaming devices for two-step login with Duo.
Installing LockDown Browser for Windows or Mac
If LockDown Browser has already been installed, skip to the section on taking a quiz/exam with LockDown Browser. If not, LockDown Browser must be installed on each computer (Windows or Mac) being used to take a quiz or exam. You must have administrative rights to install the Lockdown Browser.
1.	Navigate to the quiz or exam that will be using the Lockdown Browser.
2.	Click Take this quiz.
3.	You should see a hyperlink that says “Download Respondus Lockdown Browser". Clicking this will bring you to the download page.

5.	Open the downloads folder and run the file titled “Install Respondus Lockdown Browser.”
6.	Accept the terms, select the location where you want Respondus installed on your computer, and then complete the installation.
Note: If you have an older version of the browser already installed, you may need to uninstall it and install the latest version using the instructions above. 
Installing LockDown Browser for Chromebooks
If LockDown Browser has already been installed, skip to the section on taking a quiz/exam with LockDown Browser. If not, the LockDown Browser extension must be installed on each Chromebook being used to take a quiz or exam. You must have administrative rights to install extensions in order to install the LockDown Browser extension. You cannot install the LockDown Browser extension on Managed Chromebooks.

•	Quiz passwords (specified via the “optional password” field in the LockDown Browser Dashboard) aren’t currently supported for exams that use only LockDown Browser. For exams requiring Respondus Monitor, the optional password field is supported.

I have a Chromebook. Can I use Respondus Lockdown Browser?

I am using a Chromebook, but the App Store is locked. How do I unlock the App Store?

Respondus Lockdown Browser, Google Chrome, Opera, and Microsoft Edge are all Chromium-based browsers with source code from the open-source Chromium Project.

title: WeVideo - Creating Accessible Videos
body:
Table of Contents
•	Accessible Questions
•	Add alternative text to an image
•	Add alternative text to an equation
•	Accessible Videos  
o	Captioning
o	Audio Descriptions 
 
On May 19, 2026, PlayPosit transitioned to the WeVideo Platform.
Accessible Questions
Students who are blind or have low vision may utilize special software such as screen readers to read out loud questions, any text-based information, and content created using the text editor. 
If you insert an image or an equation into a WeVideo interaction, you must add alternate text so that the information conveyed in the visual content is available to all your students. 
Add alternative text to an image
After uploading the image with the rich text editor, instructors can enter the alternative text in the Alternative description section. The alternative text will be read out for the learners using a screen reader and will also be displayed to the learners if the image fails to load. 
Error! Filename not specified.
Note: When adding images to a WeVideo playlist, instructors will not be able to enter the image description. Instead, the screen reader will read out the image's file name. Please change the file name to the desired alternative text before uploading it to the WeVideo playlist.
Add alternative text to an equation
When entering an equation with the equation editor, please replace the text in the Label section with the alternative text for this equation. The screen reader will read out the alternative text. For example, using the NVDA screen reader:
•	2+6=8 reads as "2 plus 6 equals 8", BUT
•	(2+6)2 reads as "2 plus 6 2", but should read as "parenthesis 2 plus 6 parenthesis squared".

Error! Filename not specified.
Accessible Videos 
Captioning
Captioning allows deaf and hard of hearing students to access your content.
The following process is recommended:
1.	Upload your video to Kaltura.
Whether you have created your own video or are using one from a third-party like YouTube, you can host that video in Kaltura MediaSpace. Kaltura videos can be automatically captioned, and if you have a student with a disability, it can be sent to a third party for professional captioning. 
o	Note: If you have a student with a disability approved for captioning, please reach out to radr.aslcart@echo.rutgers.edu to ensure that your videos are being professionally captioned.
2.	Select Kaltura when creating a new interactive video, and search for your Kaltura video.
3.	Click Customize then Captions. 
o	Note: The captions are uploaded when the video is linked from Kaltura. Later, if professional captions are completed, you will need to go back and edit the video to upload the new VTT file for the video. If Kaltura's automatically-generated captions are not complete when the interactive video is created, the captions will not appear in the dropdown to view available captions.
To add captions manually after uploading the video: 
1.	In your list of interactive videos, click Edit.
2.	Click the Video Segments tab.
3.	Click the Pen icon on the top right of the interaction.
4.	Click Edit Video Segment.
5.	Switch to the Accessibility tab and under Captions, select the file.
6.	Upload your VTT or SRT caption file (which can be downloaded from Kaltura). 
It's recommended to edit any automatically-generated captions in Kaltura before uploading them to WeVideo. Please review How to Edit Kaltura Captions.
Audio Descriptions 
For blind students, the video may need audio descriptions, which are additional tracks that allow the user to listen to words displayed on the screen or actions described in the video. If you are creating your own videos, you should read out anything presented on the screen, whether text on a slide or describing images being displayed.
If a student is blind in your course, please get in touch with radr@echo.rutgers.edu to determine if your video requires audio descriptions.

title: account audits
body:
Who can have a Box account?
According to Office of Information Technology guidelines, only the following classes of people are eligible to have Box accounts: 
•	Current employees of Rutgers University
•	Current students
•	Professor Emeritus
•	Guests: individuals who are conducting University business and are directly associated with the University, but are not officially on the University's payroll. For example, visiting professors/scholars, members of auxiliary groups, and others who are working on University business or affiliated with the University. 
The following groups of people are not eligible for Box accounts:
•	Former employees
•	Employees of other organizations who are performing work at Rutgers
•	Alumni
•	Retirees
Any of the above may be eligible for a guest account if a department or division of Rutgers is willing to sponsor them. Please see the Guest Account page for further information.
Recently re-hired employees who have not yet been added to the RIAS payroll system and thereby given a Faculty or Staff role may have their department's payroll person use the Early Employee NetID form to request an early role.
How can I keep my Box account?
We determine which accounts should be closed by comparing Box accounts with the active roles (e.g., Faculty or Staff) of NetIDs listed in the University’s OpenRegistry (OR) service, which is used as the basis for the Rutgers Online Directory. The OR may have some information that needs to be corrected.
If you have received an account closure notice and you believe that this is in error, please find the group you belong to in the appropriate subsection below (Current Employees, Students, Guests, Others) and follow the instructions there.
Current Employees
You may not be listed in the OR as a current employee. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
After your department’s Human Resources person has corrected your record, your department’s Rutgers Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Students
You may not be listed in the OR as a current student. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
OIT cannot permit prior students (such as students on leave and alumni) access to Box, as the system contains Restricted data such as Protected Health Information (PHI).
Guests
Guests must determine with their sponsor if Box is appropriate for their needs.
If you are affiliated with Rutgers but not employed full-time by Rutgers, you may request a guest account. Have a sponsor at the department you are working with go to the Guest Account site, and submit a request for you, which will be sent to our Accounts Office for processing. NOTE: A domain administrator within your department must activate a Box account for you. 
Every year, you must renew your guest account. You will be notified when the time to renew your account arrives (30 days before the expiration of the account).
Your Rutgers Delegated Administrator can assist your sponsor with submitting a Guest Account request and creating your Box account, if necessary.
Others
Retirees and alumni are not eligible for a Box account. 
If you do not fit into any of the above categories, you may want to try contacting a department at Rutgers related to your work and ask if they would be willing to sponsor a Guest account for you.
We have no mechanism for people no longer associated with Rutgers to pay a fee and thus keep their accounts. 
What is the typical account audit timeline?
Once an account is found to be ineligible for Box:
•	On day one, i.e., same day found to be ineligible: The account is sent an email notification.
•	On day seven, i.e., approximately one week later: The account is closed and any existing collaborators will lose access to personally owned files. To avoid this scenario, transfer any University-owned data to a departmental resource such as a Box shared drive or a Microsoft Team.
•	On day thirty-five, i.e., approximately 5 weeks later: The account is deleted from Box.
If the account is found to be eligible for Box at any time prior to deletion, the account will exit the audit.
Like all Rutgers NetID services, Box is subject to OIT NetID authentication processes. These practices may lock your Rutgers NetID – including Box access – on a different timeline. Visit https://eas.rutgers.edu/?ht_kb=off-boarding-process for details about NetID authentication off-boarding. Recent students in the “grace period” status described on that site are ineligible for Box. However, OIT will maintain data for the full duration of the “grace period” – the “day thirty-five" deletion does not apply in this case.
What should I do before the account is closed?
If you will be losing your Box account, you may want to take some of the following steps.
•	Visit the Service Management page. Under the Box section, click Show Box Collaborators to review a list of any files/folders that are shared to/from your account, as well as the individuals associated with those shares. 
•	Notify your regular collaborators of your account audit. Ensure any shared files that are still needed are transferred to a departmental resource, such as a Box shared drive or a Microsoft Team. 
•	Contact the IT staff in your department to determine the correct protocol for the data in your account. Departments that handle PHI or other sensitive data may have procedures put in place for security.
•	You will lose access to your Box data once your account is deleted, so you will want to save any files you may continue to need to another location. Please contact your local IT staff to assist with this process.
What happens after the account is closed?
After your account is closed, you will lose access to your Box account, and you will no longer be able to sign in to the account.
Approximately 4 weeks after your account is closed, your Box account will be deleted.
After an account is deleted, you will no longer be able to access any files. 
For further assistance
If you have questions about any of the above, you can send an email to help@oit.rutgers.edu or contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: at Rutgers

Box is available to all faculty, staff, students, and guests (guests must be permitted to create an account, at which point their Delegated Administrators or the OIT Help Desk can provision one). This is an extended guide to Box Group Management and RAD synchronization.
In the Rutgers Box tenant, groups are managed through RAD and then synchronized to Box. They are not managed in Box itself. This guide explains how delegated administrators can do this and provides a number of examples.
If you are looking for a brief overview of the process instead, please see the Box/RAD group sync quickstart guide.
What you will need:
•	An -adm account in RAD
•	Ability to manage RAD groups in your OU
•	An -adm account in Box
RAD -box-sync groups
Not all RAD groups are synced with Box. If you would like a RAD group synced to Box, you must indicate that by making it a member of a box-sync group in your OU.
There are two valid locations for a -box-sync group: in your top-level OU or in a sub-OU one level down. You can have as many of the latter as you want, so long as they are in different sub-OUs.
Any group in your OU can be a member of your top-level -box-sync group, but the -box-sync groups in sub-OUs can only contain member groups in the same sub-OU. If you make a group which resides outside of the OU or sub-OU a member of one of your -box-sync groups in RAD, that group will not sync to Box.
NOTE: -box-sync groups are only used to mark groups for synchronization and are not themselves groups in Box. As such, they should not contain any users directly. If you add users to a -box-sync group in RAD, they will be ignored during synchronization.
Why create more sub-OUs?
This allows for large units to use delegated administration more effectively. By parsing groups into sub-OUs, units do not have to give one department’s delegated IT staff access to manage RAD groups in the entire unit.
What if I don’t want to use sub-OUs?
If you have a small unit or do not want to use -box-sync groups in sub-OUs for any other reason, you do not have to use them. Simply place all of your OU groups that you want synced to Box into your top-level OU’s box-sync group.
Group flattening
Box does not support nested groups. When RAD groups, which contain other groups as members, are synchronized to Box, they must produce a flattened group in Box. Only the top-level group becomes a group in Box, but all of the members of all of its subgroups in the same OU/sub-OU are included (aside from -adm accounts, which are a special case addressed in the next section of the guide).
If you want a group to appear in Box, each member must be individually a member of an appropriate -box-sync group. If it is only a subgroup of a -box-sync group member, it will not become a group in Box, although its members will be included in the parent group that is synced to Box.
Setting Box Group Admins
Any -adm accounts in a RAD group synced to Box are made into group admins in Box, provided that the admin has an -adm account in Box. Box group admins will have permissions to manage shares for the group.
Unlike regular users, -adm users in subgroups of a group that is synchronized to Box do not become members of the parent group in Box. That would have the unintended side effect of making a delegated administrator for a sub-OU into a Box group admin for an OU-wide group. -adm accounts must be placed directly into any groups synced to Box.
If your -adm account is not a member of a group you marked for synchronization to Box, the group can still be synced. However, you will be unable to see it. Groups in our tenant are only visible to their members and admins, so it may appear on your end as though the synchronization did not work. A person must be a group admin of a specific group in order to see it in the Admin Console, and must be a group admin of at least one group in Box to see the Admin Console at all.
Group naming conventions
1.	The top-level -box-sync groups must be named [ou]-box-sync. The -box-sync groups one level down must be named [ou]-[sub-ou]-box-sync or [ou] [sub-ou]-box-sync depending on your separator preference (space or hyphen).
2.	RAD groups that you want to be synced to Box should be named in one of the following ways: 
o	[ou]-[freeform portion]
o	[ou] [freeform portion]
o	[ou]-[sub-ou]-[freeform portion]
o	[ou] [sub-ou] [freeform portion]
3.	There is no limit on how many sub-OUs a group name can contain. For example, the following is fine:   
o	[ou]-[sub-ou1]-[sub-ou2]-[sub-ou3]-[freeform portion]
4.	Both spaces and hyphens are valid separators, but each individual group name must be internally consistent.
5.	Your top-level -box-sync group can contain a group named [ou]-[sub-ou]-[freeform portion] and a group named [ou] [sub-ou] [freeform portion] without any issues, but a group named [ou]-[sub-ou] [freeform portion] or [ou] [sub-ou]-[freeform portion] is not correctly formatted.
6.	If a group that is poorly formatted in this way is placed in your top-level -box-sync group, it will still sync, but if it is placed in a sub-OU’s -box-sync group, it will not be recognized as part of that sub-OU and will not sync to Box.
*This is a deliberate choice to avoid ambiguity, not a limitation of the sync script.
The “Additional information” section of this page contains answers and explanations that may be handy.
NOTE: -box-sync groups are a special exception to the internal consistency requirement; if you want to use spaces to separate your top-level OU and sub-OUs, you can do so while using the required hyphen to separate the sub-OU from “box-sync.” For example, “Pets Cats-box-sync” is as valid as “Pets-Cats-box-sync.”
Warnings & notes
•	Synchronization is not instantaneous; identifying new or renamed RAD groups and the addition/deletion of members occur every half hour.
•	Once a RAD group has been synchronized to Box, deleting the RAD group or removing it as a member of its -box-sync group will break synchronization. Do not move or delete a Box-synchronized group in RAD unless you no longer want to use the group in Box.
NOTE: The -box-sync groups are unrelated and should not be confused with the Box Sync client. Box is promoting Box Drive over Box Sync until they phase Box Sync out completely.
•	The group will be renamed in RAD to indicate an error in synchronization, so this broken state will be readily apparent to end users.
•	The group’s membership will be retained as it was after the last successful synchronization — it will no longer be editable in any way. Shares to the group will be unaffected.
•	In the case of a moved group, moving it back to its original location will resolve the issue automatically. However, there is no easy fix for a deleted group.
o	If you no longer wish to use a group in Box, you can move or delete it in RAD and then request that Box support delete the group in Box (Note: please be sure to provide the Group Name).
•	You can add users to a RAD group marked for synchronization to Box even if they do not have a Box account.
o	Without a Box account, they cannot be immediately added as a member of the group in Box; however, when they activate a Box account, they will automatically be added to all of the groups they were previously made a member of.
•	Currently, this addition will happen the next time the sync script runs, but instant addition of newly-activated Box users to their assigned groups is in the works.
•	Group names containing parentheses are not supported.
Examples
For the examples in this guide, we will use the hypothetical delegated administrator “netid1” who manages the “Pets” OU.
First, we will consider examples using the top-level -box-sync group for the OU.
 
Correct
[OU] Pets
[GROUP] Pets-box-sync
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-All Dogs
[USER] netid1-adm
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Golden Retrievers
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid2
[USER] netid3
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Corgis
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid4
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Corgis
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid4
This will result in two groups being created in Box (Pets-Dogs-All Dogs and Pets-Dogs-Corgis). If a group is placed in a -box-sync group, members of its subgroups are synced as members of that parent group in Box, so Pets-Dogs-All Dogs would contain netid1-adm, netid2, netid3, and netid4.
 
Correct
[OU] Pets
[GROUP] Pets-box-sync
[GROUP] Pets Cats Bengals
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid5
[OU] Dogs
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-box-sync
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Golden Retrievers
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid2
[USER] netid3
This will result in two groups being created in Box (Pets Cats Bengals and Pets-Dogs-Golden Retrievers).
NOTE: Groups in the “Pets-Dogs-box-sync” group must also be in the “Dogs” sub-OU of “Pets,” while groups in the “Pets-box-sync” group do not have that restriction and only need to be in the “Pets” OU. Also note that both spaces and hyphens are fine as separators so long as each individual name uses them consistently.
 
Incorrect
[OU] Pets
[GROUP] Pets-box-sync
[USER] netid1-adm
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Golden Retrievers
[USER] netid2
[USER] netid3
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Corgis
[USER] netid4
[OU] Dogs
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-box-sync
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid2
[USER] netid3
 
Incorrect
[OU] Pets
[OU] Dogs
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-box-sync
[GROUP] Pets-Cats-Bengals
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid5
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs Siberian Huskies
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid6
[OU] Retrievers
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Retrievers-box-sync
[GROUP] Pets-Dogs-Retrievers-Golden Retrievers
[USER] netid1-adm
[USER] netid2
[USER] netid3
This Will Result in 0 Groups Being Created in Box!
A -box-sync group in a sub-OU can only contain groups in the same sub-OU. Therefore, “Pets-Cats-Bengals” cannot be included in “Pets-Dogs-box-sync,” because it is in the Cats sub-OU and not the Dogs sub-OU. “Pets-Cats-Bengals” should be placed either in a top-level “Pets-box-sync” group or else in a “Pets-Cats-box-sync” group in the Cats sub-OU.
Because “Pets-Dogs Siberian Huskies” does not use separators consistently, it is interpreted as being a group named “Dogs Siberian Huskies,” which resides directly in the Pets OU. Because it is not considered to be in the Dogs sub-OU and -box-sync groups in sub-OUs can only contain groups in the same sub-OU, it cannot be synced.
There is a maximum depth of one for -box-sync groups. “Pets-Dogs-Retrievers-box-sync” is simply never looked at, regardless of its correct formatting.
Additional information
Enterprise Infrastructure’s guide to RAD
General management of Box Groups
Please contact help@oit.rutgers.edu if you have any questions.
Rationale behind the requirement for internal consistency of separators
Consider a hypothetical group whose name contains a space or hyphen in the freeform portion of its name, like “TestBox Box-Users.” Because the first separator used is a space, the script will only consider spaces as separators in this group name, so the group name is parsed as “[TestBox] [Box-Users]” (a single OU and then a freeform portion). This is the intended behavior.
If there were no requirement for internal consistency and both spaces and hyphens were treated as separators in all cases, the name would be parsed as “[TestBox] [Box] [Users]” (an OU, a sub-OU, and a freeform portion). If this group were placed in TestBox’s top-level -box-sync group, it would sync to Box and, at first glance, appear to be working. However, this would lead to unpleasant surprises. If “TestBox Box-Users” contained “TestBox Admins,” the members of “TestBox Admins” would not be synced because the “TestBox Admins” group would not be in the mistakenly-identified “Box” sub-OU.

title: group management and Rutgers Active Directory synchronization (quickstart guide)
body:
This article will provide a brief overview of how to use RAD to manage your unit’s groups in Box.
If you are looking for a comprehensive, detailed description of the process, please see the page "Group management and RAD synchronization (extended guide)."
Setting Box group admins
To make someone an admin of a Box group, add their -adm account directly to the RAD group to be synced. Unlike regular users, -adm users in subgroups of a group that is synchronized to Box do not become members of the parent group in Box. A person must be a group admin of a specific group in order to see it in the Admin Console, and must be a group admin of at least one group in Box to see the Admin Console at all.
RAD -box-sync Groups
If you would like a RAD group synced to Box, you must indicate that by making the group a member of a “-box-sync” group in your OU.
There are two valid locations for a -box-sync group: in your top-level OU or in a sub-OU one level down. The top-level-box-sync groups must be named [ou]-box-sync. The -box-sync groups one level down must be named [ou]-[sub-ou]-box-sync or [ou] [sub-ou]-box-sync.
Any group in your OU can be a member of your top-level -box-sync group, but the -box-sync groups in sub-OUs can only contain member groups in the same sub-OU. Groups located elsewhere will not sync to Box.
Group flattening
Box does not support nested groups. When RAD groups containing other groups as members are synchronized to Box, they must produce a flattened group in Box.
If you want a group to appear in Box, it must be a member of an appropriate -box-sync group. If it is only a subgroup of a -box-sync group member, it will not become a group in Box. However, its members will be included in the parent group synced with Box.
Group naming conventions
RAD groups that you want to be synced to Box should be named in one of the following ways:
•	[ou][separator][freeform portion]
•	[ou][separator][sub-ou][separator][freeform portion]
Both spaces and hyphens are valid separators, but each individual group name must be internally consistent and use one or the other.
-box-sync groups are a special exception to the internal consistency requirement; if you want to use spaces to separate your top-level OU and sub-OUs, you can do so while using the required hyphen to separate the sub-OU from “box-sync.” For example, “Pets Cats-box-sync” is as valid as “Pets-Cats-box-sync.”
Warnings and notes
Synchronization is not instantaneous; it occurs every half hour.
Once a RAD group has been synchronized to Box, deleting the RAD group or removing it as a member of its -box-sync group will break synchronization. Do not move or delete a Box-synchronized group in RAD unless you no longer want to use the group in Box. If you no longer wish to use a group in Box, you can move or delete it in RAD, then delete it in Box.
You can add users to a RAD group marked for synchronization to Box even if they do not have a Box account. Once they activate a Box account, after the next sync interval, they will automatically be added to all of the groups they were previously made a member of.
NOTE: Group names cannot have any parentheses. In addition, the entire OU path cannot have any parentheses character.

Please contact box_support@oit.rutgers.edu if you have any questions.

title: Cloud storage comparisons
body:
There are several different options for storing and syncing your data in the cloud. This guide is here to help you decide which kind of storage is right for you.
Rutgers requires that all university business be conducted on university-approved services. For example, faculty and staff email must be conducted using Rutgers Connect. In the case of storage, there are several storage categories and different options within each category. This page will help you choose among the approved cloud storage options of Box, OneDrive (Rutgers Connect), and Google Drive (ScarletApps).
Security and compliance
The first consideration when choosing a service is determining which ones are appropriate from a security and compliance standpoint. Federal and state laws, as well as university policies, govern where data can be stored. In general, information that is highly confidential and classified as restricted information can be stored in Rutgers Box and Rutgers Connect OneDrive. It is inappropriate to store this type of information in ScarletApps' Google Drive or any university information in any personal account, even a personal Box or OneDrive account.
For more detailed information about what can and cannot be stored in each type of storage service, please see the data classification and storage matrix.
Recommendations
After considering the security and compliance restrictions, multiple services can be used to provide data storage and sharing services concurrently. Before making a decision, you should consult the IT support staff in your organization.
In general, OneDrive and Box are equivalent services in terms of how data can be stored.
Choose Box if:
You will frequently transfer large amounts of data because Box is typically faster.
Choose Microsoft OneDrive if:
You require seamless integration with Microsoft Office software and tools.
Choose Google Drive if:
You require seamless integration with Google Apps:
•	When sharing data (that isn’t restricted) with students, Google Drive is listed as preferred simply because all students automatically have a Google Apps account created when enrolled. Students must open their account first to use Box. This process is simple, but it requires an extra step for the student. When students use OneDrive, this account is automatically created for them, but it is not integrated with Google Apps like Drive.
•	The services are similar in many respects, but certain tasks can be easier depending on the service. For example, since OneDrive is a Microsoft service, Microsoft Office apps easily support it. You can save and retrieve files easily and have recently accessed document lists sync between different computers. Box is a general storage service, so all software, including Microsoft Office, can work with it, but without the additional features that Microsoft builds in.
Other considerations
It’s also worth noting that these three products only represent one type of storage and that they are not appropriate for all purposes. This type of storage is not suited for storing databases that will be accessed by multiple people or for other software that requires very high-speed access to files. If you have special needs beyond general file storage and retrieval, please consult your IT support professional to determine which service is right for you.

title: Delegated administrator setup procedure in Box
body:
The process to have your area set up in Box is as follows:
1.	If you don’t already have an elevated NetID account, you should request one by visiting the Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) page. You’ll need this later.
2.	If you have not yet been assigned delegated administrator permissions, have an existing DA for your domain submit the Changes to Delegated Administration form on ServiceNow. If you are just becoming a Delegated Administrator for Box, an existing DA can provision your admin account through the Cloud Admin Tool (CAT).
3.	Once you have DA privileges and the elevated NetID account, you should be able to activate your Box admin account by navigating to the Box section on the Service Activation page. Below your account info, you will see an additional button to activate. 

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	After you click Activate Service, you will be able to verify that the netid-adm Box account was created on the same page. You should see something similar to the image below.

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	At this point, existing Box admins for your domain will be able to work with you to help set up your access to the shared accounts within your domain.
If you are making this request as a part of a domain that does not have existing Box administrators or shares setup, you will need to fill out the Box Shared Account Request Form in order to get assistance with an initial setup. You can contact OIT Box Support at box_support@oit.rutgers.edu for assistance with an initial setup or setting up and adjusting existing shared accounts. For requests like these, provide the following information:
•	The number of shared accounts you require. Generally, it's recommended to have one shared account for a domain that administrators can then create top-level departmental shares for individual groups within that domain that need departmental storage. While it's possible to set up additional shared accounts for more specific groups within a domain, that can make managing all of them harder than having everything in one primary share account. Areas that handle PHI will require two accounts — one for non-PHI and one for PHI data. If you aren’t handling PHI data, you’ll likely only need one account. You can create as many folders and shares as you need under the single shared folder and even set different permissions, so more than one shared folder will almost never be required.
•	If you need more than one shared folder (two for units that will store PHI), please explain why the additional shared accounts are needed.
Your request will be sent to the following groups:
•	Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) team: They can create an OU in RAD if you don’t already have one. They will reach out if they have any questions about your submission and then create your OU and Box Sync Group in RAD. Access will be granted to the delegated administrator’s elevated NetID account.
•	OIT Box Support Staff: They will review the application and contact you if they have any questions.

Account and information

title: Guide to managed folders in Box
body:
Storing important and/or sensitive information
Files that are important to a user’s department unit or contain sensitive information should not be stored directly in an individual user’s private Box folder. Such data should instead be owned by the unit’s shared account and placed in a shared folder to which the user is granted access.
Requesting a shared account
When your unit begins using Box and submits a request form for delegated administrators, a shared account can be requested at that time.
If you are already an approved delegated administrator for your area, you can simply email the OIT Box support address requesting a shared account. (Address is intentionally not included. General support inquiries should be sent to the appropriate OIT Help Desk). You must indicate:
•	Whether the account will be used to hold PHI in any of its subfolders (if so, the name of the top-level folder will be prefixed with “(Restricted)”)
•	Provide the desired name of the account as well as the reason your unit needs a separate shared account rather than a subfolder of your existing share if applicable
If your request is approved, you will be made a co-owner of the new shared account’s top-level folder. You can then add any other existing delegated administrators your unit would like to maintain the shared account as additional co-owners of the top-level folder.
Using shared folders
As a general rule, you should not share the top-level folder of the shared account to your users, as this grants them access to all data your unit has stored in Box, including, for example, PHI or other sensitive information. Additionally, if you grant them an editor role with this share, they can change the name of your unit’s top-level folder. Instead, you should make use of subfolders to manage permissions for users more granularly.
Once you have been made a co-owner of the shared account’s top-level folder, you can create subfolders as many levels deep as you would like. Only subfolders directly shared with users will appear in their list of files and folders when they log into Box, but they can see the name of the top-level folder if they inspect the subfolder shared with them.
Recommendation: Because the name of the top-level folder may not be immediately visible when looking at a shared subfolder, the names of any subfolders individually containing restricted data must be prefixed with “(Restricted),” but this is up to you to the delegated administrator to enforce.
A subfolder can be shared with an individual Box user or an entire Box group. This allows you to easily share information with your entire unit or departments and subgroups within your unit. Please note that you must be a group admin of any group to which you wish to share files or folders. Only group admins can share with a group to prevent unwanted mass sharing by end users. For more information on sharing to groups, please see the Box Group Management.

title: Guide to the management of Box groups
body:
Being a Box Group Admin
Only group admins can share with groups in the Rutgers implementation of Box. This is to prevent unwanted mass shares, especially to large groups. A person must be a group admin of a specific group to see it in the Admin Console and must be a group admin of at least one group in Box to see the Admin Console at all.
Creating and managing Box Groups
Group creation and member management are done in Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) and then synchronized to Box. For you to be a group admin of the Box group, your -adm NetID must be a member of the RAD group. Please refer to Group management in RAD synchronization (extended guide) for more information on group synchronization.
You can delete a group in Box, which will break any existing shares to the group. However, unless you delete the group in RAD or move it out of any -box-sync groups in RAD as described in the link above, a new group with the same name and memberships will be re-created automatically.
Sharing to Box Groups of which you are a Group Admin
If you have sharing permissions for a file or folder in your unit’s shared account (this requires a co-owner or editor role, as detailed in Box’s guide to collaborator permissions), you can go to the Admin Console, select the group in question, click to edit the list of folders shared to the group, and add the folder you wish to be shared to the group.
Sharing to Box Groups of which you are NOT a Group Admin
If you need to share a file with a Box group outside your unit, you will need to coordinate with the unit's delegated administrators who manage the target group. Reach out to one of these admins, let them know you are sharing a file or folder with their admin account, share the file or folder with them, and ask them to share it with the target group.
If another unit’s delegated administrator wishes to share something with one of your groups, once they contact you and share the file or folder with your admin account, then you can share it with your group as you would any file or folder you originally owned.
If you do not know who the Delegated Administrators are for another unit, you can find the unit's Delegated Administrators' email address.

title: Manage Box users in Connect Admin Tool (CAT)
body:
For the most part, delegated administrators in Box manage groups and shared folders rather than the accounts of individual users. However, there are several administrative capabilities available in CAT for delegated admins to work with their users’ accounts.
Which users can I manage?
Currently, admin permissions in CAT are handled based on the domain a user’s UPN is in. You will need to be a delegated Connect administrator for this domain to make changes to the user. If you are not a delegated administrator for the appropriate domain in Connect, you can reach out to the appropriate delegated admins using the Connect delegated administrator contact list and ask them to make any necessary changes.
Use the Connect delegated administrator contact list at the bottom of our OIT support page to find the appropriate delegated administrator's email address or contact information.
What can I do?
As stated in the introduction, delegated administration of Box does not entail a great deal of individual user account management.
Delegated administrators can view information about a user’s Box account, including whether it has been activated, the date it was activated if applicable, any aliases associated with the account, and more. 
Users’ Connect and @rutgers.edu aliases will be automatically synchronized to their Box accounts at regular intervals. Still, delegated administrators can click a button titled “Sync Box Aliases” to instantly sync aliases for a user. This feature will be removed once alias changes are instantaneous.
On the Collaborator's tab, you'll also see a list of any files/folders that were shared with/from that user, as well as the individuals or groups with which those shares are associated. If a collaborator's Box account is currently in the auditing/deprovisioning process, the row will be red to indicate that the share will go away soon. Please note that the collaboration report is generated once a week on Tuesday mornings.
Delegated administrators can provision a Box account for one of their users, but this should only be done for guests since they cannot select Box when they go through Service Activation.
Finally, delegated administrators can lock and unlock a user’s Box account. A NetID lock will automatically prevent the user from accessing their Box account. Still, if your unit wishes to restrict a user’s Box access while allowing them to retain access to other NetID-based services, they can selectively disable only a user’s Box account.
Additional information

title: general FAQ What is the difference between collaboration and shared links in Box?
body:
Collaboration

To access a file or folder as a collaborator, the user must create a Box account. 
The file or folder will appear under All Files when they log in to their Box account. For more information, view Box Support's page about inviting collaborators. 
Shared Links
Shared links let users quickly share hyperlinks to files stored in Box with others. Users can adjust the shared link settings to control who can open the link and what they can do with the file (edit, view, and download, or view only). 
People accessing shared link content with view-only or view-and-download access do not need a Box account to view and/or download the content. A Box account is required to edit the file. For more information, view Box Support's page for creating a shared link.

body:
I received the Box message "Uploading this will put you over your allocated space error on upload."" "
Though Business and Enterprise accounts have unlimited storage for their enterprises, Admins can limit the storage allotted to each user within their enterprise. Users must abide by this limit and will receive errors if they take any actions that exceed it.
If you attempt to upload content to a folder whose owner is approaching their storage capacity, you will receive the error "Uploading This Will Put You Over Your Allocated Space."
Troubleshooting Steps
There are two potential solutions to this issue: have the folder owner manually free up space in their account, or have the Box Admin increase the user's storage allocation.
Manually Clearing Up Storage
To manually delete unnecessary files to clear up storage, the user should:
1.	Locate content in the account that does not need to be saved in Box.
2.	Move that content to the Trash.
3.	Navigate to the Trash on the left sidebar.
4.	Permanently delete these files to free up space.

     Error! Filename not specified.
5.	Attempt to upload the files again.
Admin Increasing Storage Allocation
If you are the Box Admin, you will be able to increase the user's storage allocation by:
1.	Find who is the "owner" of the folder (co-owners don't count)
2.	Go to the Admin Console
3.	Go to the Users & Groups tab
4.	Search for this user & click on their name to edit
5.	Under the "edit user account details" section, find the storage quota
6.	Increase the number or check off the box for unlimited.
As the first option requires permanently deleting content, it is recommended to pursue the second option first, if possible. 
For more information, please visit the Box page, Uploading This Will Put You Over Your Allocated Space, to troubleshoot.

title: support FAQ I'm having trouble using Box with Outlook. How can I troubleshoot?
body:
Box for Outlook is a Microsoft add-in that brings your Box content repository directly into your Outlook interface, enabling you to store email attachments and messages directly into the Box folder of your choice. It also enables you to insert shared links to your Box files anywhere within the body of your email message, so you can share your Box content. If you encounter issues with using Box with Outlook, please read through the following guide:
Getting Box for Outlook
Your Box admin may have already deployed the Box for Outlook add-in. If this is the case, when you open Outlook, you will see the Box icon; the icon's location will depend on the platform you are using. 
If your admin has not automatically deployed the add-in to your account, or you are using a free Box account, you will need to install Box for Outlook yourself. To do so:
1.	Open Outlook.
2.	Select Home > Get Add-ins or Home > All apps.
3.	Use the search function to look for Box for Outlook.
4.	When you find the add-in, select Add.
Using Box with Outlook for the first time
1.	Open Outlook and create or open a message as you normally do.
2.	In the third-party application bar below the message body, click the Box icon. A Box window opens.
3.	At the prompt, click Authorize Access.
4.	At the following prompt, select your Outlook account.
5.	At the following prompt, click Allow. 
o	The Box pane will refresh; this is where you log into Box via Outlook.
6.	Click Log in.
7.	At the next prompt click Grant Access to Box.
Limitations
Ensure that you can use Box for Outlook integration. Below is a list of known limitations for using the add-in:
•	The new Box for Outlook integration works only for Office365 customers.
•	The integration cannot detect when you are dragging and dropping a file from your local device into an email. 
o	To attach a file, you must double-click to select it.
•	The integration does not store the location(s) where you last saved attachments. 
o	This was also a limitation of the prior Box/Outlook integration.
•	There is no preview support for *.eml (even though Outlook emails are saved as *.eml). 
o	To preview an .eml file: 
	Locate the file in Box and click Open.  
	This opens the .eml in your default mail client (such as Outlook, Apple mail client, and so on). 
	On mobile platforms you can use either your browser or email client
•	The new Box for Outlook integration is not supported with on-premises implementations of Exchange.
"Unable to Reach Box" Error Message
If you are using Outlook on a PC, and you're using Internet Explorer, the system could display the following error message: "Sorry, we were unable to reach Box. Check that you have a network connection. If the problem persists, please try later."
In this case, open the Internet Explorer Properties window, click the Security tab, and check Enable Protected Mode.
Keep Getting Logged Off from the Add-in 
If you continue to be logged off from the add-in on the Outlook Windows app, you will need to delete your browser history. To do so:
1.	Go to Internet Options > General tab.
2.	Disable Delete Browser History on Exit.
3.	Click OK.

title: support FAQ I'm unable to use Box Edit with certain file types
body:
When Box does not have a program associated with a certain file, you will not be able to open the file. For example, you may see the option to open a .docx file with Microsoft Word with Box Edit, but when attempting to open .xlsx files, Box Edit is not available.
This problem occurs when the file type that is not working, for example, .xlsx, is not associated with a program in the Control Panel. When Box Edit checks which program to use to open the file, it receives no response.
Troubleshooting Steps
Windows devices
1.	On your device, go to Settings > Apps > Default apps
2.	Scroll down and select Choose default apps by file type.
3.	In the list of files, locate the file type that is not working. 
4.	Next to the file type, you'll see the current default program; click it to reveal a list of options. 
5.	Change the default app to Box.
6.	Refresh the Box page and make sure Box Edit is now available.
MacOS devices
1.	Click the Finder icon in the Dock to open a Finder window
2.	Find the problematic file(s), then choose File > Get Info 
3.	In the Info window that comes up, find the arrow next to Open with
4.	Select the pop-up menu, then choose the app; if wanted, select Change all to open all files of this type with this app. 
For further assistance, please visit the support page on Unable to Use Box with Certain File Type.

In order to do so, you should first share your calendar with any email address outside of Rutgers Connect. This will generate two links for the calendar: one which ends in ".ics" (for use in calendar management programs) and one ending in ".html" (for viewing in browsers). These links can be copied and distributed anywhere you desire.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect How can I see who is available when creating a calendar event in Rutgers Connect?
body:
Office 365 allows you to view the availability of all relevant parties when setting up an event, making scheduling easier.
To use this feature in a web browser, create the event and select the Scheduling Assistant tab at the top of the event window. Next, add any attendees/rooms, and you will see their availability appear next to each other. You can change the event date or time, and participants’ statuses will update accordingly, helping you find a time that works for everyone.
If you use the Outlook desktop client, create the event and then select Invite Attendees. As you add participants, a list of possible meeting times will update to indicate whether everyone is free at that time or if some participants would not be able to attend; in the latter case, these participants will be named along with their conflicting event. Additionally, there will be a calendar with "Good," "Fair," and "Poor" (based on the total availability of all participants) days marked for the meeting.

title: FAQ for Rutgers Connect How can I stop items from being automatically added to my 365 calendar?
body:
When invited to a meeting or event by another user, you will have the event automatically added to your schedule and marked as tentative. This is done to avoid a third party attempting to schedule an event with you at the same time – if they view your free/busy information, they will see that you may be occupied. However, that default behavior may not be suitable for certain users, and they may desire to turn it off. To turn off this feature:
1.	Open the Outlook desktop client.
2.	Click the File tab at the top of the program window.
3.	Select Options from the list on the left. This will cause a pop-up to appear.
4.	Select Mail from its left pane, then scroll down to Tracking.
5.	Uncheck Automatically process meeting requests and responses to meeting requests and polls.

title: Adding Users to Course After the Term has Ended in Canvas
body:
Default course settings restrict new users from being added to a course site after the course end date. Teachers will need to update the course end date to accommodate the addition of users after the course has ended.
Approximately 1 year after the end of the term, academic course sites are set to a read-only state. Teachers will no longer be able to add users or edit the course dates. Please contact the help desk for assistance with these older sites. Within a year of the term end, course instructors must edit the course availability dates to make the course active to add users. 
To make this change, navigate to your course’s Settings.
1.	Under Course Details, make sure the three details below are set.
1.	Set Participation type to Course.
2.	Update the End Date to a date in the future. Leaving the field blank means the course will inherit the term date from the past.
3.	Uncheck the box to Restrict students from viewing course after course end date.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Once you have changed the settings, click Update Course Details to save the changes.
3.	You will now be able to add people to the site.
If you are planning to add someone as a teacher or similar role to the site, you can keep the box for Restrict students from viewing course after course end date checked. This option only affects the student and observer roles for the course site.

title: Adding videos to Discussions or Text Entry Boxes as a student in Canvas
body:
Your instructor may ask you to submit a video for an assignment, such as an introduction or a presentation. You can embed these videos using the Rich Content Editor (RCE), also known as a Text Entry Box.
As a student, you have several ways to add a video.
Table of Contents
•	Built-in Recorder
•	Kaltura
•	Additional Resources
Built-in Recorder
Canvas has a built-in recorder that is ideal for short videos (under 4 minutes). Please note, this tool does not allow you to record your screen. You can also upload videos, provided they do not exceed 500 MB.
To use the recorder, please follow the steps below:
1.	Click Reply for a Discussion, or for an assignment, click Submit Assignment and choose the Text Entry tab.
2.	Click on the icon that has a play icon, and choose the option Upload/Record Media.
Error! Filename not specified.
3.	A pop-up should appear. To upload an existing video, click on the Computer tab. To record, click on the Record tab and select permissions for your mic and camera. For more information, refer to the Canvas Student guide on recording media in the Rich Content Editor.
4.	To complete the process, click Finish to review the video. Then, click Save Media to complete the embedding of the media. Once embedded, students will need to click Post for a Discussion or Submit for an Assignment.
Kaltura
Kaltura, like YouTube, is a service that hosts videos for others to view and share. Videos can be uploaded, viewed, and edited through the service. This tool is integrated into Canvas and can be used by students to embed into RCEs/Text Entry Boxes. Below is a brief guide on how to use the tool:
1.	Videos can be recorded directly in the Kaltura Desktop App, or existing videos can be uploaded into My Kaltura Media, available on the left side of one's Canvas page.

3.	Click Apps (A) in the toolbar. Depending on your screen size, you may need to click More (B) to display the icon. In the Apps menu, click Embed Kaltura Media (C). You may need to click View All (D) to find the Kaltura option. However, a shortcut will be created for future use after completing this step.

title: Alternate File Storage Options in Canvas
body:
By default, each course has 5GB (5000MB) of storage space in Canvas. Files that count against the storage limit include:
•	Discussions: Attachments added to discussions count against course quotas. Attachments added to discussion replies do not count against course quotas.
•	Media Files: Canvas converts video and audio files up to 500 MB through the Media tool. If a file exceeds the 500 MB limit, it can be hosted through an external source and embedded using the Rich Content Editor.
•	Rich Content Editor: Newly recorded or uploaded media via the Upload/Record Media link does not affect file quotas. However, media files uploaded via any other method (such as the Upload Files link) count toward the course quota.
Increasing your Canvas course’s storage limit requires a consultation to evaluate file storage usage. If you are currently storing Zoom/Webex recordings in Canvas Files, additional storage increase requests will be denied.
Alternative File Storage
Rutgers offers alternative storage options available for faculty, staff, and students. It is advised that media files should be uploaded to the My Kaltura Media tool in Canvas.
My Kaltura Media
Users can create, upload, and share media content. All Users in Canvas can access their My Kaltura Media account in the global navigation.
•	How to add Kaltura content to a course
•	How to move Zoom recordings into My Kaltura Media
Kaltura Course Gallery
Within a course, you can select and post videos from your My Kaltura Media collection for your students to view in the context of the course.
If you have never used the Kaltura Course Gallery, you may need to manage your course navigation links. Review the instructions on how to add videos to the Kaltura Course Gallery.
Box
Instructors can add files from their Box accounts into Canvas Pages and Modules or utilize the embed functionality within their courses. To get started, check your Rutgers Services to ensure you have an active Box account.
If you have never used Box in Canvas, you may need to manage your course navigation links.
To embed a file from Box into a Rich Content Editor, please do the following:
1.	 While in the Rich Content Editor, click the More Apps icon, (resembles a small plug). 
2.	 Select View All to open your embedding options.
3.	 From the list, select Box and sign in with your SSO/Rutgers Box credentials.
4.	 Once your Box account folders/files are open, you can select the file(s) to be embedded and then click Choose to complete the process.
Office 365 (OneDrive)
Instructors can use OneDrive from their Rutgers Connect account. Files may be uploaded to the Office 365 app in Canvas, and then a hyperlink to that document can be created anywhere you can use the Rich Content Editor in Canvas. Several features in Canvas support the Rich Content Editor, including Announcements, Assignments, Discussions, Pages, Quizzes, and Syllabus. 
•	Open Office 365 from your Course Navigation to start uploading your files to OneDrive. 
•	Once your files are uploaded to your OneDrive, you can link individual OneDrive files to a Page/Assignment or link a OneDrive file/folder to the Course Modules. 
Please review more information on Microsoft OneDrive and Canvas Integration. 
Google Drive (ScarletApps)
Google Drive is available for staff and faculty through ScarletApps (Google). Similar to Box, Google Drive can add files into Canvas Pages and Modules or utilize the embed functionality within your courses. Files can be uploaded to Google Drive and linked using the Rich Content Editor in Canvas or as an external tool.
•	Open your ScarletApps account to start uploading files to Google Drive. 
•	Once your files are uploaded to your Google Drive, you can link individual Google files to a Page/Assignment, link Google folders to the Course Modules, or embed Google documents from Google Drive. 
Users who want to use their Google account may need to add an additional email address to their Canvas account. Please read the Google LTI – User Account Best Practices.
