title: Course Visibility Settings Options
body:
The Settings link in your course navigation allows instructors to modify the course details that affect visibility and availability for a Canvas course site. Depending on your role in a course and settings controlled by your department or school, some settings may not be available to you. This article assumes you have a teacher (full-editing) role and are teaching a for-credit course.
Course State
The course must be published for the visibility and availability settings to take effect.
Course Dates
•	Start Date: Canvas admins set the course start date to be the first day of the term; instructors may change the start date.
o	Recommendation: Set the date to be the first day of the semester and change the date to a past date/time if you would like to send inbox conversations or announcement notifications before the start of the semester.
•	End Date: Canvas admins set the course end date to be the day before the next semester begins; instructors may change the end date. Once the date passes, students will no longer receive notifications.
o	Recommendation: Set the end date to be the last day you would like the course to be active.
•	Restrict students from viewing this course after the end date: Instructors can choose to limit student access to a course site before the course start date or after the course end date. For some courses, this setting may be established by your school or program administrator, and you will not be able to change it. 
o	Recommendation: Instructor or school preference
•	Restrict students from viewing this course before the start date:
o	Recommendation: Instructor or school preference. 
Visibility
By default, only users enrolled in a Canvas course site have access to the site. Course instructors may change this setting to allow anyone with the course URL or only users logged into Rutgers Canvas to access the course.
•	Recommendation: Course
•	Customize: Instructors have the option to make available the course syllabus to Rutgers Canvas users or to anyone with the syllabus URL. Instructors may opt to change the course visibility setting at various times. During registration and add/drop period, it may be beneficial to allow Rutgers Canvas users to access the course syllabus.
o	Recommendation: Course or Institution.
•	Include this course in the public course index: Instructors may opt to list their Canvas course site in the Public Course Index. Visibility settings control access to the course content. 
o	Recommendation: Unchecked
Reminder: Instructors and academic programs may benefit by including a self-enrollable course in the Public Course Index. These courses may serve as valuable resources for students in academic programs, licensing reviews, or program onboarding. Please review the Canvas Guides concerning course settings to ensure the course is visible and accessible. Once a course is listed in the Public Course Index and is self-enrollable, any Rutgers Canvas user may join your course.
Additional Settings
In Course Settings, reviewing settings at the bottom of the page provides additional accessibility options.
•	Let students self-enroll by sharing a secret URL with them (in conjunction with adding a “Join this Course” link to the course home page). This enables instructors to enable self-enrollment, allowing students to enroll themselves in your Canvas course site. This does not affect registration in Rutgers student information systems such as Banner or REGIS.
o	Recommendation: Unchecked

title: Mobile Apps
body:
You can access Canvas from any browser on your mobile device. However, for the best user experience, it is recommended that you view Canvas through the mobile app. Please note that some features and tools may not function as expected in the mobile apps compared to viewing Canvas in a fully supported desktop browser.
Canvas pages within a mobile browser are only supported when an action in the app links directly to the browser, such as when a student takes a specific type of Canvas quiz. Support is not extended to Canvas items that cannot currently be used in the app, such as Conferences, Collaborations, Kaltura embedded content, or VoiceThread content. Canvas offers limited support for native mobile browsers on tablet devices. For details, please reference the limited-support mobile browser guidelines. Content items requiring Flash to run will not work unless your browser supports Flash. Safari, Chrome, and most free browsers do not support Flash. However, if you want to use Flash, you may want to try 360, Photon, Skyfire, iSwifter, or Puffin browsers, among other iOS Flash-supported browsers.
There are several mobile apps for Canvas. The descriptions for each app are shown below.
The Canvas App
The Canvas app allows students to access their courses and groups using a mobile device. Students may submit assignments, participate in discussions, view grades, and access course materials. The app also provides access to course calendars, To-Do items, notifications, and Conversation messages.
The Canvas App is available for both Android and iOS devices.
•	Learn more about the Canvas app

•	Canvas Android Guide
Canvas Teacher
Canvas Teacher allows teachers to facilitate their courses on the go, both inside and outside the classroom. This app provides quick access to grading, communicating, and updating—three of the most frequent course facilitation tasks for teachers through Announcements, Assignments, Discussions, and Quizzes.
Canvas Teacher is available for both Android and iOS devices.

title: Course Requests & Enrollments
body:
This page describes the different types of course sites in Canvas and how users are enrolled in them.
Live Course Sites
Live Course Sites are the official work sites for for-credit courses and are linked to the Rutgers student information systems to automatically populate their roster. Find more information on the Live Course Sites guide.
•	Course Sites: Courses properly coded for Canvas in the REGIS and BANNER scheduling systems are automatically created for the assigned instructor.
•	Enrollments: Rosters for Live Course Sites are synced daily with the student information systems.
•	Missing Roster: If a Live Course site is missing students, it may not be linked to the section correctly. If this occurs, please contact the Canvas Help Desk with your site URL and the section's 5-digit Reg Index/CRN number.
Sandbox Course Sites
Sandbox Course Sites (often referred to as a ‘template’) are not connected to a roster. These sites can be used for practice, testing, or archiving content.
•	Course Sites: Sandbox Course Sites in Canvas are not associated with for-credit course sections or academic terms. 
o	Note: Sandbox Course Sites need to be requested.
•	Enrollments: There are no attached rosters for Sandbox Course Sites. All participants need to be added manually by sub-account admins, teachers, or TA’s in the site.
Non-Credit Course Sites
The Application for Noncredit Online Registration (ANCOR) is the registration system used at Rutgers to ensure compliance with the university’s policies for non-credit student records and business practices.
The ANCOR integration in Canvas enables programs to create Canvas course sites independently and have enrollments synced in real-time. 
•	Course Sites: If a non-credit program is not using ANCOR, please email help@canvas.rutgers.edu for more information. 
•	Enrollments: If your program is not using ANCOR, the department offering the program will need to manage the rosters. If your program is using ANCOR and you have a question, please contact the ANCOR Help Desk.

title: Course Roles and Permissions
body:
This page contains information for Course Roles and Permissions. Information about Account Admin Roles and Permissions can be found in a separate guide.
Table of Contents
•	Course access in Canvas
•	Course roles 
o	Teacher
o	Student
o	Course Support
o	Course Coordinator
o	TA (Teaching Assistant)
o	Designer
o	Facilitator
o	Peer Reviewer
o	Observer
o	Undergraduate Course Assistant (UCA)
o	Accessibility Assistant (AAs)
o	ASL/CART Interpreter
•	Additional Resources
Course access in Canvas
There are two types of users in Canvas: account-level users and course-level users. Course roles are roles that allow a user specific permissions within a specific course. The roles listed below have been created for all of Rutgers Canvas courses.
Typically, users with these roles are limited to viewing only the content within their Canvas courses. Your individual school or Canvas sub-account administrator may have edited the roles listed below or created a specialized role that may be available in courses for your school.  For information about the permissions and limitations of these roles, please contact your department's support.
Course roles
Teacher
•	Primary use: For instructors who need full access to the Canvas features for instruction.
•	Permissions: Teachers have all course-level permissions, including the ability to add, edit, and delete all content in a course, edit course settings, and manually add individuals with active Canvas user accounts.
•	Limitations: None.
Student
•	Primary use: Students enrolled in a course site.
•	Permissions: The student role grants permissions to view course content and engage in course activities, including submitting assignments, participating in discussions, and sending messages to users within a course.
•	Limitations: Students cannot view or modify course settings.
Course Support
•	Primary use: For providing the same level of access as Teacher, but excluding the user from the course evaluation.
•	Permissions: Course Support has all course-level permissions, including the ability to add, edit, and delete all content in a course, edit course settings, and manually add individuals with active Canvas user accounts.
•	Limitations: None.
Course Coordinator
•	Primary use: This person is responsible for coordinating the administration of all sections of a multi-sectioned course.
•	Permissions: Same level of permissions as the teachers.
•	Limitations: Cannot add or remove Teachers to the course.
TA (Teaching Assistant)
•	Primary use: For assistant instructors and teaching assistants.
•	Permissions: TAs have permissions similar to the Teacher role. They have all course-level permissions, including the ability to add, edit, and delete all content in a course, edit course settings, and manually add individuals with active Canvas user accounts.
•	Limitations: TAs cannot add other Teachers or TAs to the course, nor publish the course.
Designer
•	Primary use: For instructional designers/technologists (and staff with similar responsibilities) who write and manage course content, but do not actually teach courses or grade student work.
•	Permissions: Create course content, discussions, announcements, assignments, quizzes, and other content features.
•	Limitations: Designers cannot view or modify grades. Designers cannot add Teachers or TAs to the course, but can add students.
Facilitator
•	Primary use: Section Instructor. This is a non-editing role intended for programs that provide complete course content for an instructor.
•	Permissions: Facilitators can view submitted student work and enter grades and comments. They can also view files, announcements, assignments, quizzes, and export course content.
•	Limitations: Facilitators cannot manage course content, import course content, or view question banks. Facilitators cannot add Teachers or TAs to the course, but can add students.
Peer Reviewer
•	Primary use: For faculty or staff requesting to observe a course as part of a peer review of teaching.
•	Permissions: Peer Reviewers have access to view course content, instructor feedback, and student grades.
•	Limitations: Peer Reviewers cannot edit any content and are not permitted to participate in course activities. Peer Reviewers are unable to make changes to the Gradebook or SpeedGrader. Additionally, Peer Reviewers cannot add other users to the course.
Observer
•	Primary use: For users who have no official role in the course, but have been given permission to view course content and discussion forums.
•	Permissions: Observers have access to view course content. This role can be linked to a student enrolled in a course in order to monitor their progress.
•	Limitations: Observers have no permissions to edit or participate in course activities or send messages to users.
Undergraduate Course Assistant (UCA)
•	Primary use: For undergraduate assistants who are allowed to make changes to course content but are not allowed to view course grades.
•	Permissions: UCAs can create course content, discussions, announcements, assignments, quizzes, calendar events, and other content features. UCAs can message all course users.
•	Limitations: UCAs are unable to perform the following tasks: add people to the course site, publish the course, or access the Gradebook or SpeedGrader. The UCA role doesn't allow for the grading of assignments within Canvas.
Accessibility Assistant (AAs)
•	Primary use: For Rutgers Access and Disability Resources (RADR) staff who monitor course content in courses with enrolled students with documented needs. 
•	Permissions: AAs can view and edit all course content, discussions, announcements, assignments, quizzes, calendar events, and other content features. AAs can message individual course users. 
•	Limitations: AAs are unable to perform the following tasks: add people to the course site, publish the course, or access the Gradebook or SpeedGrader. The AA role doesn't allow for the grading of assignments within Canvas.
ASL/CART Interpreter
•	Primary use: The ASL/CART Interpreter role in Canvas is used to identify individuals providing reasonable accommodations and services for students with disabilities. These users will provide services including American Sign Language (ASL) and Communication Access Real-time Transcription (CART).
•	Permissions and Limitations: ASL/CART Interpreter role has specific permissions and limitations covered in ASL/CART Interpreter Role in Canvas.
Additional Resources

•	Observers' Visibility and Participation

title: Differences between Courses and Sections in Canvas
body:
Courses
Courses are the virtual classroom where all course content resides and is the place where students can learn and interact with the instructor and one another. Rutgers courses are organized under sub-accounts that align with the offering unit. A single REGIS- or Banner-coded section is associated with a single Canvas course site. 
Courses contain:  
•	Section(s)
•	Content
•	Grades
•	Submissions
Sections
Sections are groups of students that have been organized for administrative purposes. When users are enrolled in a course, they are actually enrolled in one of the sections of that course. All sections of a course share the same content.
Sections contain:
•	Enrollments
Note:
•	It is possible to place more than one section in a course, but not possible to put sections within sections.
•	If multiple sections are taught by the same instructor, the Rutgers Cross-List Courses tool allows that instructor to combine their sections into a single course site and share the same content.
•	Different instructors teaching the same course should have separate course sites for their own sections.
Error! Filename not specified.
Managing Student Rosters
Creating New Sections
Instructors can add sections to their course to separate students. However, the roster for manually created sections will not sync with Rutgers' student information systems, such as REGIS or Banner. A use case for a manually created section would be to enroll auditors in a course. See Adding Guests to a Live Course Site as an Instructor. 

Students can be further organized by assigning specific tags as necessary.
Moving a Section to Another Course
 If you have multiple courses and would like to move the roster from one course site to another, this can be done with the Rutgers Cross-List Courses tool. Sections should be cross-listed before students submit to assignments. Student submissions are linked to the discussion, assignment, or quiz in a course site and remain in place even when the section is moved to another course site.

•	It may take up to 24 hours for users to receive their invitations, depending on their notification preferences. Canvas will not consider the user enrolled and won’t recognize the user anywhere in Canvas (including Conversations)—until the invitation has been accepted. If necessary, you can resend the course invitation to the student. 
•	If a user was added with the wrong role in the course, you can edit a user’s role in a course.
•	If a user was added to the wrong section in the course, you can edit a user’s section in a course.
If you need any assistance with this process or have any questions, please contact the Canvas Help Desk.

Depending on your Canvas Quiz settings, instructors may need to use both the Moderate This Quiz option to increase the time a student has to complete the quiz once launched and the Edit this Quiz option to extend the window available to complete the quiz.
•	If the Canvas Quiz settings are set so that the availability window (when a student is allowed to take the quiz) is the same as the quiz time limit, then instructors should edit the quiz settings, in particular, the Assign To: option, to provide their students with a longer availability window to take your quiz. title: Migration – Sakai to Canvas Instructions
body:
This page will explain how to export Sakai Course Content and import into Canvas.
Depending on the complexity of your course content structure, you may have to do some content reorganization. This is a good opportunity to re-evaluate your course structure.
Export Sakai Content
Although Canvas allows you to import Sakai content, you must first export using Common Cartridge packages. You need to be aware that you can ONLY import content from Assignments, Forums, Test & Quizzes, and Resources, using the Lessons tool.
1.	Navigate to ANY “Lessons” page in your Sakai site. If your site does not have the “Lessons” tool, start by adding it to your site (go to Site Info > Manage Tools and check Lessons then click Continue).
2.	Go to the “Lessons” tool in your Sakai site (note that you may have renamed the “Lessons” tool to something else, that won’t matter as long as you can find it).
3.	Click More Tools.
4.	Choose Export CC.
5.	Select the Use newest version (1.3) Better for Canvas option.
6.	Optionally choose to add your question pools (this will include all the questions that you have added to “Pools” from all your courses).
7.	Wait. The process may take some time, especially for large courses.
8.	Look in your Downloads folder on your own computer, you should see a file named something like “Sakai-export.zip”.
View the PDF Version with Images
Import Sakai Course to Canvas
1.	In Canvas, go to your course and click Settings.
2.	Click Import Content into this course (in the right-hand column of options).
3.	For Content Type, choose Common Cartridge 1.x Package.
4.	Choose the file that you exported from the Sakai lessons tool, it should have a name similar to “Sakai-export.zip”.
5.	Click either All Content or Select specific content depending on whether you want to import everything, or pick and choose.
6.	You may click the option to Adjust Events and due dates if you like. This attempts to automatically shift dates, but it may not work satisfactorily.
7.	Click Import.
8.	Wait. This may take a long time depending on the size of your course and how many files your course has stored.
9.	Under “Current Jobs” canvas will either indicate “Completed” or “Waiting for Select” (depending on whether you chose to import all content, or select specific content).
o	If you see “Waiting for Select” click Select Content, then place check marks next to the items you want to import.
o	If you see “Completed” Canvas may also show an “Issues” link. You can click Issues to see what problems Canvas ran into.
10.	Once Canvas indicates the “Common Cartridge” job is Completed you can now go to the individual areas of Canvas to make final adjustments and changes.
11.	Be sure to review the list of potential problems and things to check, below. You may want to continue with the instructions in the next section to make sure you include all your Resources.
12.	Finally be sure to edit assignment, discussions, and test/quiz settings and update questions associated with test/quizzes.
View the PDF Version with Images
Tips and Troubleshooting
•	If you renamed resources in Sakai, they will revert to the original names. You need to rename the files again in Canvas.
•	If you copy the entire site, Sakai may fail to include some Resources when exporting. You may need to upload individual files, or follow the instructions for copying Sakai Resources to Canvas.
•	Canvas does not allow you to re-order files, they will always be in alphabetical order. You need to use either the Pages or Modules tool to control the display order.
•	Canvas does not allow you to edit “Files” in place (you can download and edit them off-line, then upload again). The ability to edit in Canvas is in the “Pages” tool, but all material that is copied from Sakai will be placed in “Files” where it cannot be edited.
•	You will need to check the individual items in Canvas to make sure the dates are appropriate (do this even if you chose to “shift dates” – many dates simply will not come through the transition).
•	The Sakai “Syllabus” tool will not copy over to Canvas (this only applies to the tool, i.e., many faculty add a syllabus file to the resources tool, and that will copy correctly). If needed, you can click the “Print View” in the Sakai Syllabus tool, then copy and paste the text into the Canvas “Pages” tool.
•	Certain types of Sakai Resources will not copy over (web links, citation lists). You will need to recreate these in Canvas.
•	Sakai Lessons and Canvas Modules are not exactly comparable. Lessons will be converted into a series of links in Canvas Modules, and the content itself will end up in the Canvas Files (in a folder name “attachments”). To create an experience that is more similar to Sakai Lessons, you may want to copy your content into Canvas “Pages”.
•	Sakai discussion forums must have an added topic. Forums with no topics will not copy into Canvas.
•	The Canvas “Files” section may still be invisible to students (it will be light gray). If this happens, go to Canvas Settings, click “Navigation” then click the menu next to “Files” and choose “Enable”. You may also need to drag the “Files” item into the upper box (out of the “hidden from students” section).
•	If you copy question pools and your questions have images or attached files, you will need to re-attach those images or files again in Canvas.

title: My courses are not showing up as a student
body:
If you do not see your courses listed in your Canvas account, please review the scenarios below:
I registered in the last 24 hours.
Course rosters in Canvas are updated daily with information from a Rutgers Student Information System (SIS), either REGIS/WEBREG or Banner. However, there is a delay for new enrollments to appear in the SIS. If you registered for your course today or yesterday, please wait up to 48 hours for your Canvas account to be updated.
The Semester hasn't started yet.
Most courses are not available to students until the first day of the semester. However, if the semester is in session and the course is not listed in your account, please contact the Rutgers Canvas Help Desk.
I was removed for non-payment.
If you have not confirmed your enrollment or made any payments towards your term bill, the University may withhold your enrollment from the course roster. You can verify you are still registered for your courses on Webreg for REGIS-coded courses. 
If you are on a payment plan or are waiting on financial aid/scholarships, please contact the Office of Student Accounting, Billing, and Cashiering.
Are there additional steps I can take?
On the web version of Canvas, you can check future enrollments. Check your All Courses List in Canvas for the registered course. If the course instructor has not published the Canvas course site, the course will appear in future enrollments with an unpublished status. If so, please contact the course instructor to inquire about when you can expect the course site to be published.
If the reasons listed above do not apply, you will want to reach out to your instructor or contact the Canvas Helpdesk:
•	Contact the Instructor – If you have the instructor's name, you can find their contact information on Rutgers People Search or contact the relevant academic unit.
•	Canvas Help Desk – Please have your Rutgers NetID and the course code ready when you call or email.
Additional Information
•	Canvas Course and Enrollment Provisioning
•	Canvas Help Desk

title: Notifications in Canvas
body:
Your Canvas user account is created with a set of default notification settings to keep you informed about your courses. However, you can change these notification settings. Any changes you make apply only to you; the changes do not affect notifications sent to other users in your courses. To learn more about each notification, default settings, and notification triggers, view the Canvas Notifications Guide.
Notifications are sent as one of four delivery types: Notify Me Right Away, Daily Summary, Weekly Summary, or Don’t Send. If you change a setting, the change is made immediately to your account. Notification settings apply to all your courses unless you manage them individually for a single course. You may be able to reply directly to email notifications outside of Canvas if your reply-from email address is added to your Canvas account. Replies are updated in the Canvas Inbox. However, please note that attachments added as part of an external reply are not included with the message displayed in Canvas.
Notes:
•	Notifications are sent to the contact methods specified in your Canvas account. You cannot receive notifications if your contact methods are unconfirmed. If you are not receiving Canvas notifications, please confirm your Canvas contact methods.
•	The Canvas app supports push notification settings. However, managing settings inside the app will override settings in the browser version of Canvas.
•	You may select notification settings for an individual course. Learn how to manage notification settings for a single course.
See the following Canvas Guides for details about changing the contact method for notifications or the frequency with which you are notified:

title: REGIS: Grade Upload using Excel
body:
This article outlines the process of uploading final course grades into REGIS using the exported gradebook from Canvas and a spreadsheet template provided by REGIS. 
Before exporting your gradebook and your roster, please ensure that you have done the following steps:

Set up the spreadsheet

2.	 Export the Excel version of your roster from REGIS.
3.	In the download from REGIS, arrange your REGIS roster to sort by NetID:
1.	Click to activate the cell labeled Id and drag your cursor right to highlight all row headings, including NetID, and drag down to highlight all students.
2.	Click Sort & Filter in the ribbon menu.
3.	Click Custom Sort.
4.	In the dialog box, check the box labeled My list has headers.
5.	In the drop-down for the column, select NetID.

7.	Remove any students who may already have a grade. This should include students with a grade of “W.” To remove a student, select the row, right-click to view the menu options, and then click Delete.
4.	Arrange your Canvas Gradebook export to sort by SIS User ID and remove extra data.

3.	Delete Test Student (optional): Highlight the last row for Test Student and right-click to open the menu option. Click Delete to remove the row.
4.	Delete Assignment Grades: Click to select all grade columns for individual assignments (starting at Column F). Omit the last column for Unposted Final Grade. Right-click to open the menu option. Click Delete to remove the columns.
5.	Click the select-all box to the right of column A.
6.	Click Sort & Filter in the ribbon menu.
7.	Click Custom Sort.
8.	In the dialog box, check the box labeled My list has headers.
9.	In the drop-down, select SIS User ID for the column.

Special Note: For Canvas course sites that include more than one section, instructors will need to separate the student populations into distinct sections. title: Requesting Canvas Access for Rutgers-Developed Applications
body:
Rutgers organizational units are encouraged to develop applications and web services to meet the unique needs of their Canvas user population. Canvas features a robust application programming interface (API) that developers can utilize to build applications. A Rutgers campus, school, or unit may develop a programmatic integration with Canvas that requires API or LTI access.
If you are requesting integration support for a commercially available product, please review the External App Integration page for information on courses, schools, and/or top-level integrations. 
Application developers must:
•	Review Rutgers Account Admin Roles and Permissions
•	Request admin access
•	Work with the Rutgers Canvas admins to develop a method for accessing Rutgers Canvas by the application or web service that is independent of a user’s Canvas account.
Developer Keys, Service Accounts & Access Tokens, and LTI Applications
The method of connecting to Rutgers Canvas is dependent on the intended functionality and scope of your application. Some applications may require multiple connection methods, depending on their functionality.
Developer Keys
Developer keys provide access to Rutgers Canvas. Rutgers Canvas is organized into a nested set of accounts (akin to folders), with the broadest hierarchy starting at Rutgers University. It is further divided into campus, school, and subject levels. The two types of developer keys provide different levels of access that may take into account the heirarchy of Rutgers Canvas.
API Dev Keys
An API developer key allows an application to access Rutgers Canvas using REST API web services and is limited by the scope of the key.  Developer API keys can only be scoped by API access, not to a Canvas account; thus an API developer key will have acces to all data for a specific API endpoint. Issued developer API keys are limited in scope to protect Rutgers data. A developer key may include entitlements to search for users, view user enrollments, and search for courses. 
LTI Dev Keys
Learning Tools Interoperability (LTI) applications are web applications designed in accordance with 1Edtech standards, allowing for seamless integration with Canvas. Developer LTI keys are used to install LTI applications into Canvas, adhering to LTI v1.3 standards. Developer LTI keys may utilize LTI advantage and Names and Roles Provisioning Service (NRPS) and have their own restrictions. Application developers should collaborate with Canvas administrators on your campus, school, or department to develop, test, and install your custom application. Discussions with Rutgers Canvas admins may be beneficial to determine how Rutgers Canvas setup may affect planned functionality and features. Please review the Canvas Admin Guides for External Apps.
Service Accounts and Access Tokens
Canvas users may request an access token generated on their user account. The access token inherits the permissions of the user's account and provides scoped permissions to interact programmatically using the Canvas APIs, allowing access to the same data as the user would in the user interface. It is the responsibility of the application developers to adhere to university policies and best practices to ensure the security of Rutgers data.
Canvas service accounts will be created to generate access tokens for Rutgers-developed applications and assigned custom Canvas admin roles in the appropriate Canvas account.
•	Account and Sub-Account Role Comparison
•	Canvas Account Role Permissions
•	Rutgers Account Admin Roles and Permissions
End-User Support
Rutgers organizational units are solely responsible for providing end-user support for applications and services they have developed. As part of ensuring universal access for all users and to adhere to Rutgers University World Wide Web Accessibility Policy, applications and services used by Rutgers University are required to be assessed for accessibility. Developers and stakeholders must collaborate with the Rutgers Office of IT Accessibility to ensure that the application or web services comply with the current adopted version of WCAG. They should also complete the Accessibility Risk Assessment for IT Purchases.
How to Request Developer Keys, Service Accounts & Access Tokens, and LTI applications
To request a developer key or a scoped service account, please contact the Rutgers Canvas administrators. As you design and develop your application or web service, permissions and scopes will evolve. To begin the process, please complete the Request Canvas Access (Dev Keys, Service Accounts & Access Tokens, and LTI Applications) – Fill out form. Detailed requests are appreciated, and requests for full access will be denied.

title: Requesting Canvas Guest Accounts
body:
A non-affiliated student, staff member, or instructor who does not have an official Rutgers NetID must have a Canvas guest account created to access Canvas. Guest account creation can be requested by a Rutgers-affiliated faculty member, staff, sub-account administrator, or program coordinator. If the request includes adding users to the site(s), please indicate the site by listing the exact name of the course, course code, or course URL. Guest accounts are not intended for users who are waiting for a Rutgers NetID to gain early access; please visit the Early Employee NetID Request System. 
To facilitate user account creation, please download the Canvas Guest User Template. Fill out the following highlighted fields in the spreadsheet:
•	user_id: User(s) email address in all lower case.
•	authentication_provider_id: Use "canvas" by default. This is case-sensitive and must be in lowercase.
•	first_name: List user(s) full first name.
•	last_lame: List user(s) full last name.
•	status: Use "active" by default.
When filling in the user_id, the email address will automatically fill in the following fields: login_id, and email. 
Before sending the spreadsheet to the Canvas Help Desk, please:
•	Do not modify the headers (Row 1). Any deviation from the spreadsheet template will cause the creation to fail, and the file will be sent back for revision.
•	Remove the sample user row before inputting user data.
•	Remove capitalized letters in the users’ email addresses.
•	Save the file as a .csv (Comma Separated Values).
•	Ensure there are no extra (leading or trailing) spaces in each cell.
•	For all users added, copy the formula or fill down the formula in the adjacent columns for authentication_provider_id, login_id, email, and status to complete the spreadsheet. (See copying formula video tutorial)
•	Check if students have active NetID(s) within Canvas; this is to prevent confusion for your user(s). If the user has provided a Rutgers email address, then they have a Rutgers NetID, and you can add the user to the course with their NetID.
These new guest users will have email accounts and will log in via the Email Login option from Canvas.
Note: Account creation in Canvas does not notify the user that their account has been created. It's advised that the account requester send a follow-up email to the person with additional information on how they can sign into their Canvas account, such as how to log into Canvas with Email.

title: Setting Early Access in Canvas
body:
Course dates determine when students can view and/or participate in a live site. Please review how term dates, course dates, and section dates affect courses in Canvas.
This page explains how to provide students with early access to the course and outlines the Canvas notifications they will receive.
It is recommended that any changes be made before the start of the semester.
Course Dates Settings
The settings portion of the course is available to instructors and TAs. In Course Navigation, click the Settings link, then scroll down to the Course Dates:
Error! Filename not specified.
1.	Participation: When course sites are created, participation is set to Course.
2.	Course Start Date: The default date is set to the start of the academic term. Different schools have start dates that are earlier or later. This date can be changed by the instructors or at the department's request.
3.	Course End Date: The course end date is set approximately 1 month after the end of the academic term to prevent students from getting locked out immediately. This date can be changed if the instructor would like to extend access after the semester has ended.
4.	Restrict students from viewing course before start date: When enabled, this option prevents students from viewing the course content until the course start date. If this is unchecked when a course site is published, students can view course content at any time before the course begins.
5.	Restrict students from viewing course after end date: When enabled, this option prevents students from viewing the course content after the course end date. If this is unchecked in a published site, students can still view the course, but all content is displayed in a read-only state.
Provide Students With Early Read-Only Access
Read-only access allows students to view the course, syllabus, and non-date-restricted content. Students will not be able to submit assignments, participate in discussions, or take quizzes.  To provide students with early read-only access, change the Participation settings to:
Course Start Date: Leave default term start dates.
Course End Date: Leave default term end dates.
Restrict students from viewing course before start date: UN-CHECKED.
Restrict students from viewing course after end date: UN-CHECKED.
Error! Filename not specified.
With these settings, you can send students a message in Canvas and post course announcements that will be visible in Canvas.
•	Students will receive an email notification if you send them a message.
•	Students will not receive an email notification if you post a new course announcement. If you want students to receive email notifications for announcements, you will need to open the course to Early Full Access.
Provide Students With Early Full Access
Early full access means starting the course before the official term start date. Students can start the course and submit assignments/quizzes unless you individually set available from/to dates on each assignment, quiz, or discussion. To provide early full access to the course, change the following Course Date Settings:
Course Start Date: Empty Field.
Course End Date: Leave default term end dates.
Restrict students from viewing the course before start date: UN-CHECKED.
Restrict students from viewing the course after end date: UN-CHECKED.
Error! Filename not specified.
With these settings, you can send students a message in Canvas and post course announcements that will be visible in the Canvas LMS.
•	Students will receive an email notification if you send them a message.
•	Students will receive an email notification if you post a new course announcement.

title: Setting Grading Schemes in Canvas
body:
Using Grading Schemes in Canvas
A grading scheme is a set of criteria that translates numerical scores to letter grades to demonstrate varying levels of achievement in a course. Without a grading scheme, scores are not measured against any specific standard. It is important that you enable and accurately implement a grading scheme in your Canvas course that matches the information you provide in your course syllabus.
Important information about Grading Schemes:
Grading schemes are required to submit final grades from Canvas to REGIS or Banner. The Rutgers GradeSync tool will allow assigned REGIS graders or assigned Banner instructors to submit the course letter grade in Canvas to the Rutgers student information systems. See Rutgers REGIS GradeSync or Rutgers Banner GradeSync.
Grading schemes vary by department or school. Review your grading scheme carefully and ensure that it aligns with school or departmental policy. (Most Legacy Rutgers departments and schools will not accept B- or C- grades. Some Rutgers Health schools will only accept grades of 1, 2, 3, or 4.)
Copying content will copy over the grading scheme. When using the Import Content tool feature, any customized grading schemes will be transferred to the new course site.
Add a Grading Scheme
1.	Log in to Canvas and navigate to your course.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click Settings to access the Course Details tab.
3.	Locate the Grading Scheme category and then check the box to Enable course grading scheme.
4.	Click +New Grading Scheme to create a new course grading scheme.
5.	In the pop-up window, add a new Grading Scheme Name. 
6.	Then, choose Grade by either Percentage or Points; by default, Percentage is chosen.
7.	Adjust the Letter Grade and Range to match your department's recommendations or the grading scale set forth in your course syllabus.
8.	Once you have set a grading scheme, click Save.

Error! Filename not specified.
9.	From the Grading Scheme drop-down menu, select your Course Grading Scheme in the Course Level Category.

Error! Filename not specified.
10.	Scroll to the bottom of the Settings page and click Update Course Details.
Special Notes
•	The default grading scheme available in Canvas includes course grades that may not be valid grades accepted by your registrar. Please review your grading scheme carefully to ensure it aligns with your school's or departmental policy.
•	Each Grading Scheme needs to be named in order to be saved.
•	To earn a grade, the student must surpass the grade threshold listed in the Grading Scheme without rounding.  If your course policy allows for rounding, then the grading scheme must reflect a lower threshold for a grade range.


•	Canvas allows you to override the final course grade. REGIS GradeSync and Banner GradeSync will accept override grades.
•	Temporary and nonstandard grades must appear in the Canvas grading scheme to be assigned in the gradebook as an override grade. This includes grades such as 1, 2, 3, 4, FC, H, IP, NC, PA, S, TB, TB+, TC, TC+, TD, TF, TNC, TT, TZ, and U.
•	Alternatively, you may submit the temporary grades via REGIS first before using REGIS Final GradeSync. Instructors for Banner-coded courses should use either Banner GradeSync or manually enter the course grades in Banner; you cannot use both methods for a single course section.

General Licensing
How is ChatGPT Edu different from ChatGPT Pro?
The ChatGPT Edu license offered through Rutgers is designed to protect university data. Rutgers has executed a Business Associates Agreement and Data Processing Addendum with OpenAI to protect data stored in our tenant. Additionally, interactions and data used in our tenant will not be used to train the underlying large language models. 
How is ChatGPT Edu different from ChatGPT Plus?
ChatGPT Edu is an institutional offering designed for universities and educational environments, featuring enterprise-grade security, administrative controls, and shared workspace capabilities to support students, faculty, and campus operations. It includes access to advanced tools (data analysis, web browsing, file uploads), custom GPT creation, and enhanced language support tailored to academic deployment.
ChatGPT Plus lacks the security controls and administrative features inherent in the Edu platform, making it unsuitable for institutional use. 
How is ChatGPT Edu different from ChatGPT Free?
ChatGPT Free lacks data protection, has low messaging limits, and cannot access OpenAI’s most advanced models.
Can I use a public or free version of ChatGPT?
Only the enterprise instance of ChatGPT licensed through the university software portal can be used to process university data. The enterprise instance is configured to ensure that Rutgers data is not used for OpenAI model training and is governed by both a data protection agreement and a business associate agreement. The Rutgers instance of ChatGPT can be used for select categories of protected data. Learn more in the Data classification and AI matrix.  
Who at the university is eligible to use ChatGPT Edu?
ChatGPT Edu subscriptions must be purchased by a faculty or staff member. Subscriptions can be assigned to faculty, staff, faculty emeriti, students, and sponsored guests.
Back to top
Features and limits
Are there messaging limits on the ChatGPT Edu plan?
Yes.
Does ChatGPT Edu have access to the Team features?
Sharing GPTs in a workspace is the suggested alternative to the Team features. 
Can I purchase a personal license for ChatGPT?
ChatGPT Go, Plus, Pro, and Enterprise are not included in the university agreement. Personal accounts are not covered by our data protection agreement and may pose a risk to institutional data. 
How can I access the OpenAI API? 
Currently, API access to OpenAI Models is available through the Microsoft Azure Foundry. Units interested in purchasing an Azure Cloud Subscription can follow the directions on the Rutgers Cloud website. For those who can wait, the Office of Information Technology (OIT) is actively working to deploy an AI API Gateway to streamline access to multiple AI Models, including OpenAI, without managing a full cloud deployment. The new Gateway Service is scheduled to launch at the end of the spring semester.
Can I integrate ChatGPT with other third-party applications or systems?
You may see the message "Some apps are unavailable. Access to certain apps is limited by your workspace settings. Contact your admin to request access." 
At this time, Rutgers OIT is not approving integrations between ChatGPT and third-party applications. This is due to ongoing evaluation of security requirements and the need to establish formal policies and governance. The AI@Rutgers Working Groups are actively assessing this area and will provide updates as our guidance and governance structures develop.
Can I use ChatGPT Edu for student data analysis?
Yes. ChatGPT Edu can be used to analyze protected and restricted university data. Rutgers signed the necessary data protection agreements with OpenAI and confirmed that any content processed will not be used to train their AI models. View the AI data classification matrix for more information. 
Which models are available?
Access to ChatGPT services varies by access level. Model selection should be aligned with task complexity. In many cases, GPT-5 will meet routine academic and administrative needs. Carefully select the model that best manages your credit allotment.
OpenAI will switch from a weekly to a monthly credit replenishment model on 8/1/26. The pricing tiers and effective monthly credit allocation will remain the same. 
Current Weekly Model Ending 7/31
•	ChatGPT Base ($10/month) No additional weekly usage credits.
•	ChatGPT Standard ($30/month) 100 credits per week.
•	ChatGPT Advanced ($150/month) 750 credits per week. The advanced service is best suited for power users.
New Monthly Model Starting 8/3
•	ChatGPT Base ($10/month) No additional usage credits.
•	ChatGPT Standard ($30/month) 450 credits per month.
•	ChatGPT Advanced ($150/month) 3,250 credits per month. The advanced service is best suited for power users.
To find the new ChatGPT model names and important notes about the model, please review the ChatGPT Edu product page.  
For ChatGPT Edu customers, the following usage is included at no additional cost and does not consume credits:
•	Images: 3 generations per 24-hour rolling period
•	Deep research: 5 queries per rolling 24-hour period
The 24-hour period begins at the time of first use. For example, if a user generates an image at 10:00 AM, they can generate 2 additional images until 10:00 AM the following day.
How do credits work?
Credit consumption is based on OpenAI’s published rate cards for ChatGPT Chat, Codex, and Work. Please note that ChatGPT Chat usage is assessed differently from ChatGPT Codex and Work.
How do I monitor my usage?
OpenAI has not published a means for individuals to check their personal usage; however, all accounts have access to:
•	Unlimited access to GPT-5
•	5 Deep Research queries per rolling 24-hour period
•	Generate 3 images per rolling 24-hour period
These activities do not impact the credits associated with your account. The system will provide contextual warnings if you don’t have enough credits for specific activities.  
When does my usage limit reset?
OpenAI will switch from a weekly to a monthly credit replenishment model on 8/1. The pricing tiers and effective monthly credit allocation will remain the same. 
Prior to 8/3/2026
The weekly limits reset on a rolling basis. This weekly window starts the moment a member sends their first message that consumes credits. This means that your account may not be reset at the same time as other users. ChatGPT admins cannot see your specific reset time.  
After 8/3/2026
Monthly limits will be reset at the start of the next calendar month, in UTC.

Optimizing ChatGPT Credit Consumption Under the Flexible Licensing Model
Overview
OpenAI’s ChatGPT flexible licensing model introduces usage-based consumption aligned to model selection and task complexity. Thoughtful use of models and prompts will help you maximize value while staying within institutional guardrails.
Best Practices for Reducing Credit Consumption
•	You can switch between the models within the same conversation. 
o	Begin with Instant to brainstorm or refine your prompt before using a more costly model.
o	Process output using a lower-cost model to minimize costs.
•	Instant will typically be sufficient for routine administrative or academic tasks. Try your query in Instant before using more costly models.
•	Select ChatGPT Instant to prevent messages from consuming credits. Instant may automatically switch to Medium when a request requires more reasoning.
•	For credit-consuming models, consolidate your request into a single, well-scoped prompt rather than multiple iterative queries. Use instant to help develop a multi-step prompt. 
•	Consider generating images on alternate platforms.
•	Align usage with the credit allocation schedule to maximize your plan. 
o	All plans include five Deep Research queries and three Image Generation requests per rolling 24-hour period.
o	Individual credit pools are currently reset weekly after 8/3; they will reset monthly.
o	Unused credits do not carry over.
Match the Model to the Task
ChatGPT offers multiple model modes tailored to different levels of effort and cost. Review the ChatGPT Rate card for the current consumption costs:
•	Instant: Best for everyday tasks such as answering questions, summarizing documents, drafting emails, brainstorming ideas, and basic editing. It provides the fastest responses, uses the fewest credits, and has unlimited access. For most day-to-day work, Instant should be your default choice.
•	Medium: Best for tasks that require more deliberate reasoning, such as writing with multiple constraints, comparing options, analyzing policies, organizing complex information, or solving multi-step problems. Use Medium when Instant doesn't provide enough depth or accuracy.
•	High: Best for work requiring extensive reasoning and careful evaluation, including complex coding, advanced troubleshooting, detailed financial modeling, research synthesis, strategic planning, and nuanced decision-making. This consumes the same number of credits as Medium in Chat, but costs more in Codex and Work.  
•	Pro: Reserved for the most demanding tasks where maximum reasoning capability is needed, such as highly complex software architecture, sophisticated technical design, difficult research problems, or analyses where accuracy is especially critical. Pro consumes the most credits and should be used selectively after determining that High is insufficient.
When should I use Deep Research?
Deep Research is a task-based feature designed for comprehensive analysis, multi-source synthesis, benchmarking, and policy or report development. Each Deep Research request consumes credits and should be reserved for work that genuinely requires structured investigation and validation rather than iterative conversation.
All plans include five Deep Research queries per rolling 24-hour period. Users should avoid using Deep Research for exploratory questions, early ideation, or drafting, as these tasks are usually handled more effectively by Instant or Thinking models.
Optimizing ChatGPT Codex and ChatGPT Work Usage
All activities through the ChatGPT desktop app are billed according to the Codex rate card. This pricing differs from the ChatGPT Chat functions, even though the experience may be similar.
ChatGPT Codex workflows can consume more credits due to larger inputs and outputs. To optimize:
•	Use the appropriate model for the task; avoid higher-effort reasoning levels for simple edits.
•	Avoid pasting large amounts of unnecessary code or documentation.
•	Break large projects into smaller, targeted requests.
•	Limit overly long outputs when detailed explanations are not needed.
•	Keep prompts concise and focused on the specific coding request.
•	Thoughtful prompt design helps preserve your daily allotment while maintaining high-quality results.
•	Limit the number of MCP servers you use. 
•	Optimize your AGENTS.md files. If you work on a larger project, you can control how much context you inject through AGENTS.md files by nesting them within your repository. 
Image Generation
All plans include three Image Generation requests per rolling 24-hour period. Additional images are assessed according to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Rate Card. All individuals at Rutgers have access to free image generation through Adobe Creative Cloud, Copilot, and Gemini.

title: AMP FAQ What is a Cisco Secure Endpoint (formerly AMP) Group?
body:
For IT staff members, the Cisco Secure Endpoint (formerly AMP Endpoint) management console allows for segregating sets of clients from each other in the form of Groups. These are similar in concept to Active Directory domains but are generally unrelated.
Cisco Secure Endpoint Groups comprise a unique list of user and administrator accounts, as well as a distinct set of policies. They are ideal for allowing departmental unit computing managers and specialists to have full control over their Secure Endpoint deployments without having to manage their own server infrastructure. Only the super-administrators of the Cisco Secure Endpoint management server can pass between Groups. Policies, Groups, User Accounts, and Lists can only be created and deleted by Super-Admins of the Cisco Secure Endpoint Management Service. Each Group administrator is restricted to their own environment.

title: AMP FAQ What is Cisco Secure Endpoint (formerly AMP)?
body: Cisco Secure Endpoint (formerly AMP) is a complete, optionally managed security solution provided by Rutgers OIT to faculty and staff. Cisco Secure Endpoint prevents attacks by providing the latest global threat intelligence to strengthen defenses, a built-in antivirus (AV) engine to detect and block attacks at point-of-entry, built-in sandboxing technology to analyze unknown files, and proactive protection capabilities that close attack pathways and minimize vulnerabilities. If malware evades these prevention measures and gets inside, Cisco Secure Endpoint continuously monitors and records all file activity to quickly detect malicious behavior, retrospectively alert security teams, and then provide deep visibility and a detailed recorded history of the malware’s behavior over time—where it came from, where it’s been, and what it’s doing. Cisco Secure Endpoint can then automatically contain and remediate the threat. Cisco Secure Endpoint protects endpoints—like laptops, workstations, servers, and mobile devices—running Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

title: Support RU–Camden IT classroom technology FAQs
body:
Table of Contents
•	Enhanced classroom equipment isn’t working. Who do I report it to?

•	Why is the screen on my Toshiba laptop not displaying on the projector?
•	Why is the screen on my PowerBook not being projected?
Enhanced classroom equipment isn’t working. Who do I report it to?
For classroom equipment assistance, email the Help Desk at help@camden.rutgers.edu or call 856-225-6274.
Do you offer training for using the classroom equipment?
Training is available by appointment. To schedule, send an email to help@camden.rutgers.edu
Do I need to register my laptop with OIT to use it in a classroom?
No. Registration of a laptop for use in a classroom is not necessary. You should use RUWireless. See the RUWireless FAQ for details.
How can I get software installed on a classroom instructor's PC?
Faculty members who need specific software to be available in classrooms for the semester should provide the software to the RU-Camden Information Technology Help Desk (at help@camden.rutgers.edu or by calling 856-225-6274) at least four weeks before the semester starts. Last-minute requests will not give staff enough lead time to load and test software before the new term starts.
Check with Help Desk to be sure the software will be compatible with current hardware and to discuss any other technical considerations affecting the software’s performance in the lab or classrooms.
Where can I obtain a wireless microphone to use in a classroom?
Science Lecture Hall: See the secretary on the first floor.
Fine Arts 110 and North Conference Room: The microphone is stored in the podium.
Penn 401 and Walt Whitman Center: The microphone is located in a drawer inside of the AV rack.
None of the other rooms are equipped to support a wireless microphone.
Are remotes available for the VCR/DVD players in the classrooms
Yes, you have to request it by emailing help@camden.rutgers.edu.
You can borrow it for one class or the entire semester.
What should I do if the device I am using via the smart panel is producing sound but no video?
You should first try switching to another device and back to the one you are using. For example, if you are trying to use the Instructor computer and no video is coming up, try switching to Personal Laptop and back to see if that works. If that doesn’t work, try powering down the projector and turning it back on. Sometimes, the projectors go into sleep mode, and they don’t wake up when prompted. When you power down the projector, wait 2-3 minutes before turning it back on.
Why is the screen on my HP laptop not displaying on the projector?
Sometimes the laptop needs to be put in a different display mode. To do this on your HP laptop, press the Fn + F4 key combination either once or twice, depending on whether you want the screen displayed only through the projector or on the laptop as well.
Why is the screen on my Toshiba laptop not displaying on the projector?
Before using a PowerBook in one of the smart classrooms, you may need to rescan the displays to use them. To do this, connect the PowerBook to the VGA cable on the smart panel. Next, go to Displays in System Properties, or, if the display icon is in the menu bar, click it. Finally, you should choose rescan. When the computer is done, you should be able to use the F5 or F7 key to switch display modes (laptop only, laptop and projector, or projector only).
Why is the screen on my PowerBook not being projected?
Before using a PowerBook in one of the smart classrooms, you may need to rescan the displays so they can be used. To do this, connect the PowerBook to the VGA cable on the smart panel. Next, go to Displays in System Properties, or, if the display icon is in the menu bar, click it. Finally, you should choose rescan. When the computer is done, you should be able to use the F5 or F7 key to switch display modes (laptop only, laptop and projector, or projector only).

title: and Telephones What different webinar options are available?
body:
Rutgers offers several options for hosting webinars, each with distinct features. Zoom Webinars and Microsoft Teams Webinars both allow for the hosting of large-scale virtual events, but they differ in their pricing, capacity, engagement features, integrations, and security controls.
Often, the tool used for hosting webinars can be determined by the webinar's reach and needs. Due to its widespread use, Zoom is often chosen for external events that require advanced customization. Teams' integration into Microsoft 365 means greater cost-effectiveness, enhanced compliance, and seamless enterprise integration, making it a popular choice for internal or hybrid use.
Key Differences
Some key differences between the two webinar tools include:
•	Scale 
o	Zoom supports up to 10,000 attendees.
o	Teams Town Halls' support up to 20,000 attendees.
•	Customization 
o	Zoom offers more external-facing branding and registration customization.
o	Teams emphasizes compliance, security, and integration with Microsoft apps.
•	Use Case Fit 
o	Zoom Webinars are often the preferred choice for marketing events, external training sessions, and large public-facing events.
o	Teams Webinars are often the choice for University communications, internal training, and events where Microsoft 365 integration is critical.

title: Admin Tool (CAT) FAQ How can I ensure a retiring/otherwise departing user will continue to receive email?
body:
When a user is ready to depart from their role at the university but needs to continue receiving mail sent to their netid@domain.rutgers.edu address, a delegated admin can use CAT to set up a Mail User, which essentially acts as a forward.
Below are the steps for delegated admins to accomplish this process:
1.	The admin must search for the user in CAT and delete the user’s alias for their domain, and any @rutgers.edu aliases the user has associated with their Microsoft 365 account.
2.	Search for the user within CAT and within the Microsoft 365 action menu, use the Modify UPN menu option to change their UPN to the @connect.rutgers.edu domain. 
o	If they have an @rutgers.edu address set as their primary SMTP address, change that to be netid@connect.rutgers.edu by using the Modify Primary SMTP menu option.
3.	Remove any domain-specific and @rutgers.edu aliases from their Microsoft 365 account by using the Modify Aliases menu option. Once they no longer have any domain-specific email addresses associated with their account and they no longer have any @rutgers.edu aliases assigned to their Microsoft 365 account, wait 30 minutes for the changes to take effect.
4.	Navigate to the Mail Users area in CAT and click Create Mail User, enter the user’s NetID and old domain in the Email Address field, and the non-Connect address at which they would like to receive mail in the External Email Address field.
For more information, see the help documentation in CAT for Mail Users.

title: Admin Tool (CAT) FAQ How can I license a new user?
body:
If users who should have a Connect license currently do not have one assigned, delegated administrators can license them using CAT.
1.	Log into CAT and use the search box to find the user.
2.	Within the Microsoft 365 action menu click Assign License. 
o	It’s recommended that you then set their UPN to your domain by using the Modify UPN menu option.
The process will take about 30 minutes to complete.
For more information, see the help documentation in CAT for Managing Users.

title: Admin Tool (CAT) FAQ How can I lock a user's Connect account?
body:
Delegated administrators do not need to contact OIT and request that an account within their unit be locked. They can lock the account themselves using CAT by looking up the user and then, from within the Microsoft 365 action menu, selecting Modify Account Status. If the account needs to be unlocked later, the process is identical.
More information is available in the CAT Documentation.

title: Admin Tool (CAT) FAQ How can I move users between domains in Connect?
body:
Through cooperation between the delegated admins for both domains, a user can be moved from one domain to another without the admins having to contact Connect Support.
1.	The delegated admins for both the old and new departments should coordinate a time for the move.
2.	The delegated admin for the user’s original domain should look up the user in CAT and change their UPN to “connect.rutgers.edu”. 
o	30 minutes should be allowed for the domain change to sync with Azure AD; the user will not be able to log in during this time.
3.	After this waiting period, the delegated admin for the user’s desired domain should then use CAT to change the user’s UPN from “connect.rutgers.edu” to the new domain. 
o	Again, 30 minutes should be allowed for this change to sync.
The email addresses of delegated administrators for other departments can be found on the Departmental IT Contact page.

title: Admin Tool (CAT) FAQ How do I manage Unified Groups?
body:
Delegated administrators can create groups and edit the settings of already-created groups in their domain using the Unified Groups section within CAT. Membership of Unified Groups can be managed via the following methods:
•	Owners of a Unified Group can add/remove group/team members via Outlook. 
o	In Outlook, users can be added to the group as either owners or members; in most cases, users should be added as members so that they do not have administrative privileges over the entire group. Outlook can also be used by group members and owners to access a shared planner, notebook, and more. Some settings, such as MailTip and Message Approval, must be edited through EAC by an admin.
•	Domain admins can add/remove members of a Unified Group through EAC; however, the Domain Admin must first be listed as an owner of the Unified Group. Domain admins can add/remove owners via the CAT tool. Please note that the CAT tool cannot be used to add/remove members.
For more information, see the help documentation in CAT for Microsoft 365 Unified Groups.

title: Management Google LTI – Getting Started in Canvas
body:
Sharing Google documents provides flexibility for collaboration, and the Google LTI integration in Canvas simplifies the workflow if users have a Google login associated with their Canvas account. Prior to using Google LTI in Canvas, please review Google LTI – User Account Best Practices.
Table of Contents
•	Google Limitations
•	Authorization
•	Assignments 
o	Cloud Assignments
o	File Upload Assignments
•	Collaborations
•	Modules
•	Rich Content Editor
•	Canvas Mobile App Features
Google Limitations
As part of the Canvas integration, some functionality is limited by Google. Users should be aware of the following limitations by Google in Canvas:
•	Account sharing permissions can prevent sharing outside of an institution’s domain. Google admins can change the sharing permissions to allow documents to be shared outside the institution.
•	Document permissions can prevent files from previewing in a course. Users should ensure that permissions are set correctly for a document before sharing it with others in Canvas.
•	Document owners may not see the email addresses of users who have access to the document.
Authorization
Users can authorize the Google Drive (LTI 1.3) to view their Google Drive account. If authorization to Google Drive is not successful the first time, authorize the application again. Users can only authenticate to one Google Drive account at a time.
Assignments
Cloud Assignments
Instructors can create an embedded online assignment using an external tool. With the Google Assignments (LTI 1.3) external tool, this assignment type creates a template that provides a document copy to the student for assignment submission. Accepted assignment types are Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
Notes:
•	Peer reviews cannot be used with External Tool assignments.
•	Rubrics can be added to external tool assignments in Canvas, though the rubric must be added to the assignment before the assignment is set as an external tool assignment. Students can view the rubric in the assignment details page, and instructors can view it by clicking on the Assignment.
File Upload Assignments
Instructors can continue to create regular file upload assignments. However, when an instructor allows file uploads, students can view the Google Drive tab and upload files directly from Google Drive.
Collaborations
Users can collaborate on Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides. The creator can add individual users from the course to participate in the collaboration. Collaborators can be added or removed at any time, but once a user is added to a collaboration, the user always has access to it in the user’s Google Drive folder. Collaborations require a name before they can be saved.
Modules
Google Drive (LTI 1.3) displays as a Modules external tool. Instructors can add links to Google Drive documents as an external tool; this does not create a student-owned copy of the file. 
Rich Content Editor
Google Drive (LTI 1.3) displays a Google Drive icon in the Rich Content Editor. The icon displays everything in a user’s Google Drive account and allows users to display documents as inline links or embed them directly. Students and teachers can view the icon anywhere they can access the Rich Content Editor, such as discussions and pages (as allowed).
If the icon does not appear directly in the toolbar, it is available in the More External Tools drop-down menu.
Canvas Mobile App Features
Currently, the Google Drive (LTI 1.3) integration is very limited in the Canvas app and Canvas Teacher apps from Instructure. Instructors who incorporate cloud assignments into their coursework should inform students that these assignments are not currently supported in the Canvas app.

User Account Best Practices in Canvas
Many Canvas courses use Collaborations, powered by Office 365, to share documents and assignments. The following best practices will ensure you have access to your documents:
•	Add an Office 365 account email address to your Canvas Account as an additional contact method. 
o	The Rutgers email domain “@rutgers.edu” is not an Office 365 account; however, “@ScarletMail.rutgers.edu” and Rutgers Connect accounts are.
o	You can activate your ScarletMail account at Rutgers by visiting the NetID Activation page and clicking the Service Activation link.
o	ScarletMail account logins will work for both Google and Office 365.
o	In your Canvas profile, the Office 365 account does not have to be the default email account, but it must be listed in the user’s profile, and the email address must be confirmed in your Canvas Account Settings. You may set different notification preferences for additional contact methods so you do not receive duplicate notifications.
•	When authorizing Office 365, users should either sign in to only one Office 365 account or use a private browser tab (incognito). To access an incognito browser from Google Chrome, click on File > New Incognito Window. In Firefox, click on File > New Private Window.
•	If you have previously shared a different Office 365 account than the one you intend to use or see the request access screen, you will need to clear your browser’s cache & cookies on your Mac or Windows computer before authorizing another Office 365 account.
•	If you access your Canvas Collaboration document and are prompted to Request Access, then complete the steps above to associate an Office 365 Account with your Canvas account, then ask your instructor/document owner to reshare the document via Canvas Collaborations.
•	If you access your Canvas Collaboration document and have View Only access to the Canvas Collaboration, please close the Collaboration, navigate to your Canvas Account settings, and in the Approved integrations section, please click on the trash can to remove the token for Office 365 LTI.
Add your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account to your Canvas profile.
Before accessing or sharing content in Canvas with a Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account, users will need to associate a Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account with their Canvas account.
1.	Click Account in the Canvas sidebar.
2.	Click on Settings.
3.	On the right side of the page, select Add contact method.
4.	Click on the Email tab, enter your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account email, and then click on Register Email to associate your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account with Canvas. You will be sent a confirmation message. Please log in to your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail account and click on the link to confirm your email account.
Access your OneDrive files in Canvas
Users can view all their files within their Office 365 (OneDrive) folder through the Course Navigation Menu in Canvas.
1.	On the left-hand navigation menu of a course, click on the Office 365 link. If it is not listed, please enable Office 365 in the course navigation menu or ask your instructor. 
2.	You will be prompted to enter your OneDrive credentials to log in. Click Log in.
3.	Once logged in, you will be able to view your OneDrive files. If students click on this link, they will be prompted to log in to their own OneDrive account. To hide Office 365 in the course navigation, course instructors can manage their course navigation links.
Share OneDrive files using the Rich Content Editor
Instructors and students can link documents from their OneDrive folders anywhere in Canvas using the Canvas Rich Content Editor. Instructors may embed Office 365 documents in Canvas Announcements, Assignments, Discussions, Pages, Quizzes (as instructions and questions), and Syllabus. Students may embed Office 365 documents in discussion and announcement replies, quiz answers, and assignment submissions.
1.	Access the Canvas Rich Content Editor page (found in Pages, Assignments, Discussions, and Syllabus) and click the Apps icon from the toolbar. Select Microsoft Office 365 from the list, or select View All to find Microsoft Office 365.
2.	Select the desired file, then click Attach File. A link to the document will then be created, opening it in a new tab when checked.
Enable Canvas Collaboration using a OneDrive file
Users can create a collaboration in Office 365 using a Microsoft Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file. Users can select individual users, groups, or both for a Canvas Collaboration.
1.	On the left-hand navigation menu of the course, click Collaborations.
2.	Click Start a new collaboration, then choose Office 365 in the drop-down.
3.	Next, choose the type of file you wish to collaborate on (Word, Excel, or PowerPoint), add a document name and description, and add people/groups as collaborators.
4.	When finished, click Save at the bottom of the page.
Getting Started for Instructors
Functionality for Instructors
 Instructors can:
•	Share OneDrive documents in Canvas Modules.
•	Create Cloud assignments based on a OneDrive template file.
•	Access OneDrive from their course navigation.
•	Create links to specific OneDrive files via the Rich Content Editor.
•	Include Office 365 documents in your Modules
•	Allow students to submit assignments via OneDrive.
•	Create and participate in Collaborations.
•	Grade student assignment submissions in SpeedGrader via the Office 365 Viewer.
Share OneDrive Documents in Canvas Modules
Instructors can easily share OneDrive files within the Modules tool in Canvas.
1.	In Course Navigation, click Modules.
2.	Select the plus icon under the desired Module, then choose External Tool from the drop-down. See the How do I add an external tool as a module item? for more information.
3.	In the Add [Item Type] To drop-down menu, select Office 365.
4.	A new dialog will appear. Navigate to the file you want to attach, then click Attach File.
5.	In the Add [Item Type] To drop-down menu, click Add item. 
Create Cloud Assignments directly from a OneDrive file
Instructors can create an online assignment that integrates a document (Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel) directly from their Office 365 (OneDrive) folder. When students open the assignment, Office 365 will automatically create a copy of the file as the student’s submission. Students will be able to open the document and make necessary changes. The student can then return to the Canvas assignment page and submit the assignment, while keeping a copy in their course OneDrive folder. Also, course instructors can view each student’s document copy in SpeedGrader for grading.
1.	In the left-hand course navigation menu, click Assignments or from Modules Add [item type]: assignments). See How do I add course content as module items? for more information.
2.	Then click Add Assignment.
3.	Enter the assignment name, add a short description, specify the number of points, select the assignment group, and select the grading type.
4.	In the submission type drop-down, select the External Tool option. Then, click on the Find button and select Office 365 Cloud Assignment.
5.	When ready to publish your assignment, click on the Save & Publish button.
Getting Started for Students
Functionality for Students
Students can:
•	Upload OneDrive files for an Assignment Submission.
•	Access OneDrive from their course.
•	Create links to specific OneDrive files via the Rich Content Editor.
•	Access direct links to instructor-provided files.
•	Edit and submit Cloud Assignments.
•	Participate in Collaborations.
Upload OneDrive files for an Assignment Submission
Students can upload files directly from their Office 365 (OneDrive) folder. When clicking on the Submit Assignment button, select the Office 365 tab to link your Office 365 account in Canvas. This will let you select a file from OneDrive and submit it.
Access your OneDrive files in Canvas
Students can view all their files within their Office 365 (OneDrive) folder through the Course Navigation Menu in Canvas, if enabled by your course instructor.
1.	On the left-hand side of the course menu, click Office 365.
2.	Click Login.
3.	In the pop-up window, you will see a Microsoft login screen. Enter your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail address.
4.	Click Next.
5.	Enter the password you use to access your Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail.
6.	Click Sign in.
7.	When logged in, you will be able to view your OneDrive files directly in Canvas.
 
Limitations
•	Faculty and students must have accounts in the same Microsoft domain. Only Rutgers Connect and ScarletMail accounts may successfully share documents using Office 365.
•	Users with Rutgers Connect accounts may only share documents with other users who have Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail accounts.
•	Document permissions can prevent files from previewing in a course. Users should ensure that permissions are set correctly for a document before sharing it with others in Canvas (anyone in the institution).
•	When displaying Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files, files with font conflicts will not display. Best practice is to use standard Microsoft fonts in all documents.
