Technologies such as printers, routers, cloud vendors, and HVAC systems sometimes need to send email, but they generally cannot use Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail. To support these products, the Office of Information Technology (OIT) offers a portfolio of mail relay services. 
Access to these services is available through an application. 
Table of Contents
•	Commonly Accepted Usages 
•	Commonly Excluded Usages 
•	Available Services
•	Request Process
•	Exclusion and Audits
Commonly Accepted Usages 
•	Networked printers (e.g. toner/paper notification email)
•	Switches/routers (e.g. operational email)
•	Automated HVAC systems
•	Emergency generators (e.g. fuel status email)
•	Software performing “basic authentication” (i.e. authentication is not performed via OAuth or a similar modern protocol). This software is incompatible with Rutgers cloud email providers
•	Products that are unable to use a password when sending an email. 
Commonly Excluded Usages 
•	Individual email accounts/aliases 
•	Usage from individual computers can be performed using Outlook, webmail, etc. 
•	Products not able to perform email encryption (e.g. SSL or TLS) 
•	Service to shared infrastructure; for example, to an outside vendor that cannot ensure exclusive Rutgers resources
•	Usage by non-Rutgers affiliates 
Software/applications running on dedicated servers, virtual appliances, and vendor-provided IT services will be considered on a case-by-case basis, with consideration to the applicable policies and guidelines. The platform should be formally procured by Rutgers and use appropriate measures that ensure Rutgers IT resources are only provided for Rutgers-related usage. To confirm compatibility, you are encouraged to engage OIT promptly whenever email integrations are required. 
Available Services
OIT currently offers four classes of mail relay service. The request process will guide you to a suggested offering. If you have an explicit service requirement, please note that during the request process. 
•	SMTP AUTH mail sending service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. Note that this service requires the security of TLS or SSL encryption. Email may be sent as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address.
•	IMAP or POP3 mail receiving service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. A mailbox is created for that special NetID, which will receive email for retrieval (via IMAP or POP3) under the security of TLS encryption. Your Rutgers Connect domain administrator may create an alias in Rutgers Connect that will “hide” the special NetID for marketing purposes. (If the special NetID will only be used by automated processes, a marketing alias is not required.)
•	SMTP AUTH with IMAP or SMTP AUTH with POP3: If there is a requirement to both send and receive email, this offering is a combination of offerings #1 and #2.
•	IP-based mail sending service: The IP address of your University-affiliated device will be permitted to send email, using SMTP, as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address. This is the only offering available for devices that cannot ensure the security of a Rutgers NetID and password, such as devices that lack encryption support. This offering is generally restricted to RUNet-connected devices.
Request Process
Mail relay privileges can be requested by the appropriate Administrative or Technical Contact for the device by logging into the request web tool.
Upon submitting a completed online application, the request will be assessed, and its status communicated via email. All accepted and rejected submissions will be acknowledged via email to the submitter. Rejected submissions may also include details on reasons for the rejection and corrective actions that must be taken prior to resubmission. 
Exclusion and Audits
Exemption from NetID authentication does not constitute exemption from the relevant University policies, guidelines, and technical standards. If a device is found in violation, mail relay permission may be denied and/or revoked. Generally, we will first attempt to remedy this situation with the contacts listed on the application. 
OIT reserves the right to conduct audits of devices with mail relay permission. Timely responses to OIT audits are mandatory for continued permission to utilize Rutgers services. 
If a device is excluded, OIT must receive verification that the conditions that led to the device’s exclusion have been corrected and verified prior to reinstatement. 
For more information on the standards of data protection required of authorized devices, please visit Rutgers’  Information Security Compliance Program.

title: Debugging Mailman error messages
body:
Table of Contents
•	Post by non-member to a members-only list
•	Post to moderated list
•	Message body is too big: XXXX bytes with a limit of XX KB.
•	Message has implicit destination
•	Too many recipients
Mailman follows several rules when handling mail to be sent to a Mailman list. When a message is forwarded to the Owners and Moderators it is because one of the rules said to check with them first.
Moderation Messages arrive with five pieces of information included in them.
•	List is the name of the Mailman list that requires moderation.
•	From is the email address that sent the message being held.
•	Subject is the Subject of the email.
•	Reason is the reason why Mailman held the message for moderation.
•	And the message body itself.
Below are the most common reasons messages are held for moderation:
Post by non-member to a members-only list
The list is set so only members can send to it, and this message was sent by a non-member.
This often catches owners, as being an owner doesn't give any privileges except editing the configuration of the list. For an owner to send mail to a member only list, they must either subscribe OR add themselves to the accept_these_nonmembers option on the Sender filters page. You can add non-owners to the accept_these_nonmembers to allow them to post without subscribing also.
Post to moderated list
The sender is moderated. This could mean that only this individual user is moderated or that all members of the list are.
To change moderation for just one user, find them on the Membership Management page and un-check mod for them. Submit your changes to save the change.
To change moderation for all users, scroll down to the bottom and select Off under Set everyone's moderation bit, including those members not currently visible and select Set to save.
Message body is too big: XX bytes with a limit of XX KB.
The sender is allowed to send mail, but the size of the mail is larger than the preset limit.
The default limit is 40k, which is a fairly large email and allows for small attachments. You can increase the limit by changing the value of max_message_size option on the General Options page.
However, email is not the best venue for sending large attachments (a list with 500 members, each receiving a 2MB file means 1GB of email). Rutgers recommends that this value is not changed as too many large attachments going out can seriously degrade Mailman service. Any list causing this kind of degradation may be temporarily shut down to preserve the Mailman service. In most cases, you would be better served hosting the attached file on a web page and point to that web page in an email.
Message has implicit destination
This means Mailman received this message but that the message did not have the List Name in either the To or Cc fields.
This most often occurs because the message is forwarded to the list from another person/list or because the mail is spam. Spammers often obscure the list of recipients when they send mail. If you had one list subscribed to another, the mail sent to the parent list would be flagged with this reason. To avoid this, you can go to the Recipient filters and add the parent list name to acceptable_aliases option. Submit your changes to save the change.
Too many recipients
This is mostly a spam interference option. Spammers often send mail with large amounts of recipients listed in the To or Cc fields. This defaults to a limit of 10 recipients. If you find that you are often sending to more than 10 mailing addresses at once, you may want to consider requesting an additional Mailman list.

title: Mailing lists
body:
With mailing lists, emails can be sent to multiple people with one click of a button, and groups of people can communicate with ease. The University offers two types of mailing lists for Faculty, Staff, and Students to use.
How the service might be used
Mailing lists are recommended for emailing a large group (50 or more) of individuals. Mailing lists can also be useful for smaller groups, such as a half dozen members of a small department, quickly communicating with one another.
Mailman
Mailman is for University-affiliated ad hoc mailing lists. Examples include lists for department supervisors, club or sport team members, project team members, Route 18 construction alerts, and more.
To obtain a Mailman list, follow the directions on how to create a new mailing list in Mailman.
RAMS official mailing lists
RAMS is the Rutgers Automated Mass-mailing System. It enables the generation of an email list based on demographic information from the registrar or payroll data, and provides for automated updates to the list membership in response to changes in the demographic information.
RAMS lists are intended to be used for communicating official university business to targeted student and employee populations. They are not intended to be a conduit for advertising, commercial solicitations, event promotion, or personal business.
You can create your own class or course RAMS list for those which you have roster privileges, or you may request the creation of a new RAMS list. 
Eligibility
Mailman is available to Faculty, Staff, and Students.
RAMS mailing lists can only be created by Faculty and Staff.
Support information
For more information, visit the Rutgers Mailman website or the Rutgers RAMS website.
Contact the OIT Help Desk for more information or questions.

title: information and guidelines about creating new Mailman lists
body:
To facilitate electronic communication among large groups of networked computer users, the Rutgers University Office of Information Technology provides electronic mailing list services to faculty, staff, and students.
Advantages of a Mailing List
A mailing list permits you to address an entire group of predesignated individuals by specifying only one address to your email software – a convenience for contacting groups with whom you correspond frequently and also for sharing information among people with common interests. If you want to send an email to a large group of people at once, then a mailing list is most likely an effective means for delivering information.
Guidelines for Mailing List Creation and Use
The Mailman service has usage restrictions regarding Protected Health Information (PHI) or other confidential University information. This service must not be used to communicate or store University-restricted data or patient Protected Health Information (PHI). Doing so represents a violation of the Federal HIPAA Privacy/Security rules, State Privacy Laws, or University policies. Users will be responsible for complying with any restricted data as defined in University Policy.
For additional information regarding restricted data, please reference the Information Classification Policy [Rutgers Policy Library]. Any further questions or concerns, please contact the OIT Help Desk.
Who can request a mailing list?
Any individual with a valid Rutgers University NetID can request the creation of a mailing list. A list can be established for your department, working group, or organization.
Scope and Usage of Mailing Lists
All lists must be used for University-related business/activities. While individuals and groups outside of the University are welcome to subscribe (add their email addresses) to lists maintained at Rutgers, they will not be permitted to set up mailing lists.
Responsibilities of the List Administrator
Only individuals with a valid Rutgers University NetID may serve as a list administrator, and the default email address used for list administrators will be of the form NetID@rutgers.edu. In all cases, the list must have a designated administrator responsible for its maintenance. These responsibilities include, but are not limited to, maintaining an up-to-date list of members. Invalid email addresses subscribed to a list can unnecessarily overburden Rutgers’ systems and personnel resources. For these reasons, the Rutgers Mailman Service Administrator may take action to help maintain lists.
In response to potential consequences to the Mailman service (i.e., risk of blacklisting by third parties and performance degradation) if issues arise concerning a list, the administrators for that list will be contacted via email and have 10 business days to acknowledge and/or fix the issues; otherwise, the list will be deactivated. Upon deactivation, it is the responsibility of the list administrators to contact help@email.rutgers.edu to facilitate the resolution of any issues. Once the issues have been resolved and confirmed, the list will be reactivated in 1-2 business days.
If there are complaints about the management of the list, they should be addressed with the list administrator; if this is not possible, the complaints should be escalated to the manager or dean who has disciplinary authority over the list administrator. If infractions of the University Code of Student Conduct are brought to our attention, e.g. lists promoting prejudices, biases, or illegal activities, OIT will bring this to the attention of the administrator and if need be, to disciplinary authorities.
Mailing List Review
The established mailing lists will be reviewed periodically. Twice a year, a review may occur for every list that has not been posted in over a year. This review may include, but is not limited to, verifying whether the list is still actively used and/or validating the email addresses of the list administrators. If no action is taken regarding any inquiries made to the list administrators within one week, we will attempt to contact them again. Failing confirmation a second time, the list will be removed. During the review, the lists must be successfully posted to keep the list active.
Requesting a Mailing List
After a successful Rutgers CAS login, prospective list administrators will see a Create New List button.
Deleting a Mailing List
List owners can delete a list (all settings and membership data will be lost) by using the Delete button located on the list's management page. The list deletion is permanent and cannot be recovered. 
Note: List archives are NOT deleted. Please see the next section on how to request that they be deleted as well.
Deleting a Mailing List Archive
List owners must send an email requesting archive deletion to help@email.rutgers.edu from their owner email address. Ensure that you provide the list name.

title: What is a Mailman mailing list?
body:
A mailing list permits you to address an entire group of designated individuals by specifying only one address to your email software. This is very convenient for contacting groups with whom you correspond frequently, or for sharing information among people with common interests. If you want to send an email to a large group of people at once, a mailing list is likely one of the most effective means for delivering information.
Mailing lists are recommended for emailing a large group (50 or more) of individuals. Mailing lists can also be useful for smaller groups, such as a half dozen members of a small department, quickly communicating with one another.
Rutgers University Computing Services offers two different options for mailing lists, Mailman and RAMS.
What is Mailman?
Mailman is software for managing electronic mailing lists. It is used for University-affiliated ad hoc mailing lists. Examples include lists for department supervisors, club or sports team members, project team members, Route 18 construction alerts, and more.
Mailman is integrated with the web, making it easy for users to manage their accounts and for list owners to administer their lists. It supports built-in archiving, automatic bounce processing, content filtering, digest delivery, spam filters, and more.
Mailman is freeware distributed under the GNU General Public License.
More information on Mailman can be found on the GNU Mailing List Manager - Main Mailman site. 
Why do we use Mailman?
As the university's needs grew, it became evident that our previous mailing list could not scale to our needs. At times, the service was so busy that web browsers would time out before the service could process the web requests. The previous system also sometimes experienced several hours of delays in delivering mail.
Mailman has met these needs without any problems.
Where is Mailman hosted?
More information and the login page can be found on the Rutgers Mailman website. 
What is RAMS?
The Rutgers Automated Mass-mailing System (RAMS) enables the generation of an email list based on demographic information from the registrar or payroll data, and provides automated updates to the list membership in response to changes in the demographic information. Examples include all students in New Brunswick, all students in a single course, all third-year students, and more.
RAMS may be a better choice for you if you intend to use your mailing list to contact specific groups or categories of Rutgers users.

title: Comms and Emergency Notifications Sender Authentication policy outline
body:
Table of Contents
•	Motivation for Policy
•	General Risk Mitigation Policy
•	Policy Per Technology 
o	Domain Message Authentication Reporting (DMARC)
o	Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM)
o	Sender Policy Framework (SPF)
•	Policy Per Domain 
o	Utility Domains
o	Rutgers.edu
o	Camden.rutgers.edu
o	Newark.rutgers.edu
o	ScarletMail.rutgers.edu
o	Connect Hosted Domains
o	Web Page Domains
Motivation for Policy
MaCS stands by the existing recommended guidelines for 3rd party mailers for achieving DMARC compatible sender authentication. (See document) Utility domains issued per service are the most flexible and robust solution, so they are our general recommendation. However, when a vendor/unit can't or won't abide by the guidelines, there are still limitations we must place on the process for practical, technical, or security reasons. Our policy is designed to minimize these risks and prevent them from being delegated upward without clear communication and collaboration.
General Risk Mitigation Policy
With sender authentication, there is a general risk that vendor configurations may be fine individually, but mutually incompatible. When such incompatibility arises, MaCS will prioritize the function of day-to-day email service and broadly shared services. Using utility domains minimizes the chance of being impacted by such mitigations.
Policy Per Technology
Domain Message Authentication Reporting (DMARC)
A policy of quarantine will be implemented on the Rutgers.edu root domain. This policy will be configured to apply to all subdomains of Rutgers.edu by default. If a subdomain has no DMARC policy of its own, the Rutgers.edu policy will be used per the RFC for DMARC. If any subdomain wishes to have a policy of 'none' or 'quarantine', those can be set per subdomain by request. Note: a policy of one may not practically differ from a policy of quarantine with some free email vendors, as they will use a failure of DMARC alignment in spam scoring and deliver both spam and quarantined mail to a user's junk folder.
Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM)
DKIM uses cryptographic hashes to validate the authenticity of an email. The public key must be published directly in a TXT record, or a pointer to the key must be published via a CNAME record.
If a vendor uses a shared, default TXT record for all customers, we recommend avoiding that vendor. If that vendor must be used, it will be restricted to use with a utility domain. This is because without proper policy enforcement by the vendor, there is a potential for one customer to exploit this at the expense of other customers. Additionally, if the private key is compromised, replacing a key due to compromise or obsolescence requires coordinated action between the vendor and all customers, or the vendor to disable the service without warning until customers can comply. It generally indicates a lack of understanding or care on the part of the vendor, and the risk that this implies must be minimized.
Many vendors use shared common CNAME records to publish one or more keys. This permits the vendor to replace the key(s) in short order if they become obsolete or are compromised. However, they are still prone to potential customer-to-customer exploitation. These can be used with utility domains and with connect-hosted domains if they do not delegate risk upward.
Some vendors use TXT records, but they are unique to each domain and customer account. While these still require a service outage or customer coordination to replace, they are at least safe from customer-to-customer exploitation. These can be used with utility domains and connect hosted domains. The university customer is responsible for requesting any maintenance.
Some vendors use multiple CNAME records, each unique to a specific domain and account. These are the gold standard for DKIM implementation and can be maintenance-free for life. However, the vendor may decide to change them periodically anyway. These can be used with utility domains and connect hosted domains. The university customer is responsible for requesting any maintenance. 
Sender Policy Framework (SPF)
SPF requires a domain owner to publish a TXT record indicating all machines designated as permitted email senders for that domain. Unfortunately, the method used can result in lookup loops. To prevent unintentional denial of service from a single initial query, SPF is limited to 10 lookups for any entity not explicitly referenced as an IP address. This is extremely limiting for an entity as large as Rutgers that has a complex IT infrastructure. It is also limiting when including cloud services due to the scale and dynamic nature of large cloud infrastructure. Most of Rutgers' email infrastructure involves significant on-premises infrastructure and both Google and Microsoft cloud infrastructure. This is sufficient to experience intermittent failure due to the ten-lookup limit. Adding more cloud vendors that themselves may be built on top of yet more cloud vendors would exacerbate this problem. SPF is limited to utility domains.
Policy Per Domain
Utility Domains
Utility domains are simply subdomains requested by the customer. They must not be in use, confusing, offensive, or otherwise problematic. They must use either vendor systems for inbound mail handling, or MaCS' XARE aliasing system. We recommend that they be used in a one-service-per-utility-domain configuration, but they may be shared across multiple vendors, provided the customer is willing to accept the risks that entails. MaCS does not monitor utility domains for any changes that might impact services. After initial configuration assistance, they are the customer's responsibility.
Rutgers.edu
The Rutgers.edu domain is a highly shared resource severely vulnerable to impersonation abuse and vendor collisions. Use of this domain with vendors is restricted to centrally administered services shared across the university and groups with broad central authority (e.g. President's Office).  This domain cannot accommodate SPF, and cannot use shared DKIM keys for security reasons. Not all uses eligible to use this domain by policy may be technically compatible.
Camden.rutgers.edu
Camden.rutgers.edu is a highly shared resource vulnerable to impersonation abuse and vendor collisions. Use of this domain with vendors is restricted to campus services shared across the campus and groups with broad campus authority (e.g. Chancellor's Office).  This domain cannot accommodate SPF, and cannot use shared DKIM keys for security reasons. Not all uses eligible to use this domain by policy may be technically compatible.
Newark.rutgers.edu
Newark.rutgers.edu is a highly shared resource vulnerable to impersonation abuse and vendor collisions. Use of this domain with vendors is restricted to campus services shared across the campus and groups with broad campus authority (e.g. Chancellor's Office).  This domain cannot accommodate SPF, and cannot use shared DKIM keys for security reasons. Not all uses eligible to use this domain by policy may be technically compatible.
ScarletMail.rutgers.edu
Scarletmail.rutgers.edu is a highly shared resource that is supposed to be exclusively for student, alumni, and retiree email. It is not to be used for official communications. This domain cannot accommodate SPF, and cannot use shared DKIM keys for security reasons. Not all uses eligible to use this domain by policy may be technically compatible.
Connect Hosted Domains
We recommend against using these domains with bulk vendors. This domain cannot accommodate SPF. MaCS discourages the use of common/shared DKIM keys on these domains. If the customer chooses to accept that risk, MaCS is not responsible for any negative consequences. If those consequences impact day-to-day email services, MaCS will disable any offending sender auth configs immediately and without warning if necessary to preserve service functionality. Not all uses eligible to use this domain by policy may be technically compatible.
Web Page Domains
Generally, subdomains used to host web pages may be used as utility domains if they have no existing MX record. If the subdomain uses a CNAME record, it cannot be used as a utility domain as it can't have an MX set. Additionally, DKIM and DMARC require subdomains of the subdomain to be configured, and CNAME records cannot have subdomains. Due to this, they may be technically excluded from use. MaCS will offer advice for configuring these subdomains as utility domains, but the customer is responsible for ensuring that any suggested changes are not incompatible with existing uses of the subdomain.

Microsoft-provided Copilot agents are now available to any department or individual who has purchased a Microsoft 365 Copilot license through the Rutgers Software Portal.
You can browse the full list of Microsoft 365 agents on Microsoft's adoption page.

•	Study and Learn – An interactive, conversational learning agent designed for students.
•	Learning Agent – Delivers personalized, in-the-flow AI and Copilot skill-building tailored to each user's role and daily activity.
•	AI Learning Advisor – Teaches and troubleshoots Microsoft's AI and low-code stack, including Copilot, Copilot Studio, and Power Platform.

title: Windows Activation for University Owned Equipment Only
body:
Key Management Server (KMS) Method
To activate Windows, the simplest method is to use a Key Management Server (KMS). The Rutgers KMS has the hostname kms.rutgers.edu. If your machine is connected to the Rutgers Active Directory (RAD), you will automatically attempt to activate against the Rutgers KMS host and you may not even need to perform the activation process manually. However, if you have not been able to activate automatically, follow the procedure below to activate against the Rutgers KMS host.
1.	Open an elevated/administrator command prompt.
2.	Click Start > type cmd > right click Command Prompt > Run as Administrator > Click Yes on the UAC prompt 
o	Type the following 2 lines and press enter after each one. 
	cscript %windir%\system32\slmgr.vbs /skms kms.rutgers.edu
	cscript %windir%\system32\slmgr.vbs /ato
Multiple Activation Key (MAK) Method
The second option for activating Windows is typically best for machines that cannot contact the KMS host frequently enough to maintain activation. This method is called Multiple Activation Key (MAK).
•	Obtain your MAK from the My Software section of the Software Portal.
•	The key will be found in the License section next to your Windows product listing.
Once you have obtained the key, you can enter it in two ways:
1.	From the System control panel: 
o	Windows Key + Pause/Break
2.	From the command line as follows:
1.	Open an elevated/administrator command prompt.
2.	Click Start > type cmd > right click Command Prompt > Run as Administrator > Click Yes on the UAC prompt.
3.	Type the following 2 lines and press enter after each one. 
	cscript %windir%\system32\slmgr.vbs /ipk YOUR_MAK
	cscript %windir%\system32\slmgr.vbs /ato

title: Teams Common use cases for Microsoft Teams
body:
Microsoft Teams combines some of the best components of Office 365 into a single tool. One of its biggest goals is collaboration. You are most likely going to benefit from using Teams within a department, group, team, or project. A new Team -- or new channels within a Team -- can be made for new goals in mind. We’ve listed below some of the most common use cases for Microsoft Teams.
Organizational Management
Managing, administering, and collaborating within a department or unit can be made easy through Teams. You can track discussions in message threads across various channels, schedule meetings or training sessions in the team’s calendar, organize files in the team’s OneDrive component, and more, all in one place. Restrictions can be implemented and configured by a team’s owner, which can be beneficial for submitting documents, viewing private files, or chatting in private spaces.
Chatting and Video Conferencing
Teams allows you to host remote virtual meetings within your team or between users individually. You can screen share, join conference calls, or hold a video conference for team members to join. They can be scheduled in advance or made on the spot. A great feature of Teams meetings is that they can be recorded and saved to Microsoft Stream, providing an option for others to view later or reference. This can be used for orientations, training sessions, interviews, and more.
Student Project Sites
Individual or group work efforts are made easier with Teams. Students can make their own Teams with either their ScarletMail or Connect accounts. External users can also be added to these self-created Teams. Creating a Team provides students with the ability to virtually meet and work with group members, store all project-related files and documents in one space, collaborate on updating documents, mark due dates on calendars, and more.
Research Sites
Teams can act as a repository for research-related activities. Each Team has its own files component with unlimited HIPAA-compliant storage and an associated email address. Sharing and reviewing research files is made convenient -- you can email the group a document that can be viewed (and saved) in the Team space. You can reference files in a discussion thread within Teams while editing the files in real-time. External collaborators can also be included or restricted to certain files, channels, and discussions.
Cooperative Project Sites
If a department has multiple projects that need managing, Microsoft Teams is a great tool for the job. Whether your project involves software development, lab work, hiring, promotion tracking, or committee organization, having multiple Office 365 products in one space can help make tasks run smoothly. With SharePoint, OneDrive, OneNote, Power Automate, and other integrations at your disposal, you can work on and manage your projects in a simple and intuitive application that has everything in one place.

title: Teams Creating a team in Microsoft Teams
body:
Creating a Team
Rutgers Connect users can self-create their own Teams through the Teams application. Upon logging in and viewing all Teams, you will see a Join or create team option in the top right corner of your application.
Here, you will be provided with four different creation options: Class, Professional Learning Community (PLC), Staff, and Other. To better understand which Teams option is best for you, please refer to Microsoft's documentation on choosing a team type. Class teams function similarly to class sites, where students and teachers can collaborate on projects, assignments, and classwork. Staff teams work best for staff members working on a project together. PLC teams offer a space for faculty members and educators to collaborate, while “Other” is more for personal, casual teams or groups.
Previously, Microsoft Teams was only available to Rutgers Connect users through the creation of a unified group; this option remains available for users who would like a team based on an existing or new Office 365 group. Any changes made to the group will be synced with Teams automatically, and can simplify the process of inviting/managing members. Group files are also displayed inside of Microsoft Teams.
There are two primary roles in Microsoft Teams: team owner and team member. Owners create the group, or are assigned ownership to a group by a delegated administrator (depending on the team that’s been created). Owners can designate any member of their team as a co-owner; multiple owners enable you to share responsibilities and manage settings. Team members are invited by the owners or added to the team group by delegated administrators.
There are notable differences between self-created teams and departmental teams that users should be aware of before making their decision:
Departmental Teams
•	Must be requested and created by contacting your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator
•	Only faculty/staff can request creation
•	You can open and view a unified group mailbox associated with the Team
•	Has an associated email address for the group that is created with the Team
•	No restrictions for the team name, but restricted to the department’s or user’s domain (i.e. @oit, @echo, etc.)
•	Owners cannot update the name; only delegated administrators are able to
Self-created Teams
•	Any user with a Connect account can create a team via the Teams application
•	Stand-alone; no unified group mailbox to view in Rutgers Connect
•	Can only send mail to specific channels within the team itself
•	Teams are restricted to the @teams domain and have a stricter naming policy
•	Owners can update or change the name of their Team in the Team's settings
•	Faculty, staff, and students can self-create
•	Teams inactive for 400 days will expire automatically. Starting 30 days prior to expiration, the Team owner(s) will receive email notifications from Microsoft stating that their Team will expire unless action is taken. 
Select a Team and Channel
A team is a collection of people, conversations, files, and tools — all in one place. A channel is a discussion topic in a team. The best way to get familiar with teams and channels is to select a team and channel and start exploring.
1.	Select the Teams icon. If you’re not on a Team and want to create one, refer to “Creating a Team” above.
2.	Select a channel and explore the Conversations, Files, and Notes tabs.
Channels can be a department, project, or topic. For more info, see Teams and channels.
Getting to Know the Microsoft Teams Layout
When you open Microsoft Teams, a search bar is centered at the top of the screen. This helps you quickly locate the Team, file, message, or person you are looking for. Microsoft Teams usually opens to the last view that was used. If it’s a fresh session or your first time, you may not see any Teams displayed. Alternatively, you may also open to a list of teams you are a member of or own, that you can select.
A vertical toolbar resides on the left side of the screen. Its upper left corner contains buttons for the main views: Activity, Chat, Teams, Calendar, Calls, and Files. You can also add more items to your left sidebar for easy access. Note that some buttons may not be available, depending on your account type. In the lower left corner of the toolbar are the buttons for Apps that are integrated with Teams and Help for feedback and training. Notification settings are synced with the server; changes made in the browser will be reflected in the desktop client.
The rest of the screen is divided into two panes. Pane content depends on the current view. The left or list pane is used to navigate within the view. It always contains the Search field. The rest of its contents depend on the selected view. For example, if you select Chat on the toolbar, the left pane contains a list of your favorite, recent, and suggested contacts.
The right or main pane takes up most of the screen. It shows the content of the selection you have made in the left pane. For example, if you selected Chat on the toolbar and then selected a recent contact in the left pane, the right pane contains your conversation history with that person. The right pane also has tabs to keep the content organized. For example, the Files tab contains a list of the files shared between you and the selected contact, the Teams tab shows a list of all of your Teams, and so on.
A breakdown of the default tabs:
•	Activity - list of notifications and call history
•	Chat - direct messages between other users or groups
•	Teams - list of teams you have access to, and where you can view your team’s content
•	Calendar - displays your Rutgers Connect calendar
•	Calls - where you can easily host meetings or call another user/group
•	Files - view recent files you’ve accessed, recent notebooks you’ve worked in, files shared with you, downloads you’ve done, etc., across all teams & groups you have access to (as well as your own personal OneDrive).
Individual Team Layout
Once you open and access your team via the Teams tab, the right pane reveals numerous new options, tabs, and features for you to use. The default view is the “General” conversation channel, which is a dedicated section within a team to keep conversations organized. Various viewing/access permissions can be granted per channel, along with file access. Each team has “General” as the default channel. The name can be changed, more channels can be added, deleted, moved, and archived in the team settings. Channels are ordered alphabetically.
At the top of the team display are different tabs -- what’s displayed will be different depending on the type of team you created. The default is Posts where discussion channels live. Files lets you open the files within the team’s SharePoint site that houses OneDrive files. You can move around and add other tabs, including Forms, OneNote, Planner, Excel, and various other integrations that have been enabled in Teams.
The ellipses in the top right corner of your team brings up channel notification settings, channel management settings, an email address for each channel that you can send mail to directly, and a link to a channel that you can provide to members. Connectors cannot be modified by team owners or members, they are managed at the admin level. The ellipses on the left side of the team next to your team’s name lets you open the team’s settings (as an owner), add channels, leave the team, edit the team, or get a link to take members directly to the team.
The ability to start a conversation, mention someone in a conversation, comment on a thread or file, post a file, start a meeting, and more can be found at the bottom of your team’s layout.
If you delete a team, all associated files, conversations, and notes related to the team will also be deleted. To inquire about a team that needs to be restored, please contact your delegated administrator.
Learn more about Microsoft Teams
The Teams application features a “Help” section dedicated to educating users on how to utilize Teams to its full potential. The “What’s New” section displays recent news or changes to Teams.
Microsoft has also implemented a chat feature called “T-Bot” where you can utilize it to ask questions. To access T-Bot, select Chat, then search for T-Bot as a contact. Type your question in the message box and press Enter.
You can also view more organizational tips from Microsoft.

Information protection in Teams
To meet your legal, regulatory, and content security needs, Teams offers the following information protection capabilities through the Office 365 Security & Compliance Center:
Capability	Description
Archive	Any content stored in any Teams-related workload needs to be preserved immutably according to the enterprise corporate policy.
Compliance content search	Any content stored in any workload can be searched through rich filtering capabilities. All content can be exported to a specific container for compliance and litigation support.
eDiscovery	Rich eDiscovery in-place capabilities, including case management, preservation, search, analysis, and export, are available to help our customers simplify the eDiscovery process and quickly identify relevant data while decreasing cost and risk.
Legal hold	When any team or individual is placed on in-place hold or litigation hold, the hold is applied to both the primary and archived messages (excluding edits and deletes).
Audit log search	All team activities and business events must be captured and available for customer search and export
Exchange online protection	Email messages that are sent to a channel are filtered for spam, malware, malicious links, spoofing, and phishing via Exchange Online Protection and Advanced Threat Protection for Office 365.
Conditional access	We ensure that access to Teams is restricted to devices that are compliant with your IT admin or corporate organization's set policies and security rules. This includes MDM and MAM support with Intune for iOS and Android.
For more information about these compliance features, see Overview of security and compliance in Office 365.
For more details about content searches and Teams, see the Teams section of Run a Content Search in the Office 365 Security & Compliance Center.

•	Safari 11.0 uses Intelligent Tracking Prevention to block third-party tracking cookies. Because of the way Intelligent Tracking Prevention categorizes cookies, login.microsoftonline.com gets lumped into this category (even though it is not a tracking domain), and Microsoft Teams is prevented from opening.
•	If you want to use Teams in Safari while the Safari browser support is in preview, go to Preferences > Privacy and uncheck the "Prevent cross-site tracking" setting. Then, close your browser and navigate back to teams.microsoft.com in Safari.
Notes:
•	Changing this setting may impact your experience on other websites.
•	Once Safari is fully supported for Teams, you will no longer need this workaround.
When you are done using Teams in Safari, go to Preferences > Privacy and recheck the Prevent cross-site tracking setting.

title: - Rooms
body:
What are Microsoft Teams Rooms?
Microsoft Teams Rooms are a way to connect conference room equipment to a Rutgers Connect calendar. There are two variations of this product:
•	Microsoft Teams Panels 
o	These are devices (usually tablet-sized) that display the meetings scheduled for a room. Some even come with status lights to indicate from a distance if the room is currently occupied when the device is mounted outside the conference room door in the hallway. If this is all that is needed, then a Microsoft Teams Shared Space license can be used to activate the room calendar with a Teams Panel device.
•	Microsoft Teams Room 
o	Consists of one or multiple devices that allow integrating the room calendar with the conference display. Typically, this setup includes a Front of Room Display, which often features a microphone, speakers, and a camera, paired with a touchscreen console and an optional Teams Panel. Some hardware configurations will not have a separate console but will have a touchscreen on the Front of Room Display. All actions typically done on the touchscreen console will instead be done on the touchscreen Front of Room Display. Based on the room calendar, upcoming meetings are displayed on both the display and console, with a one-touch meeting join button available on the console. Either a Teams, WebEx, or Zoom icon will accompany the join button to indicate which application interface will be used in the meeting. If the room was not invited to the meeting, attendees can enter the meeting information manually and join it ad hoc. A Microsoft Teams Room Pro license is needed per room calendar and supports any combination of Front of Room Display, Touchscreen Console, and Teams Panel; up to five devices. 
o	Attendees or presenters can use Microsoft Teams Rooms for a Microsoft Teams Town Hall or a Microsoft Teams Webinar. Microsoft has additional information on joining the events, using the Green Room, and switching between presenter and attendee views.
For either solution, QR codes can be enabled to provide an easy way to access the room calendar, eliminating the need to look up the room in the address book. They can also be used to join an ongoing meeting from their mobile device, reserve and start an ad hoc meeting, or cast content from their mobile device to the Front of Room Display. Depending on the hardware chosen, additional features may be available or not.
Using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Cisco hardware
For Microsoft Teams Rooms on Cisco hardware, One-Touch Joining of events is supported for WebEx, Zoom, and Teams meetings. Invite the room calendar to the meeting or forward the meeting details to the room calendar so that the event appears on their calendar. It may take 5 to 10 minutes for an invitation to be processed and appear on the calendar. If the meeting does not appear on a room calendar, double-check that it is not being rejected due to one of the following situations. Refer to the Cisco One Button to Push (OBTP) documentation for additional information. 
Microsoft Teams Rooms on Cisco hardware shares similarities with Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android devices. Microsoft has additional information on what to expect when using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android devices.
Important notes when creating Microsoft Teams Rooms
•	Make sure the meeting does not overlap with someone else's booking. If the meeting is recurring, ensure that none of the future events overlap, or the entire series will be rejected.
•	Room reservations cannot be made more than 1,080 days (approximately 3 years) in advance. If the meeting recurrence has a span greater than 1080 days, the entire series will be rejected. To fix this, shorten the period between the first and last meetings to be less than 1,080 days. If, two years into the future, the meeting needs to be extended for another two years, a new series can be created to start after the existing one ends, or the Start/End By dates of the existing meetings' recurrence can be adjusted.
How to manually join Microsoft Teams Rooms
If the meeting information does not get automatically pulled from the calendar event, try the following to join manually:
•	Teams: Click the "Join with an ID" button, select the appropriate provider, and then click "Next." Enter the meeting ID and Passcode, and then join the meeting.
•	WebEx: A fly-out menu is located on the center-right edge of the touch console. Touch it to make it slide out onto the screen. Click on either the Call or Webex button, and type in the WebEx meeting number with the "@rutgers.webex.com" suffix.
•	Zoom: A fly-out menu is located on the center-right edge of the touch console. Touch it to make it slide out onto the screen. Click on the Zoom button to join by access code and password. If the conference room has multiple screens, this method may need to be used instead of simply hitting the Join button to utilize all screens.

title: - Town Halls
body:
What are Microsoft Teams Town Halls?
The Town Hall meeting style in Microsoft Teams is intended for large, broadcast-style events that focus on sharing information across broad audiences. Unlike Teams Webinars, which are designed around registration and structured participation, Town Halls emphasize presentation and delivery by providing a platform for organizational updates, leadership communications, or campus-wide announcements. 
Town Halls provide a streamlined, one-to-many experience, where presenters control what attendees see and hear, helping to maintain focus and consistency throughout the event. Attendees join in a view-only format, with options for moderated Q&A and post-event reporting available to organizers. 
Town Halls can be scheduled directly from the Teams calendar and configured for internal or public audiences. With Teams Premium, organizers can take advantage of additional features, including higher attendee limits, enhanced analytics, live translated captions, and advanced production controls. Teams Premium licenses are not required to host Town Halls, but they can be purchased through the Rutgers Software Portal for additional controls.
Key settings to review before creating a Town Hall in Microsoft Teams
•	Organizers should begin planning Town Halls several weeks in advance to allow time for scheduling, setup, and promotion. High-attendance events may require additional testing, especially if large numbers of external participants are expected. Early preparation ensures a smoother experience for both presenters and attendees. 
•	Decide whether the Town Hall should be open to the public or limited to internal Rutgers participants. Public Town Halls are accessible to anyone with the event link, while internal Town Halls restrict access to members of the Rutgers organization. External attendees can only join if the event is set to public. 
•	Next, assign roles and confirm responsibilities. Determine who will serve as presenters, co-organizers, and moderators. Each role contributes differently. Presenters share content, co-organizers manage logistics and transitions, and moderators handle Q&A and attendee engagement. 
•	Plan the event content and layout. Identify which speakers will be spotlighted, what materials will be shared, and how transitions between segments will occur. Consider incorporating consistent branding or imagery to achieve a professional look. 
•	Before the event, conduct one or more technical rehearsals using the Town Hall green room to verify audio, video, screen sharing, and transitions. Testing network performance and device setup ahead of time helps minimize disruptions during the live broadcast. 
•	For large-scale events, ensure your organization's content delivery network (eCDN) settings are optimized. Microsoft eCDN is enabled by default for Teams Premium users, but other options can be configured if needed. 
•	Once all preparations are complete, publish the event and distribute the invitation through your department's channels. Reminders can be sent closer to the event date to encourage attendance. 
For additional guidance on preparing large-scale Teams events, review Microsoft's tips for setting up large meetings and events in Teams. 
For more information about setting up Town Hall, review Microsoft's guide on getting started with Town Hall in Microsoft Teams. 
Creating a Town Hall in Microsoft Teams 
1.	Open Microsoft Teams.
2.	Go to Calendar > New meeting > Town Hall.
3.	When the Town Hall form opens, enter the following: 
o	Title of the Town Hall.
o	Date, start time, and end time.
o	Description for the event.
4.	Add presenters and co-organizers as needed.
5.	Review the settings, then select Save to publish the Town Hall.
Error! Filename not specified. 
In the event form, organizers can configure the Town Hall's access. By default, events are set to internal, meaning only accounts within the Rutgers organization can attend. If the event is to be open to external guests, change the access type to 'public' before saving, ensuring that anyone with the event link can join the broadcast. 
Organizers can add agenda items or notes to the Meeting notes section. These notes are visible only to presenters and co-organizers and can be used to outline talking points, assign presentation segments, or provide internal instructions. 
After saving, Teams will generate the event in your Teams calendar and automatically send invitations to presenters and co-organizers. Organizers can then configure advanced settings such as enabling Q&A, controlling attendee visibility, or customizing the event layout.  
After reviewing all configurations, publish the event and share the Town Hall link with attendees through appropriate communication channels such as email, departmental newsletters, or campus announcements. The event will remain visible and editable from the Teams calendar, allowing organizers to manage details, update participants, or duplicate the setup for future sessions. 
After the conclusion of the Town Hall, all recordings, Q&A history, and engagement reports will be accessible from the calendar entry. 
For full details, refer to Microsoft's guide on creating a Town Hall in Microsoft Teams.
Important notes and tips for using Microsoft Teams Town Halls
•	Town Hall attendees join with audio and video off by default. Only presenters and organizers can share their audio and video. Engagement is via Q&A or other controlled interactions. 
•	Audio/video latency is expected (delays in one-to-many broadcasting).
•	If a past Town Hall is duplicated, many settings will carry over; however, some production options may reset or require reconfiguration.
•	Be aware of retention and expiration settings for recordings. By default, published Town Hall recordings expire after 30 days; in some cases, organizers can extend this period to 60 days. 
•	Use real-time analytics and telemetry (especially with Premium) to monitor audience viewership, performance, and network quality. 
Frequently asked questions about Microsoft Teams Town Halls
•	Who can schedule a Town Hall? 
o	People who have permission and a license (typically enterprise Teams users). Advanced features (e.g., increased attendee limits, analytics, eCDN) require Teams Premium. 
•	Who can attend a Town Hall? 
o	For public Town Halls, both internal and external users are welcome to attend.
o	For internal Town Halls, only users within the organization or domain can join. External or anonymous users cannot. 
•	Do attendees need a Teams account? 
o	External attendees can join via a web browser without a Teams account (if the event is public). Internal attendees typically sign in with their Rutgers organization credentials.
•	What interaction do attendees have? 
o	Attendees' mics and cameras are turned off by default. They can interact via Q&A, chat (if enabled), and possibly reactions depending on configuration.
•	Can external presenters be added? 
o	Yes. Organizers can invite presenters outside the organization; they'll receive a unique link with presenter rights. 
•	What happens after the Town Hall? 
o	Organizers can download and publish the event recording. Published recordings send email notifications to attendees. Attendance and engagement reports become available. Real-time analytics dashboards may be accessible with Premium licensing. 
•	Where can I find the Town Hall recording after it ends? 
o	Once the event ends and the recording is published, attendees will receive an email with a link to view the recording. Organizers and presenters can also access the recording from the meeting details in Teams. The recording can be found in the Teams calendar, just like a regular meeting. The recording and reports are available in the Teams calendar event details page. Recordings are stored in OneDrive or SharePoint, depending on where the Town Hall was scheduled. Organizers and co-organizers own the recording and can share or download it as needed.
•	How many attendees can join a Town Hall? 
o	Up to 10,000 under standard licensing. With Teams Premium, the capacity can reach 50,000 attendees, as per Microsoft documentation.
•	How is a Town Hall different from a Webinar or a regular meeting? 
o	Meetings are collaborative, where everyone can unmute, share, and chat freely.
o	Webinars are structured events that require registration and typically limit the number of attendees.
o	Town Halls are large-scale, broadcast-style events designed for one-to-many communication, featuring moderated Q&A and robust production controls. 
•	How long can a Town Hall last? 
o	Town Halls can run for up to 30 hours, allowing for extended programming or back-to-back sessions if needed.
•	Who can present or moderate during a Town Hall? 
o	Each Town Hall has Organizers who schedule and manage the event, configure settings, and access reports. Presenters share content, speak on camera, and manage Q&A. Producers/Co-organizers assist with production, manage what attendees see, and handle transitions. Only assigned presenters and co-organizers are permitted to speak or share content during the event.

title: - Webinars
body:
What are Microsoft Teams Webinars?
The webinar meeting style is event-oriented, making it suitable for hosting organized, presenter-led events such as trainings, briefings, or information sessions. Webinars are best suited for scenarios where participants primarily attend to view and listen, rather than actively collaborate, as in traditional meetings. It's a style that focuses on one-way communication from presenters to the audience, offering a more controlled and formal setting.  
Webinars can be scheduled in advance, shared publicly or within the organization, and managed through the Teams calendar like any other meeting type. With Teams Premium, additional capabilities become available, such as manual registration approval, waitlists, and enhanced branding and security features. Teams Premium licenses are not required for the webinar service, but can be purchased for additional webinar features from the Rutgers Software Portal.  
Teams Premium offers numerous features that impact all meeting types, including Town Halls and Webinars.  
Key settings to review before creating a Microsoft Teams Webinar
•	Organizers should plan and prepare the Teams Webinar for several weeks in advance to allow enough time for registration, promotion, and preparation. Verify whether the event should be open to the public or limited to internal Rutgers participants. Public webinars allow anyone with the registration link to sign up, while private webinars restrict access to accounts within the Rutgers organization. Anyone, whether inside or outside the organization, can register via public webinar links. Note, webinars may default to "Public" if not specified otherwise. This setting can be changed before publishing the event.
•	Next, design a registration form that best collects the required information from attendees. Organizers can use this registration form to gather insights, triage registrants, or track attendance. Once the form is finalized, invite presenters and co-organizers. Each role has distinct responsibilities: presenters share content and lead discussions, while co-organizers assist with event management, moderation, and logistics. Organizers should invite both internal and external speakers and determine who will help with managing registration, moderation, Q&A, and other tasks.   
•	Organizers are also encouraged to prepare an agenda, draft talking points, and perform technical checks in advance. Testing the cameras, microphones, and network connectivity before the event helps avoid disruptions. Consider joining the webinar from multiple devices to confirm that both presenters' and attendees' views appear as expected.
•	After finalizing details, publish the webinar and share the registration link through the appropriate channels, such as email, newsletters, or department announcements. Once the event is published, presenters and registered attendees will automatically receive an invitation containing the event details. 
For more guidance on preparing large-scale Teams events, see Microsoft's article on tips for setting up large meetings and events in Teams. 
More information about the Webinar setup can be found in Microsoft's article on how to get started with Microsoft Teams Webinars. 
How to create a Webinar in Microsoft Teams 
1.	Open Microsoft Teams.
2.	Go to Calendar > New meeting > Webinar.
3.	When the webinar form opens, enter the following: 
o	Title of the webinar.
o	Date, start time, and end time.
o	Description for attendees.
4.	Add presenters and co-organizers as needed.
5.	Review the settings, then select Save to publish the webinar. 
Error! Filename not specified. 
In this new webinar format, organizers can add an agenda or notes to the Meeting Notes section. These notes are visible only to presenters and co-organizers and can be used to outline topics, assign responsibilities, or prepare discussion materials. Note that by default, new webinars are created as public, meaning anyone with the registration link can sign up. If the event should be limited to members of the Rutgers organization, change the access setting to Your organization before saving. This format restricts registration and attendance to internal users only. 
After saving, Teams will create a registration page, send invitations to presenters, and allow the organizer to preview or edit the registration form. After reviewing the form, publish the event to make it accessible to attendees. The registration link can be shared directly or included in campus communications and event listings. After publishing, the event should appear in your Teams calendar and be manageable like any other meeting. Organizers may edit details, update registration settings, or duplicate the event to reuse its configuration for future sessions. Recordings, attendance reports, and chat history will also be available from the duplicate calendar entry once the webinar has concluded. 
For complete guidance, refer to Microsoft's article on scheduling a webinar in Microsoft Teams. 
Important notes and tips for using Microsoft Teams Webinars
•	When duplicating a Teams Webinar, most settings are carried over (theme, forms, emails), although the meeting options may revert to default if the original event was unused for more than 60 days. 
•	For external presenters, Teams will generate a unique join link; external presenters don't always need to wait in the lobby. 
•	Be sure to check registration form settings before publishing.
•	If a user purchased a Teams Premium license, they receive additional webinar capabilities, such as:  
o	Manual registration approval: Organizers can approve or reject registrations. 
o	Waitlists: Automatically manage oversubscription by queuing additional registrants. 
o	Enhanced branding & customization: More control over the look and feel, branded emails, and logos. 
o	Security & advanced analytics: Additional reporting, controls, and telemetry. 
Frequently Asked Questions about Microsoft Teams Webinars 
•	Who can schedule a Teams Webinar? 
o	By default, any user who can schedule Teams Meetings can also schedule Teams Webinars, including all faculty, staff, and users with full Rutgers Connect accounts. 
•	Who can attend a Teams Webinar?  
o	In a public Teams Webinar, anyone (internal or external) can register.
o	In an internal/private Teams Webinar, only users within your organizational boundary can register and attend. All Rutgers University members should be considered internal. 
•	What happens during the Teams Webinar? 
o	External attendees join a lobby and must be admitted. Presenters control the experience, as they can mute attendees, turn off video, promote attendees, use polls, and more. Attendee audio/video is off by default (unless granted permissions). 
•	What is available after the Teams Webinar?  
o	Organizers can download detailed reports (attendance, engagement, registration). It is also possible to share recordings (if available) and follow up with participants as needed.
•	Where can I find my Teams Webinar after it ends (including recordings)? 
o	After a Teams Webinar concludes, it can be found in the Teams calendar, just like a regular Teams Meeting. Go to Calendar in Microsoft Teams and open the completed webinar event. If the webinar was recorded, the recording link will appear in the meeting chat and on the meeting details page. Recordings are stored in the organizer's personal OneDrive, or in a resource's SharePoint site if the meeting was held in a Teams channel. To access stored recordings, navigate to My Content > Meetings.
o	Note: The organizer and presenters typically own the recording. They can share the link with attendees or download it if needed. Recordings are subject to Rutgers' data retention and sharing policies.
•	Can I edit or delete a Teams Webinar after it has been published? 
o	Yes. The organizer can return to the event in the Teams calendar and open the webinar page. From there, they can also edit the title, description, presenters, registration form, or event access (public vs. internal). If the event has already been published, attendees will receive updated invitations when major details are changed.
•	Can I duplicate a past Teams Webinar to reuse its settings? 
o	Yes. To save time and duplicate a past event, open the webinar and select Duplicate event from the toolbar. Most details, including the theme, registration form, and presenter list, will carry over if the event has been recent enough. The date, description, and registration options can also be edited before publishing. 
•	Do attendees need a Microsoft Teams account to join a Teams Webinar?  
o	Not necessarily. For public webinars, anyone with a valid registration link can join via web browser; a Teams account isn't required. For internal (organization-only) webinars, attendees must sign in with their Rutgers credentials. 
•	How long are Teams Webinar recordings kept? 
o	It depends on where the recording is kept. If the webinar recording is stored in the organizers' personal OneDrive, it may be subject to audits. Recordings stored in SharePoint will honor the Teams' retention policies. By default, Teams recordings are automatically deleted after 120 days. Always download or back up recordings that can be reused.
•	Can Teams Webinar include breakout rooms or polls? 
o	Webinars support most standard Teams meeting features, including polls, reactions, and Q&A. Breakout rooms are supported in Webinars with fewer than 300 attendees. 
•	Can I add external presenters or co-organizers?  
o	Yes. External presenters can be added by email. They'll receive a unique join link with presenter permissions. Co-organizers, however, must be members of the Rutgers tenant.
•	What's the attendee limit for a Teams Webinar?  
o	By default, up to 1,000 interactive participants can join a Teams Webinar. If attendance exceeds that number, Teams automatically switches overflow attendees to a "view-only experience", supporting up to 10,000 attendees (or 20,000 with Teams Premium). 
More troubleshooting questions can be found in Microsoft's article on troubleshooting meeting issues in Microsoft Teams.

title: for Students
body:
Rutgers University provides free access to various Microsoft Office products for all current students, which includes Microsoft Teams. Students can download and access Microsoft Teams using their Rutgers email accounts: Non-RBHS students have access to the product by logging in using their ScarletMail accounts, while RBHS students can download and access Teams directly from their Rutgers Connect accounts.
Microsoft Teams is a great way for students to collaborate with classmates virtually by managing tasks, video conferencing, direct messaging, and storing files all in one place. It has also replaced Skype for Business as the suggested product for voice and video conferencing in the Office 365 suite, offering real-time updates to files and conversations. Rutgers University students have the ability to both join existing Teams and create new ones.
Students will have continued access to their Teams files, conversations, and data until their student role expires, after which the Office 365 Suite will no longer be available. Much of the data that’s stored via Teams can be accessed or shared from the student’s OneDrive (also available in the Office 365 Suite for students). Because students are using a ScarletMail address to access these spaces, there is no Office 365 mailbox attached to these products. Students can still receive mail from Teams at their ScarletMail accounts.
If a student has been invited to join a team, or is eager to create their own collaborative space, follow the instructions below to login.
Log in via the Teams web app
1.	Open a web browser.
2.	Navigate to teams.microsoft.com to access the Teams login page.
3.	Log in with your Rutgers ScarletMail* credentials. The login name should be entered as netid@scarletmail.rutgers.edu*.
4.	Enter your NetID password.
5.	Select Sign in.
*If you are an RBHS student, or if you were provisioned with an Office 365 account, you must login using your connect.rutgers.edu credentials instead of your ScarletMail account.
Log in via the desktop app
1.	After downloading the application from getoffice.rutgers.edu using your student account*, you will be asked to sign in with your work or school account.
2.	The login name should be entered as netid@scarletmail.rutgers.edu*.
3.	Enter your NetID password.
4.	Select Sign in.
*If you are an RBHS student, or if you were provisioned with an Office 365 account, you can download Teams directly from getoffice.rutgers.edu using your connect.rutgers.edu credentials instead of your ScarletMail account.
Log in via mobile applications
Students that would like to access teams from their mobile devices will need to first register the device via mobile device management. The process involves downloading the Rutgers Company Portal application in order to register the device via Microsoft Intune, as is the case for most Office365 applications on mobile devices. More details about the MDM process can be found here.
This measure is in place to secure devices in order to meet University compliance. MDM does not interfere with personal privacy or personal usage of a device. It instead provides an extra layer of security on the device and works to prevent the compromisation of University data. RBHS students can view their specific MDM policy information here. For any issues with MDM, please contact the OIT Help Desk for assistance.
Instructions for downloading the Company Portal Application can be found below
1.	Download the Microsoft Intune Company Portal application from your respective app store.
2.	Follow instructions for setup based on your device:
o	iOS instructions
o	Android instructions
3.	After setup, open the app and navigate to the Apps section.
4.	Under Apps, search for/select Microsoft Teams to download it.
5.	After download, you should be able to login with your ScarletMail (or Rutgers Connect) information.
Remember: RBHS students (or any student with a Connect account) can sign-in to Teams directly from their Connect accounts. 
Getting Started
Once signed in, you should be brought to the main Teams tab where you can view any Team you are a member of, or create a new Team using the Join or create a team option. There are also sections for direct calls/messages, recent activity, and a calendar where you can view or schedule meetings.
Teams are made up of two types of channels — standard (available and visible to everyone) and private (focused, private conversations with a specific audience). Each channel is built around a topic like "Team Events," a department name, or just for fun. Channels are where you hold meetings, have conversations, and work on files together. The tabs at the top of each channel link to your favorite files, apps, and services. Tabs vary for each channel. Microsoft offers various support videos to help users become familiar with the product.
You can also watch a demonstration on how the Rutgers University environment works from the Rutgers IT Lecture Series.
Key Features in Teams for Students
Manage Notifications
1.	Select the ellipses at the top of your application > Settings > Notifications.
2.	To be notified about all your shown channels, under the Teams and Channels section, select All activity.
3.	To be notified only when you are @mentioned or when you receive replies to your messages in channels, select Mentions & replies.
4.	You also have the ability to set custom notifications.
o	In order to see personal @ mentions, team mentions, and to better engage with team posts or direct messages, ensure that Banner and Feed is selected for the options of your choice. This will provide you with a prompt directly on your device even if the application is minimized or closed.
o	The Only show in feed option will still flash notifications on the desktop taskbar when notifications arrive, but no pop-up will show on your desktop.
Pinning Posts
•	To pin a post within a channel, hover over the post that you want to pin, select the More options at the top right, and then choose Pin.
•	To remove a pinned post, go to the original post, select More options, and then choose Unpin.
o	Note: If you can't pin a post, check with a team owner or channel moderator to see if you have permissions.
Application Behavior
•	This section allows you to update if the Teams application opens on startup, runs in the background, etc.
•	Click the ellipses at the top of your application > Settings > General > Application.
Add Multiple Teams Environments
•	If you have access to Teams from different accounts, you can add the account to your Teams application to easily alternate between them. The environment that you have access to with your student account is titled “Rutgers University” seen in the top right.
•	To add another account, such as a personal Microsoft address, click the ellipses at the top of your application > Settings > Account > Add account.
Background Blur for Meetings
•	You can set your own custom background during a video call to help disguise things in the background. You can also blur out the background. Both settings can be found before you join a call/meeting. You can head start this by going to Calendar > Meet now > Start meeting.
•	Prior to a call/meeting, turn on your camera and select Background filters.
Pop-out Chat
•	Right-click on a chat, select pop-out chat to isolate the window.
For more information, see our frequently asked questions or see our Teams support page. Any questions or concerns regarding Teams please contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: information for Delegated Admins
body:
There are two types of Teams: those created by a user and those built from a Unified Group. All Teams are technically built behind Unified Groups -- self-created Teams have all of the features that a Unified Group would have (different policies/restrictions), but they do not have a mailbox that is accessible to them. They would only be navigating the Teams interface. There’s a SharePoint “mailbox” instance that includes conversations in the Team, but mail has been turned off for the @teams domain. So there should not be mail delivered there. If users want to utilize the mail feature, you should create a Unified Group.
Users can choose to create a team themselves or request the creation of a Unified Group with Teams access from a delegated administrator. All self-created Teams are automatically provisioned in the @teams domain, to which the Help Desk (help@oit.rutgers.edu) has administrative access. Unified Groups created by DAs with the Teams value set to “on” in CAT will be created in the respective department’s domain. To search for a Team, you can type its associated email address in the search field in CAT. Each team will have an email address (though it cannot be used for mail in the case of self-created Teams). To view all groups/teams within your domain, navigate to the “Unified Groups” tab in CAT and select your domain in the “Manage Unified Groups” section of the page. This tab also lets you create new departmental groups/teams.
There are notable differences between self-created teams and departmental teams that users should be aware of before making their decision. For more information, refer to the Microsoft Teams Knowledge article. 
Departmental Teams
•	Must be requested and created by a delegated administrator
•	Users can open and view a unified group mailbox associated with the Team in Rutgers Connect
•	The associated email address can be utilized for the group
•	No restrictions for the team name, but restricted to the department’s or user’s domain (i.e. @oit, @echo, etc.)
•	Owners cannot update the name; only delegated administrators are able to
•	Only faculty/staff can request creation
•	Unified Groups do not expire, so the Team will not expire
Self-created Teams
•	Any user with a Connect account can create a team via the Teams application
•	Stand-alone; no unified group mailbox to view in Rutgers Connect
•	Can only send mail to specific channels within the team itself
•	Teams are restricted to the @teams domain and have a stricter naming policy
•	Owners can update or change the name of their Team in the Team’s settings
•	Faculty, staff, and students can self-create
•	Teams inactive for 400 days will expire automatically
For instance, if a user wants more access over how their Team is named or if they want a mailbox associated with their team, they should create a Unified Group with their DA. For self-created Teams, the team owner can update the name, ownership, membership, and more within the Teams application.
Connect Support is currently developing a de-provisioning process for self-created teams. Information will be provided to Domain Admins prior to rolling out the process. 

When this is rolled out, the process will be the following: 

The de-provisioning process for self-created Teams is as follows:
•	After 400 days of inactivity, the Team owner(s) will receive an email notification from Microsoft stating that their Team will expire in X amount of time unless action is taken.
o	The first notice is sent 30 days prior to soft deletion, the second notice is sent 15 days prior, and a final notice is sent 1 day prior to deletion.

body:
