About Teams Phone
Rutgers now offers a softphone solution that utilizes the Microsoft Teams client (available to anyone with a Rutgers Connect account) while continuing to support the existing Cisco hardware and infrastructure used for desk phones. This hybrid approach offers you the flexibility of mobile communication without compromising access to the robust voice architecture already in place. 
The Teams softphone is an ideal solution for individuals who aren’t anchored to a single office location. Whether working remotely or off-site, you are not limited to using a desk phone in a physical workspace. You can make and receive calls from anywhere with just an internet connection and your Teams client. The softphone license includes a dedicated calling interface and dial pad. It works across multiple devices (desktop and mobile), and while the experience may vary slightly depending on your device, there is consistency across platforms to route desk phone calls directly to your Teams account. All Teams' softphone traffic is encrypted end-to-end with logging and analytics available upon request.  
If you choose to purchase the Teams softphone license, please note that it will effectively replace your physical desk phone. Both cannot operate simultaneously, and once the license is assigned, the desk phone will no longer function (except for emergency 911 calls). You will receive a reminder of this change at the time of purchase. Additionally, only individuals with a Rutgers Connect account are eligible for the softphone license. You who have the Teams softphone license will still be able to place and receive calls with colleagues who do not have the license. 
Once the Teams softphone license has been purchased and licensed, you will see a dial pad added to your Teams client on desktop, mobile, tablet, and even on dedicated Teams-certified hardware. This license enables faculty and staff to make and receive calls, just like a traditional desk phone, but fully integrated into the collaboration environment you use every day. The goal was to achieve consistency, flexibility, and modern functionality, reducing reliance on legacy desk phones, improving mobility, and providing a seamless voice experience across all Teams-enabled environments. 
To get started, you can purchase the softphone license from the Rutgers Voice Services Team by emailing td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu. Once purchased, the license will be assigned to your Rutgers Connect account, and you will gain the ability to make and receive calls from your Teams client. Questions or concerns about the purchasing and billing of this license feature should be directed to td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu.
When the purchase is made and the license is attached to the Rutgers Connect account, you will begin to see a dial pad in your Teams client. It will appear under the Calls app or tab in both mobile and desktop clients. Remember, once you have been given the softphone license, your desk phone will no longer operate, as the number is now being used by Teams. Questions about call connectivity, Teams operability, and/or calling functionality should be directed to the OIT Help Desk, which will work with the Connect Support team to provide support. 
Before You Begin 
1.	Ensure you have an active Rutgers NetID and you are signed into Microsoft Teams.
2.	Confirm that your Rutgers Connect account is enabled for Teams Calling. If you are unsure, please contact your department's IT support, who can check the status, and/or the voice services team at td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu. 
o	It may take up to 24 hours to see the new license features after purchasing. 
3.	Ensure you have a stable internet connection. 
A quick way to determine if you have the correct license is to locate the new dial pad in your Teams client, under the Calls tab.   
Checking Call Quality 
1.	During any Teams call or meeting, click More actions (?) on the toolbar.
2.	Select Call health from the dropdown.
3.	A panel will appear showing live data such as: 
o	Network strength
o	Audio/video device performance
o	Bitrate and packet loss
o	Local system status (CPU, memory, etc.) 
This is particularly useful if someone’s audio sounds choppy, video freezes, or there is a lag. It provides a quick insight into whether the issue is a network problem, a device issue, or something else. 
Certified Devices & Hardware 
You can sign into Teams on a desktop or laptop and use the native calling interface with a wired USB or certified Bluetooth headset. On mobile devices, the Teams mobile app allows you to make and receive calls using your Rutgers phone number, utilizing standard Teams app controls. On Teams-certified desk phones, you get a standalone Teams endpoint experience that's ideal for shared office spaces or where traditional desk phones remain preferred. Certified Teams Rooms hardware and peripherals enhance meeting room calling and conferencing, though most Teams softphones don’t require these specifically.
Interface on desktop 
 Error! Filename not specified. 
Interface on mobile
 Error! Filename not specified.     Error! Filename not specified.  
Making a Call 
1.	Open Microsoft Teams on your computer or mobile device.
2.	Select Calls from the left-hand navigation bar.  
o	If you don’t see the dial pad, you may not be provisioned for Teams Calling. Contact the software portal team if you’ve already made a purchase for this license and do not see the dial pad. 
3.	In the dial pad that appears, you can,  
o	Type the phone number you wish to call and press Call.
o	Search for a name or contact in the search bar and select the call icon next to your name.
4.	Your call will start, and you can manage it using the on-screen controls (mute, keypad, hold, transfer, etc.). 
Receiving a Call 
1.	When someone calls your Rutgers number, Teams will ring on all your signed-in devices (desktop, laptop, or mobile).
2.	Click Accept to answer or Decline to send it to voicemail. 
Checking Voicemail 
Voicemail moves over from Cisco to Teams once the Teams softphone license has been purchased and enabled on a Rutgers Connect account. Remember, calls will stop ringing on the desk phone once the license has been purchased and enabled. 
You can receive voicemail messages directly within the Teams app, whether on your desktop or mobile device. You will also receive a copy of the voicemail in an email to your Rutgers Connect account. 
1.	Go to the Calls tab in the Teams client. 
2.	Select the Voicemail tab to see and listen to messages. 
Voicemail transcription is available, making it easy to read missed messages. Notifications are sent instantly for new messages. You can customize greetings and manage voicemail settings under Settings > Calls > Configure Voicemail. 
If you are forwarding all desk calls to a personal cell phone number, the voicemail will be generated on the device that is receiving those forwarded calls.  
International Calling 
With the Teams softphone, you can make outbound international calls directly from the Teams client across supported countries and regions. Calls are routed securely through Rutgers’ existing voice infrastructure and Microsoft’s cloud-based calling services. 
Rates for international calls vary by destination. Contact Voice Services at td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu for details or restrictions. 
Tips for Best Call Quality
•	Use a wired headset or Teams-certified USB/Bluetooth device for clear audio.
•	Ensure you have a stable internet connection, wired preferred.
•	Avoid speakerphones unless necessary. It can introduce echo or feedback, especially in shared spaces.
•	Close background applications, such as video streaming services. Large downloads can consume significant bandwidth and negatively impact call quality. 
•	Try minimizing other internet activity during calls. Streaming, large uploads, or gaming can bog down the connection.
•	Use the Call Health dashboard: During a call, click the More actions (?) > Call Health to monitor your connection, device status, and real-time diagnostics.
•	You can also adjust Teams device settings by going to Settings > Devices in Teams to select and test your preferred mic, speaker, and camera. 
If you experience persistent call quality issues, please note the time and call details, obtain an example call that the IT teams can reference, and include information from the Call Quality Dashboard. Then, contact the OIT Help Desk. 
Options for Multiple Numbers in Teams 
A standard Teams Phone license allows one direct phone number per you. There are ways to support it, but phone masking and multiple numbers are not natively supported when purchasing the softphone license. If you are requesting multiple phone numbers to be tied to the same softphone license, please contact td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu with your request prior to purchasing a license to discuss options.  
Emergency Calling Behavior 
Teams softphones are configured to support location-based emergency calling to 911. Location information is tied to the Teams client settings, so be sure to update your location information in your Teams client once the license is purchased. You can also check your emergency location below the dial pad in the Calls tab.  
Teams will reuse saved locations when you reconnect to the same network. In the Calls tab underneath your phone number, there is a section under your listed number that includes your current emergency location. Ensure that the correct location is set; you may need to adjust your machine's location settings.  
Enable Location Services on Your Device 
Windows
1.	Go to Start > Settings > Privacy & Security > Location.
2.	Turn on Let apps access your location.
3.	Ensure Microsoft Teams is listed and enabled under desktop apps 
macOS
1.	Open System Preferences > Security & Privacy > Privacy.
2.	Unlock settings and go to Location Services.
3.	Check the box for Microsoft Teams Helper (GPU).
Open Teams and Access Emergency Location Settings 
1.	Launch Microsoft Teams.
2.	Click the three dots next to your profile picture (top right).
3.	Select Settings.
4.	Go to the Calls section.
5.	Scroll down to find Emergency Location. 
Add or Update Your Emergency Address 
1.	Under Current Emergency Location, click the dropdown.
2.	Choose Add or Reset.
3.	Enter your full address manually (use correct punctuation and spacing). 
o	Example: 902 East Main Street, Anytown, Florida, 33801, US
o	Avoid abbreviations like 902 E Main St Anytown FL 33801 US
4.	Confirm and Save the address.
Microsoft will attempt to best-guess your emergency location if no location has been specified or verified. It’s important to verify your emergency address within the Teams client to avoid complications.  
Phone Number Masking 
There is limited support for phone number masking due to complications with combining two different systems. Though masking is not enabled by default for Teams softphones, you can submit your request, use case, and requirements to td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu for review.  
FAQs 
•	What is a Teams softphone and how does it work?
•	Do I need to keep Teams running to receive calls? 
•	Can I use Teams softphone on mobile devices?
•	How do I make a call using Teams softphone?
•	Can I transfer or forward calls?
•	Can I add multiple people to a call? 
•	Is voicemail available? 
•	Can I mask my phone number during calls?
•	Is Teams softphone secure for sensitive conversations?
•	Why can’t I receive calls on Teams?
•	How do I find my Teams softphone number?
•	Can I use my softphone number for MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication)?
•	Can I switch between devices during a call?
•	Is there a difference in functionality between desktop and mobile apps?
•	How long is call history retained in Teams?
•	Does chat during a call get saved?
•	Will frequently contacted people show up in search?
What is a Teams softphone and how does it work?
A softphone in Teams allows you to make and receive calls over the internet using the Teams app, similar to a traditional phone but without physical hardware. 
Do I need to keep Teams running to receive calls? 
Yes, the Teams app must be logged into and connected to the internet to receive softphone calls. Make sure your mobile Teams application is set to run in the background and that you are logged into your Teams desktop applications to ensure call delivery.  
Can I use Teams softphone on mobile devices?
Yes. Teams has a mobile app that works on iOS and Android, and calls can be made or received via the mobile app. Make sure you are using the Teams application from the Company Portal application on your registered mobile device.  
How do I make a call using Teams softphone?
Open your Teams client and use the dial pad in the Calls tab, or start a call from a chat or contact. 
Can I transfer or forward calls?
Yes, you can transfer calls, record calls, put calls on-hold and transfer between calls seamlessly. You can also set up call forwarding in your Teams settings.  
Can I add multiple people to a call? 
Yes, you can initiate group calls or add participants during a call.  
Is voicemail available? 
Teams includes cloud-based voicemail with transcription. A copy of the voicemail will live in your Teams client under the “Calls” section, and a copy should be delivered to your Rutgers Connect mailbox. You can record greetings, adjust your “send to voicemail” settings, and check past messages in the Teams client.  
Can I mask my phone number during calls?
you can request phone masking from the Rutgers Voice Services team, as masking is not natively included with the Teams softphone license. To get started, submit your request to <td-voice@oit.rutgers.edu>. 
Is Teams softphone secure for sensitive conversations?
Yes, Teams uses enterprise-grade encryption and supports compliance features like E911. 
Why can’t I receive calls on Teams?
Check your internet connection, ensure Teams is running, and verify your phone number assignment and license purchase.  
How do I find my Teams softphone number?
Your number is typically listed in the Calls tab in your Teams client, or can be provided by the voice services team.  
Can I use my softphone number for MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication)?
Though it is possible, we strongly recommend NOT adding the Teams softphone number to your MFA devices as it is less secure than standard push notifications.  
Can I switch between devices during a call?
Yes, Teams supports seamless transitions between desktop and mobile apps. 
Is there a difference in functionality between desktop and mobile apps?
Some advanced features (like call parking or delegation) may be easier to manage on desktop. 
How long is call history retained in Teams?
Typically, call history is visible for 30 to 45 days. 
Does chat during a call get saved?
Yes, chat activity during calls is stored in your mailbox and follows retention policies. 
Will frequently contacted people show up in search?
Yes, Teams suggests contacts based on collaboration history.

body:
What new meeting options are available in Microsoft Teams?
The Rutgers Connect M365 tenant now offers two new Microsoft Teams meeting styles – Webinars and Town Halls. These new meeting styles are an extension of the existing Microsoft Teams meetings that Rutgers already supports, including 1-1 calling, ad?hoc meetings, and traditional scheduled meetings. Teams' webinars and Town Halls are unique; each meeting style comes with different capabilities available to all Rutgers faculty, staff, guests, and students who use Microsoft Teams.  
To identify which meeting style best suits users' needs, please refer to Microsoft's article comparing meetings, webinars, and town halls. 
Locating the new meeting options in Microsoft Teams
1.	Open Microsoft Teams.
2.	Go to Calendar > New Event. 

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Open the drop-down menu to view the available meeting types.

Error! Filename not specified.
If the Webinar or Town Hall options are missing, check both the desktop and web clients to confirm they are unavailable. Ensure you are signed in to the correct Teams account, and try restarting or signing out and then signing back in. If the options still do not appear, contact help@oit.rutgers.edu for assistance.
For more information about using Meetings, Webinars, and Town Halls in Microsoft Teams, please refer to Microsoft's meeting overview guide.
Deciding between a Webinar and a Town Hall in Microsoft Teams
Webinars are best suited when: 
•	The event is a structured, presenter?led session for a moderate?sized audience (up to 1,000 attendees).
•	The format includes both presentations and interactive elements, such as polls, Q&A sessions, or moderated discussions.
•	Attendee information must be collected in advance through registration, and access needs to be controlled.
•	A more formal environment is required than a standard Teams meeting, but with less production complexity than a town hall.
•	Post-event reporting, engagement metrics, and follow-up capabilities are necessary.
•	A familiar meeting interface is preferred for presenters and attendees, with optional branding or registration customization.
Town Halls are best suited when: 
•	The event is intended for a large audience (10,000+ attendees).
•	The experience is primarily consumption?focused, with attendees watching or listening rather than actively participating.
•	A polished, production?style presentation is desired, including layout control, presenter transitions, and branding.
•	An extended runtime (up to 30 hours) is required for continuous coverage or multi?segment sessions.
•	Attendee audio, video, or open chat is not required, and interaction will occur through Q&A or other moderated engagement. 
See Webinars in Microsoft Teams for further guidance on webinars and Town Halls in Microsoft Teams for additional information about town halls.

title: Teams What is Microsoft Teams
body:
Microsoft Teams is a collaboration tool that is part of the Office 365 suite of services. Teams enables remote or dispersed groups to work together and collaborate through a common workspace. Features such as team chat, one-on-one chat, document collaboration, and more exist to streamline collaboration. Teams is integrated with a variety of other Office 365 services, including OneDrive, OneNote, Planner, Exchange, and SharePoint.
It brings your team’s conversations, meetings, storage, files, application integration, and notes together into a single place for open and seamless collaboration.
Learn more in the video What is Microsoft Teams?
What can I do with Teams?
Teams makes communicating one-on-one and with groups a snap. Teams is built on top of Office 365 Groups in Rutgers Connect and provides group members with an option for real-time collaboration using a chat-based workspace. Chats are kept for easy searching, and the experience is customizable so that you can follow the discussion channels that interest you and hide those that do not. Teams will allow you to be more agile and spontaneous in your communication, including impromptu meetings with your group members, whereas groups are used more for occasional communication through conversations.
It’s also a great resource for accessing your group’s files and communications in one place. Instead of navigating from your group’s mailbox to its OneDrive, then to the group’s OneNote and SharePoint site, you can view it all in a single location. Teams allows you to integrate a variety of Office 365 applications that you or your group may use, while making it easier to open a discussion or reference files.
How do I transition to Teams?
With Teams, you can engage in more real-time collaboration, such as editing a document simultaneously with all your group members. You also get chat, forum, and email archives in a more streamlined interface, utilizing chat-based discussion channels. You can instantly meet within Teams with one or more members of your group. If you have a site with files that you’d like to migrate, OneDrive offers unlimited storage for groups.
Consider switching to using Teams for your weekly status meetings or to enhance your hiring process by gathering feedback on candidates.

title: Teams FAQ How can I use Teams for real-time collaboration?
body:
Keeping everyone in your group informed can be challenging, but Teams allows you to create channels of chat-based discussion on the topics important to your group. You can do everything from brainstorm ideas for a new building design to conducting an informal poll on where to go for lunch. You can choose which tabs appear within each channel so that everyone can see important shared content like project specifications or links to Office documents like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Need to get immediate feedback on a project idea? With Teams, you can hold an online Skype-based meeting instantly with all members of your group or have a private meeting with your manager. While you could use Skype for Business as well, the conversations and meetings are not saved in a single, organized location. Teams lets you keep your conversations and meetings within the context of your discussion channels for easy reference when you need it.
For more information about communication and collaboration within Microsoft Teams, please visit Team and channel topics FAQ on Microsoft Support.

title: Teams FAQ How does integration with your existing applications work in Teams?
body:
Microsoft Teams is designed to work seamlessly with both Microsoft 365 applications and a wide range of third-party tools, helping organizations enhance productivity without disrupting their existing workflows. Its integration capabilities allow you to bring the applications your teams already use directly into the Teams environment. Teams enables integration through the use of connectors and apps that can be added to channels. These connectors make it possible to receive real-time updates and notifications from external systems like project management platforms, customer support tools, bug-tracking software, and analytics dashboards—all within the context of your ongoing team discussions. 

Microsoft Teams acts as a central hub that connects your people, content, and tools by integrating with the applications you already depend on. Whether you’re enhancing communication with third-party services, streamlining document collaboration through SharePoint, or building custom extensions to support your processes, Teams enables a more unified and productive digital workplace.

title: Teams FAQ What is Teams?
body:
Microsoft Teams is a chat-based collaboration tool that is part of the Office 365 suite of services. Teams enables remote, global and dispersed teams to work together and collaborate through a common workspace, team chat, one-on-one chat, document collaboration and more.
Teams is integrated with a variety of other Office 365 services, including Skype, Yammer, Exchange, and SharePoint. It’s a messaging app that brings your team’s conversations, meetings, files, and notes together into a single place for open and seamless collaboration, where the latest updates can be accessed by everyone on the team. It’s a place for teamwork to happen in the open.
Why should you use it? It makes communicating one-on-one and with groups a snap. Collaboration happens in real time. All your stuff is there for everyone to help work on. Further information regarding Microsoft Teams at Rutgers can be found on the Rutgers IT site for Microsoft Teams.

title: Teams FAQ What is the knowledge base within Teams?
body: Because all of the chats within Teams are searchable, you can gather useful knowledge on any issues within your group. These issues could be turned into process and guideline documentation. An example of this could be a service unit that gets a lot of student foot traffic. The questions asked by students and the answers could be initially obtained via discussions in a chat channel, but later could be turned into a Wiki tab for new employees.

title: Teams FAQ What should I be aware of with Teams?
body:
There are several things to consider when adding Teams to your groups. Guest access is available; however, there are some limitations. Visit Microsoft's support page for additional information on guest access.
If you have an existing OneNote notebook in your group, it will not be visible from within Teams. You can only create new sections within Teams and view existing and new sections of your notebook in the OneNote app directly or in the notebook of your group. You can access Teams on a variety of platforms, but some browsers, such as Firefox or Chrome, may provide a better experience.

title: Teams FAQ Why should I use Teams?
body:
Microsoft Teams is a communication and collaboration platform developed by Microsoft as part of the Microsoft 365 suite. It is designed to bring people, content, and tools together in one place, making it easier to collaborate efficiently whether you're in the same office or working remotely. 

Teams integrates chat, video meetings, file storage, and app integration, making it a hub for teamwork. One of the key advantages is that it brings together different modes of communication into a single platform. You can move seamlessly between sending a quick message, starting a video call, or collaborating on a shared document without needing to switch tools. Security and compliance are built into the platform. Teams follows enterprise-grade security protocols and supports a range of compliance standards, including data loss prevention and information governance. This ensures that organizations can maintain control over sensitive information while still enabling productive collaboration.
Microsoft Teams serves as a centralized platform that brings together communication, collaboration, and productivity tools in a way that aligns with the needs of modern workplaces. By combining chat, meetings, file sharing, and app integrations in one secure and scalable environment, it helps teams stay connected, organized, and efficient, no matter the location.

title: Early Employee NetID for faculty and staff
body:
Any faculty member, full-time staff member, or graduate assistant whose information has been entered into the payroll system ("on-boarded") and approved by University Human Resources can activate a NetID. If the faculty/staff member needs an active NetID before the entry is approved, the departmental payroll person can apply for an Early Employee NetID.
Please note the following before submitting a request:
•	Please do everything possible to complete the HR onboarding process before requesting Early Employee NetID assistance.
•	It is expected that you will work with the department and/or HR to resolve any outstanding issues within 30 days.
•	The Early Employee NetID process cannot accommodate new employees who do not yet have a Social Security Number (SSN).
•	Please verify the exact spelling of the new employee's first and last name, personal email address, SSN, and date of birth. Errors and inaccuracies may lead to data conflicts and consistency issues upon completion of onboarding.
Regarding onboarding:
•	It is recommended that new employees be onboarded as soon as possible and well in advance of their start date. Onboarding can be performed several months before the start date.

•	The I-9 may be completed several months in advance of an employee's start date and MUST be completed within 3 days of the employee's first day of work. HR will approve a hire request before the I-9 is completed.
How the service might be used
An Early Employee NetID can be temporarily used just as a NetID to access many of the electronic services available to you at Rutgers.
How to request this service

Additional assistance
For assistance, please contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: How to authorize Foundation users
body:
This article is intended for service owners who would like to configure a service to allow access to Rutgers Foundation staff.
•	Provisioning and Deprovisioning
•	Identifying Foundation users
•	LDAP Attributes
•	AD Attributes
•	SSO Integration
Provisioning and Deprovisioning
Foundation users are provisioned/de-provisioned in the IdM systems in two ways.
Via the Daily PeopleSoft feed.
Users are provisioned with the STAFF role. Subsequent updates and termination to the staff role is maintained within the HR system.
Via the IdM Guest System.
These type of Foundation users are generally provisioned with a GUEST role by an external HR system and entered manually by the Foundation's Guest admins in the IdM system. Subsequent updates and termination are handled by the designated Foundation Guest admins.
Identifying Foundation users
Services that consume Foundation authorization information from a relational database can identify Foundation users based on the following Department/organization and Org/Dept codes.
Foundation org codes
ORGANIZATION	ORG_CODE
ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT	10011
ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - CMD	10012
ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - NWK	10013
RUTGERS UNIVERSITY FOUNDATION	10010
LDAP Attributes
For services that consume Foundation authorization information from the IdM LDAP, the following attributes in LDAP can be used to identify Foundation users.
•	employeetype: This attribute can have any of the following values (‘STAFF’,’GUEST’)
•	rutgerseduorganizationcode: This attribute can have any of the following codes ('10010','10011', '10012', '10013')
•	rutgersedustaffdepartment: this attribute will have any of the following organization/Department names: 
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - CMD
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - NWK
o	RUTGERS UNIVERSITY FOUNDATION
An example of a search:
'(&(uid=xyz)(|(rutgersEduOrganizationCode=10010)(rutgersEduOrganizationCode=10011)(rutgersEduOrganizationCode=10012)(rutgersEduOrganizationCode=10013)))'
AD Attributes
For services that consume Foundation authorization information from the Enterprise Active Directory (RAD), the following attributes in AD can be used to identify Foundation users.
•	businesscategory: This attribute can have any of the following values (‘STAFF’,’GUEST’)
•	departmentnumber: This attribute can have any of the following codes ('10010','10011', '10012', '10013')
•	department: this attribute will have any of the following organization/Department names: 
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - CMD
o	ALUMNI ENGAGEMENT - NWK
o	RUTGERS UNIVERSITY FOUNDATION
•	memberof: This attribute will have the following group membership values (CN=ru-Rutgers-University-Foundation-Staff,OU=Rutgers-University-Foundation,OU=departments,OU=Groups,DC=rad,DC=rutgers,DC=edu) or (CN=ru-Rutgers-University-Foundation-Guest,OU=Rutgers-University-Foundation,OU=departments,OU=Groups,DC=rad,DC=rutgers,DC=edu)
An example of a search:
'(&(samaccountname=xyz)(|( departmentnumber=10010)( departmentnumber=10011)( departmentnumber=10012)( departmentnumber=10013)))
SSO Integration
For services that would like to consume Foundation authorization information via the SSO Integration, if your service is integrated with one of the IdM SSO systems (CAS or Shibboleth). IdM can pass to your service, along with the NetID of the users', a group membership for the foundation. If you would like to add this to your current integration, please reach out to the idm_operations@email.rutgers.edu for further assistance.

title: When do I no longer have an 'active student role' at Rutgers?
body:
Access to various services at the university is related to your “role” at the university. For students, the last semester that you are registered for classes determines when you no longer have an "active student role" which refers to your affiliation with Rutgers and how it is managed within information technology and other systems. 
When do you no longer have an active student role? 
Your status as a student is based on the last semester that you took classes.
Note that if you are still associated with the University in another capacity, such as faculty or staff, you maintain access to services in accordance with those roles. 
Fall semester
If you are not registered for Spring classes after the Fall semester, then by mid-January you will no longer have an active student role at Rutgers.
Winter session
If you are not registered for Spring classes after taking classes during the Winter session, then on January 31, you will no longer have an active student role at Rutgers. 
Spring semester
If you are not registered for Fall classes after the Spring semester, then by mid-August you will no longer have an active student role at Rutgers. 
Summer session
If you are not registered for Fall classes after taking classes during the Summer session, then on August 31, you will no longer have an active student role at Rutgers. 
Transitioning to Alumni
After graduating, former students are considered alumni and receive access to Rutgers' services in accordance with this new affiliation. This happens after the Registrar initiates a process showing that a student actually graduated. This may take a month or two after the actual graduation date. 
May graduates typically maintain their active student roles until they officially transition to being Alumni. 
December graduates may briefly not have an active student role before getting their Alumni status, since the student role is removed in mid-January, and graduation information may not necessarily be entered by then.  
Alumni will never lose this affiliation with Rutgers.
Withdrawing from the University
If you stop taking classes at the University without officially graduating, you will not be considered an Alumni. Depending on your withdrawal date, you may lose your active student role shortly after withdrawing, or in accordance with the timeline noted above. Afterward, you will have no active affiliation with Rutgers unless you re-enroll as a student or are eligible for another, such as being a faculty or staff member.

title: and Connectivity Management Wi-Fi troubleshooting
body:
If you are experiencing wireless connection or reception problems, try one or all of these fixes:
1.	Restart your device. Simply turn your Wi-Fi off and then on and/or restart your computer or device to see if it solves the problem.
2.	Make sure you are connecting to the right network. You should connect to the RUWireless Secure network if you're affiliated with Rutgers. If you are a guest, you should be connected to the RUWireless network. 
3.	If you are using an Apple device, it may automatically connect to an inappropriate wireless network, resulting in slower performance. To fix this issue, erase ALL (both Rutgers and personal) existing wireless network configurations from your device and start fresh with just the RUWireless Secure network. To do so on an iOS device, open Settings on your device then select General > Reset > Reset Network Settings, then follow these instructions to configure your iOS device to connect to RUWireless Secure.
4.	Revert a recent operating system update. If you recently updated your computer or device's operating system (OS) and are experiencing connectivity or speed issues, you may want to consider reverting to the previous OS and wait until an updated version of the new OS is released.
Other things to try
1.	Confirm that you have followed the correct steps to configure RUWireless Secure access for your device.
2.	Check to make sure that Wi-Fi/wireless is turned on for your laptop or device and that you are connected to RUWireless Secure. If not, you are probably experiencing slow cell service and should contact your service provider (e.g., Verizon, AT&T, etc.) if the issue persists.
3.	Make sure that you are logging in with a current NetID and password. An old password may be saved on your device if you changed it recently.
4.	Make sure you are in an official Rutgers building that would have RUWireless Secure provided. 
5.	Move your computer/device a few feet in any direction. Move away from large metal or masonry obstructions (shelves, walls, etc.).
6.	Confirm that your computer or device's clock is displaying the correct time and time zone; if not, update them to the correct time and time zone.
7.	Test your NetID and password to see if it is working properly by logging into MyRutgers. If not, try following the steps to reset your NetID password. 
Advanced Troubleshooting
If you feel comfortable with more advanced technical troubleshooting, you may wish to try the following:
1.	Update your WLAN (wireless card) drivers.
2.	If using Microsoft Windows, flush the DNS cache. To do so, select Start > Run, type cmd. Then in the command prompt type ipconfig/flushdns. When complete, try reconnecting to RUWireless Secure.
3.	If you have firewall, antivirus, or P2P (peer to peer) software enabled or are using non-Windows wireless connection applications, try to disable this/these applications and try connecting again. If you can connect, one of those software applications is likely causing the issue. If your antivirus program appears to be the root of the issue, consider uninstalling it and switching to the available Rutgers licensed anti-virus software. If not, be sure to immediately re-enable any antivirus software you temporarily disabled.
Still having issues?
If none of the above steps resolve the issue, or you need assistance with any of them, contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: Accounts How do I request a NoID account?
body:
NOID, NO IDentity accounts have a username and password just to access restricted mail services. Basically, a NOID user exists solely to access and use some or all of our MailRelay (MR) Services.
 Some common reasons for a NOID account
•	Web applications, housed on or off RU IP space
•	Your service is hosted on a non-static IP
•	For SMTP-auth, username and password for mail sending (for some dumb printers/scanners/fax machines, etc)
•	Your service needs mail reading services
•	Your service needs mail to be independent of the server that hosts it
For each and every NOID account request, answer all the questions:
•	The requester's contact info: 
o	Name
o	Email address
o	Phone number
o	Department (no acronyms)
•	Specify which type of NoID account you need. There are five types of NoID accounts, depending on whether you want POP3 or IMAP, and if you need sending/SMTP access:
o	noids = Send/Smtp only account (most common choice)
o	noidi = Imap only account
o	noidis = both Imap and Send/Smtp account
o	noidp = Pop3 only account
o	noidps = both Pop3 and Send/Smtp account
•	Provide a brief description of the departmental use (info to help us pick your NOID username [aka $NOID_USER])
•	Provide a brief description of the service that requires the account (e.g., "ticketing system for local problem tracking").
NOTE: Does that service process PHI (Protected Health Information) or University Restricted data, including NPPI (Non-Public Personal Information)? See the Data Classification Guide if you are unsure whether the mail data is in either category. We need a clear statement for each data type. For example, "No, my service handles neither PHI nor NPPI data"
or "My service handles NPPI data, but not PHI data."
•	Does your entity involve processing PHI (yes/no)?
•	Will your email contain any PHI or University Restricted data info (yes/no)? 
o	If yes, what is the nature of the PHI/University Restricted Data in the email?
•	If there are any existing email addresses associated with the
service, please note them. (example: help@rutgers.edu)
•	If needed, what IP address will be used to access the Inbox for the NoID account?
(This is only required for IMAP or POP type NOID requests)
•	If needed, which hostname (s) will access the Inbox in question?
(This is only required for IMAP or POP type NOID requests, aka your initial Access Control List)
•	If you're sending an email via the NoID account, what is the "FROM" address you will be using?
"FROM" REMINDER: Always use a FROM address that is a real working address that can receive mail. We are concerned about you getting error/bounce messages and other internal negative mail tagging. Your FROM address needs to be valid $FROM@$SOMETHING.rutgers.edu or $FROM@rutgers.edu for mail to work correctly, the CAT tool can confirm if the FROM address is valid. If you need help with any of this, contact your local IT Delegated Admin or the OIT Help Desk.

Always ensure your FROM is valid when using our MailRelayServices (MRS) for any current or future systems. We will begin the NOID approval review and creation process after we receive all the information requested above.
Once a NoID account has been approved, you will receive a link to a secure website containing the following information, which can be used to configure your device:
•	Account name: e.g., “deptacct”
•	Account password: e.g., “CAPS123lower”

title: Benefits of Privileged Access Management (PAM)
body:
Privilege Access Management (PAM) safeguards access to critical systems and data, including student information systems (SIS), research data repositories, administrative records, and financial systems. PAM solution offers a comprehensive suite of tools to prevent unauthorized access and mitigate risks associated with privileged accounts.
•	Protecting Sensitive Data: Implementing a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution enables the management of access to the Rutgers student information system, which houses sensitive information, including grades, financial aid details, and personal identifiers. This approach not only upholds data integrity but also ensures compliance with various regulatory standards, such as FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and GDPR, safeguarding against unauthorized access and data breaches.
•	Securing Research Data: Rutgers University's cutting-edge research often involves confidential and proprietary information. Implementing Privileged Access Management (PAM) can protect research data from potential intellectual property theft, ensuring that only authorized researchers and staff can access specific data sets.
•	Enhancing IT Infrastructure Security: Rutgers University’s complex IT infrastructures can leverage Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions to manage and monitor privileged access across various systems and platforms, from legacy systems to cloud-based services. This can significantly reduce the attack surface and thwart potential cyber threats.

title: Identifying Accounts for Privileged Access Management (PAM) Implementation
body:
To leverage PAM solutions effectively, it's crucial to identify and prioritize accounts that require protection. These typically include:
•	Accounts with access to student and faculty personal information.
•	Accounts authorized to access regulated data to ensure compliance with relevant regulations, including FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and GDPR.
•	Administrative accounts with high-level access to financial and operational systems.
•	Research accounts holding sensitive data about ongoing projects.
•	Vendor and third-party accounts with access to institutional IT systems.

title: The strategic implementation of Privileged Access Management (PAM)
body:
OIT has a service contract with CyberArk as the primary tool for our PAM implementation. 
OIT embarked on a multi-year project to improve the security of privileged accounts. The following are some of the important steps we will be taking to achieve this goal: 
•	Assessment, Discovery and Planning: Conduct a comprehensive review of the current security posture and privileged account usage. Identify systems and data critical to the institution's mission that require enhanced protection.
•	Stakeholder Engagement: Engage with stakeholders across the institution, including faculty, IT staff, and administration, to align on the importance of Privileged Access Management (PAM) and gather input on specific needs and concerns.
•	Tailored Implementation: Develop an implementation plan considering the institution's unique structure and needs. This plan may involve phased rollouts, starting with the most sensitive systems.
•	Training and Awareness: Implement training programs to educate staff and students about the importance of privileged access security and ensure that users understand their roles in maintaining the security of the systems they access.
•	Continuous Review and Adaptation: Establish ongoing monitoring and review processes to ensure the Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution remains effective against evolving threats. Regularly update policies and practices to reflect changes in the institutional environment and threat landscape.
In the initial phase of this endeavor, which began in 2024, the focus was on applying PAM controls to specific Rutgers Enterprise Active Directory (RAD)- enabled services within OIT, with the goal of expanding it to other units and endpoints (UNIX, Database, Cloud, Network, DevOps, etc.).
By focusing on the strategic implementation of Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions, Rutgers University can significantly enhance the security of its privileged accounts, protecting against unauthorized access and potential cyber threats. We look forward to working together to strengthen our institution's cybersecurity posture.

title: Support Changes to Print Spooler Authentication Level on PaperCut Print Servers
body:
The PaperCut Support team configured all PaperCut print servers to use a higher level of authentication when communicating with client computers. This change will enhance the security level of the underlying Windows print server configuration that the enterprise PaperCut system relies on, and will require that all Windows and macOS client computers that print via PaperCut have received recent security updates.
Detailed Overview
Microsoft released a knowledge base article in 2020 announcing details on new authentication settings and levels for the Print Spooler service. In this document, Microsoft announced that the increased security level offered by these changes would be put in place in phases:
•	January 12, 2021: Initial Deployment Phase: The added security levels would be in place and available after installing the January 2021 Microsoft security updates, but would be set to be disabled by default.
•	September 14, 2021: Enforcement Phase: The added security levels would be set to enabled by default after installing the September 2021 Microsoft security updates.
After testing the increased security level on various versions of Windows and macOS computers prior to September 2021, the PaperCut Support team found that macOS computers could no longer add or print to the shared printers on the PaperCut print servers. Therefore, this increased security level was manually disabled to make sure that printing continued to work for macOS clients.
The PaperCut Support group continued to monitor updates from Apple regarding the resolution of this issue for the macOS operating system. This issue has now been resolved on all macOS versions for which Apple still actively issues security updates. Therefore, the PaperCut Support group has enabled the increased security level for the Print Spooler service on the PaperCut print servers.
Technical Details for Client Operating Systems
This change will require that all Windows and macOS client computers have received recent security updates. It's recommended that each client system be upgraded with the most recent security update for its respective platform. title: Devices What is the Mail Relay Service?
body:
Technologies such as printers, routers, cloud vendors, and HVAC systems sometimes need to send email, but they generally cannot use Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail. In order to support these products, the Office of Information Technology (OIT) offers a portfolio of mail relay services. 
Access to these services comes via application. 
Commonly Accepted Usages 	Commonly Excluded Usages 
•	Networked printers (e.g. toner/paper notification email)
•	Switches/routers (e.g. operational email) 
•	Automated HVAC systems 
•	Emergency generators (e.g. fuel status email) 
•	Software performing “basic authentication” (i.e. authentication is not performed via OAuth or a similar modern protocol). This software is incompatible with Rutgers cloud email providers. 
•	Products that are unable to use a password when sending email. 	•	Individual email accounts/aliases 
•	Usage from individual computers that can be performed using Outlook, webmail, etc. 
•	Products not able to perform email encryption (e.g. SSL or TLS) 
•	Service to shared infrastructure; for example, to an outside vendor that cannot ensure exclusive Rutgers resources. 
•	Usage by non-Rutgers affiliates 
Software/applications running on dedicated servers, virtual appliances, and vendor-provided IT services will be considered on a case-by-case basis with consideration to the applicable policies and guidelines. The platform should be formally procured by Rutgers and use appropriate measures that ensure Rutgers IT resources are only provided for Rutgers related usage. To confirm compatibility, you are encouraged to engage OIT promptly whenever email integrations are required. 
Available Services
OIT currently offers four classes of mail relay service. The request process will guide you to a suggested offering. If you have an explicit service requirement, please note that during the request process. 
•	SMTP AUTH mail sending service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. Please note that this service requires the security of TLS or SSL encryption. Email may be sent as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address. 
•	IMAP or POP3 mail receiving service: A special NetID and password, allocated to your service and not any one person, is created for your request. A mailbox is created for that special NetID, which will receive email for retrieval (via IMAP or POP3) under the security of TLS encryption. Your Rutgers Connect domain administrator may create an alias, in Rutgers Connect, that will “hide” the special NetID for marketing purposes. (If the special NetID will only be used by automated processes, a marketing alias is not required.)
•	SMTP AUTH with IMAP or SMTP AUTH with POP3: If there is a requirement to both send and receive email, this offering is a combination of offerings #1 and #2.
•	IP-based mail sending service: The IP address of your University-affiliated device will be permitted to send email, using SMTP, as any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address. This is the only offering available for devices that cannot ensure the security of a Rutgers NetID and password — for example, devices that cannot support encryption. This offering is generally restricted to RUNet-connected devices.
Request Process
Mail relay privileges can be requested by the appropriate Administrative or Technical Contact for the device by logging into the request webtool: Request Mail Relay Access
Upon submitting a completed online application, the request will be assessed, and its status communicated via email. All accepted and rejected submissions will be acknowledged via email to the submitter. Rejected submissions may also include details on reasons for the rejection and corrective actions which must be taken prior to resubmission. 
Exclusions and Audits
Exemption from NetID authentication does not constitute exemption from the relevant University policies, guidelines, and technical standards. If a device is found in violation, mail relay permission may be denied and/or revoked. Generally, we will first attempt to remedy this situation with the contacts listed on the application. 
OIT reserves the right to conduct audits of devices with mail relay permission. Timely responses to OIT audits are mandatory for continued permission to utilize Rutgers services. 
If a device is excluded, OIT must receive verification that the conditions that led to the device’s exclusion have been corrected and verified prior to reinstatement. 
For more information on the standards of data protection required of authorized devices, please visit Information Security Cybersecurity Compliance Program.

•	Can I change my e-mail address that is used for receiving scanned documents via email?
•	I have already allowed PaperCut to save scanned documents to my OneDrive. Why have I received another email asking me to allow this access?
Who has access to Scan to OneDrive at the University?
While Scan to OneDrive will be listed as a scan option for all PaperCut users, only users who have access to OneDrive on Rutgers Connect will be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive. This includes:
•	
o	Students
o	Faculty
o	Staff
There are roles within the University that do not receive Rutgers Connect access by default but can be granted access with local IT approval. These roles include:
•	
o	Emeritus
o	Guest
Also, there are some roles within the University that are not granted Rutgers Connect access and, therefore, would not be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive. These include:
•	
o	Alumni
o	Retiree
Please note that a person can have multiple roles with the University, and if they are assigned at least one role that is granted Rutgers Connect access, they will be able to save scanned documents to OneDrive.  For example, someone who is an Alumni and a Staff member would be granted access to saved scanned documents to OneDrive via their Staff role.
How do I allow PaperCut to save scanned document files to my OneDrive?
The first time you scan to your OneDrive, you'll need to follow the instructions to allow Papercut access to your OneDrive. 
Where are scanned documents saved in OneDrive by default? Can this default location be changed?
The default location in your OneDrive is under My Files > Apps > Scans for PaperCut MF. This default location cannot be changed. However, you can move the scanned document file to any other folder once it has been saved to your OneDrive.
Can the filename of the scanned document be changed?
The filename of the scanned document can be changed during the scanning process while using the multi-function printer. If you tap the filename, a touchscreen keyboard should appear to let you edit the filename:
     Error! Filename not specified.

Please note that when saving scanned documents to OneDrive, you could experience issues if you happen to re-use the name of a scanned document that already exists in the destination.  If you still would like to change the name of the scanned document, here are some suggestions to avoid these issues:
•	
o	Leave the filename generated by PaperCut during the scan process, which contains a timestamp to help avoid duplicate names. The scanned document can be renamed once it arrives in your OneDrive.
o	Edit the filename, but leave the timestamp portion of the generated document name, guaranteeing that a file of the same name doesn't already exist in OneDrive.
Can I change the email address I use to receive scanned documents via email?
All emails sent from the PaperCut system will be sent to your netid@rutgers.edu email address. If you are unsure if your netid@rutgers.edu address delivers to Rutgers Connect or ScarletMail, go to the Manage Email Addresses page, and check the delivery location under Delivery Addresses for Personalized Email Addresses.
I have already allowed PaperCut to save scanned documents to my OneDrive. Why have I received another email asking me to allow this access?
If you haven't saved a scan to your OneDrive in the past 90 days, the authorization token created during the initial confirmation process will expire. You'll need to follow the instructions to allow PaperCut access to your OneDrive to create a new authorization.

OIT offers three wide-width printers (plotters) for poster printing.
Location
One is located in the College Ave Computer Center in the Academic Building on College Avenue, another is in the Allison Road Classroom Computing Lab on Busch, and an additional one is in the Loree Computing Lab on Cook/Douglass. Poster printers are not available on the Livingston campus. 
Cost
The cost for printing is $1.50 per square foot. For example, a 3ft x 2ft poster would cost $9.00. 
Supported File Types
You can use several software programs to print to the plotter, but Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Adobe applications are most commonly used. The plotters work with files that are .doc, .pdf, .ppt, or .tiff; however, .pdf is the recommended file type. 
Please ensure the size of the printed file is not too large. File sizes of 200MB or greater may cause issues where the print job will not appear when you go to get the print released. If the file size is large (exceeds 100MB), please try flattening the PDF using Adobe Photoshop or the images used within the poster. If the original PDF width and height don't match the sizes mentioned below in the Available Sizes section, please use Photoshop to resize the dimensions of the PDF. You can flatten or resize PDFs in Photoshop by doing the following:

8.	Resize, rotate, and adjust the pasted content as needed using Ctrl + T to enable transform mode.
9.	Press the checkmark icon in the top bar or Enter, to finalize the transformation.

Printing overview for Students, Faculty and Staff" "
Printing is available for Students, Faculty, and Staff at the Office of Information Technology computer labs. You may print to black-and-white or color printers from lab computers, wirelessly via personal devices on RUWirelessSecure, or through Virtual Computer Labs.
You must release the print jobs via the print release stations in each computer lab printing location in Rutgers–New Brunswick, Rutgers–Newark, and Rutgers–Camden. Your RUID card is required to release print jobs.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps Are there specific risks due to some of Google's servers being hosted in other countries?
body:
By law, some intellectual property should not be stored outside of the United States. Individuals handling sensitive materials are reminded not to share this information via email regardless of the email provider.
Ultimately, an email that is intended for a user within the U.S. can be easily forwarded.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps How does Google address privacy and security?
body:
Google is very concerned about the security and privacy of its users' data. Please see Google’s Privacy Policy.
Google provides information regarding how to stay safe online, how to manage your data, and the safety of your data on the web and on Google. Visit Google’s Safety Center for more information.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps How does ScarletMail handle spam and viruses?
body: Google filters for viruses and spam before delivering the message. For more information, please see Google’s information on spam filters.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps Is email a secure form of communication?
body:
Sensitive information should NEVER be sent through email. We advise against sending sensitive information via email for the following reasons:
•	Email could be intercepted and accessed by an unauthorized party
•	Email could be shared inappropriately by the recipient
•	Email could be compromised for as long as it is retained by you or the recipient
•	There are no retention controls over the recipient’s system
•	Accessing your email over an insecure network (i.e., Internet Cafe or open wireless network) can expose your user account information
•	Although encrypted connections can mitigate the risks of having ones’ authentication credentials compromised, email itself is still plain text when traveling between the sender and the recipient and can be easily intercepted
Regardless of the provider, email is not a secure method of communication. This applies to our current campus email systems as well as most third-party email providers.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps Some of my ScarletMail emails contain confidential material. How will you maintain email privacy?
body:
Confidential or sensitive information should NEVER be sent through email.
Google maintains Privacy Policies for each of its applications. For a complete list and access to each of these policies, please visit Google’s Privacy Center.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps What are the Policies or Terms of Service for the Google products and services I use?
body:
All of the products, applications, and services used in the ScarletApps at Rutgers environment are subject to the Rutgers University Acceptable Use Policy and Google’s Terms of Service for that product.
Individual products, applications, and services may have supplemental terms of service applied in addition to Google’s general Terms of Service. These supplemental terms of service can most often be found by selecting the link on the bottom of the page for that product under Terms and Policies.
If there is ever a conflict between Google’s Terms of Service and the Rutgers AUP, the Rutgers AUP takes precedent.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps What constitutes sensitive information in the context of electronic communications?
body: Sensitive information is information such as Social Security numbers, driver license numbers, credit card information, medical/health conditions, etc. None of this information should be sent via email, regardless of the email provider. As a general rule, privacy experts advise to consider whether it would be appropriate or desirable for the contents of the email to appear in a public forum (e.g., newspaper). Email operates as a postcard that can easily be read in transit and at the destination by unauthorized parties. It could be retained forever, or shared with unintended readers. For more information, please visit the Rutgers Information Classification Policy and Data Breach Management Policy.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps What is the ScarletMail name policy?
body:
Use your common first and last name. Impersonation is a serious issue. Pretending to be someone else could cause your profile to be deleted.
Follow Google's guide on how to change your Google account picture, name and other info.
Misrepresenting a user’s identity in any electronic communication is against Rutgers' Acceptable Use Policy.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps Who owns the intellectual property rights?
body: Although data will be stored by Google, Rutgers retains all intellectual property rights of its data.

title: and security FAQ for ScarletApps Will my personal information from ScarletApps be shared with anyone outside of Rutgers?
body: Please refer to Google’s Privacy Policy for more information.

Canvas External Tool Configuration
As an instructor for a First Day™/Inclusive Access course, you will need to add the First Day Course Materials link in Canvas so that students can opt out of the program, if they wish, during the opt-out period only. If the material is an eTextbook only, students can also access their titles at this link.

1.	Log in to Canvas with your instructor username and password and navigate to the course site that requires the First Day Course Materials link.
2.	Click Settings from the left-hand course navigation.
3.	Click the Navigation tab, and scroll down to the hidden items at the bottom of the list.
4.	Look for the First Day Course Materials in the list.
5.	Click and hold First Day Course Materials, then drag it up to the list of active navigation links, or select the three dots next to the tool and choose Enable.
6.	Click Save.
7.	The First Day Course Materials link will now be available in the left-hand navigation of your course. You may have to refresh your window to see it.
8.	Repeat these steps for any additional Canvas course sites that require the First Day Course Materials link.

To enhance your learning experience and provide affordable access to the right course material, this course is part of an inclusive access model called First Day™. title: & Textbooks Library Tutorials – An Introduction for Instructors
body:
Many college students arrive on campus without essential information skills, creating gaps between faculty expectations and student ability. Our tutorials help bring them up to speed in a convenient, easy-to-use format.
Table of Contents
•	What is this content? 
o	On-Demand Lessons
o	Master Courses
•	Who can use this content, and who is providing it?
•	When can I use the lessons in my course?
•	How will these skills help my students succeed?
•	Which Library Tutorial do I use?
•	Who do I contact for more information?
What is this content?
Our tutorials are high-quality, standards-driven learning objects designed to introduce students to the basics of locating, evaluating, and using information. They include video lessons as well as quizzes to assess understanding.
Tutorials let you focus precious classroom time on your course material rather than research skills. Your students can return to these activities for easy reference throughout the semester.
On-Demand Lessons
On-demand lessons for easy access to our most frequently requested topics:
•	Types of sources
•	Refining search results
•	How to read scholarly materials
•	Academic integrity
•	What is plagiarism?
•	Why citations matter
•	Citation style guides
•	Copyright
•	And more!
Master Courses
These tutorials provide comprehensive deep-dives that can be embedded directly into Canvas:
•	Communication, for increasing the effectiveness of oral, written, and visual communication
•	Critical Thinking, for developing the ability to evaluate, analyze, and synthesize information
•	Health Science, for building skills to locate health resources, apply appropriate research methods, and participate in evidence-based practice
•	Information Literacy, for building skills to locate, cite, manage, and ethically use information
The lessons are mapped to instructional standards, including the Association of American Colleges and Universities (AAC&U VALUE) Rubrics for Information and Literacy and others, the Association of College and Research Libraries (ACRL) Framework for Information Literacy, and the ACRL Visual Literacy Standards.
Who can use this content, and who is providing it?
The Scholarly Information Tutorials content is provided by the Rutgers University Libraries through licenses with Weave and Credo Reference, two leading library instruction providers, for use by Rutgers University instructors on all campuses.
When can I use the lessons in my course?
Tutorials are available as both on-demand lessons that can be accessed on the Libraries’ website and master courses that can be embedded directly into Canvas.
•	As a flipped classroom or to prepare for specialized library instruction: Assigning students to view a video or work through a lesson before they attend a specialized library instruction class can encourage more productive class time.
•	At various points during a scaffolded assignment: Rather than introducing students to multiple concepts at once, you may want to deploy them to students at various points in their process. If you have scaffolded an assignment, with milestones such as a research question, topic choice, working thesis, or annotated bibliography, consider having students review individual lessons as they begin that particular component of the assignment. Quizzes associated with many of the lessons will help you assess their understanding of a particular aspect of research or information literacy concepts.
•	In a first-year or transition class: Many of the lessons can help students appreciate the big-picture importance of information literacy, strong research and evaluation, and communication skills. You may want to select these lessons at the beginning of a unit or as one component of their success in a first-year experience course.
•	At the beginning of a major project: Students may be overwhelmed at the beginning of a major project and not know where to get started. The multimedia lessons cover a wide range of topics essential to success in research, from choosing a topic to evaluating sources.
•	At the point of need: Your students may be working on an assignment independently, but you want them to have access to resources that can help them throughout the research process as needed, such as a tutorial on database searching when they are in the process of finding sources, or a video about the citation style they need to use.
How will these skills help my students succeed?
•	Getting Started with Research – Introduce your students to the basics of conducting research, from selecting appropriate sources to refining search results.
•	Presenting Research and Data – Empower students to communicate their findings effectively in papers and presentations.
•	Academic Integrity – Help your students use information ethically by understanding plagiarism and copyright.
•	Writing and Citing – Step-by-step guides to citing in AMA, APA, Chicago, and MLA styles.
Research has found that students who receive information literacy instruction have higher retention rates and GPAs, as well as successfully complete more credit hours per year than peers who did not receive such instruction (Greater Western Library Alliance, “The Impact of Information Literacy Instruction on Student Success: A Multi-Institutional Investigation and Analysis,” 2017).
Library tutorials help prepare students with the skills they need to successfully evaluate information both inside and outside the classroom.
Which Library Tutorial do I use?
The tutorials are ideal for undergraduate students who need an introduction to the foundations of scholarly research or for anyone who wants to brush up on the key skills needed to successfully accomplish any research-based project.
Your library liaison can help you select the most relevant lessons for your course.
Who do I contact for more information?
For questions about the Library Tutorials content or to supplement the online instruction, please contact the Rutgers Libraries Instructional Support Team.

•	Library Tutorials in Canvas

title: & Textbooks Library Tutorials – Instructor Quick Start Guide
body:
The following are items to do or consider doing when setting up a Library Tutorial course for use:
•	Each assignment (e.g., lesson, quiz, activity) in the course is unpublished (i.e., in a draft state). Once you have imported the course, please review all the content and publish the assignments that you would like your students to see.
•	Each assignment has been set up with 0 points. To make an assignment required or to include quiz assessments in your course grade, you will need to change the points and due date. If you would like to set the point value and make other edits, such as setting due dates and assignment availability, edit the assignment. You may change the assignment group according to your course assignment breakdown as described in your syllabus.
•	You are encouraged to move the assignments to the appropriate modules in your course so that they work cohesively with your topics. Change the order of the assignments to align with your syllabus.
•	There are four citation styles addressed in the Information Literacy course. If only certain styles are appropriate for your discipline, you are free to select and publish the assignments for just those styles if you wish.
It is recommended that you work with instructional support from the Rutgers Libraries when importing content to your course.

title: Securing Qualtrics Surveys
body:
Any survey is susceptible to spam from Bots or other unwanted responses. Qualtrics has several tools available to help prevent these instances from compromising your survey and possibly skewing your data. 
Recommended minimum security settings
Captcha Verification
In captcha verification, the respondent is presented with a picture (or “challenge”) of words or characters, and the respondent must correctly type out those characters to proceed. This is especially important for surveys using a single link that allows anyone to take the survey anonymously. 
Survey Availability
With the survey availability setting, you can make your survey available until a set expiration date when the survey will be closed to new respondents. This is vital to ensuring surveys do not continue collecting responses long after the survey should have ended. 
Securing your Survey
Securing how someone accesses your survey is always an essential first step. These options can increase your survey’s security and help protect it from unwanted responses. Detailed instructions on enabling these features can be found on the Qualtrics Support page for Security Surveys Options. 
Survey Access
There are two ways a respondent can enter your survey. The first is to do so anonymously by clicking an anonymous link. The second, more secure way, is to click a unique link generated for specific individuals.
Password Protection
You can set a single, general password that any respondent must enter to access your survey. This is helpful when using the anonymous link and restricting who can enter the survey. 
Add a Referral Website URL
Specify the URL your respondents must come from to access your survey. This setting is useful if your survey link is posted on a particular website.
Prevent Indexing
Search engines create an index, or a map of all pages on the Internet, so they can be searched quickly. This keeps search engines from finding and presenting your survey in their search results.
Spam and Fraud Detection
In addition to securing your survey, it is recommended that you take further action to prevent bots or malicious actors from skewing your data. Detailed instructions on enabling these features can be found on the Qualtrics Support page for Fraud Detection. 
Prevent Multiple Submissions
This works by placing a cookie on the respondent's browser when they submit a response. The next time they click the survey link, Qualtrics will see this cookie and not permit them to take the survey again.
Bot detection
Every response is rated on the probability that the respondent was a bot, and their responses are flagged accordingly. 
Security Scan Monitor
Prevent email scanning software from inadvertently starting a survey session when a survey link is included in an email.
RelevantID
Analyze a respondent’s browser, operating system, and location to determine the likelihood that the same respondent is answering repeatedly.

title: Sharing or Utilizing Groups for Qualtrics Surveys
body:
The use of the Qualtrics collaboration feature is always recommended prior to creating a Group since it is entirely controlled by you with no outside assistance needed and serves the purpose in most cases. Groups can be created, if necessary, but are subject to the process listed below anytime a change is required.
Collaboration
This is the recommended method of sharing a survey with another person. The collaboration feature allows you to give other people with Qualtrics accounts access to your surveys when they log into their accounts. That way, you can work on the same project without giving out your account information. You can even choose to restrict what type of access other people have to your project.
Groups
Groups allow you to work as a team with a shared library to store survey templates, contact lists, etc... Groups can only be created and managed by a Qualtrics Brand Administrator. 
Creating a new group
To request a group be created, send an email to qualtrics_support@oit.rutgers.edu and include:
•	Your name and NetID.
•	Brief, yet descriptive, name for the Group.
•	Names and NetIDs of the users they want to add to the group. They must have a Rutgers Qualtrics account already in order to be added.
Updating group membership
To either add or remove members to a Group, send an email to qualtrics_support@oit.rutgers.edu and include:
•	Your name and NetID
•	Name of the Group
•	Names and NetIDs of the users you want to add or remove. They must have a Rutgers Qualtrics account already in order to be added.
