To connect your laptop, phone, or tablet to the wireless network for use across all Rutgers buildings, reference the instructions on how to connect to RUWireless Secure. 
Game consoles, smart TVs, streaming devices, some smart devices, and wired (Ethernet) desktops can be connected to the Rutgers Residential Network (ResNet), which is available only in the residence halls.
Anyone connecting to the Rutgers Network must follow the Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources [PDF]. If you are caught violating this policy, your connection may be terminated without warning.
Wireless Devices
To connect devices wirelessly, such as Google Home, Amazon Echo, gaming consoles, smart devices, etc, you will need to generate your own unique Passphrase, which is your password to use on the Wireless network SSID: RUatHome
Important information for the RUatHome network
•	Each student has their own unique Passphrase (password) to add devices to the network. Do not share your password with others. 
•	In some instances, devices from the same brand, such as Apple or Android products, may automatically share wireless network passwords with your other devices, like a watch or tablet. Those devices may automatically connect to the network. You should check your connected devices and have them disconnect from the RUatHome network. 
•	The RUatHome network is only available to students in residence halls. It is not accessible by faculty/staff, and it is not available in other University buildings. 
o	The exception is faculty and staff living in On-Campus housing.
•	Some devices may require your phone to be on the same network as your device to complete the setup process or change device settings. In this case, you will have to add your phone to the RUatHome network as well. Phones should only be on the RUatHome network to assist with configuring your smart device. Once you are done configuring your device, you should promptly "Forget" the RUatHome network and connect to RUWireless Secure. This will ensure your phone maintains a wireless connection in all Rutgers buildings.  
Connecting your wireless devices
1.	Go to the Passphrase Portal. 
2.	Log in with your NetID and NetID password if you are not automatically logged in. 
3.	For devices with a camera, you can scan the QR code to automatically connect. 
4.	For other devices, note the password in the Passphrase field.  
o	These are valid for 1 year. You will automatically get an email as the expiration date approaches, prompting you to renew the key for an additional year. 

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	On your device, navigate to the wireless network settings. 
6.	Select the RUatHome network, which is only available in the residence halls. 
7.	Enter the Passphrase from step 4 as the network password. 
Disconnecting your wireless devices
•	To temporarily disconnect a device, you can power it off to ensure it no longer has an active wireless connection or go into the device's wireless network settings and choose to "Disconnect" from the network. 
•	To permanently disconnect a device, go into the device's wireless network settings and choose to "Forget" the network. You can always enter your Passphrase again if you want to reconnect it. 
Resetting your Passphrase 
You have the option to generate a new Passphrase. This should only be done in the rare event you need to, or are instructed to do so by the OIT Help Desk, as a step in troubleshooting any potential issues. 
1.	Go to the Passphrase Portal. 
2.	Log in with your NetID and NetID password if you are not automatically logged in. 
3.	Click on Generate New PassPhrase. 
4.	You'll receive a confirmation message that your current one will expire in 24 hours. Click Yes. 
5.	Your password will be updated and shown in the Passphrase field. 
6.	This also resets the expiration date of it to 359 days. 
7.	You will need to update any device using the old Passphrase. 
Devices still using the old Passphrase will remain connected for 24 hours after generating a new Passphrase.
Wired Devices 
For devices connecting to a Network port via an Ethernet cord, follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet.

If you do not fall into one of these categories, you will be unable to access the Passphrase portal. If you believe you qualify and can not access the portal, contact your local OIT Help Desk.

o	Incorrect Password for "RUatHome": Confirm that you entered your Passphrase correctly by logging into the Passphrase Portal and looking in the Passphrase field.

title: Support Connecting Wired devices to ResNet
body:
To connect devices over WiFi in the residence hall, follow the instructions on how to connect your smart devices, streaming devices, and gaming consoles.
To connect a wired device through an Ethernet cord, follow the instructions below. 
For wired devices, you will have to submit a request to get your device connected. Please note that if you previously registered your device last year, you will not need to complete this form to reconnect it. Connecting via this method is only supported in the residence halls. 
Requirements
•	You must have an Ethernet cord connecting your device to the black or grey network port in your dorm/suite. If your device does not have an Ethernet port, you may purchase an adapter to use for a wired connection and use the MAC Address of the adapter when submitting your request.
•	Prior to submitting the form, ensure you have connected the device to the network port using an Ethernet cord and powered on your device.  
o	If requesting multiple devices, leave each device on and connected to the port for at least 30 seconds before connecting the next device.
•	Know the Wired MAC Address of your device. Note that a device that supports both wireless and wired network connections will have a different MAC Address for each. Ensure you use the wired MAC Address on the form. Otherwise, your request will not be processed, and you will experience a delay in establishing a Wired connection. 
•	If you need to connect multiple wired devices simultaneously and your residence lacks sufficient ports, you can use an Unmanaged Switch to expand the number of available ports. 
Submitting a request
1.	Find the Wired MAC Address of your device. 
2.	Log in to the Rutgers IT Help Portal and complete the EI - Wired ResNet Device Bypass form. 
3.	After submitting the form, your request will be reviewed. 
4.	You will receive an email once your request is processed, indicating whether or not your device was successfully added.  
o	Note: this is not an immediate process. 
5.	If it is a Windows device, you will need to disable the Wired Autoconfig service for it to connect properly. 
Supported devices
The following is a list of devices that have been tested on the residential network. This is a live list, as testing is done continually and is subject to change. 
Supported in Residence Halls	Prohibited in Residence Halls

•	PlayStation
•	Desktops
•	Roku	•	Networked Printers
•	Routers
•	Video Doorbells

How to locate your MAC Address
Locating a device's MAC address is dependent on its manufacturer. Below is a list of commonly used devices and instructions on locating the MAC address.

o	Xbox One
o	Xbox Series X or Series S
o	Switch
o	Apple TV
o	Android TV

o	Amazon Echo

o	Google Home Mini
Windows
1.	Open the Windows start menu, then type cmd in the search bar.
2.	Press Enter to open Command Prompt.
3.	Type ipconfig/all
4.	Press Enter.
5.	Under the Ethernet adapter section. The Physical Address is the MAC address.
Mac
1.	Go to the Apple menu > System Preferences > Network.
2.	Make sure that the Ethernet interface is selected on the left side.
3.	Click on Advanced on the right, and then the Hardware tab. 
PlayStation
1.	Power on without a disc in the system.
2.	On the main menu navigate to Settings.
3.	Click on Network.
4.	Navigate to View Connection Status.
5.	You will see the Wireless Mac Address and the Wired Mac Address.
Xbox One
1.	Go to My Xbox in the dashboard and select Settings.
2.	Select Network.

title: Support Getting your computer connected to ResNet in the residence halls
body:
The Rutgers University Office of Information Technology provides connections in residence halls. 
Students using computers in their rooms, connected to the Rutgers Network, must follow the ResNet Network rules regarding computer usage. If caught violating any of the rules, your connection may be terminated without warning.
How to connect to the network
Laptops should be set up to use RUWireless Secure. 
To gain access to the network with an Ethernet (wired) connection, follow the instructions on connecting your wired device. 
Configuring your operating system to obtain an IP automatically (DHCP)
Most devices will automatically use DHCP to obtain an IP address. If yours does not, follow the instructions below based on your operating system:
Windows
1.	Click on the Search Windows bar > search Control Panel. 
1.	At the top right where it says View by, if it says Category, change it to Small Icons or Large icons. This will show more options. 
2.	Click the Network and Sharing Center.
3.	Click the link for Local Area Connection.
4.	Click on Properties.
5.	Uncheck the box for Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6).
6.	Double-click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4).
7.	Select or check that the radio buttons for Obtain an IP address automatically and Obtain DNS server address automatically.
8.	Click OK to save the changes and close the window. Click OK to close the Properties window. Click Close in the Local Area Connection Status window.
MacOS
1.	From the Apple menu, select System Preferences. Select Network (Under Internet and Network). NOTE: Authentication may be required via the lock icon in the lower left corner.
2.	Select Ethernet on the left menu.
3.	Set Configure on the right screen to Using DHCP.
4.	Click the Apply Now button, then quit the System Preferences application.

title: Support ResNet FAQ: Antivirus software and spyware
body:
My computer is infected with a virus. Why was my network connection shut off?
The OIT Acceptable Use Policy states that ResNet has the right to remove any machines deemed a threat from the network. Many viruses, "worms," and "Trojan horses" are designed to infect other computers they can find on the network. Computers identified as being infected with a virus will be disconnected from the network to protect others' computers from becoming infected. Please consider this as a protective measure and not as disciplinary action against you.
Where can I get anti-virus software?
Visit our Antivirus software page for more information. 
My computer is infected with a virus. What antivirus software should I use?
You can use any antivirus software you wish to keep your computer virus-free. Once your computer is disconnected due to a virus infection, you must either update your existing antivirus software or install the programs as recommended in the browsing best practices page above and eliminate the problem before your network connection is restored. You may also reimage or reformat your hard drive to remediate the problem.
Why does my web browser sometimes go to sites that I do not want it to go to?
You may have any of a variety of programs running invisibly. To remedy this situation, you must scan your computer for malicious software that may have been installed without your knowledge. We recommend programs like AdwCleaner and Malwarebytes to protect your machines from spyware.
Why does my internet/computer seem slower than usual?
Since spyware runs in the background of an operating system, it will still use some system resources. If a computer has enough spyware, there may be a noticeable slowdown in Internet speed, general computing speed, or both. Programs such as AdwCleaner or Malwarebytes can be used to help address this problem.
Why do I get popups when my computer is not attended?
Popups are most commonly seen when surfing the web but may also occur even when you are not at your computer. Pop-ups are typically caused by adware. Adware differs from spyware because adware is software that may have been installed on your computer by a remote site. Many free utilities that you download from the Internet will install hidden software that sends details of the websites you visit and other information from your computer (which can include your email address) to advertisers so they can target you with popup ads and spam. The easiest way to ensure your computer is clean from adware is to use AdwCleaner and Malwarebytes.

title: Support ResNet network rules
body:
Students using computers in their rooms connected to the Rutgers Network must follow rules regarding computer usage. If caught violating any of the rules, your connection may be terminated without warning.
Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources [PDF]
To ensure high-quality infrastructure for your academic purposes and consistent with the OIT Acceptable Use Policy, you must protect the access and integrity of your personal devices connected to the Rutgers Network, including but not limited to LANs behind personal routers and PCs running any operating system. The Office of Information Technology recommends that residents follow the best browsing practices outlined in the Antivirus section of the Rutgers IT website.
For more details regarding computer security, visit the Information Security site for tips and suggestions on how to keep your computer and information safe.
Below is a list of things NOT allowed on computers in the Residence Hall Network.
•	FTP servers containing copyrighted material (Software, MP3 Files, etc)
•	Excessive amounts of data, either inbound or outbound.
•	Web servers containing commercial content or used for commercial purposes.
•	Mail Servers: you cannot run a mail server on your computer.
•	Providing Network connections to ANYONE else. If your roommate wants a connection, they can get their own. It is perfectly OK to allow someone else to use your computer, you just cannot extend the Network to other people.
•	Ping attacks on other computers.
•	Servers and/or programs that end up using a lot of bandwidth.
•	Attempting to access computers on which you do not have accounts.
•	Registering your TCP/IP address with outside Domain Name Services.
•	Running ‘Bots’ (Robots) of any kind doing anything to other computers, especially IRC bots.
Router Use
Personal wireless routers are not allowed in Residence Halls. Unmanaged switches can be used in cases where you want numerous wired connections. Please contact the OIT Help Desk with any questions or if you believe your Residence Hall may not have full wireless coverage.

title: Support ResNet Wired & Wireless Setup
body:
Table of Contents
•	How do I get connected to the wired network?
•	Where can I purchase networking cables?
•	There are more residents assigned to my room than there are available Ethernet ports. How can everyone connect to the Internet?
•	Can I connect more than one device to the wired network in my room?
•	How do I set up my console gaming system on the network?
•	I got a new computer or device. What do I need to do to get connected?
•	Can I connect more than one device to the wireless network in my room?
•	Can I set up my printer in my room?
•	Can I set up my own wireless network or wireless access point in my residence hall?
•	Are there any devices that will not work on RUWireless Secure?
 
How do I get connected to the wired network?
Plug one end of your Ethernet cable into the Ethernet port on your computer. Plug the other end into the Ethernet jack in the wall. The jack is usually black, and the faceplate is labeled with a number and the letter "D". Follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet. 
Where can I purchase networking cables?
Ethernet cables are available to Camden, Newark, and New Brunswick students at the kite+key Rutgers tech stores, and local electronics stores.
There are more residents assigned to my room than there are available Ethernet ports. How can everyone connect to the Internet?
In most cases, there is one Ethernet port available in each dorm/suite. You can obtain and use an Unmanaged Switch to connect multiple devices. 
Can I connect more than one device to the wired network in my room?
Although you can only connect one device per port to the wired network at a time, there is no restriction on the total number of network devices in a room. Residents who want to use more wired devices than there are ports would be required to disconnect the current device and then connect the new device to the same Ethernet port. You would still have to follow the instructions on connecting Wired devices to ResNet. 
If you need to have multiple wired devices connected simultaneously and you do not have enough ports in your residence, you may use an Unmanaged Switch to expand the number of available ports. 
Wireless routers are not permitted in residence halls, as they interfere with RUWireless.
How do I set up my console gaming system on the network?
If you wish to use a console on the network, you can connect wirelessly or through a wired connection. Follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops. 
I got a new computer or device. What do I need to do to get connected?
For laptops, phones, and tablets, please refer to the instructions on how to connect to RUWireless Secure. For all wired desktops and smart devices, follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops. 
Can I connect more than one device to the wireless network in my room?
There is no limit to the number of wireless devices you can connect to RUWireless Secure or RUatHome at a time.
Can I set up my printer in my room?
Wireless and wired capabilities of personal printers are not supported, but you can still connect with a USB cable to print.
Can I set up my own wireless network or wireless access point in my residence hall?
All Rutgers residence halls offer full RUWireless coverage. As a result, ResNet does not support the wireless feature for personal routers, as it interferes with the RUWireless signal for other residents. If you are unable to connect to RUWireless in your room due to poor coverage or believe RUWireless does not cover your residence hall, get in touch with your local OIT Help Desk for assistance.
Are there any devices that will not work on RUWireless Secure?
If your device does not support the RUWireless Secure installer, you may connect it to the RUatHome wireless network or configure it for a wired connection. These devices include wired desktops, game consoles, handheld game consoles, smart TVs, and smart assistants. Follow the instructions on connecting your smart devices, streaming devices, gaming consoles, and desktops.  
Please note that some devices may experience reduced functionality on the Rutgers wireless network compared to your home wireless network. Some wireless devices that support 2.4 GHz only may not be able to connect; it is recommended to use a wireless device capable of 5 GHz. 
Additionally, some devices are not supported on our residential wireless networks in any capacity. These devices include:
•	Google Chromecast
•	Certain Smart Plugs & Lights
•	Network Printers

title: Support TV service at Rutgers
body:
Rutgers is making significant updates to the television services provided on campus. In response to the evolving media landscape and your changing viewing habits, we have phased out traditional cable television service. This change will affect both residential areas, including rooms and apartments, as well as public spaces throughout the university. 
Traditional cable television service is discontinued in all on-campus residence hall rooms, apartments, and community lounge spaces. This decision comes as a direct response to your preferences and habits. 
Your feedback over the years has informed a significant shift towards online streaming content. Platforms like YouTube, Netflix, and others are not just your choices, they are part of your daily life. These streaming services offer more flexibility and variety, over traditional cable connections. This trend is evident in the increased use of our campus Wi-Fi system for accessing content, signaling a departure from coaxial cable. 
It’s important to us that all our students enjoy a wide range of media content without financial barriers. To this end, we put together a comprehensive guide to various streaming services that offer either free content or attractive student discounts. 
These options are tailored for use on personal devices within our residential buildings, ensuring that you can easily access your favorite shows and movies right from your dorm room or apartment. To make use of these plans, all you need is to show proof of your current enrollment at Rutgers. 
Learn more about the available streaming plans and how to take advantage of these student discounts.

title: Active Directory (RAD) Azure Hybrid Join configuration profile
body:
Hybrid Azure AD Join has been implemented with Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) and is available for use. A device is said to be hybrid joined if it has both an AD object and an Azure AD (AAD) object, which allows users of that device to sign in with a RAD user account.
With Hybrid Joins the university can now leverage:
•	Device Based licensing for Office 365
o	This allows Office to be tied to the Device rather than the User, making it ideal for enterprise or shared devices.
•	Reduced logins due to the device being assign both RAD and Azure authentication tokens
A device in Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) can end up in a hybrid joined state one of two ways:
•	If the computer is already joined to RAD.
•	The computer was built using Rutgers Autopilot, which allows for hybrid-joining via configuration profiles.
A hybrid joined computer is joined to both AD and AAD, but the AD join is primary because the device initially uses AD authentication. Only Windows devices can be hybrid joined.
Azure Hybrid Join Configuration Profile
AD Join from Azure Configuration Profile. NOTE: This is NOT required if the device is already part of RAD. It is only required for new deployments or Azure Only Joined devices.
1.	Log in to Microsoft Endpoint, then click on Devices. Under the Policy heading, click Configuration Profiles.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click Create Profile, select Windows 10 and Later as the Platform and Templates as the Type.


Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Find Domain Join in the list and click Create.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Name your Configuration and click Next.

Error! Filename not specified. 
5.	Here we will specify the prefix for the system, domain, and OU for it to be placed in.
1.	The Computer Name Prefix can be 12 characters long, allowing Azure to randomly assign the last 3 characters to be unique. This prevents us from pre-populating computer names in RAD.
2.	Enter the Domain you wish to join.
3.	Add the FQDN of the OU where you wish for the devices to be added.
4.	Click Next.

title: Active Directory (RAD) How to get started with RAD (Rutgers Active Directory)
body:
Management of your AD environment is done through delegated Organizational Units (OU) in RAD. To manage your AD environment, a request from IT Leadership within your organization is required. Delegated OUs provide a secure Windows domain environment. Delegated OUs will enable RU to remove Windows domain silos, share resources, and reduce costs, making it easier to share resources.
Requesting Delegated Organizational Units
Requests for a delegated OU can be made from the IT Leadership in your organization by submitting the RAD Data Collection form. In the request, ensure that you include the technical contacts, the department head, and the suggested OU name. Delegated OU names should be short; we will typically recommend using the Departmental Code as assigned in Cornerstone. (i.e., OIT, ORA, SAS)
It can take between a couple of days to a couple of months to join, depending on the complexity of your existing environment. We’ll help you assess whether joining is the right decision, guide you through the necessary steps to get started, and assist in establishing a timeframe to complete the work.
Also reference the RAD Naming Conventions.

title: Active Directory (RAD) Managing your Delegated OU in RAD
body:
Designated department IT staff will use a non-standard NetID account in RAD with elevated rights to perform the functions below. These are known as ADM accounts. Learn more on how to get access to Rad ADM accounts. Once created, these accounts would be added to the Departmental-OU admins or Departmental-Workstations admins group, depending on the level of access required.
OIT has defined naming convention guidelines for RAD objects. When creating these objects, OIT requires that you prefix the object with your delegated OU name if our naming standards do not meet your requirements.
Delegated -OU Admins will have full rights to manage their OU’s, as described below, except for manipulating standard NetID accounts. These accounts all reside in the People OU, which is managed by IDM, and any changes should originate from IDM processes. Passwords should be managed through netid.rutgers.edu to ensure all accounts stay in Sync (Portal, Luminous, AD, Email).
Create and edit group policies
OIT will create a Workstation baseline GP at the root of your delegated OU to enforce Loopback Group Policy-Merge and populate the Built-in Administrator’s group of each managed workstation with the departmental Workstation Admins group.
•	Group Policy Loopback Processing needs to be set to ‘Merge’. Since all user accounts are located in the People OU, we need to instruct the PC Objects to process the user policies assigned to the machine. This allows user configurations to run on machines when the user isn’t in the same OU. This only needs to be set once on a machine, and other delegated areas will set it in their workstation baseline policy.
•	Share mappings can be configured on this GP, and it can also be used to push PC settings down to all Workstations within the delegated OU.
•	Additional information can be found on the Microsoft site: Loopback processing of Group Policy.
Security groups
OIT will create these default groups when setting up your delegated OU. All other groups will be created by the delegated OU administrators.
•	OU-OU Admins
•	OU-Workstations Admins
•	OU-All Users
•	OU-All Workstations
•	OU-Restricted
Important notes regarding OU Admins vs Workstations Admin Group
Non-ADM accounts should NOT be members of the OU Admins or OU Workstation Admin groups.
ADM accounts should only be in one group or the other. Being in the OU Admins group can grant technicians more access than they need. OU Admins are already nested members of the Workstation Admin groups. If they only need Workstation Admin rights, they would be in the Workstation Admin group only. 
OU Admins: Users in this group are recommended to have the following permissions and responsibilities:
•	The permissions to modify rights over Groups, OUs, Group Policies, and Printers.
•	Creating and assigning group policies to control settings for the users and computers within the delegated OU.
•	Delegating certain administrative tasks to other users or groups within the delegated OU.
•	OU Admins are already members of the Delegated OU-Workstation Admins group.
Workstations Admins: Users in this group are recommended to have the following permissions and responsibilities:
•	The rights to migrate workstations to the domain, administrative rights over delegated OU workstations, and can add machines to the Delegated OU-All Workstations group.
•	Installing, configuring, and updating software applications on workstations.
•	Managing hardware configurations and drivers on individual computers.
•	Troubleshooting and resolving issues related to specific workstations.
•	Ensuring that workstations are compliant with security policies and updates.
•	Providing user support for workstation-related problems.
Organization Units (OUs)
Each OU admin will have the ability to create and delete Sub-OUs within their Delegated OU.
Printer objects
Listed in the directory and able to be set up as print queues or mapped by direct IP printing. Print Management is performed through an MMC snap-in, which is configured to connect to the print server hosting your print queue.
You can request that print queues be created on the Enterprise RAD print server (ASBRADPRINT01, 172.29.219.151) using this form. 
•	Please ensure the Request Category: RAD-Rutgers Active Directory, and the Request Type = Printers. We need the following info to set up a print queue.
•	Print queue name: Must begin with Delegated OU name.
•	IP: Please ensure that you can access our print server from your subnet.
•	Driver to user: link to the driver you want us to use for this print queue.
Shared drives
Managing Restricted Drive NTFS Permissions: Only applies to schools that have requested Enterprise On-premises storage.
•	Each School’s OU admin group will be given 'Modify' rights over the storage allocated to their school.
•	Each School will have a Global Restricted (R) drive.
o	User would have to be added to the top-level Restricted group to have the drive mapped (OU-Restricted)
o	For each folder within this Drive, there should also be a corresponding AD security group created and added to the security of the folder
o	Access Based Enumeration (ABE) is enabled on Enterprise storage Servers, ensuring users will only be able to view folders they have permission to access
o	User would need to be a member of the following groups
	OU-All Users
	OU-Restricted
	OU-Restricted (Name of Folder)
•	Each school will have a Shared (S) drive mapped.

title: Active Directory (RAD) Migrating to RAD
body:
Prior to migrating your department resources to RAD, the following items should be addressed and/or considered during the migration planning process.
•	Firewall:
o	Does your location/building have a perimeter firewall that will need/allow required access to RAD resources (Domain Controllers, Storage, Print Servers, DFS)?
•	Storage:
o	Will you continue to use your current department storage or will you move your data to RAD enterprise storage?
o	Initial enterprise storage amounts for departments are provisioned on a case by case basis and based on the number of the department staff and faculty.
•	Data access:
o	Will you require a new set up with new directories and new permissions, or will you require the use of a tool to migrate SID to ACL of new file structure?
•	Administrative rights:
o	Will specific users require Admin rights to Managed Workstations/Servers?
o	Group Policy will control administrative rights for specified Users on RAD PC’s.
•	Member servers:
o	Many member servers can be removed from the old domain and added to the new domain. Some member servers running SQL or IIS may require a re-ACLing or other preparation to insure a smooth service transition.
•	Group policies:
o	Do you have any existing policies being applied that will have to be setup in the new domain?
•	Service/generic accounts:
o	Are they currently being used? Will you need them in the new Domain?
•	OU configuration:
o	How do you see your OU structure once it's migrated?
o	Who are your OU admins?
•	Printer migrations:
o	If you are currently hosting print queues, please perform a print queue export, which would then be imported into the RAD Enterprise Print Servers.
o	If you are using direct IP Printing, OIT-EI recommends you use print queues once migrated to RAD.
Departmental IT staff can initiate a migration to RAD by submitting the Rutgers Active Directory Migration Request Form.
Migration methods
A typical migration can be performed at your own pace where you can pre-set up your group policies and migrate your resources and computers on your own timeframe. Using a temporary domain trust and leveraging dual ACLs on your resources can help smooth the transition period while some users are operating in the old domain and some users are operating in RAD. The RAD support team can assist you in developing your migration plan.
A sample migration blueprint can be found here.
Successful migration
After the successful migration to Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) Domain, you will now have access to the following managed services. Support for these services can be made by submitting an ServiceNow ticket with the appropriate details.
•	Enterprise Storage:
o	OIT will provide centrally funded storage to RAD members.
o	Storage is backed up and presented in a load balanced manner.
o	Quotas can be applied to Enterprise storage.
o	Home Drive Quotas are currently set to 10 GB.
o	Shares are mapped through Group Policy by DFS Links.
•	Enterprise Printing:
o	Papercut will be offered as a RAD offering.
o	Print queues can be installed on RAD managed print servers.
	Driver management, Printer Discovery, and Centralized print management are a few benefits of using Print servers.
•	Group Policy Settings:
o	RAD Managed workstations can have Group policies setup to globally manage PC settings and Rights.
o	ADMIN Rights- Assign administrative rights to a workstation to a specific user or group.
o	Internet Browser settings
	Setting Home pages
	Web Page Restrictions
	Setting Proxy Server
o	Secure workstations
	Customize Desktop
	Remove Control Panel Items
	Lockdown Start Menu
•	Enterprise Server Management:
o	Patched and rebooted
Post migration tasks
•	Testing
o	Managed Applications
o	Network Access to RAD devices
•	DNS Resolution – Ensure you are able to access RAD resources by FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name).

title: Active Directory (RAD) RAD ADM (Active Directory Management) accounts
body:
Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) uses ADM accounts for elevated rights to modify an Organizational Unit's (OU’s), groups, printers, group policies, servers, and workstations within your organization. An ADM account will be based on your existing NetID.
If you are onboarding your department for RAD, you should identify who in your organization requires ADM accounts for OU or Workstation admin access and have them go through the request process below. Only Staff, Faculty, Guests, and Student Workers can request ADM accounts.
Request an Elevated/ADM account
Follow the instructions on how to request and setup a RAD ADM account. 
If you had an ADM account prior to when the Request process was implemented, you will have to still go through the Request process to link your existing ADM account to your NetID.
Once your ADM account has been provisioned correctly, the password for that account can be managed by logging into the NetID Management page with your standard NetID credentials. Once successfully logged in, you should see an option in the left-hand menu to manage your RAD Admin account. Passwords for ADM accounts must be different than the password for your standard NetID account.
Elevated/ADM Privileges
ADM accounts will not have any extra access unless added to the appropriate AD group or provided through a Group policy. If you are not sure what access is needed, please contact the OU admin for your department.
Restrictions
ADM accounts should not be used to log into workstations. If admin rights are needed, the ADM credentials should be entered in the elevated prompt.

title: Active Directory (RAD) RAD architecture
body:
Table of Contents

The purpose of this site is to outline the proposed architecture for the Microsoft Enterprise Active Directory. The Office of Information Technology is committed to providing leadership and support for the effective use of technology, offering an extensive range of resources that support education, research and clinical environments. These enterprise-wide services provide technology solutions and secured standards to the Rutgers community.
•	Active Directory Configuration
•	DC Placement
•	DNS
•	Active Directory Schema
•	Provisioning and Sync Integration
•	Directory Structure
•	Desktop Management
Active Directory Configuration
The Rutgers Active Directory (RAD) is built across multiple domain controllers. The operating system of the domain controllers is currently Windows Server 2012 R2 and will be kept within one major rev of the latest released operating system. LDAP configuration settings are generally set to the Active Directory defaults.
DC Placement
The RAD domain controllers are geographically dispersed, with each main geographic location having at least one or more domain controllers. The domain controllers reside in physically secure datacenters that also co-locate with Rutgers’ core network infrastructure to ensure redundant high-bandwidth links to RUNet.
The domain controllers for RAD reside on Rutgers private address space and cannot be accessed from outside Rutgers without the aid of VPN. The DNS information for the domain controllers is also only advertised on Rutgers private address space. This space includes Rutgers Newark, Piscataway, New Brunswick, and Camden campuses and the Rutgers Biomedical and Health Science campuses.
A NAT boundary exists on the Rutgers network as a result of the merger between Rutgers and UMDNJ. The domain controllers reside on specific NAT-exempted networks, allowing their IP addresses to be accessed freely across the NAT boundary between the legacy Rutgers space and the RBHS space. Currently, the system implements multiple DNS views, so DNS resolution is handled correctly depending upon which side of the NAT boundary the query is coming from. Other key enterprise RAD components also reside on these networks. Although all clients and resources can get to central RAD resources no matter which side of the NAT they reside, clients may not necessarily be able to communicate directly to each other across the NAT boundary. For example, a PC on the legacy Rutgers space may not be able to reach another PC on the other side of the NAT boundary on the legacy UMDNJ space, even though both machines are members of RAD.
Although the domain controllers are available on all Rutgers spaces, departments or units running their own firewalls may need to allow incoming access from the domain resources to ensure proper communication. Detailed information can be obtained by inquiring to rad-support@oit.rutgers.edu.
DNS
DNS for RAD has been offloaded from the domain controllers and is completely handled by the University Infoblox DNS grid. The Infoblox grid supports secure Dynamic DNS for both forward and reverse lookups and fully supports the DNS service records required for Active Directory. The Infoblox grid also supports multiple DNS views so that DNS queries are handled correctly on both sides of the NAT boundary within the university. There is a separate DNS view for the legacy Rutgers space and for the legacy UMDNJ space.
Active Directory Schema
The Rutgers Active Directory schema is open to changes and includes both vendor and Rutgers custom schema elements. The RAD admin team will entertain any schema modification requests. All schema modifications must follow schema best practices. Vendors tend to follow these best practices. Custom schema modifications are also possible.

This will be used through a transition period for some of the early adopters of RAD. The intention is to eventually put in place a RU Groups Service powered by Grouper to handle all group creation and management. When ready, creation of groups will go through the RU Groups Service web interface and propagate to RAD.
Default Group Policy Objects

Directory Structure

The Rutgers Enterprise Active Directory is a single forest/single domain.
All NetID Based accounts are under the top-level People OU. There are almost 300,000 accounts residing in this OU.
All other non-NetID accounts (Service, Admin, Resource, and Application) are located under the top-level OtherPeople OU. The OtherPeople OU is separated into sub OUs by Org Type requesting the account.

Most computers and other directory objects specific to Rutgers clients are under the top-level Delegated OU. title: Active Directory (RAD) RAD Hybrid Join FAQ
body:
Hybrid Azure AD Join has been implemented with RAD and is now available for use. A device is defined as hybrid joined if it has both an AD object and an Azure AD (AAD) object, which allow users of that device to sign in with a RAD user account.
With Hybrid Joins, the University can now leverage:
•	Device-based licensing for Office 365
o	This allows Office to be tied to the device rather than the user, making it ideal for enterprise or shared devices.
•	Reduced logins due to the device being assign both RAD and Azure authentication tokens
For information view the support page for Azure Hybrid Join Configuration Profile.
•	What are the benefits of adding devices to Azure?
•	Does a Rutgers department need to have an OU in RAD to participate in hybrid join?
•	How does this affect devices that are already joined to RAD?
•	What operating system is supported for hybrid join?
•	Can iOS or Android devices be managed using this method?
•	Will devices be encrypted with Bit locker?
•	Are Autopilot devices already Hybrid Joined?
•	Does the computer object need to be created in Azure or RAD before I can take advantage of Hybrid Join?
•	Is there a separate interface to see these in Azure or as an OU Admin?
•	Can I disable an Azure AD joined Device?
•	How do I disable Hybrid Join if I no longer wish to use it?
What are the benefits of adding devices to Azure?
•	Single Sign-On for Office 365 reduces authentication (Learn more)
•	Auto-activation for Microsoft Windows through Azure and RAD Group Policy
•	Device Based licensing for Office 365 (What is Device Based Licensing?)
Does a Rutgers department need to have an OU in RAD to participate in hybrid join?
Yes. Departments would need to have their own OU in RAD. There is no central group currently to manage devices for departments.
How does this affect devices that are already joined to RAD?
Devices already connected to RAD will see no difference. If a department would like to have RAD devices Hybrid Joined, a request needs to be submitted to EDM_support@oit.rutgers.edu to enable the synchronization.
What operating system is supported for hybrid join?
Devices running Windows 10 Pro and above are currently supported.
Can iOS or Android devices be managed using this method?
No, however, iOS and Android devices can be managed in Intune.
Will devices be encrypted with BitLocker?
Devices can be encrypted through BitLocker through RAD or Azure.
Are Autopilot devices already Hybrid Joined?
No, however, an Autopilot device can be joined to RAD via Configuration Profiles.
Does the computer object need to be created in Azure or RAD before I can take advantage of Hybrid Join?
The domain automatically synchronizes RAD-joined objects to Azure, and the device becomes hybrid. If the device does not exist in Azure or RAD, it must be joined to the RAD domain either via a profile or manual join.
Is there a separate interface to see these in Azure or as an OU Admin?
Yes, the interface for Azure is the Microsoft Intune Admin Center. 
Can I disable an Azure AD joined Device?
You should only disable an Azure AD device if you have lost it or if it is no longer in use. If you disable an Azure AD device, you will be unable to perform any Azure AD authentications from that device. You will not be able to re-enable it. There is a significant impact on the end user if an Azure AD device is mistakenly disabled.
Microsoft Office products (including Microsoft 365 Apps) require the device to be registered with the user's Azure AD account to allow sign-in.
How do I disable Hybrid Join if I no longer wish to use it?
To disable Hybrid Joins, email EDM_support@oit.rutgers.edu to stop the synchronization of the requested OU.

title: Active Directory (RAD) RAD Migration Blueprint
body:
Follow the steps below for the RAD Migration:
1.	Rename local domain users to match Rutgers NetID users.
2.	Rename groups on the local domain to match RAD domain standards.
3.	ReACL all local domain resources to add RAD equivalent users/groups (so both local domain and RAD domain are included).
4.	Change all local group policies to act on computer objects with loopback instead of on users.
5.	Remove logon scripts, roaming profiles, Terminal Service profiles, and other user attributes where possible using the RAD User Workaround options.
6.	Document the user attributes that are still required on user objects and investigate whether they can be set in the RAD domain.
7.	Import RAD users and groups into SQL environments and apply the same roles.
8.	Replicate the OU structure in your delegated OU. Request special directory permissions from OIT.
9.	Export your GPO-based IPSec rules and either redeploy them as local IPSec rules or ask OIT to implement them as GPO-based for you.
10.	Export/import your group policy objects to the RAD domain and link as appropriate.
11.	Reconfigure new computer deployment processes to target the RAD domain.
12.	Ensure you’ve got the cross-forest GPO setting in place in your local domain.
13.	Update all IIS default domain settings if using your local domain for authentication.
14.	Change ownership of profiles from local domain user to RAD user.
15.	Change the default logon domain on all computers to the RAD domain.
16.	Disable local domain users.
17.	Adjust the change domain suffix on the domain join setting as needed.
18.	Migrate workstations on whatever time scale that works. Disable the local domain computer account when it is moved to keep track.
19.	Migrate servers on whatever time scale that works. Start with the least complex servers.
20.	Until all computers are migrated, leave a single domain controller behind with a logon script to automatically migrate missed computers like laptops.
21.	Decommission your old domain.

title: Active Directory (RAD) Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) Overview
body:
Supported Operating Systems
Windows LAPS is now available on the following OS platforms with the specified update or later installed: 
•	Windows 11 22H2 - April 11 2023 Update
•	Windows 11 21H2 - April 11 2023 Update
•	Windows 10 - April 11 2023 Update
•	Windows Server 2022 - April 11 2023 Update
•	Windows Server 2019 - April 11 2023 Update 
•	Windows Server 2025        
Configuration
Windows LAPS is configured on-prem via Group Policy. Below are the settings that group policy controls, along with the recommended settings. 
Windows LAPS Policy Settings 
The following settings are located in Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > System > LAPS.
Windows LAPS Policy Settings 
Setting 	Description 
Password Settings 	If enabled, you can configure the following aspects of the password that is generated: 
•	Password Complexity: Determines what type of characters are used to generate the password. The available actions are:  
o	Large letters 
o	Large letters + small letters 
o	Large letters + small letters + numbers 
o	Large letters + small letters + numbers + specials
o	Passphrase (long words) - (Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025)
o	Passphrase (short words with unique prefixes) - (Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025)
o	Passphrase (short words) - (Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025)
•	Password Length: Determines how many characters the password will be in length.? This must be a number from 8 – 64.? The default value is 14.
•	Password Age (Days): This is the number of days that will be used to set the password expiration time.? This must be a number from 1 – 365.? The default value is 30. 
•	Passphrase length: This is the number of words that will be used in the passphrase (when Password Complexity is set to a passphrase option). This must be a number from 3 to 10. The default value is 6.
(Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025).
Name of administrator account to manage 	The name of the local administrator account whose password is managed. 
Set this only if you want Windows LAPS to manage an account other than the built-in Administrator account. 
The default, when not specified, is the built-in Administrator (by its well-known RID). 
Notes: If you specify a disabled account, the password will be managed by the account, and the account will not be enabled by LAPS.? If you specify an account that does not exist.? If you specify an account that is not a member of the local Administrators group, LAPS will not add it to the local Administrators group. 
Configure automatic account management	(Windows 11 24H2 and Server 2025)
Note: the DSRM account on domain controllers cannot be configured for automatic account management. This policy has no effect on domain controllers and will be ignored even if configured for a DC.
•	Specify the target account to manage: specifies whether the built-in admin account or a custom account should be managed.
•	Automatic account name (or name prefix): specifies the name, or name prefix, to use for the managed account. 
o	If this policy setting is configured, Windows LAPS will use it as the target account's name or name prefix.
o	If this policy setting is not configured, Windows LAPS will use "WLapsAdmin" as the account name or name prefix.
o	Note: this name is treated as a prefix when account name randomization is configured, see comments below.
•	Enable the managed account: specifies whether the managed account should be enabled. 
o	If this policy setting is configured, Windows LAPS will enable the specified managed account.
o	If this policy setting is not configured, Windows LAPS will disable the specified managed account.
o	Note: Windows LAPS regularly maintains and rotates the password of the managed account, regardless of whether the account is enabled or disabled.
•	Randomize the name of the managed account: specifies whether the name of the managed account should be randomized with a random numeric suffix. 
o	If this policy setting is configured, Windows LAPS will add an eight-digit random numeric suffix to the managed automatic account name and re-randomize the account name each time the password is rotated.
o	If this policy setting is not configured, Windows LAPS will use the managed automatic account name.
o	If the managed automatic account name prefix is configured, Windows LAPS will use up to the first twelve (12) characters of that name as a prefix for the random name. If the managed automatic account name is not configured, Windows LAPS will use "WLapsAdmin" as the name prefix.
Enable password encryption 	Enabling this setting has no effect unless the password is configured to be backed up to Active Directory and the Active Directory domain functional level is Windows Server 2016 or higher.
If enabled, the password is encrypted before it is backed up to AD. 
If disabled, the password is not encrypted before it is backed up to AD. 
If not configured, the default value is Enabled. 
Enable password backup for DSRM accounts 	When you enable this setting, the DSRM administrator account password will be managed and backed up to Active Directory.
Enabling this setting has no effect unless the managed device is a domain controller and password encryption is also enabled.
Do not allow password expiration time longer than required by policy 	 
If this setting is enabled or not configured, planned password expiration that exceeds the password age set by the "Password Settings" policy is NOT allowed. When such an expiration is detected, the password is changed immediately, and password expiration is set according to policy.
If this setting is disabled, password expiration time may be longer than required by the "Password Settings" policy.
 
Configure size of encrypted password history 	 
Use this setting to configure how many previous encrypted passwords will be stored in Active Directory. This must be a number from 0 – 12.
This setting only applies when encrypted passwords are being backed up to AD.
This setting may help out when reverting to a VM shapshot where an older password was in use at the time the snapshot was taken, or when using a system restore point.
The default value, if not configured, is 0.
 
Configure password backup directory 	Use this setting to configure which directory the local admin account password is backed up to.
The allowable settings are:
•	0: Disabled
•	1: Azure AD only
•	2: Windows Server (on-prem) AD only 
If not specified, this setting will default to 0 (Disabled).
If this setting is configured to 1, and the managed device is not joined to Azure Active Directory, the local administrator password will not be managed.
If this setting is configured to 2, and the managed device is not joined to Active Directory, the local administrator password will not be managed.
If this setting is disabled or not configured, the local administrator password is not managed.
Configure authorized password decryptors 	When enabled, you will specify the user or group authorized to decrypt the password in AD. 
You must provide one of the following as the decryptor 
•	The SID of the group or user
•	The name of the group or user in the following format: RAD\<name> 
Warning: If the device cannot resolve the SID or name provided, the password will not be backed up. 
This setting applies only when encrypted passwords are backed up to AD. 
The default value when not specified is the Domain Admins group. 
Post-authentication actions 	Specify an action that will be triggered after the successful authentication of the account whose password is being managed. 
The available actions are: 
•	Take no actions
•	Reset the password
•	Reset the password and log off the managed account
•	Reset the password and reboot the device 
Grace period: specifies the amount of time (in hours) to wait after an authentication before executing the specified post-authentication actions.
The grace period must be set greater than 0; if set to 0 the action will not be triggered.
If this setting is disabled or not configured, post-authentication actions will default to "Reset the password and logoff the managed account" after 24 hours.
If you want it to take no action, enable this setting and select Take no action. 
 
Example GPO:
Error! Filename not specified.
You must set up Configure authorized password decryptors and assign it to your Workstation Admins group or another group of users who can decrypt the stored passwords. If this is not configured, only Domain Admins can see the password. Once configured to your Workstation Admins group, Domain Admins will not be able to decrypt the password. 
If you want to manage an account that is not the default Administrator account on the computer, set the Name of administrator account to manage. Keep in mind, LAPS can only manage one account. 
Retrieving the LAPS password
Through the GUI, open ADUC or Active Directory Administrative Center using your -adm account. Find the computer, open Properties, and click the LAPS tab. If using ADUC, make sure you turn on Advanced Features under View to be able to view the LAPS tab. 
In Powershell, launch powershell as your -adm account, then you can run:
Get-LapsAdPassword -Identity <computername> -AsPlainText 
If you plan on using password history, the only way to view it is through powershell, run the following command to see the history: 
Get-LapsAdPassword -Identity <computername> -AsPlainText -IncludeHistory 
PowerShell Module
Cmdlet 	Description 
Get-LapsAdPassword 	Gets the saved password(s) from Windows Server Active Directory. 
Invoke-LapsPolicyProcessing 	Initiates the processing of the current LAPS policy. 
Reset-LapsPassword 	Immediately rotate the password for the currently managed local account.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) How to request a new RAMS list

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) RAMS list archives and statistics
body:
The Archives are available through the main RAMS page. You can also bookmark the direct link to the Archives Tool.
The Archives tool provides access to the archived postings to a list, as well as to statistical information about that list. The Archives tool can also be used to diagnose list problems.
All lists are archived. However, some may have Public Archives, which can be viewed by anyone with RAMS access, while others may have Admin Only Archives, which can be viewed only by a list's manager.
Selection
When you go to the Archives tool, you will be presented with a list of mailing lists to choose from. Click on a list name to get to the archives and statistics for that mailing list.
Archive Page
The Archive page consists of two sections. The top section is the Archives section, and the bottom section is the Statistics section.
Archives
The archive lists all the messages posted in the list, from newest to oldest, beginning with the first message posted after archiving was turned on. For every message, it lists:
•	Date: the date and time the last copy of the message left the RAMS system to be mailed to the list members.
•	Subject: the contents of the Subject header of the message.
•	Sender: the address in the From header of the message.
•	Recipients: the number of addresses it was sent to.
•	View: click to show the text of the message.
A message will only appear in the archives if the post passes through moderation and spam filtering. If it is still being held for moderation or if spam filters prevented it from being delivered, it will not be added to the archives.
The Archives list all messages that have been processed by RAMS for the list, but they do not guarantee that those messages reached all members of the list. For example, if a recipient's mailbox is full, RAMS will add the message to the archive even though it could not deliver the message.
If no messages have yet been posted to a list, or if you are viewing an Admin Only Archive and are not a manager for the list, you'll see "No Messages Found" instead of the archives.
Statistics
RAMS tracks several statistics:
•	Number of messages: is total number of messages that have been posted to the list.
•	Average number of recipients: is the average number of recipients per each message that has been posted to the list.
•	Total number of recipients: is the total of all recipients over the life of the list.
•	Last message sent: shows the date of the last message RAMS processed for the list. This is very useful for determining if a recent message has been delivered to the list.
•	Average message size: shows the average byte size of each message.
•	Total message size: shows the total byte size of all messages the list has received.
If a message is not successfully posted to all members of a list, no statistical information will be generated for that message. A successful posting is one that has been sent out to all members; it does not mean that each of the addresses is actually valid or reachable. For example, if an email address no longer exists or cannot accept mail for some reason, this will not affect the RAMS statistics.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) RAMS list moderation - Managing messages sent to a RAMS list
body:
What is a moderated list?
All messages sent to a moderated RAMS list must be approved before they are delivered to the list members.
How does moderation work?
When a message is sent to a moderated RAMS list, a notification is first sent to the list's moderators. Once approved by a moderator, the message will be forwarded to everyone on the list.
Approving and declining messages by email
To approve a message, select the approval link included in the RAMS confirmation email. The link opens the RAMS interface, where the message can be reviewed and approved. Each message must be approved individually. If another moderator has already approved or deleted the message, an informational email will indicate that no pending message exists.
No action is needed to decline the message.
Approving and declining messages with the List Manager in the web interface
1.	You will first need to log in to the List Manager using your NetID and password.
2.	Select which list you want to review.
3.	The Pending Moderation card lists messages awaiting approval by the list moderator. By default, messages that are considered spam are not displayed. Turn the Show Spam Messages slider to On to see messages flagged as spam.
4.	Use the Search Moderation field to find messages by subject or sender.
5.	Select View next to a message to read its full content. 
6.	To approve or delete messages, select the desired messages in the table by clicking on the row. The row will become highlighted. Click again to deselect a row.
7.	Select Approve Selected Messages or Delete Selected Messages. 
o	Those two buttons will only appear after messages are selected in the table.
8.	If you would like to delete all messages in the table, select Delete All Messages.
Please note you cannot approve and delete messages at the same time.
Additional information
See the list editor manual for more information on activating moderation.
For additional information, including the latest RAMS updates, view the RAMS documentation.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) RAMS list operator’s guide
body:
The Rutgers Automated Mass-mailing System (RAMS) is a collection of databases, web-based applications, and automated processes that deliver mass email to portions of the Rutgers population based on demographic information. The web-based applications allow authorized users to create and manage mailing lists, and to view their archives and statistical data.
At the heart of RAMS are two databases: one gathers information from various university databases and consolidates it into a single local database. This is done primarily to avoid maintenance hours on other systems conflicting with the best hours for sending bulk mailings. This database is updated daily.
The other database contains all the information for the mailing lists. When a message is sent to a list, RAMS looks up the list's rules in this database and uses them to compose the address list from the first database.
The web-based application provides the main user interface for RAMS. It is used to update information in the list database and trigger actions or automated processes. The important thing to remember is that it interacts with the database in real time. 
Automated processes keep RAMS functioning. Daily database updates keep demographic information current, and daily backups preserve the list information. Other processes handle the incoming postings, and a primetime process runs every hour to manage pending primetime mailings.
The life cycle of a message
Here's what can happen in RAMS when a message is posted to a list.
Open list
If the list is an open list (i.e., anyone can post to it), you send the message, which is received by the mail server.
1.	The mail server hands it over to the RAMS automated process.
2.	The process parses it and checks if the list actually exists.
3.	If the list exists, it checks whether it has a primetime restriction. 
o	If there is no primetime restriction or the mail arrives at a time when it can be broadcast, it posts the message, and the process is complete.
o	If there is a primetime restriction, the mail is put in the primetime queue to be processed when it is within the list's scheduled primetime
Closed list
If the list is closed, the process is the same, except that RAMS also checks whether the message sender is a list member. If they are, it proceeds as described for an open list. If they are not, it sends them an error message, and the process is complete.
Moderated list
If the list is moderated, the process is somewhat different.
1.	First, the mail is received by the mail server.
2.	Then, it hands the message off to the RAMS automated process.
3.	It queues a copy of the message in the moderation queue and then appends another copy to a confirmation email request sent to all the moderators.
4.	A moderator may select the approval link included in the RAMS confirmation email to approve the message for posting, or they may approve it via the List Manager. 
o	If approved via the approval link in the confirmation email, the approval is sent to the mail server, handed off to the RAMS process, and the moderation queue is checked for the message. If it is there, it sends it out or pushes it to the primetime queue as appropriate for the list.
o	If approved via the web application, the application checks the primetime restrictions and either sends the message out or pushes it to the primetime queue to be sent out later.
5.	Once the approval link is selected, the process is complete.
6.	Once a moderator approves a message, it will no longer appear available for moderation in the web application, and any further attempts to confirm by the approval link in the confirmation email will generate informational error messages.
Moderating messages
1.	Log in to the RAMS List Manager using your Rutgers NetID and NetID password.
2.	Select the appropriate list and locate the Pending Moderation section.
3.	By default, messages considered spam are not displayed. Turn the Show Spam Messages slider to On to see messages flagged as spam. 
4.	Select View next to a message to read its full content.
5.	To approve or delete messages, select the desired messages in the table by clicking on the row. The row will be highlighted; click it again to deselect it.
6.	Once you have selected all the messages you wish to approve or delete, select Approve Selected Messages or Delete Selected Messages below the table. Those two buttons will only appear after messages are specified in the table. 
What do I need to do to operate my list?
Your responsibilities depend on the type of list you have.
General mailing lists
These are static lists of member email addresses provided and maintained by the list's owner. General mailing lists are handled by Mailman, not RAMS. Information on requesting Mailman mailing lists can be found in the Mailman knowledge article.
Official mailing lists
These are primarily for official University announcements. The owner of the list specifies a demographic category, and the list of member email addresses is sourced from Rutgers databases. Follow the guide on requesting a new RAMS list.
Class mailing lists
These are for announcements and class discussions outside of regular class meeting hours and are created through the class list creator.
The list creator requires a valid Rutgers NetID and password. In addition, access to class sections is governed by your roster privileges, which may be obtained by contacting your Dean/Director/Department Chair or your designated assistant responsible for assigning privileges.
Tips, caveats, and other information
•	If you want to confirm that a message has been sent to the list, look in the Archive section of that list.
•	If you need to ensure a mailing is approved immediately, don't wait for the approval link in the confirmation email. Instead, use the web interface.
•	If it is an emergency and you need a message sent immediately, you can skip the primetime wait by using the List Manager's override feature. 
o	Please note that the primetime override feature is monitored. Abuse of this feature may be construed as a violation of the University's Acceptable Use Policy and may turn your list off.
•	Do not reply to informational messages advising that your message has been submitted to the moderator for approval. You will keep receiving more of them as the system treats replies as new message submissions.
•	Suggestions for new RAMS list features or ways to improve RAMS are welcome. Submit your comments to help@oit.rutgers.edu.
Additional information
Further information can be found in the RAMS documentation.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) RAMS troubleshooting guide
body:
Table of contents
•	Troubleshooting sending issues 
o	I submitted a message to a list, but nothing happened
o	Messages are sent twice
o	Subscribing to a list
•	Troubleshooting recipient issues 
o	Changing a recipient's email addresses
o	Some people are not receiving emails from the list
o	Receiving unwanted email
•	Troubleshooting moderation issues 
o	I can moderate messages through the web, but not via the approval link in the confirmation email
•	Troubleshooting administrative issues 
o	I cannot log in to the web tools
o	A member of my list does not want to receive email/wants to be removed
•	Additional information
Troubleshooting sending issues
I submitted a message to a list, but nothing happened
•	Many lists are moderated, and your message will not be delivered until a Moderator approves it.
•	Approved messages will be delivered immediately if the list has no primetime hours set or if the message was sent during the list's primetime hours. For lists with primetime hours, any messages sent outside those hours will be held until the list's primetime.
•	If the primetime hours have passed and you have not seen your message and cannot find it in the archives, you should contact the list owner to check the email's status. To do so, send an email to listname-owner@rams.rutgers.edu (replace listname with the actual name of the list).
Messages are sent twice
•	This is most likely a problem with your email client or server. Contact your local Help Desk for assistance with this issue.
Subscribing to a list
•	Many lists will accept additional recipients. Contact the list owners by email at listname-owner@rams.rutgers.edu (replace listname with the actual name of the list) and explain your request to be added to the list.
•	RAM technical Support Staff do not have the authority to add you to lists.
Troubleshooting recipient issues
Changing a recipient's email addresses
•	RAMS delivers mail to the email address listed in the Rutgers Online Directory. If someone is no longer receiving emails at that address, they must visit the NetID Management Tool page and select Manage Display Address to change the email address. If the listed email address is correct and they still cannot receive mail, they should contact their campus Help Desk for assistance.
Some people are not receiving emails from the list
•	Verify that those who did not receive the email are on the list.
•	Verify that the people who did not receive the message are reading emails from the address listed in the Rutgers Online Directory. This is the email RAMS uses to deliver mail. If they use the address in the Rutgers Online Directory, ask them to check their Junk or Spam folders. If they still cannot find the message, contact your local Help Desk.
•	If they read the email from an address other than that listed in the Rutgers Online Directory, please ask them to read it at that address and/or update their Directory entry. They may update their entry by visiting the Manage Display Address tab in the NetID Management Tool.
Receiving unwanted email
•	RAMS lists are generated with demographic data. If you are receiving mail from a RAMS list, it is because you fit the demographics for that list. Examples are all students in a course or all full-time Newark employees. If you believe you are receiving a RAMS list you should not be on, contact your local Help Desk and ask them to check whether you are receiving email in error. If the Help Desk can verify an error, you will be removed from the list. If the Help Desk cannot verify the error, they will not be able to remove you from the list.
•	You may contact the list owners by sending an email to listname-owner@rams.rutgers.edu (replace listname with the actual name of the list) and request that they remove you from that list. Please remember that these are official University lists, and the Administrators are not required to remove you just because you do not wish to receive the list email. Some of the official announcements are made by the university under legal obligation.
Troubleshooting moderation issues
I can moderate messages through the web, but not via the approval link in the confirmation email
•	Verify that your email address is listed as a moderator for your list. If it does not match, either send your approval messages from the listed moderator address or update the listed email address. If your email address does not match the listed moderator address, contact your local Help Desk for assistance.
Troubleshooting administrative issues
I cannot log in to the web tools
•	Your NetID is needed to log in to the RAMS administrative features.
•	If you believe you are entering your NetID and password but still cannot log in, contact your local Help Desk for assistance.
A member of my list does not want to receive email/wants to be removed
•	RAMS lists are populated based on rosters or demographically selected members. RAMS does not allow you to remove members from those lists. If a list member does not wish to receive these emails and the list Administrator (professor or department chair) approves, you can turn off email delivery for those who do not want to receive them.
•	Review the RAMS documentation for more information on Managing Membership. 
Additional information
Further information can be found in the RAMS Documentation.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) Requesting a new class or course RAMS list
body:
Class or Course Mailing Lists are for announcements and class discussions outside of normal class meeting hours.
How Do I Request a Class or Course Mailing List?
The RAMS Class List Creator is a tool for creating automated mailing lists based on the roster information for a class or class section. It allows professors or teaching assistants to create mailing lists for any combination of all the sections of all the classes they have roster privileges for.
To get roster privileges, contact the dean, director, or department chair of the department for the class you need access to. RAMS and Help Desk personnel will not be able to assist you with getting roster access.
1.	To create a Class Mailing List begin by going to the Class List Creator.
2.	RAMS will request you login with your NetID and NetID password.

	Allowed characters: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - or _

o	Archiving Policy: The message archiving policy for this mailing list:

o	Posting Policy: The policy governs who can post to the list, for more details, please refer to the List Management Posting Policy for more details. Please note, that for Moderated, Admin Only, and Closed Moderated it will also require you to fill in the Moderator NetID and Moderator Email fields.
o	Owner NetID: The NetID of the person who will be the primary owner and maintainer of the list. Additional owners can be added later from the List Management Manage Administrators area.

This field is only visible when the Posting Policy is set to Moderated, Admin Only, and Closed Moderated.
4.	If there have been no errors, you have completed creating your RAMS list.
Reusing a Class List
