title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) Spam filtering for RAMS
body:
All email sent through RAMS is processed by a spam tagging program called SpamAssassin. SpamAssassin applies a series of tests to each email that comes in. Each test has a score value that is assigned to the email. SpamAssassin combines the test results into a global score. The higher the given score, the more spam-like the message is. A score of 10.0 or more is very likely to be spam, while a message of 4.0 or less is far less likely to be spam.
List owners can turn spam filtering on or off as well as set a score threshold for each of their lists. 
Please note that it is possible for a legitimate email to end up with a high spam score, sometimes resulting in what's called a false positive. These false positives, as well as all other spam, are placed into a Moderator Queue that can be viewed by logging into the RAMS List Manager. Please see the RAMS: List Moderation documentation for more information on approving and deleting messages held for moderation.
Activating and Setting Spam Filtering
1.	To activate spam filtering and set your spam threshold value, first log into the RAMS List Manager using your NetID.
2.	Once logged in, select a list to work on.
3.	Select Manage Configuration in the Actions section.
4.	Set Spam Filter to On.
5.	Enter a number in the Spam Threshold. The Office of Information Technology (OIT) recommends starting with a spam threshold of 5, which is also the default if no number is entered. You may adjust this number at any time if you decide you need your list to be more or less restrictive.
Note: Spam filtering defaults to On for RAMS lists.
How RAMS handles Spam
For RAMS lists with spam filtering turned on, messages that meet or exceed the spam threshold number will be placed in the moderation queue for that list. This mail is not sent to the list or to owners or moderators and can only be accessed via the web interface. Please see the RAMS List Moderation documentation for information on how to view, approve, or delete these messages.
Managing Spam in the Moderation Queue
All messages in the Moderation Queue will be deleted 30 days after it arrives. This means no action is needed by owners, moderators, or editors unless you wish to review the spam to check for false positives. Please see the RAMS List Moderation documentation for instructions on how to review the messages in the Moderation Queue.
Managing Spam in the List
If spam manages to get through to the list, you can choose to lower the threshold number, making the spam filter more strict. OIT recommends lowering it one level at a time to avoid false positives. For example, don't jump from 5 to 2, but instead lower it first to 4 and, if necessary, lower it again later.
If you continue to struggle with spam reaching your list, you might wish to consider switching the list's posting privileges to more restrictive settings: going from Closed to Moderated, or Closed Moderated. If spam is overwhelming the moderators, you may wish to consider increasing security by changing your list to a Closed Moderated or Admin Only list (see the List Manager Manual for more information).

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) Using RAMS to send and receive messages
body:
Submitting a Message to a List
When submitting a message to a RAMS list, use the address as listname@rams.rutgers.edu, (where listname is the actual list name). Anyone wishing to submit a message to the list simply sends an e-mail message to the address. How the message is processed depends upon the list type:
Closed List
When a message is sent to a closed RAMS list, the message sender's e-mail address is checked against the RAMS list's members. If the sender is a member of the RAMS list, the message will be forwarded to all list members. If the message's sender is not a member of the RAMS list, the message will not be forwarded to the list and the sender will get a rejection notice informing them that they are not authorized to post to that list.
Note: A message sent by someone who subscribes to a closed list under one address but replies from another address will be rejected. People who forward their mail to another account may be affected by this.
Moderated List
Many lists are moderated. When a message is sent to a moderated RAMS list, a notification is first sent to the moderators of that list. If a moderator approves it, the message will be forwarded to everyone on the list. If it is rejected, the sender will get a rejection notice. If no action is taken, the message will remain in the moderation queue for the list until it is either approved, rejected, or deleted.
Admin Only
With this type of list, if the message's sender is not an Owner, Moderator, or Editor of the RAMS list, they will get an error message. Mail from Owners, Moderators, and Editors is held until approved. Once approved, the message will be forwarded to everyone on the list.
Closed Moderated
If the message's sender is a member of the RAMS list, it will be held until a Moderator or Administrator approves it. Messages from non-members will be rejected with an error message.
Primetime
Many lists have a Primetime setting. This setting controls when e-mails are allowed to be forwarded to a list. List Administrators do not control a list's Primetime setting but can request changes by e-mailing their campus Help Desk.
•	The default Primetime window for an official New Brunswick list is from 19:00 (7 PM) to 08:00 (AM).
•	The default Primetime window for an official Camden or Newark list is from 17:00 (5 PM) to 08:00 (AM).
Once approved, any message sent to a list with a Primetime setting is held until the Primetime window. Mail sent to a list during Primetime will be immediately delivered. Mail sent to a list outside its Primetime hours will be held until the Primetime hours.
Class lists and specific announcement lists do not have a Primetime setting. A message will be sent to these lists as soon as RAMS receives it.
Additional Resources
Further information can be found in the RAMS documentation, or you can contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: Automated Mailing Systems (RAMS) Using the RAMS list manager
body:
The RAMS List Manager allows you to maintain each of your RAMS mailing lists.
The List Manager will require you to log in unless you have already done so. Use your Rutgers NetID and password to log in.
Once you have logged in, you will be presented with a list of RAMS lists for which you have administrative access. Select the name of the list you would like to administer to view it. 
Table of Contents
•	List Information 
o	General
o	Statistics
o	Logs
•	Actions 
o	Manage Membership
o	Display Class Membership
o	Manage Administrators
o	Manage Configuration
o	Manage List Definition
•	Pending Moderation 
o	Approve or Delete Pending Moderation Messages
•	Pending Primetime 
o	What Does Primetime Mean?
o	Release or Delete Pending Primetime Messages
•	Archive
•	Additional Information
List Information
The List Information card contains multiple tabs (some of which you may not see depending on your level of access).
General
The General tab provides a quick overview of a mailing list's configuration and settings. 
Statistics
The Statistics tab provides an overview of the mailing list's activity and includes the following metrics:
•	Number of messages: Displays the total number of messages sent through the mailing list.
•	Average number of recipients: Shows the average number of recipients per message.
•	Total number of recipients: Indicates the cumulative number of recipients for all messages.
•	Last message sent on: Provides the date and time of the most recent message sent.
•	Average message size: Displays the average size of messages in bytes.
•	Total message size: Shows the cumulative size of all messages in bytes.
Logs
The Logs tab is only visible to RAMS administrators and provides a detailed history of changes made to the mailing list.
Actions
Manage Membership
Allows mailing list owners the ability to manage the mailing list's membership exceptions list. The exception list allows owners to include additional people, along with excluding people from the mailing list. Enter a new or existing recipient's email address, select the appropriate Exception Type, and select Update.
The following exception types are available:
•	Receive and Post Emails: The user can both receive emails and post messages to the mailing list.
•	Only Receive Emails, No Posting: The user can receive emails but cannot post messages to the mailing list.
•	No Emails, Only Posting: The user cannot receive emails but can post messages to the mailing list.
•	No Emails, No Posting: The user is excluded from both receiving emails and posting messages to the mailing list.
To remove someone from the exceptions list, if necessary, search for them using the Search Exception List field. Once you have found the person you want to remove or modify, select them in the table and click Remove Selected Exceptions that will appear below the table. You can then add them back again with a new exception type if necessary. No changes are made until Save is selected.
Display Class Membership
This action is only available for class mailing lists and allows mailing list owners to display the current members of the class mailing list.
Search Members
Use the search field to quickly locate a member by name, email address or course number.
Pagination
At the bottom of the table, you will find a pagination section to navigate through multiple pages of members. You can adjust the number of rows displayed per page using the # entries per page option at the top of the table.
Export options
At the bottom of all tables, you will see two export options that allow you to download the table's list into a CSV or Excel file.
Manage Administrators
Enables mailing list owners the ability to assign or remove administrative privileges (owners, moderators, editors) for the mailing list. Add a new administrator by entering their Rutgers NetID; once you move to the email address field, it'll attempt to automatically populate that field with the person's Rutgers Connect email address. Select the new role for the administrator and then click +.
The following roles are available:
•	Owner: Makes the administrator an additional owner of the list. Owners can modify the configuration of a list, as well as moderate messages through the web interface. 
•	Moderator: Gives the administrator the ability to moderate messages that are sent to the list through email or by using the web interface. Moderators can not modify a list's configuration or membership.
•	Editors: Gives the administrator the ability to moderate messages sent to the list, but they will only be able to do this through the web interface and not through email. Editors will also not receive an email notifying them that there are messages pending moderation. Editors can not modify a list's configuration or membership.
Please note: Do not leave a list without an owner. Navigating away from the page with no owner defined may prevent you from logging back into your list's configuration pages.
Manage Configuration
Provides mailing list owners the ability to modify mailing list settings, such as archive and posting policies, spam filtering, and where mailing list error emails should be sent.
Archiving Policy    
The message archiving policy for the mailing list:
•	Public: All posted messages are archived and available to the public.
•	Admin Only: All posted messages are archived and available to the mailing list administrators only.
Posting Policy    
The policy governing who can post to the list:
•	Moderated: Posted messages are first sent to a moderator for approval. If no action is taken, the message remains in the Pending Moderation area. If approved, the message will be sent out immediately, unless the mailing list has a primetime restriction; in that case, the message is held until the release period opens.
•	Admin Only: Only owners, moderators, or editors of the mailing list can post messages; all others will receive a rejection notice. Posted messages are first sent to a moderator for approval. If approved, the message will be sent out immediately, unless the mailing list has a primetime restriction; in that case, the message is held until the release period opens.
•	Closed: Only members of the mailing list can post messages. If an email is sent from an email address not in the owners, moderators, editors, or members list, the message will be rejected, and the sender will receive a notice. Once a message is received, it will be sent out immediately, unless the mailing list has a primetime restriction; in that case, the message is held until the release period opens.
•	Closed Moderated: Only owners, moderators, editors, or members of the mailing list can send messages; all other messages will be rejected, and the sender will receive a notice. Messages sent to these mailing lists are first sent to a moderator for approval. If approved, the message will be sent out immediately, unless the mailing list has a primetime restriction, in that case the message is held until the release period opens.
•	Open: Anyone can post messages to the mailing list. Once a message is received, it will be sent out immediately unless the mailing list has a primetime restriction; in that case, the message is held until the release period opens. This option is only available to RAMS administrators, not mailing list owners, because this posting policy is dangerous and rarely allowed.
Spam Filtering    
Whether or not spam filtering should be enabled for this mailing list. It is recommended that you always leave this set to On and modify the spam threshold as necessary. Spam filtering simply hides messages that look like spam; you can still see them by using the Show Spam Messages sliders in the Pending Moderation area.
Spam Threshold    
A numeric value that determines at what level a message should be considered spam. To learn more about using the spam filter with RAMS, read Setting a Spam Filter in RAMS.
Errors Setting    
If there is an error notification that needs to be sent, if this setting is set to Owners, all owners of the mailing list will be sent the error notification. When this is set to Ignore, no error notifications will be sent by this mailing list.
Manage List Definition
This action is exclusive to class mailing lists and allows creators to update the course sections that define the membership of an existing class mailing list.
1.	Select the new Year and Term (semester) for the class and click Get Course Sections.
2.	If you have access to classes for the selected year and term, you will be presented with a list of course sections.
3.	Select one or more course sections that you wish to be a part of this mailing list. Multiple course sections can be selected by using the Ctrl/Command or Shift keys along with your mouse. 
4.	Click Save to update your class mailing list.
Pending Moderation
The Pending Moderation card lists messages awaiting approval by the list moderator. By default, messages that are considered spam are not displayed. Turn the Show Spam Messages slider to the on position to see messages flagged as spam. The table supports pagination, allowing you to adjust the number of rows displayed (entries per page) and navigate between pages (bottom right of the table). Use the Search Moderation field to find messages by subject or sender. Select View next to a message to read its full content. If you wish to export the table, select CSV or Excel at the bottom of the table. If you wish to export all messages in the table, first change the Entries per page at the top of the table to All and then export. Use the Refresh icon above the table to refresh the table and load the latest messages.
Approve or Delete Pending Moderation Messages
To approve or delete messages, select the desired messages in the table by clicking on the row. The row will become highlighted. Click again to deselect a row. Once you have selected all the messages you wish to approve or delete, click Approve Selected Messages or Delete Selected Messages below the table. Those two buttons will only appear after messages are selected in the table. If you would like to delete all messages in the table, simply select Delete All Messages.
Pending Primetime
The Pending Primetime card lists messages scheduled for release during the primetime hours (Release Period). The table supports pagination, allowing you to adjust the number of rows displayed (entries per page) and navigate between pages (bottom right of the table). Use the Search Moderation field to find messages by subject or sender. Select View next to a message to read its full content. If you wish to export the table, select CSV or Excel at the bottom of the table. If you wish to export all messages in the table, first change the Entries per page at the top of the table to All and then export. Use the Refresh icon above the table to refresh the table and load the latest messages.
What Does Primetime Mean?
Many RAMS mailing lists have a primetime setting (release period) that controls when emails can be sent. If a message is sent outside the primetime window and does not require moderation, it will be held and not released until the primetime window is entered. Similarly, for moderated emails, even if a moderator or owner approves the message, it will still be held until the primetime window is entered if the mailing list has a primetime setting. Class mailing lists and some announcement lists do not have this setting. The default primetime for New Brunswick mailing lists is 7 PM to 8 AM, and for Camden and Newark mailing lists, it's 5 PM to 8 AM.
Release or Delete Pending Primetime Messages
This section is primarily for emergency messages that need to be sent outside the regular schedule (Release Period). Owners, moderators, and editors can release these messages by selecting the desired messages in the table by clicking on a row. The row will become highlighted. Click again to deselect a row. Once you have selected all the messages you wish to release or delete, select Release Selected Messages or Delete Selected Messages below the table. Those two buttons will only appear after messages are selected in the table.
Archive
The Archive card provides access to past messages sent through the mailing list. Owners, moderators, and editors can filter messages by date range or search for specific messages using the Search Archive box. The archive includes details such as the date, subject, sender, number of recipients, and spam level, along with who approved and released the message. Select View next to a message to read its full content. If you wish to export the table, select CSV or Excel at the bottom of the table. If you wish to export all messages in the table, first change the Entries per page at the top of the table to All and then export. Use the Refresh icon above the table to refresh the table and load the latest messages.
Additional Information
For additional information, including the latest updates to RAMS, view the RAMS documentation.

title: Connect Apple Mail Connectivity Issue - 04/05/2026
body:
Overview
Connect Support was made aware of an issue affecting newly enrolled devices in the Rutgers Connect tenant. These devices are experiencing failures when attempting to connect Apple Mail to Rutgers Connect work email accounts. The issue appears immediately after device enrollment. 
 
This Apple Mail connection issue may affect you if:
•	You recently enrolled an iPhone or iPad using Microsoft Intune
•	Your device is registered through Mobile Device Management (MDM)
•	You use Apple Mail for Microsoft 365 work email
•	Microsoft Authenticator is not installed on your iOS device
Common Symptoms
•	Work email does not sync in Apple Mail after device enrollment
•	Repeated sign?in prompts that never complete
•	Apple Mail account setup stalls or returns an authentication error
•	Work email, calendar, or contacts do not appear or load
Important Application Distinction
•	Company Portal: Used to enroll your device and verify compliance with company policies.
•	Microsoft Authenticator: Required to reach device compliance, does NOT need to be logged into/used.
Both applications are required on iOS devices for Apple Mail to complete authentication and sync work email successfully.
Fixing Apple Mail
The resolution we found is to install the Microsoft Authenticator application from the Intune Company Portal on the affected device. Once the Authenticator is installed, Apple Mail will complete the authentication handshake and begin syncing email normally. You do not need to log in to the Microsoft Authenticator application; simply have it downloaded on the device.? 
1.	On your Apple device, you can find and open the Company Portal application. This was installed when you enrolled your device with Intune. 
2.	Sign in to Company Portal with your work credentials (your work email address and password) if prompted. 
3.	Once signed in, tap or click the Apps section in Company Portal. This section lists all applications that your organization has made available. 
4.	Locate Microsoft Authenticator in the apps list. You can use the search bar at the top if needed, and search for "Authenticator" or look for it in the Category “Productivity”. 
5.	Tap Install (iOS/iPadOS) next to Microsoft Authenticator. Company Portal will begin downloading and installing the application. 
6.	Wait for the installation to complete. You will see a confirmation once the app has been successfully installed on your device. 
7.	Go to Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Rutgers Connect and sign in. 
8.	Return to Apple Mail. If the app is still showing an authentication prompt or error, remove the work account and re-add it: go to Settings > Mail > Accounts, remove your work account, then add it again using your work email address. 
9.	Apple Mail should now be able to complete authentication and begin syncing your work email, calendar, and contacts. 
Verify the Fix
After completing the above steps, confirm the following to ensure the issue is resolved:
•	Microsoft Authenticator is installed and visible on your device's home screen/app library 
•	Apple Mail shows your work inbox with emails loading successfully 
•	Sending a test email from Apple Mail completes without error 
•	Calendar events from your M365 account appear in the Apple Calendar app (if configured) 
If you re-add your account and are still seeing issues, try rebooting your device after installing Microsoft Authenticator, then attempt to add the account again in Apple Mail. 
Support
If the steps above do not resolve the issue, contact your IT Help Desk and provide the following information: 
•	Device type and OS version (e.g., iPhone 15, iOS 17.4) 
•	Date and time that you received the error message
•	Serial number of the device, especially if the user has multiple devices registered. 
•	A description of the error or behavior you are seeing
•	Confirmation that Microsoft Authenticator has been installed via Company Portal 
Please note: Connect Support will be automatically pushing the authenticator application to iOS devices at a later date. This fix addresses issues on iOS devices.

title: Connect Changing your default email address in Rutgers Connect
body:
When a Rutgers Connect account is created, the default email address the account will send mail from is in the format (netid@domain.rutgers.edu). This is referred to as your account's Primary Address. Some users may prefer to change their primary address to a personalized email address (john.doe@rutgers.edu). Your Rutgers Connect account can only be configured for one primary address at a time. You can change and update this address at any time; however, you will only be able to send email from your primary address.
To change your primary address in Rutgers Connect, please follow the directions below. Changes may take up to 2 hours to take effect. 
1.	Go to the NetID Management page and click on Manage Email Addresses.
2.	Log in with your NetID and NetID password.
3.	Scroll down to the Rutgers Connect Account Information section and choose a primary Email Address from the drop-down box.
4.	Click Update.
How to set your primary address in OWA and Mail Clients:
•	Outlook Web Access (OWA) will automatically update your default address to be the primary address you selected.
•	Outlook will automatically start sending mail from the primary address you selected. Please note that the "From" field in Outlook will still show as your sign-in address (netid@domain.rutgers.edu), but your mail will be sent from the primary address you selected.
Please note you can log into your Rutgers Connect account with your primary address or your netid@domain.rutgers.edu.
If you would like confirmation on what your Rutgers Connect sign-in information is, please go to the NetID Management page and click on Manage Email Addresses. Your sign-in name can be found in the Rutgers Connect Account Information section.
The Rutgers Connect Account Information page will also show you the secondary addresses your account can receive mail at in Rutgers Connect. You will not be able to send mail using these addresses unless you select one of them to be your primary address.

title: Connect Clipchamp
body:
Microsoft Clipchamp is available for all Faculty and Staff through their Rutgers Connect accounts. 
Clipchamp is Microsoft’s supported video editing tool and works with content created across Microsoft 365. With it, you can edit items such as PowerPoint screen recordings, Teams voice or video recordings, and other video files stored in OneDrive or SharePoint. The tool supports basic editing tasks, such as trimming clips, combining recordings, adding text or captions, and exporting finished videos.
You can access Clipchamp from the Microsoft 365 app launcher or from the Clipchamp website. You may also see options to open or edit certain recordings in Clipchamp as part of existing workflows (for example, after creating a screen recording). title: Connect Common use cases for SharePoint
body:
The right collaboration environment is crucial for department performance, engagement, and innovation. SharePoint’s versatility allows the service to be utilized for a large variety of objectives ranging from basic information storage to complex project dashboards.
Table of Contents
•	Content Management
•	Intranets
•	Business process Automation/Workflow Management
•	Project Management
Content Management
SharePoint allows users to create, edit, submit, approve and publish 2.5 TB worth of content for a given site collection or group. This content can be shared and made viewable to specified users. Using built-in document libraries and lists, users can organize where they store their content within a site. Content can consist of a variety of types (text, video, graphics, audio). The most important content management capabilities of SharePoint include:
•	Versioning
•	Real-time collaboration
•	Approvals
•	Indexing
•	Search
Intranets
SharePoint excels as an intranet platform as it offers a wide variety of out-of-the-box functionalities. These capabilities let users design an effective intranet for their department with ease. These features consist of:
•	Branded home page
•	Multi-functional web parts that integrate with various Microsoft services
•	Custom navigation
•	Flexible content sharing options
•	Modern/classic team and communication sites
•	Social features (communities, forums, media galleries)
•	Mobile access
Error! Filename not specified.
Business process Automation/Workflow Management
SharePoint supports business process management as it offers a variety of options for implementing, maintaining, and executing workflows. Many common workflow processes come built-in to the service such as getting approvals, collecting feedback, and acquiring signatures. Furthermore, SharePoint integrates with a variety of Office 365 tools (Word, OneNote, OneDrive) which facilitates the creation of content-related workflows. Users can create custom workflows through SharePoint’s integration with Power Automate (formerly Microsoft Flow).
Project Management
SharePoint is a popular and practical solution for project management, as it allows a project’s information to be stored in a central place. Using the out-of-the-box project management features, SharePoint holds the capabilities for successful project visibility, reporting, collaboration, and delivery. A SharePoint site acts as home for a user's project information and content. A SharePoint site collection collects multiple projects into a project portfolio. title: Connect Creating and updating Email signatures in Connect
body:
Creating or updating your signature
To create your email signature on Rutgers Connect, follow the instructions below. You may also create and update your signature on both the Classic and New versions of Outlook for Windows or Outlook for Mac. 
1.	Log in to Rutgers Connect and click the gear icon at the top right-hand side.
2.	Navigate to Mail > Compose and Reply > Email Signature.
3.	Create your signature using these recommendations: 
o	Type and format your signature inside the Outlook signature window. Creating your signature in an outside program (like Word) and copying into the window may cause formatting issues. 
o	Use a common font such as Calibri or Times New Roman. Other fonts may not display correctly.
o	Use a single font color such as black or gray.
o	Example signature format: 
	First Name Last Name (pronouns optional)
Job title
Department/group/unit
Specific campus and/or Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
Preferred contact phone number
Office address (optional)
Website/social media links (optional)
4.	You may also add a Rutgers logotype to your signature. Instructions on how to get a Rutgers logotype for use in your signature is listed in the section below.  
1.	Click in your signature where you want the logotype to appear.
2.	Click on the Insert Image icon in the toolbar.
3.	Navigate to the file you want to use, as described in the next section, and click Open. 
4.	Resize the image as needed. 
5.	Click Save. 
Getting the Rutgers logotype for use in your signature
Using the standard Rutgers University logotype
1.	Go to the Email Signatures section of the Rutgers University Stationery and Templates page. 
2.	Select the desired logotype format.
3.	This will bring you to a SharePoint page where you can download the .SVG file to be used in your email signature. The all Red option is best for both light and dark mode on devices. The Red and Black option is most visible in light mode on devices. 
Using your departmental specific logotype
If your department has a specific logotype (ex: Office of Information Technology, Mason Gross School of the Arts, New Jersey Medical School, Office for Research, etc.) you have to first obtain it from the Rutgers University Signature Generator. Note that the Signature Generator does not create a signature for you; it only provides the logotype file to be used in your signature. It's recommended to use the .SVG file type for an email signature. 
1.	Log in to the Rutgers University Signature Generator.
2.	Click Search to look through the existing approved logotypes. 
3.	Locate the department you are in and click Download Package.  
o	Any packages that are labeled "(vertical R)" do not contain the email signature logotype. Download a package not labeled as vertical instead. 
o	If your department is not listed, you may return to the previous page and click Request to fill out the form requesting a logotype be created for your department. 
4.	Open the .zip file that was downloaded. 
5.	Open the E-SIGNATURE folder and use the .svg file.

title: Connect Email encryption for Rutgers Connect
body:
Under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), all communications containing Protected Health Information (PHI) must be encrypted. To ensure the confidentiality of private information sent via email and comply with HIPAA privacy regulations, Rutgers Connect uses multiple approaches to keep your information safe.
All email sent by users with PHI flags is automatically protected with TLS Secure email. TLS is a cryptographic protocol that provides security between email servers. Most email servers are configured to receive email sent via TLS. Rutgers is aware of some common email servers that are not equipped for TLS. If a PHI-flagged person sends an email to one of these known email servers, Rutgers Connect will automatically use the built-in capabilities of Office 365's Office Message Encryption (OME) to protect your email.
If a PHI-flagged person attempts to send an email to an email server that does not support TLS and is not known to Rutgers Connect, the sender will receive a bounce-back. Please review the following article to learn more about what to expect if you encounter this issue.
Please note: For backward compatibility with our previous encryption service, Zix Corporation, any message containing the keyword “ZIXSECURE” in the subject or body and leaving Rutgers Connect will have OME encryption applied. OIT does not recommend using keywords to force encryption. The keyword feature has been retained for specialized cases and may be removed completely in the future, as it is being replaced by OME's encryption features.
Secure messaging is not just a government mandate; it is a practical way to conduct business. Email is not a private conversation; unencrypted email messages can be intercepted and read. Users can also protect emails that do not contain Protected Health Information by using the options provided by Office Message Encryption (OME).
The following documentation pages explain how Office Message Encryption (OME) works.
•	Recipient Experience
•	Sending Encrypted Email

6.	Wait for the installation to complete. You will see a confirmation once the app has been successfully installed on your device. 
5.	You do not need to log in to the Microsoft Authenticator application; simply have it downloaded on the device.? 
6.	Go to your iPhone/iPad Settings > Apps > Mail > Mail Accounts > Rutgers Connect and sign in. 
7.	Return to the Apple Mail app. If the app is still showing an authentication prompt or error, remove the work account and re-add it: go to Settings > Mail > Accounts, remove your work account, then add it again using your work email address.

Additional information can be found in the article Apple Mail Connectivity Issue - 04/05/2026.

title: Connect Exporting Publisher files
body:
Microsoft has announced permanent retirement for Microsoft Publisher on October 1, 2026. After that date, Publisher will no longer be included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions, and support for existing versions will end. 
Considering this, it's recommend to convert your existing files to another format before the October 1, 2026 support cutoff. After this date, you will no longer be able to open or edit these files in Microsoft Publisher.  
Details
After October 1, 2026:
•	Publisher will be removed from Microsoft 365 installations.
•	Microsoft 365 subscribers will no longer be able to open or edit Publisher (.pub) files in the application.
Versions include:
•	Publisher for Microsoft 365
•	Publisher 2021 (see note)
•	Publisher 2019 (see note)
•	Publisher 2016
•	Publisher 2013
•	Publisher 2010
Note: Standalone versions (e.g.: "Publisher 2019", "Publisher 2021") may continue to function but will no longer receive updates or security fixes from Microsoft.
Exporting and Modifying Publisher files
Converting Publisher files to PDF (for viewing) 
To view content after Publishers retirement, you can convert the file to a PDF format by:
1.	Open Publisher file.
2.	Go to File > Save as.
3.	Choose a location to save the file.
4.	Select PDF as the file type and Save.
Converting numerous Publisher files
It is highly recommended that you have an IT representative assist you with this method. For assistance in finding or contacting your departmental IT or the OIT Help Desk.
To convert many Publisher files, consider automating this process by using a PowerShell script. You can refer to Example conversion script (located as a dropdown option below the paragraph on the linked site) as a guide.
Converting Publisher files to Word (for editing)
To edit content after Publishers retirement, you can convert the file through Word or through a third-party conversion tool (noted in Alternate option section).
For Word:
1.	Open Word.
2.	Go to File > Open.
3.	Locate and open the PDF file.
4.	Select OK in the dialog box.
From here your document will open as a Word file.
Note: The converted Word document will be optimized for text editing. As a result, its layout may vary from the original PDF—particularly if the document includes many graphics.
Alternate option to convert Publisher files
Using a third-party conversion tool to convert directly from Publisher to another file type.
Note: These services vary in quality and capabilities, and Microsoft does not provide support for them.

     Error! Filename not specified.
Select a Team and Channel
A team is a collection of people, conversations, files, and tools — all in one place. A channel is a discussion topic in a team. The best way to get familiar with teams and channels is to select a team and channel and start exploring. If you're not on a Team and want to create one, please talk to your domain admin.
1.	Select the Teams icon.

     Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Select a channel and explore the Conversations, Files, and Notes tabs.
Channels can be a department, project, or topic. For more info, see Teams and channels.
Getting to Know the Microsoft Teams Layout
When you open Microsoft Teams, the name of the current view is centered at the top of the screen. Microsoft Teams usually opens to the last view you used. A vertical toolbar resides on the left side of the screen. Its upper left corner contains buttons for the main views: Activity, Chat, Teams, Meetings, and Files. Some buttons may not be available, depending on your account type. In the lower left corner of the toolbar are the buttons for Feedback and Settings (your icon). Notification settings are synced with the server; changes made in the browser will be reflected in the desktop client.
The rest of the screen is divided into two panes. Pane content depends on the current view. The left or list pane is used to navigate within the view. It always contains the Search field. The rest of its contents depend on the selected view. For example, if you select Chat on the toolbar, the left pane contains a list of your favorite, recent, and suggested contacts.
The right or main pane takes up most of the screen. It shows the content of the selection you have made in the left pane. For example, if you selected Chat on the toolbar and then selected a recent contact in the left pane, the right pane contains your conversation history with that person. The right pane also has tabs to keep the content organized. For example, in Chat view, the Conversation tab contains the conversation history, the Files tab contains a list of the files shared between you and the selected contact, the Organization tab shows the position of the selected contact in the organization chart, and so on.

title: Connect Manage your Connect Devices and Licenses
body:
With the number of devices now used for work, it can be confusing to figure out which site you need to go to to troubleshoot issues you might be facing. The following guide is intended to help you reach the correct device management page for Connect-related services.
•	Personal Device Registrations – These are devices you may have registered through the Intune Company Portal app to access your email or other services offered by Rutgers. In most cases, these are cell phones, but if you registered a tablet, it would fall under this category as well.
•	Office Activations – Your Office license includes 5 activations you can use on any devices you want. The devices that will show on this list are the ones you’ve signed into Office with your Connect credentials.
•	Accidental Device Registrations – These often come up during an Office activation.
Personal Device Registrations
Registering your device through the Intune Company Portal app allows you to access various Rutgers-approved apps for work use and, most importantly, provides access to your email and calendar on the go.
You can have up to 20 devices registered, with no more than 5 per OS (iOS, iPadOS, Android, Android for Work, Windows). It is recommended to remove device registrations when you no longer use those devices. You can manage your Intune-registered devices in two locations:
•	Via the Microsoft Device Portal.
o	This will take you to a landing page where you will see any device currently registered through the Intune Company Portal app. You can click on each one to see more details. More information on all the available options on this page can be found on Microsoft’s self-service guide.
•	Through the Intune Company Portal app on your registered device
o	By launching the app, you will see a list of your registered devices by default, where you can tap any device to see more details.
If you need to add a new device or remove an old one, please review the guides on enabling mobile device management on Android or iOS, which will walk you through the entire process from start to finish.
Office Activations
You may see an error that you cannot use Microsoft apps after signing in to Office, and receive an alert that it’s running in “reduced functionality” mode. This usually means that you have too many Office activations, and it isn’t necessarily a problem with your device itself. While Microsoft says it will automatically deactivate the oldest registered device, it is best to verify this by visiting the Get Office webpage.
Once it loads, you should see a Devices dropdown menu where you will then be presented with all the devices you are currently signed into Office with that are using an activation.
Error! Filename not specified.
To free up activations for whatever new device you’re trying to register with, click the Sign out button on any extra devices you know you aren’t using Office apps on. Once you’re under the limit, you should be able to use the Office apps installed on the new device.
Accidental Registrations
At some point, you may have accidentally registered a personal computer with Rutgers without even realizing it. While it might not be immediately noticeable, accidentally linking your work account to your personal computer can have unintended consequences that may interrupt your use of the machine. Make sure to follow this guide through to completion prior to your Faculty, Staff, Student, or Guest role with Rutgers ends. Otherwise, you might be left needing to completely format your Windows PC if you wait until after you’ve left the university, retired, or become an Alumni.

title: Connect Microsoft 365 groups
body:
Microsoft 365 Groups is a collaborative feature within Rutgers Connect that enables users to access shared versions of the following:
A Microsoft 365 group lets you choose a set of people you want to collaborate with and easily set up a collection of resources for them to share. Items in the group's resources (Calendar, OneDrive, OneNote) will automatically be shared with the group's members.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page on adding/removing Group members.
Microsoft 365 groups within Rutgers Connect currently offer the following resources.
Shared inbox
Each group has a shared inbox accessible to all members. This shared inbox is fully searchable, creating a living archive of the group's messages. Newcomers to the group can search or scroll through the history to quickly get up to speed on what's been posted.
Messages addressed to the group's common email address will be delivered to this inbox. Members of the group can elect to have group messages appear in their personal inbox by subscribing to the group via email.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared Email.
Shared files library
Your group has a SharePoint file library where your users can store, share, and collaborate on documents, workbooks, presentations, images, or any other kind of file they need to work on.
Files stored in the group's file library can be edited using Microsoft Office desktop products as well as Office Online (Word Online, Excel Online, PowerPoint Online, etc.). These files have version control, which will track all changes made and also allow recovery to previous versions. Group libraries can also be shared with users external to the group.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared files library.
Shared calendar
Each group owns a shared calendar to post events related to the group. Each member who has subscribed to the group is automatically invited to events posted to the calendar, so those events can also appear on their personal calendars if they wish.
Group calendars can be shared with users external to the group.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page for Office 365's Shared Calendar.
Shared OneNote Notebook
The group automatically has a shared OneNote notebook where group members can collect and collaborate on information.
•	
o	OneNote allows information to be organized in multiple tiers – notebooks, sections, pages, and subpages – which makes it easy to peruse only the relevant documentation. It also offers highly capable search functionality; users can search across all the information they have access to, or search only in a single page, section, or notebook. Additionally, it allows embedding a wide variety of media types, including images, audio recordings, and videos, to provide a more immersive and in-depth information-gathering experience.
o	Another common application is creating and storing meeting notes. As mentioned, OneNote allows users to embed audio recordings, and it also lets users record audio within OneNote. Recording can start at the beginning of the meeting without preventing any further note-taking; the person responsible for meeting notes can continue taking notes for the duration of the recording. Furthermore, any notes taken during this time will be associated with the appropriate time in the recording. If there is a brief note about a topic of interest, the note can be clicked on at a later time, and the recording will jump to the point at which that note was taken, so there is no need to sift through a long recording to find the bit of information you want.
o	Another feature of OneNote is handwriting recognition, so those who are more comfortable taking notes by hand can do so on a tablet or touchscreen-enabled computer, and their handwriting will be automatically converted to typed text.
Although there are many other uses for OneNote, the last one mentioned here is brainstorming. As the notebook is shared with all group members and can be updated in real time, colleagues can collaborate remotely by typing and drawing on a virtual paper that everyone can see at once.
To access OneNote, select the Notebook located on the top navigation bar in the group's view.

     Error! Filename not specified.
Guest access
You could add external contacts to distribution groups before, but all they got was email. With groups, you can offer guests access to email conversations, files, and even the shared OneNote notebook.
For additional information, visit the Microsoft page on Guest access.
If you would like to request the creation of an Office 365 group, please contact your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator.

title: Connect Microsoft Bookings
body:
Microsoft Bookings is a scheduling tool that assists with booking appointments, and it is included with your Rutgers Connect Office 365 license. There are many ways to use Bookings in a university environment. An individual faculty member could use it to create a calendar where students could request office hour appointments, or a department chair or administrator could create an office hours calendar with slots for multiple faculty members.
You should be able to see the Bookings tab listed in the application menu after logging in to Rutgers Connect. Before you can access Bookings, however, you must either create a new Booking Calendar or be added to an existing Booking Calendar.
A Booking Calendar is a space where scheduling appointments can be made. Please note that currently, you are not able to create a Booking Calendar yourself through the Bookings application. You can contact your department or unit IT support to set up your Booking site to begin scheduling appointments. Once your Booking Calendar has been created by your department or unit IT support and you have been made an owner, you should be able to open the Bookings tab via your Rutgers Connect account and immediately access the site.
You can learn more about Bookings in this article from Microsoft, which goes into greater detail about the product.
     Error! Filename not specified.
Table of Contents
•	Scheduling
•	Calendar
•	Booking Page
•	Staff
•	Services
•	Business Information
•	Additional Information
Scheduling
Bookings can be scheduled by either a user looking to make an appointment or a staff member with access to the Booking calendar. You can set up a booking page that allows users to schedule their own appointments, similar to what you might see if you have booked an appointment online to get a haircut or have your car serviced. Alternatively, you or another faculty or staff member can enter the bookings manually, such as when a user or customer calls for an appointment.
Calendar
The Calendar section lets you manually create and assign new Booking slots to users and staff members. It’s also where you can view all slots in your Bookings Calendar.
In order to manually set up and assign Booking slots, you will first need to create an entry for the customer in the “Customers” Booking tab. This will allow you to schedule appointments on behalf of users by inputting their contact information and details – the same details a user would need to provide if they were scheduling themselves for a Bookings slot. Next, navigate to the “Calendar” tab. Here you will be able to assign a Booking to both a customer and a staff member for a specific slot. This is a great feature for those who wish to keep their calendar hidden and keep track of appointments themselves within the app.
Booking Page
The Booking Page tab lets you make changes to and publish or unpublish the Booking Calendar. It also provides you with notification and scheduling settings that you can configure for your calendar. Here is what a published Bookings site looks like, where users can assign themselves to slots on a calendar when specified. 
     Error! Filename not specified.
Staff
Staff members are the employees that the users or customers book appointments with. If, for example, you were making a Bookings Calendar for an academic department office hours, these would be the department faculty. To add staff members to your Bookings Calendar, navigate to the Staff page and select Add Staff Member. This will bring up details you can edit for each member you wish to add. You can edit a staff member’s availability, contact information, and role: Administrator, Viewer or Guest.
Staff members can then be assigned to a variety of slots based on the availability presented on their Rutgers Connect calendar.
Administrators	Can open and configure the Booking Calendar. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be the department chair or the administrative assistant. It could also be the faculty members if they want to manage their own booking calendar.
Viewers	Can open the Booking Calendar and view settings, but can’t make changes. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be a student worker who you want to be able to view, but not change, appointments.
Guest	Can be assigned to a Booking slot, but cannot open the Booking Calendar. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be a faculty member who is not managing the entire Booking calendar.
Customers	Are users who are booking the slots in the Calendar with a staff member. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be the students booking office hours appointments.
 
     Error! Filename not specified.
Services
The Service tab is where you can edit the name of the service you are providing through your Booking Calendar. This is what customers see when a Booking Calendar is published – it should define the purpose of the Booking. If we use the example of a department using bookings for faculty office hours, this might be "Office Hours."
Business Information
The Business Information tab lets you configure the overall name of your calendar as well as the business/office hours, contact information and logo so that customers can easily identify the group associated with the service.
The slots that are created in the calendar are unique to the Booking Calendar itself.
Additional Information
You can find more advanced documentation on using Microsoft Bookings on Microsoft's support site.
Be sure to explore all capabilities of Bookings before publishing your calendar. If you have any questions or concerns regarding Bookings, please contact your local IT or the OIT Help Desk.

title: Connect Microsoft Publisher End-of-Life
body:
End of Support October 1, 2026
Microsoft has announced that it will permanently retire Microsoft Publisher on October 1, 2026. After that date, Publisher will no longer be included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions, and support for existing versions will end.
While Publisher is not widely used across Rutgers, it is currently installed on a number of university-managed devices and has been launched by approximately 500 users over the past year. We are sharing this information now to ensure awareness well in advance of the retirement date.
Details
After October 1, 2026:
•	Publisher will be removed from Microsoft 365 installations.
•	Microsoft 365 subscribers will no longer be able to open or edit Publisher (.pub) files in the application.
Versions include:
•	Publisher for Microsoft 365
•	Publisher 2021 (see note)
•	Publisher 2019 (see note)
•	Publisher 2016
•	Publisher 2013
•	Publisher 2010
Note: Standalone versions (e.g.: "Publisher 2019", "Publisher 2021") may continue to function but will no longer receive updates or security fixes from Microsoft.
User preparation
Microsoft recommends converting existing .pub files to PDF or Word prior to October 2026. It is understood that file conversions may not fully preserve formatting or layout, and users should plan accordingly. 
Next steps
It's recommended that departmental IT begin identifying any supported users who may rely on Publisher so they can plan ahead. The Office of Information Technology has created documentation instructions for exporting Microsoft Publisher files that are in the .pub format to PDF or Word, as well as recommendations for Rutgers-supported alternate applications.

title: Connect Migrating Rutgers Connect Personal Data to ScarletMail
body:
Upon separation from the University, please arrange to transfer all Rutgers property (including electronic data) to the appropriate authority. For departing faculty and staff, the Offboarding Checklist may prove useful. 
After transferring all Rutgers data, you may find some amount of personally owned data remains. Examples of such data include personally-owned scholarly works and student coursework, as described in University Policy 50.3.7. You will not have access to this data on Rutgers Connect following your separation. However, as an alumni or retiree, you may be provided continuing service on ScarletMail. This document describes OIT's suggested method of moving data from a Rutgers Connect account to a ScarletMail account.
This procedure must be used exclusively on personally-owned data. Data classified as Restricted or Critical ePHI under Rutgers Information Classification Policy 70.1.2 must not be transferred to ScarletMail nor any other non-Rutgers system. Doing so may represent a violation of the Federal HIPAA Privacy/Security rules, State Privacy Laws, and/or University policies. Please prepare your data accordingly prior to the migration procedure.
Your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator may have additional details regarding unit-level data practices. Please feel free to engage them with your questions or concerns.
To export the data, you will need to download the Google Workspace Migration Tool. To use this tool, you will need access to:
•	Your ScarletMail account
•	A Microsoft Exchange Profile or an export of your Rutgers Connect account in a .PST file. View Microsoft's support article on How to Create a PST file.
o	Important: If you're using Cached Exchange Mode, Outlook will only export the items in your current cache. By default, your cache contains items from the past 12 months. To export more than the past 12 months of data, turn off Cached Exchange Mode first. For more information, see Turn Cached Exchange Mode on or off.
•	Microsoft Outlook 2010, Microsoft Outlook 2013, Microsoft Outlook 2016, or Microsoft Outlook 2019
•	Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10, or Windows 11. MacOS is NOT supported
This tool will allow you to import mail, calendars, and personal contacts from your Rutgers Connect account to your ScarletMail account.

title: Connect Mobile device management policy
body:
Mobile Device Management for Office 365 has been enabled for all Rutgers Connect Accounts. Mobile Device Management (MDM) helps secure mobile devices to ensure compliance with University policies. While enrolling your device in MDM through the Company Portal App, you will see a notice stating that administrators will be allowed to make a number of changes to your device, but the University will not use those features, as they are beyond policy.
If you are associated with RBHS, review the Mobile Device Management policy for RBHS. 
The MDM policies that are currently in effect for all Rutgers staff and faculty are:
•	A password is required on the device. 
o	Google has set the minimum for personal devices to be a non-repeating, non-sequential 4 digit pin.
o	Apple has set the minimum for personal devices to be a 4 digit pin.
•	Jailbroken or rooted devices (devices that have had basic security measures stripped away from the operating system) will not work.
•	Managing email profile will be required.
•	Remotely wipe a mobile device if it is lost or stolen (this will not occur without the explicit consent of the device’s owner).
•	A device OS version that matches or exceeds the minimum supported version listed in the Office Suite Supported Versions article.
Instructions for enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS and Android devices can be found at the links below.
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on Android Devices
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS Devices

•	BlueMail
•	Newton
•	Typeapp
•	MyMail

title: Connect Mobile device management policy for RBHS
body:
Mobile Device Management for Office 365 has been enabled for the Connect Accounts of those who have PHI flags. The PHI flag is in place to denote those who have access to Protected Health Information (PHI) and must abide by HIPAA regulations on how to store or send their email. Mobile Device Management (MDM) is a way to secure mobile devices so that they are compliant with the requirements of handling PHI. While enrolling your device in MDM through the Company Portal App, you will be prompted by a notice that states administrators will be allowed to make a number of changes to your device but the University will not utilize those features as they are beyond policy.
The MDM policies that are currently in effect for all staff who handle PHI data are:
•	Devices will be wiped after 10 sign-in failures
•	A password will be required on the device. 
o	For iOS, iPadOS, and Corporate Android devices: 
	The password must be at least 6 characters.
	The password must be alphanumeric with 2 character sets (including at least one special character).
o	For Personal and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Android devices: 
	Use either a password with at least 6 alphanumeric characters or a PIN with at least 8 digits.
	Repeating or ordered sequences of 4 or more characters or digits are blocked.
•	Devices will be locked after 15 minutes of inactivity.
•	Devices must have data encryption enabled. Apple devices (iOS devices) have built-in encryption that is automatically enabled but Android devices will need to enable encryption manually. This process is battery-intensive and may take up to an hour to complete, so make sure your device is plugged in while encrypting.
•	Jailbroken or rooted devices (devices with basic security measures stripped away from the operating system) will not work.
•	Managing email profile will be required.
•	A device OS version that matches or exceeds what's listed on the Office Suite Supported Versions article.
•	Removable storage on devices cannot be used.
Note: If your device utilizes a removable media device/removable storage (such as an SD card) the Help Desk advises that you copy the data to another location prior to enabling your device for MDM. Failure to properly copy your data prior to enabling your device may result in a loss of data.
Due to the implementation of MDM, IMAP has been turned off on both mobile and desktop devices for those who have access to PHI. This will require you to connect using Exchange when using your Connect account, which will enforce the MDM rules. You will need to access your Connect account using Outlook Web Access (OWA), Outlook, or a mobile device enrolled in MDM.
Instructions on how to enable iOS and Android devices for Mobile Device Management can be found in the links below.
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on Android Devices
•	Enabling Mobile Device Management on iOS Devices
There are known mail applications that bypass the restrictions of MDM. These applications should not be used as they violate the Rutgers Connect MDM Standard. Below is a list of the currently known applications that are noncompliant:
•	CloudMagic
•	BlueMail
•	Newton
•	Typeapp
•	MyMail
•	SparkMail
If you are leaving the university or no longer wish to have your device enabled to access Rutgers Connect on your mobile device, please remove the Intune Company Portal app from your device.

title: Connect Mobile Device Supported Operating Systems for Rutgers Connect
body:
With each major update of a mobile device's Operating System (OS), Microsoft also updates the minimum supported version of OS's for the Office Suite. Devices below this threshold are no longer supported by Microsoft and their apps will not receive feature and/or security updates. To improve security and support, the University will be setting OS minimums that devices must maintain or they will be un-enrolled from our tenant. These minimums will be updated as new OS versions are released. These limits currently are:
•	iOS/iPadOS minimum OS: 18
•	Android minimum OS: 13
If you have a device below these limits, you will receive a notification on your device the next time it checks in. If an OS update is not applied to the device, the notification will come up again on day 7, 14, 21, and 28. If the you do not update by day 15, you will receive an email notification that your device needs to be updated. On day 30 your device will be un-enrolled from Intune Company portal and removed from the Rutgers tenant. This would be the same as if the you had manually un-registered your device from the Intune Company Portal.

title: Connect OneDrive for Business
body:
OneDrive for Business is a feature of Rutgers Connect (Office 365) that lets you store, sync, and share your work files in the cloud. With OneDrive for Business, you can share and collaborate on work documents with co-workers.
Please note that OneDrive is designed to securely upload your documents to the cloud so you can access your data from any device. You may want to move your Desktop or My Documents folders to OneDrive to sync them with the cloud, but we recommend against uploading your entire hard drive. Attempting to sync system, program, and configuration files will unnecessarily consume your OneDrive quota and may affect OneDrive's ability to efficiently sync your important files.
When you store your files with OneDrive, you can:
•	Access and update files from anywhere on any device.
•	Manage your business files on the road.
•	Collaborate on documents with others at the same time.
•	Synchronize files from the cloud service to your desktop and work with them offline.
Instructions for setting up OneDrive on your computer can be found at the links below.

•	Setting up OneDrive for Business on Mac
Find out more about OneDrive on Rutgers Connect.

title: Connect Recommended university-supported alternatives for Microsoft Publisher
body:
Microsoft has announced permanent retirement for Microsoft Publisher on October 1, 2026. After that date, Publisher will no longer be included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions, and support for existing versions will end. For more information, see the Exporting Publisher files documentation. 
Across all features and capabilities, Adobe InDesign is the most comparable to Microsoft Publisher. However, list of recommended alternatives that are Rutgers-supported include:
•	Adobe Creative Cloud 
o	Adobe Acrobat Pro (Digital Operations & Document Finalization)
o	Adobe Express (Personal & Event Design)
o	Adobe Illustrator (Vector-Based Designing & Branding)
o	Adobe InDesign (Professional Multi-Page Layout & Visual Architecture Publishing)
o	Adobe Photoshop (Raster Imaging & Visual Manipulation)
•	Microsoft 
o	PowerPoint (Presentation Design & Linear Storytelling)
o	Word (Business Operations, Correspondence & Data-Driven Documents)
 
Rutgers-supported alternative software feature comparison
Software	Functionality	Availability & quality of assessed features	Details
Adobe Acrobat Pro
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Back to top	Business Stationery & Operations	Best	The gold standard for fillable forms, password protection, and legally binding e-signatures.
Mail Merge	Technical Only	 Does not have a "Mail Merge" button. It uses "Form Data Injection" where you import a data file to populate existing form fields.	
Object Nudging	Basic	 You can nudge objects with arrow keys in "Edit PDF" mode, but there is no coordinate system for precise mathematical placement.	
Page Guides	Manual	 You can pull guides from the rulers, but they are static. They don't "snap" as intelligently as InDesign's and cannot be set on a Master Page.	
Personal & Event Design	Poor	 Lacks artistic brushes, effects, and the "canvas" feel needed for creative design work.	
Professional Marketing	Limited (Final Prep)	 You cannot easily build a layout from scratch. It is used to "preflight" (verify colors/resolution) before sending a file to a professional press.	
Text Box Linking	Not available	 Text exists in isolated blocks. If you add a sentence to Paragraph A, it will not push Paragraph B to the next page; it will simply overlap.	
Adobe Express	Business Stationery & Operations	(For Business Stationery)
Excellent	Best for creating the visual templates for letterheads, business cards, and envelopes. You can "lock" the Rutgers logo so it can't be moved by mistake.
Back to top	(For Business Operations)
Good (Front-End)	Great for designing the "shells" of documents (invoices, resumes, certificates). It does not handle back-end math or database links.	
(For Brand Kits) 
Best-in-Class	You can upload Rutgers Scarlet and official fonts into a "Brand Kit." With one click, you can "Brandify" any template to match university standards.		
(For PDF Management) 
Very Good	It can import, edit, and stylize existing PDFs. It’s useful for making a boring operational PDF look professional without needing Acrobat.		
(For Automation) 
Poor	No native Mail Merge or database connectivity. You cannot use it to generate 500 personalized invoices from a spreadsheet.		
Mail Merge	Not available	There is no native way to connect a spreadsheet to Adobe Express to generate personalized versions of a design.	
Object Nudging	Excellent	Very intuitive. It uses "Magnetic Guides" that show you exactly when an object is centered or aligned with another element. You can also nudge with arrow keys.	
Page Guides	Basic	It provides a "Grid" view and automatic snap-guides, but you cannot drag custom, permanent non-printing lines onto the canvas like you can in InDesign.	
Personal & Event Design	Best	This is the tool's core strength. Thousands of high-quality templates for invitations, posters, and "Save the Dates."	
Professional Marketing	Good (Templates)	Excellent for social media, simple flyers, and digital ads. It’s less ideal for high-end print brochures that require CMYK color accuracy.	
Text Box Linking	Not available	Express is a single-frame design tool. You cannot link text boxes to flow content across pages; each page is a separate design canvas.	
Adobe Illustrator	Business Stationery & Operations	Excellent	Best for designing the "source" files for letterheads and business cards to ensure logos stay crisp at any size.
Back to top	Mail Merge	Technical (Variables)	Possible via the "Variables" panel and XML files, but it’s a high-friction process compared to Word or InDesign.
Object Nudging	Best	Offers hyper-precise nudging. You can set your "Keyboard Increment" in Preferences to literally any decimal of a point or millimeter.	
Page Guides	Robust	Uses "Artboards" instead of pages. You can have global guides or artboard-specific guides, plus "Smart Guides" that snap to every anchor point.	
Personal & Event Design	High	Great for "from-scratch" creative work (custom illustrations, complex typography), but overkill for simple template-based flyers.	
Professional Marketing	Excellent (Single Page)	The gold standard for logos, icons, and single-page assets like posters or decals that need to be infinitely scalable.	
Text Box Linking	Good (Area Type)	Supports "Threaded Text" between shapes, but it’s less stable than InDesign for long documents and doesn't handle "Overset" text as gracefully.	
Adobe InDesign	Business Stationery & Operations	Excellent	Handles precise letterheads and business cards; supports interactive PDF forms for operations.
Back to top	Mail Merge	Powerful	Features a robust "Data Merge" tool that pulls information from .csv or .txt files into business stationery, badges, or catalogs. The "Data Merge" panel allows you to automate thousands of personalized documents using .csv data.
Object Nudging	Precision-Grade	Extremely precise nudging via arrow keys or the "Step and Repeat" function. Nudge by 0.001pt increments. Includes "Step and Repeat" for creating perfect grids of objects instantly.	
Page Guides	Robust Architecture	Features "Parent Pages" (Master Pages), Baseline Grids, Supports "Liquid Layouts," custom margins, and non-printing document guides for perfect and precise alignment across hundreds of pages.	
Personal & Event Design	Excellent	Total creative freedom, though it lacks the one-click templates found in Express or Designer.	
Professional Marketing	Best	Designed specifically for high-end print and digital marketing (brochures, magazines, brand guides).	
Text Box Linking	Native Feature	Uses "Text Threading." Text flows automatically between or across frames, pages (including across non-consecutive pages), and even different sections.

Back to top	Mail Merge	Technical (Variables)	It has a "Variables" feature to swap images/text based on a data set, but it is far more complex to set up than Word.
Object Nudging	Best	Pixel-perfect control. Use the arrow keys for 1px nudges or Shift + Arrow for 10px "super-nudges."

Personal & Event Design	Excellent	PowerPoint's user-friendly drag-and-drop interface enables anyone to effortlessly create professional-quality event invitations and social media graphics.	
Professional Marketing	Moderate, Good (for Single Page)	Good for text-heavy newsletters or resumes, but poor for complex image-heavy brochures. Excellent for posters, flyers, and simple social media graphics. It’s much easier to move objects around than in Word.	
Text Box Linking	Not available	PowerPoint cannot "thread" or "flow" text from one box to another. If your text overflows Box A, you must manually cut and paste the remainder into Box B.	
Microsoft Word	Business Stationery & Operations	Best-in-Class	The absolute gold standard for letterheads, memos, and internal reports. It integrates perfectly with the rest of Rutgers' Outlook system.
Back to top	Mail Merge	Industry Leader	The most powerful and user-friendly mail merge available. It connects directly to Excel or Outlook contacts.
Object Nudging	Good	You can nudge with arrow keys, but Word's "Layout Options" (Wrap Text) often make objects jump unexpectedly.	
Page Guides	Poor	Word doesn't have "Design Guides." It relies on Margins and Rulers. You can't drag a "non-printing line" onto the page to align a logo.	
Personal & Event Design	Basic	Best for "utilitarian" events (meeting agendas, basic flyers). It lacks the creative templates and layering tools of Adobe Express.	
Professional Marketing	Moderate	Good for text-heavy newsletters or resumes, but poor for complex image-heavy brochures.
