title: account audits
body:
Who can have a Rutgers Connect account?
According to Office of Information Technology guidelines, only the following classes of people are eligible to have Rutgers Connect accounts:
•	On-boarded (current and future) employees of Rutgers University
•	Current students that handle Protected Health Information (PHI), such as RBHS students
•	Professor Emeritus
The following groups of people are not automatically eligible for Rutgers Connect accounts:
•	Former employees (including teaching/graduate assistants who may still be students but are not actively working for Rutgers)
•	Employees of other organizations who are performing work at Rutgers
•	Students (current and future) who do not handle PHI
•	Alumni
•	Retirees
Students from other units may be eligible if the departments or divisions they work for wish to sponsor them. Additionally, Rutgers Connect accounts may be provided to Guests, who are individuals who are conducting University business and are directly associated with the University, but are not officially on the University’s payroll. Examples of guests include visiting professors/scholars, members of auxiliary groups, and others who are working on University business or affiliated with the University.
These guests and students may be eligible for a Rutgers Connect account if a department or division of Rutgers is willing to sponsor them. Please contact your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator for details.
Recently hired employees may be on-boarded to payroll by departmental HR staff, even with a future start date. The Rutgers Connect account will then automatically be available. If full on-boarding is not possible, departmental on-boarding staff may use the Early Employee NetID form to request early provisioning from OIT.
Note: Most students, retirees, and alumni are not eligible for Rutgers Connect; however, these groups are automatically eligible for an account on Rutgers ScarletMail. Please see the ScarletApps page for information about opening ScarletMail accounts.
How can I keep my Rutgers Connect account?
We determine which accounts should be closed by comparing Rutgers Connect accounts with the active roles (e.g. Faculty or Staff) of NetIDs listed in the University’s OpenRegistry (OR) service, which is used as the basis for the Rutgers Online Directory. The OR may have some information which needs to be corrected.
If you have received an account closure notice and you believe that this is in error, please find the group you belong to in the appropriate subsection below (Current Employees, Students, Guests, Others) and follow the instructions there.
Current Employees
You may not be listed in the OR as a current employee. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, contact your department’s Human Resources person.
After your department’s Human Resources person has corrected your record, your department’s Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Students
OIT cannot permit prior students (such as students on leave and alumni) access to Rutgers Connect, as the system contains Restricted data such as Protected Health Information (PHI). Students who are still in need of a non-PHI email account may use ScarletMail.
If you are a current student, first verify your status in OR. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
After you have corrected your course registration(s), your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Guests
Guests will have to determine with their sponsor if Rutgers Connect, ScarletMail, or even no Rutgers email account (for example, using a home institution’s email service) is appropriate for their needs.
If you are affiliated with Rutgers but not actually employed full-time by Rutgers, you may request a guest account. Have a sponsor at the department you are working with go to the Guest Account site, and submit a request for you, which will be sent to our Accounts Office for processing. NOTE: A domain administrator within your department must activate a Connect account for you.
Every year, you must renew your guest account. You will be notified when the time to renew your account arrives (30 days prior to the expiration of the account).
Your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can assist your sponsor with submitting a Guest Account request and creating your Rutgers Connect account, if necessary.
Others
Retirees and alumni are automatically entitled to an account on Rutgers ScarletMail.
If you do not fit into any of the above categories, you may want to try contacting a department at Rutgers related to the work you do and ask if they would be willing to sponsor a Guest account for you.
We have no mechanism for people no longer associated with Rutgers to pay a fee and thus keep their accounts. These people should be able to pay for a full account on any number of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) or obtain a free email account from various web services. Rutgers cannot recommend one such group over another.
What is the typical account audit timeline?
Once an account is found to be ineligible for Connect:
•	On day one, i.e., same day found to be ineligible: The account is sent an email notification.
•	On day seven, i.e., approximately one week later: The account is locked out of Connect.
•	On day thirty-five, i.e., approximately 5 weeks later: The account is deleted from Connect.
If the account is found to be eligible for Connect at any time prior to deletion, the account will exit the audit.
Like all Rutgers NetID services, Rutgers Connect is subject to OIT NetID authentication processes. These practices may lock your Rutgers NetID – including Rutgers Connect access – on a different timeline. See the off-boarding process article for details about NetID authentication off-boarding. Please note that recent students in the “grace period” status described on that site are ineligible for the Rutgers Connect service. However, OIT will maintain data for the full duration of the “grace period” – the “day thirty-five" deletion does not apply in this case.
What should I do before the account is closed?
If you will be losing your Rutgers Connect account, you may want to take some of the following steps.
•	Use the Manage Email Addresses function to ensure you continue to receive Rutgers email. For example, retirees and alumni may be entitled to continuing email service on ScarletMail. They can set that as their delivery address and consider Migrating Rutgers Connect Personal Data to ScarletMail if appropriate.
•	Contact the IT staff in your department to determine the correct protocol for the data (email, contacts, and calendar) in your account. Departments that handle PHI or other sensitive data may have procedures put in place for security.
•	Notify your regular correspondents, mailing lists, etc., about your change of address. We cannot forward mail from a deleted account to another address.
•	You may want to use the “automatic reply” feature (available in the Settings after logging in at https://connect.rutgers.edu) to set up an automatic response, telling correspondents of the account’s eventual closure. Remember that the automatic reply feature will no longer work for you once your account has been fully deleted.
•	If you have it configured, remove your Work Hours and Location on your calendar. 
•	You will lose access to your Office 365 data once your account is deleted, so you will want to save your OneDrive for Business files to another location. Please contact your local IT staff to assist with this process.
What happens after the account is closed?
After your account is closed, you will lose access to your Rutgers Connect account. Your account will still receive email and any Office 365 applications associated with your account should still function as expected; however, you will no longer be able to sign in to the account.
Approximately 4 weeks after your account is closed, your Rutgers Connect account will be deleted.
After an account is deleted, you will no longer be able to access Office 365 services like email or OneDrive for Business. Your Office applications will move into a read-only, reduced functionality mode and display Unlicensed Product notifications.
Any e-mail addressed to such an account will be returned to the sender (“bounced”) with an automatic message of the type “Access denied”.
For further assistance
If you have questions about any of the above, you can send an email to help@oit.rutgers.edu or contact the OIT Help Desk.

body:
Table of Contents

o	Encrypt
o	Do Not Forward

o	Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
o	Keyword Triggered
•	Outlook Application
Office 365's Office Message Encryption (OME) provides you the ability to customize the level of protection for any specific email you choose to encrypt. You can choose to encrypt the email, ensuring it is received exclusively by your intended recipient, or to limit their ability to forward it to others. For messages that require the greatest amount of security, you can choose to allow the email to only be viewed by or forwarded to other Rutgers Connect users, or even limit the Rutgers Connect recipient to view the email and be unable to copy, print, forward, or otherwise interact with the message. These options will be described in more detail later.
How to Encrypt an Email
Navigate to Rutgers Connect and log in. You can use these functions by clicking the Options tab on the ribbon, then clicking the Encrypt button at the top of your email in the Outlook Web App.
Error! Filename not specified.
In the Outlook Web App, when you click Protect, a banner appears at the top of your email that says "Do Not Forward: Recipients can read this message, but they can’t forward, print, or copy content." It will also include options to change the permission level or remove the protection altogether.
Error! Filename not specified.
If you select the option to change the permission level, you will see four options.
Error! Filename not specified.
Error! Filename not specified.
Encrypt Options
Encrypt
If you choose Encrypt, the message's contents will be encrypted. You can learn more about encryption here, but at a very basic level, you can imagine this as your message being converted into a secret code, with only authorized users (your intended message recipient) having the key to decrypt that encoded text back into your original message.
When you choose Encrypt, the recipient can do whatever they want with the message once they receive it. They can copy text from the message, print it, save it to their computer, reply to it, or forward it to other users. Encryption adds a layer of security that ensures your intended recipient is the only one who can receive your message – but it does not control what they can do with it once they have.
Do Not Forward
If you want a little bit more control over the message you are sending, you can choose the Do Not Forward option. This option encrypts the message as described above and also prevents the user from copying, printing, or forwarding its contents.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential
Choosing this option will only allow the message to be sent to other Rutgers Connect users. It is similar to Encrypt in that, while the message is protected, the recipient can still save, reply to, and forward it. It may only be forwarded to other Rutgers Connect users.
Rutgers Connect – Confidential View Only
This is the most restrictive option. If you choose this option, the recipient – who must be a Rutgers Connect user – will be able to view the message only. They will not be able to reply, forward, copy, or edit the message.
Keyword Triggered
For backward compatibility with our previous encryption service, Zix Corporation, any message containing the keyword "ZIXSECURE" in the subject or body and leaving Rutgers Connect will have OME encryption applied to it. OIT does not recommend using keywords to force encryption. The keyword feature has been retained for specialized cases and may be removed completely in the future, as it is being replaced by OME's encryption features.
Outlook Application
In the Outlook application, which can be installed locally on your computer for more robust email management, you can find the option with the Encrypt button when you select Options.

From Outlook, once you click Encrypt you will see a message stating "Encrypt Only – This message is encrypted." You can change the permission level by clicking the small arrow to the right of the Encrypt button.

title: Connect SharePoint roles and permission levels
body:
SharePoint offers default and custom permission levels to better manage user roles on specific sites. Below is a breakdown of common out-of-the-box permission levels and their intended roles.
Permission Level	Role
Read	•	Read and download site content
•	Browse site content
•	Search site content
•	Request higher access level
Contribute	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above role
•	Create, edit and delete list items and documents
Edit	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Can add, edit and delete lists
Design	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Create/Edit libraries
•	Change page structure and visual design
•	Add/Edit web parts
Full Control	•	All rights and responsibilities of the above roles
•	Administer permissions
 
These permission levels are collections of individual user permissions and can vary depending on the SharePoint template being used. The ones above are just some of the most common you will find on most sites. It is important to note that these are just collections of permissions; in order for them to be effective, they need to be applied to permission groups on the SharePoint site. SharePoint sites by default come with the following groups that have one of the above permission levels applied to them:
 
Permission Group	Permission Level
site-name Visitors	•	Read
site-name Members	•	Edit
site-name Owners	•	Full Control
 
As an example, a Teams-connected SharePoint site will have the site members' permission group populated with the 365 group's members, and the site owners' permission group will be populated with the 365 group's owners.
Visit the SharePoint website for additional information regarding sharing files, folders, and sites in SharePoint Online.

Microsoft SharePoint offers a wide variety of sites to fulfill business objectives ranging from document storage to communicating department initiatives. Below is an outline for various SharePoint sites and their unique advantages.

Team Sites
Team sites allow members to collaborate on projects, events, or ideas by connecting them to the content, information, and web apps they need. On a team site home page, you can view links to valuable team files, web apps, and pages, as well as view recent site changes in the activity feed. Team sites are integrated by default within a wide range of Microsoft collaboration tools, such as Microsoft Planner and Microsoft Teams.

At the top of the team site, you will see a header with the site name, site logo, and whether the site is public (anyone in the organization can view) or private (only specific members can view). Site members with edit permissions will also see a “New” button that allows them to add a new list, document library, page, news post, or web app.

Left-hand Navigation and Search Pane
At the top left of the site, you will see a search box where you can find files stored on the team site. Under the search box, you will see links to the default team document library, team OneNote notebook, site pages, site contents, site recycle bin, and custom links.

Overview
Best for: Central location for team collaboration and document storage.
Permissions: Includes Office 365 group permissions, as well as default SharePoint group and permission levels.
Content Authors: All members who can create and edit content are content authors.
Availability: Can be created by the site owner or administrator as a site collection or subsite.
Use Cases: 
•	Project team working together to share ideas and manage tasks
•	Team storing important documents for current projects
Communication Sites
Communication sites are used to share information in a visually compelling format, featuring news posts, reports, events, statuses, and lists. These sites are great for displaying information to a broad audience, with a few members contributing to the content. When creating a team site, you can start with a blank site or choose a template (showcase or topic) site design that comes with a default set of web parts.
Topic Site Design

Error! Filename not specified.

•	Site showcasing new department initiative.
•	Intranet site for the HR department, including news posts from various employees.
Hub Sites
Hub sites are used to showcase, connect, and organize a wide variety of related sites into a central site. By connecting a family of team and communication sites, discovering related content, such as news and various site activities, becomes easier. Sites associated with a SharePoint hub site will have a hub site navigation bar added to the top of the site.
Error! Filename not specified.

Best for: Central site used to display and navigate to related team and communication sites.
Permissions: Default SharePoint permission levels.
Content Authors: The hub site owner defines the hub navigation and theme. Hub site members create content on the hub site. Site owners and members of sites associated with the parent hub site create content on their respective sites.

Although SharePoint sites allow for advanced customization based on a variety of needs, there are limitations to the content management system. Below are a few to keep in mind:

title: Connect Using Scheduling Poll to Schedule Meetings
body:
As of December 2023, the FindTime add-in has been retired. Scheduling Poll is the replacement feature and is built directly into Outlook as a native feature. 
The new Scheduling Poll feature, in replacement of the FindTime add-in, is used to schedule meetings via polling. The organizer can send multiple time options through the Scheduling Poll feature and minimize the back-and-forth emails about scheduling. 
The Scheduling Poll feature is currently available to users of Microsoft 365 Apps for business or enterprise plans that include Exchange Online. It is currently supported for GCC tenants, excluding GCC High.
A meeting organizer is required to have a mailbox in Microsoft 365 Exchange Online to be able to use the Scheduling Poll feature, while anyone with a valid email address can be an attendee in a meeting that utilizes the Scheduling Poll feature for polling. This feature is not available to organizers with mailboxes on an Exchange On-Premises server.
Access Scheduling Poll
1.	Navigate and log in to your Rutgers Connect account. 
2.	Create a new email or select an email to reply to.
3.	List required attendees for the meeting in the To field and optional attendees in the Cc field.
4.	Select Scheduling poll in the Message tab, which is displayed in the Simplified Ribbon or Classic Ribbon. 

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.
5.	Create a new meeting event or select an existing event to edit it.
6.	List required attendees in the Invite attendees field and click Optional to add optional attendees.
7.	Select Scheduling poll in the Event tab, which is displayed in the Simplified Ribbon or Classic Ribbon. 
Create a Scheduling Poll
The organizer can send multiple time options through the Scheduling Poll and minimize the back-and-forth emails about scheduling. 
1.	Select the meeting settings.
o	View all your polls: Click this link to view and manage all the polls created by you.
o	Time zone: Select the time zone dropdown menu to change the time zone for the meeting.
o	Duration: Select a meeting duration from the list.
o	Meeting hours: Check to limit suggested meeting times to workdays and working hours only.
o	Date Picker: The date picker will allow you to pick different dates to see time availability. You can add times from different dates to a poll. Alternatively, you can use the left and right arrow buttons to go to the previous or next day and use the calendar icon (between the arrow buttons) to jump back to today.
2.	Scheduling Poll looks through the attendees' schedules (if available) and suggests a list of suitable meeting times. Factors used to determine the best options include how many attendees are free, how many required vs. optional attendees are free, and whether conflicted attendees have tentative or busy commitments on their calendar. 
o	People Icons: Hovering over the person icon will show participants’ availability and whether they are required or optional.

3.	Select a few suitable meeting times. The Next button will be enabled if you select one or more options.
4.	Select Next. You will be presented with the list of selected times and poll settings before you can finish creating the poll.

1.	To delete any selected meeting times, click the delete icon in the Selected times list. 
2.	Enter meeting location if needed.

	Schedule when attendees reach consensus: A calendar event is automatically scheduled if all required attendees have voted in favor of a specific time option. If multiple options are available, the earliest option will be scheduled.
	Hold selected times on my calendar: A tentative event is placed on your calendar for each time option you propose. All holds are removed when the meeting is scheduled or the poll is canceled.
	Notify me about poll updates: You’ll receive an email each time an attendee votes. The message includes the current poll status and an option to schedule.

	Lock poll for attendees: Attendees will not be able to suggest new times or edit other attendees.

title: Connect What to expect when sending to an unknown domain without TLS
body:
All email sent by users who have PHI flags is automatically secured with TLS Secure email. TLS is a cryptographic protocol that provides security between email servers. Most email servers are equipped to receive email that is sent via TLS. Rutgers is aware of some common email servers that are not equipped for TLS. If a PHI flagged user sends an email to one of these known email servers, Rutgers Connect will automatically use the built-in capabilities of Office 365's Office Message Encryption (OME) to protect your email.
If a PHI flagged user attempts to send an email to an email server that does not support TLS and is not known to Rutgers Connect, the sender will experience the following behavior:
•	Approximately 24 hours after you attempt to send the message, you will receive a standard delivery failure message similar to the following:

     Error! Filename not specified.
•	After your attempt to send the message, during those 24 hours, Rutgers Connect will retry to deliver the message in case the issue with TLS was temporary.
•	If you receive a similar failure message, you can resend the message and manually apply OME encryption by using the Encrypt button, as shown in the sending encrypted email article.

title: Connect FAQ
body:
A suspicious-looking email was removed from my inbox, did someone go into my account?" "
No email filtering system is perfect, so occasionally a dangerous phishing message may get past Office 365's spam filtering. In the event that this happens, OIT will protect users by removing these messages from the mailboxes of all recipients post-delivery. Users may be concerned when they notice these messages disappearing from their mailboxes, but it is important to note that this removal does not indicate any compromise. The messages are removed without anyone from OIT accessing the user’s mailbox or reading their mail; it is done in bulk, and this admin activity is logged. Copies of the removed messages are preserved for a short period of time to ensure no unintended messages were removed.

title: Connect FAQ Am I required to install Intune and use MDM in order to use Rutgers Connect on a personal device?
body: It is only required to use Mobile Device Management if you want to use native Office applications on your mobile device or access your email through your phone's native mail app. This is to protect your private information and any University data shared with you in the event your mobile device is lost or stolen. You can use a mobile web browser to access your Rutgers Connect email and calendar without having to install Intune.

title: Connect FAQ Can I forward email from Rutgers Connect to ScarletMail or other external mail systems?
body:
No. The Acceptable Use Policy states that all university business be conducted using the official university email and calendar service, Rutgers Connect. This is necessary to meet federal, state, and local legal, regulatory, and statutory requirements (e.g., HIPAA, OPRA, FERPA, GLBA), and to ensure business continuity, enable proper eDiscovery, and handle data securely and in compliance.
However, you may resend an individual message to an external email account.
We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause, but to keep it safe and secure, you are unable to forward mail automatically from Rutgers Connect.

title: Connect FAQ Can I send email as an address other than my actual Rutgers Connect address?
body:
Yes. Rutgers Connect allows users to send mail using a Personalized Email Address. Learn more about changing your default email address in Rutgers Connect.
Please note you will continue to need to use your primary email address in order to log in to Rutgers Connect.

title: Connect FAQ Can the administration search Rutgers’ email traffic and use eDiscovery tools to view email?
body:
All requests for access to email are carefully screened by Rutgers Legal and Compliance departments. Rutgers has been required to provide such data using various tools in the past, and the requirement remains unchanged.
Rutgers email administrators have always had the capability to access account holders’ email, but have done so only under the direct guidance of Rutgers Legal in response to subpoenas, eDiscovery requests, and OPRA requests. Additionally, Microsoft maintains strict records of who accesses accounts, which Rutgers cannot modify.

title: Connect FAQ How do I change how my name is displayed in Rutgers Connect?
body:
By default, your name in Rutgers Connect is displayed as it appears in the payroll system. If you are in the process of a legal name change and your name will be changed in the payroll system, this change will be reflected in Rutgers Connect as well after it has been processed.
If you want your name displayed differently than how it appears in payroll, you will need to speak to your Rutgers Connect domain administrator. Not all changes are allowed, as your name must still identify you. Listed below are some common examples of acceptable display names:
•	Using an abbreviation of your first name (e.g., Bob instead of Robert, A. instead of Arthur).
•	Displaying your middle name instead of your first name, or an abbreviation or common form of your middle name.
•	Displaying a nickname instead of your first name.
•	Displaying your first name (or alternative forms) and last name in a different order.
Please note that this change will only affect the Global Address List. If anyone has you manually saved as a personal contact, that name will not be affected by the global change.

title: Connect FAQ How do I deal with messages that are incorrectly marked as Junk in Rutgers Connect?
body: You can first mark the message as not junk by clicking the Not Junk button above the message. This will also whitelist the sender, so future messages from them do not go to your junk folder. If you notice that the Junk filtering system inappropriately and consistently marks certain messages as junk, you can forward messages to not_junk@office365.microsoft.com which can help improve the filtering system.

title: Connect FAQ How do I set up automatic replies/vacation messages in Rutgers Connect?
body:
Automatic replies can be enabled in the Outlook web app through the settings menu.
1.	Select the Gear icon next to your profile picture.
2.	Select View all Outlook settings.
3.	Under the Mail tab, navigate to Automatic replies.
Here, you can enable or disable automatic replies, format your away message, and select a time span for them to automatically begin and end.

title: Connect FAQ How do I share a file on OneDrive with users who are not affiliated with Rutgers University?
body:
To share an anonymous link:
1.	Select the file or folder and choose Share from the ribbon.
2.	You will see an option that usually says People You Specify Can Edit.
3.	Select this button and then choose Anyone.
4.	You will then have a link you can share externally.

title: Connect FAQ How do I turn off Conversation view in Connect Outlook Web App (OWA)?
body:
There are two methods to turn Conversation view off in the Outlook web app. 
Method 1
1.	Select the Gear icon in the top-right corner of the window, next to your profile picture.
2.	Under "Arrange message list," select Show each message separately.
Method 2
1.	In the ribbon, select the View tab.
2.	Select Messages > Conversations > Show each message separately.

title: Connect FAQ How do you attach an email to an email?
body:
Specific steps will vary depending on the email program you are using.
Outlook web app
1.	Open the folder containing the message to be attached.
2.	Create a new email message.
3.	Drag the message from the folder list into the new email message.
4.	Address the message and send it as usual.
Outlook desktop client
1.	Open the folder containing the message to be attached.
2.	Highlight the email in question.
3.	Press the Ctrl+Alt+F keys.
4.	Address the message and send it as usual.
Gmail (ScarletApps)
Method 1
1.	To the left of each email you want to forward, select the checkbox.
2.	At the top, click More and then Forward as an attachment.
3.	Address the message and send it as usual.
Method 2
1.	Right-click an email and select Forward as attachment.
2.	Drag and drop the file into the body of a new message.
3.	Address the message and send it as usual.
Thunderbird
1.	Open the folder containing the message to be attached.
2.	Create a new email message.
3.	In the Preview pane, click on the message and drag it into the body of a new message.
4.	Address the message and send it as usual.

title: Connect FAQ How does Rutgers Connect do searches?
body: There are separate search tools within each of the major applications. For more information, visit Microsoft's articles on searching in the Outlook Web Application, Calendar, and OneDrive.

title: Connect FAQ How does Rutgers Connect handle folders and subfolders?
body: Rutgers Connect has a hierarchical file structure, the same as most modern email programs.

title: Connect FAQ How private is the information I keep on Rutgers Connect?
body:
In general, information on accounts on Rutgers services, including Rutgers Connect, is accessible only to the specific account holder until it is shared with others by that account holder. However, as Rutgers is a public university, all information on Rutgers services may be subject to legal requests, such as Open Public Records Act (OPRA) requests, court orders, or litigation.
Aside from such requests, the only people authorized to view these documents, other than the account holder, would be system administrators who have special privileges usable under very limited circumstances for this purpose.
At Rutgers, only a few highly trained individuals working for the Office of Information Technology (OIT) have this type of privilege. They work under clearly stated rules on privacy, user responsibilities, system administrator responsibilities, and violation handling. We take this very seriously. The specific circumstances are covered in the Acceptable Use Policy found in the Rutgers Policy Library.
For more information, visit Microsoft's privacy support page. 
Account holders should keep in mind that Rutgers email services are for work purposes and, as such, are not truly private.

title: Connect FAQ I'm not seeing all my folders in the Outlook Web Application. How do I see them all?
body:
When you first log in, the Outlook Web Application (OWA) displays only the most recently used folders. Click More below the folder list to see all of your folders. 
The first set of most recently used folders will appear as Favorites. The list of all other folders will appear below that, under your name.
A scroll bar will appear next to the folder list, if needed.
If a folder has sub-folders, the parent folder will have a “v” symbol next to it. Click that to see the sub-folders, which turns the “v” into “^”. Click the “^” again to hide the sub-folders.
For more information, visit Microsoft's article on working with message folders in Outlook on the web.

title: Connect FAQ Is IMAP/SMTP enabled for Rutgers Connect?
body: IMAP/SMTP settings are disabled for all users by default. If you require the ability to use IMAP/SMTP with your Connect account, contact your Rutgers Connect delegated administrator.

title: Connect FAQ
body:
Is it safe to store Non-Public Personal Info (NPPI), HIPAA, or other restricted data on Office 365?" "
Office 365 is compliant with HIPAA, FERPA, GLBA, and others. See Microsoft's page on data management.
Microsoft has provided Rutgers with a BAA.
Security for sensitive data needs to occur not just in the cloud but also on the Rutgers side, including how the data is stored, transmitted, and handled within the given department/unit of the University, and by users who have access to that data. A department/unit handling sensitive data may also want to speak to the Rutgers Ethics and Compliance office.
For HIPAA-covered units/departments, outgoing email will be routed through Zix for additional protection within Rutgers Connect.

title: Connect FAQ Is Rutgers Connect FISMA Compliant?
body:
No, Rutgers Connect is not currently FISMA-compliant. For more information on what can be stored on Connect, please review the data classification and storage matrix. 
The US Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) was established to provide a standardized approach for assessing, monitoring, and authorizing cloud computing products and services under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), and to accelerate the adoption of secure cloud solutions by federal agencies.
Additional information can be found on Microsoft's FedRAMP website.

title: Connect FAQ Is there an alternative login page if connect.rutgers.edu is not working?
body: If you are experiencing issues with connect.rutgers.edu not loading properly, try logging in via outlook.office.com. You should be able to sign in as usual.

title: Connect FAQ What are the email attachment size limits for Rutgers Connect?
body: Attachments are limited to 150 MB within Rutgers Connect, although the mail server used by a recipient outside of Rutgers Connect may not accept such a large attachment.

title: Connect FAQ What email accounts are retirees granted access to?
body: Eligible retirees have access to a ScarletMail address. They should be migrated from Rutgers Connect to ScarletMail before their Guest, Faculty, or Staff role expires. You can learn more about retiree benefits at the Rutgers Retired Faculty and Staff Association page. Only retirees with an Emeritus role are eligible for continued access to their Rutgers Connect accounts. If a retiree believes they should be Emeritus, they should contact the Retiree Center or University Human Resources.

title: Connect FAQ What is the retention period for deleted items or items in my Connect junk folder?
body:
Deleted items will be kept in the trash or junk folder for 30 days, after which they will be moved to a recoverable items folder for an additional 30 days.
This is the maximum possible retention period.

title: Connect FAQ What type of spam filtering is available on Connect?
body:
Microsoft provides its own spam filtering service.
Learn more about the Junk Email Filter (for the Microsoft Outlook application) or learn about Junk email and phishing (for Outlook on the web).
If you receive a phishing scam or other malicious email, follow the directions on the Rutgers page on reporting suspected scams, breaches, or theft.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Can I adjust a resource's settings in Connect?
body:
From the Exchange Admin Center, a delegated administrator can click their profile picture on the top right; a menu titled My accounts will appear. Then select Another user... and search for the resource they would like to configure. After opening the edit menu, you should be able to make the appropriate adjustments.
More information about admin access to resources in EAC is available within CAT Documentation.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins How can contact information in Rutgers Connect be updated?
body:
If the information displayed at Rutgers Search for a user is correct, but the contact information in Rutgers Connect is incorrect, please contact the OIT Help Desk.
If the information displayed in Rutgers Search is incorrect, the user will need to contact their department’s HR representative to have it corrected. Once the information is correctly updated in Rutgers Search, it should update in Rutgers Connect. If the corrected information has not been updated in Rutgers Connect after 1-2 business days, please contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins How can I collect and send email headers in Mail on my Mac?
body:
1.	Go to the Mail app on your Mac.
2.	Choose View > Message > All Headers.
3.	To view fewer header fields again, choose View > Message > Default Headers.
This email can then be sent to the appropriate support staff as directed.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins How can I collect and send email headers in Thunderbird?
body:
1.	Open the email whose headers you would like to collect.
2.	Click View Source, which may be found under a dropdown labeled More above the email or under View in the menu at the top right corner of the Thunderbird window.
3.	Copy all text up to the first blank line and paste it into an email or a document that you can attach to an email.
This email can then be sent to the appropriate support staff as directed.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins How can I configure an auto-response for a shared or resource mailbox?
body:
From the Exchange Admin Center, a Delegated Admin can do the following.
1.	Click their profile picture on the top right.
2.	Click My accounts will appear.
3.	Select Another user...
4.	Search for and select the mailbox they would like to set up an auto-response for. 
5.	Choose Set up an automatic reply message and configure the auto-response as desired.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins How will eDiscovery and similar requests be handled for Connect?
body:
eDiscovery currently applies to all files stored on Rutgers Connect, including email, calendars, and OneDrive files. Office 365 features that are not HIPAA-compliant, etc., will not be available through Rutgers Connect for this reason. eDiscovery and OPRA requests will be centrally administered by OIT, removing this time-consuming task from departmental/unit IT staff. There are also eDiscovery tools and an Archive available for eDiscovery that simplify the handling of eDiscovery and OPRA requests.
Because all Rutgers Connect data is subject to such requests, people should not use Rutgers Connect for personal files or messages.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Is there a limit to how many owners an Office 365 group or distribution list can have?
body:
Yes. Office 365 groups and distribution lists have a limit of 100 owners. However, this limit does not apply to members, and as a general rule, collaborators should be added as members rather than owners.
For a more detailed look at Office 365 group limits, see Microsoft's Group limits overview.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins
body:
My user's Connect account is being audited, but they cannot change their password" "
There are rare circumstances during account audits when a user loses the ability to reset/change their password because they are no longer active in our authentication protocols. This would be true if the user no longer holds any roles at the University.
If you have a user who falls into this category, there are two options available:
•	Get the user a Guest NetID. You can set the guest role to remain active for an appropriate period so the user can access their Rutgers Connect account and remove the data they are interested in. Guest accounts can be requested through the Guest Request site
•	With the user’s consent, a domain admin may grant themselves full access to a user’s Rutgers Connect account. This can be done through the “mailbox delegation” section in EAC. Once a domain admin has full access to the account, they can create a PST of the user’s inbox to share with the user or extract the needed data.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Who has access to the data in OneDrive?
body:
Any delegated administrator for your given domain will have access to the data in OneDrive, as is the current practice at Rutgers.
Data stored in OneDrive via Rutgers Connect is hosted on servers within the US. See Microsoft's security statements for more information.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Why are the delegates for my room in Connect being asked to accept or decline booking requests?
body: Currently, rooms use any listed delegates for the room, even if the room is set not to require delegate review of booking requests. Administrators can change various room settings, including delegation. If you do not need to use delegates for a room you have admin access to, you should remove the delegates. More information about admin access to resources in EAC is available in CAT Documentation.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Why can't I share a resource calendar in Connect when I have Full Access?
body:
In Office 365, Send As permissions are distinct from Full Access permissions; you can have one without the other. If you are a delegated administrator with Full Access but not Send As, you can access a resource’s mailbox or calendar, but cannot share it. However, this can be easily remedied by granting yourself Send As privileges:
1.	Find your resource in the Exchange Admin Center and double-click it.
2.	Choose the tab in the pop-up window labeled Mailbox delegation, and add yourself to the Send As list.

title: Connect FAQ for Delegated Admins Why have I been getting so much spam in Connect since I whitelisted one of my other email addresses?
body:
When an email address is whitelisted in Connect, all mail forwarded to Connect from that address is whitelisted, causing an increase in spam volume. If a user has an outside address that forwards to Connect, spam sent to that address will be forwarded to Connect as well. Normally, Connect would filter the messages being forwarded from that address and sift out the spam, but if the address is whitelisted, then Connect will not apply spam filters and a higher-than-normal level of spam will accumulate in the user’s Connect inbox.
Users can check their whitelist themselves to see if they have whitelisted their own address; to navigate to your blacklist/whitelist in the Outlook Web App:
1.	Click the gear icon.
2.	Select View all Outlook settings.
3.	Select the Mail category and choose Junk email.

Rutgers VPN uses the Cisco Secure Mobility Client to provide secure remote access for end users running Windows, macOS, or Linux. The Cisco client is the only officially supported method for VPN connections at the university.

o	For Faculty/Staff, if you do not have the administrative rights or privileges on your computer to complete this install, contact your departmental IT for assistance.
The VPN knowledge base has specific OS instructions for:
•	iOS
•	Android
Using the VPN on a computer
1.	Once the installation is complete, the “Cisco Secure Client” will be located in your Start menu, under the Cisco folder. It may also already be running in your system tray. The icon will look like this:

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Enter the address of the VPN: vpn.rutgers.edu
4.	Click Connect. 
5.	You will see fields for Username, Password, and Duo Action/Second Password (see below).

title: VPN - Enterprise Virtual Private Network (VPN) FAQ
body:
Table of Contents
•	How do I register for the VPN?
•	Where can I download the VPN?
•	Is Administrator access required to install the Cisco Secure Client?
•	What is the current Operating System supported for the VPN?
•	Who can use the VPN?
•	When I engage the VPN, I can no longer print on my local network.
•	Is Campus VPN Full Tunnel?
•	I’m connected to VPN, but cannot access department resources.
•	What happens if I receive a pop-up after entering my credentials, like the one below?
•	What are the different VPNs, and what should I be using?
•	Is there anything I should be mindful of while using the VPN?
•	Why can I log into CAS but not VPN?
•	What applications are available without the use of a VPN?
•	Need further assistance?
How do I register for the VPN?
Obtaining a NetID does not automatically enroll you in VPN. You must first register for the VPN service for your NetID. Ensure you have activated the VPN service for your account on the Service Activation page.
Where can I download the VPN?
The latest version of the VPN software for your computer is available on the Software Portal. For mobile devices, it can be found in your device's App Store. 
Is Administrator access required to install the Cisco Secure Client?
Administrator access to your PC or laptop is required to download and install the VPN software. For faculty and staff, contact your departmental IT for assistance with installation, if needed.
What is the current Operating System supported for the VPN?
•	Windows 10 (32 and 64 bit)
•	Linux Red Hat 6 and 7
•	Ubuntu – Please refer to Ubuntu's documentation for currently supported releases
•	MacOS X – Please refer to the vendor for currently supported versions of Mac OS X
•	iOS
•	Android
Who can use the VPN?
Current students, staff, faculty, and university guests are eligible to use the VPN. A student is defined as full-time and currently registered in courses with the university. If you feel you need access and do not fit into any of these categories, you may apply for a guest account.
When I engage the VPN, I can no longer print on my local network.
There is a setting under Preferences that can resolve this issue:
1.	Start the Cisco VPN.
2.	Click the Settings (gear) icon.
3.	From the menu, select Anyconnect VPN > Preferences.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Check the box labeled "Allow local (LAN) access when using VPN."
5.	Your settings changes will not take effect until the next time you start the VPN client.
6.	To test the new settings, quit the VPN client, restart it, and connect again to the VPN.
7.	If that does not work for you, then disconnect from the VPN when you need to print.
Is Campus VPN Full Tunnel?
The Campus VPN is a Full Tunnel.
The “full tunnel” sends all your traffic through the VPN connection, and then out to the Internet through Rutgers’ connection.
This is useful when accessing resources that expect to see your connection coming from Rutgers, such as library journals.
I’m connected to VPN, but cannot access department resources.
If you’ve already connected to the VPN and can’t access a non-general resource, contact your departmental IT. Many departments have been provided with dedicated VPN IP space for areas needing to restrict remote access to their internal administrative environments. This access is controlled by delegated Active Directory RAD groups that local areas manage. Additional firewall access may be necessary to reach your resources. If you’re unable to get the help you need, contact soc@oit.rutgers.edu.
What happens if I receive a pop-up after entering my credentials, like the one below?
Error! Filename not specified.
This means that you are part of a group that provides additional restricted access. Click Accept to complete your connection. If the group does not match your affiliation, send a message to soc@oit.rutgers.edu so it can be investigated.
What are the different VPNs, and what should I be using?
You should make every effort to use vpn.rutgers.edu for the remote access VPN. While other VPN endpoints are available, they may lack address space or licensing to handle the load of users accessing VPN services.
Is there anything I should be mindful of while using the VPN?
Yes. While you are free to perform other activities during your session, VPN is intended for Rutgers University business. Please disconnect from VPN when you’re finished working. Additionally:
•	VPN sessions are capped at 24 hours. A countdown timer will be present in the application. You can always reconnect at any time.
•	VPN is an additional step when connecting to Rutgers’ resources that don’t require it. A list of those items is below.
•	Web browsers or Internet-based apps may need to be restarted after launching or closing the VPN client
Why can I log into CAS but not VPN?
It is possible that your password has expired. Visit the NetID Management page to change your password.
What applications are available without the use of a VPN?
•	Box Storage
•	Canvas Learning Management
•	Linkedin Learning (lynda.com)
•	myRutgers Portal (and the Cornerstone applications accessible inside myRutgers)
•	Scarletmail
•	Rutgers Connect (Office 365)
•	Webex Meetings
•	Qualtrics Survey Tool
Need further assistance?
Contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: VPN - Enterprise VPN for Linux
body:
Rutgers offers several methods of establishing Remote Access VPN connectivity on devices running various Linux distributions. The methods described on this page have been tested with Red Hat and Ubuntu. 
Cisco Secure Client for Linux
1.	Ensure the VPN service for your account is activated on the Service Activation page.
2.	Download the most up-to-date version of the Cisco Secure Client software for your operating system from the Software Portal. 
3.	Open the file once the download completes. 
4.	Follow the prompts and Accept the terms to install the software.
5.	The installer requires administrative privileges to run. Sign in with your administrative credentials for your computer to proceed.
6.	Afterwards, the Cisco Secure Client should now be installed on your machine
7.	Follow the instructions for using the VPN. 
OpenConnect Open Source Client
A VPN connection can also be established using the Open Connect Open Source Client. Both the openconnect and networkmanager-openconnect packages are available in the repositories for most Linux distributions.
Installation
Install the OpenConnect package from your distribution’s repositories.
Usage
OpenConnect can be used with NetworkManager, or manually via the command line.
NetworkManager (Optional, but recommended)
Install the network-manger-openconnect package. After installation, restart your computer. Then configure and connect with your desktop environment’s network settings. You will want to use vpn.rutgers.edu for the gateway. Save and connect. It will prompt you for a password twice. For the first prompt, enter your NetID password. For the second prompt, enter one of the following four DUO actions.
1.	Enter a 6 digit duo passcode
2.	Type "push" to send a push
3.	Type "sms" to text new passcodes
Command Line
Run the following command: openconnect vpn.rutgers.edu, and it will prompt you for a password twice. For the first prompt, enter your NetID password. For the second prompt, enter one of the following four Duo actions.
1.	Enter a 6 digit duo passcode
2.	Type "push" to send a push
3.	Type "sms" to text new passcodes
If you're having trouble connecting, please contact the OIT Help Desk.

body:
This page describes how an instructor will use Banner Final GradeSync to send final course grades from Canvas to Banner. Banner GradeSync is not available for REGIS-coded courses. To send final grades to REGIS, view How to use REGIS Final GradeSync. 
Please contact Rutgers Canvas Help if you experience issues using Banner GradeSync.

o	How do I test my grade scheme for rounding?
o	I am getting an error that says I am not logging in with my NetID but I am. What do I do?

o	I can't launch Banner gradeSync. What should I do?
Banner Final GradeSync Requirements
•	The grading period must be open in Banner and active in Banner Final Grade Sync.
•	The Canvas course site must contain at least one section tied to one CRN in Banner.
•	The Canvas course site must have a grading scheme enabled with valid grades accepted by Banner.
•	The Canvas instructor’s NetID is enrolled in the Canvas section within the course site as a Canvas Teacher.
•	The Canvas instructor is assigned the role of instructor or higher for the Banner section.
•	The Canvas instructor has an active faculty or staff role for the current semester.
Canvas Grading Best Practices
•	Before using GradeSync, it is best to grade all student assignments and post all grades. Ideally, there should be no blank or empty spaces in your gradebook. You have not posted all grades if you see an eye with a slash icon. See How do I use the icons and colors in the Gradebook?
•	The letter grade that the instructor sees in the Canvas Grades Total column will be sent to Banner. If the Total column has an eye icon with a slash, the student may see a different letter grade than the instructor. This occurs if there are still unposted grades in the gradebook. Posting all grades ensures there is no confusion for the student.
•	Instructors may prefer to hide totals in students’ grade summaries and hide grade distribution scoring details from students.
•	Instructors may choose to override a student’s final letter grade.
•	Communicate with co-instructors as to who will be sending grades to Banner. 
Instructions for Final GradeSync
Banner Final GradeSync can only be used once to send grades to Banner for a student and will not overwrite grades that exist in Banner.
Before using Banner Final GradeSync, your Canvas site may need additional setup. The instructions for setting up your Canvas Gradebook and using Banner Final GradeSync are split into three parts below.
1.	Confirm Grade Scheme Setup in Course Settings.
2.	Finalize Assignment Grading in Gradebook.
3.	Send Grades to Banner with Final GradeSync.
Part 1: Confirm Grade Scheme Setup in Course Settings
1.	Log into Canvas and navigate to your course.
Error! Filename not specified.
1.	Click Settings to access the Course Details tab.
2.	Locate the Grading Scheme category and then check the box to Enable course grading scheme.
3.	Click +New Grading Scheme to create a new course grading scheme.
4.	In the pop-up window, add a new Grading Scheme Name.
5.	Then, choose Grade by either Percentage or Points; by default, Percentage is chosen.
6.	Adjust the Letter Grade and Range to match your department's recommendations or the grading scale outlined in your course syllabus.
7.	Once you have set a grading scheme, click Save.

Error! Filename not specified.

Special Notes
•	The default grading scheme available in Canvas includes course grades that may not be valid grades accepted by your registrar. Please review your grading scheme carefully to ensure it aligns with school or departmental policy.
•	Each grading scheme needs to be named to be saved.
•	To earn a grade, the student must surpass the grade threshold listed in the grading scheme without rounding. If your course policy allows for rounding, then the grading scheme must reflect a lower threshold for a grade range.
•	Canvas allows you to override the final course grade. Banner Final GradeSync will accept override grades.
•	Temporary and nonstandard grades must appear in the Canvas grading scheme and be assigned in the grade book as an override grade. This includes grades such as I, INC, I/C, I/R, I/S, IU, IP, and IN.
•	Alternatively, you may submit the temporary grades via Banner before using Banner Final GradeSync.

2.	Ungraded work will be displayed as a dash or a square icon and will not impact the score in the Total column; thus, ungraded or excused assignments will not be counted against a student’s course grade.
3.	You may use the Set Default Grade function to bulk insert a grade for students without assignment submissions.
4.	Review each column header. The grade for each assignment may be posted to students. Unposted or hidden grades are reported in the displayed course grade in the gradebook for the instructor and are included in the course grade.
5.	To exclude assignments from the final course grade, navigate to the Assignments tool in your course navigation and edit the assignment settings.

Part 4: Review Processed GradeSync Submissions
Banner GradeSync sends grades to Banner once per hour. The Banner Status for each grade is marked with a pending icon when any course instructor returns to the Banner GradeSync page and the grades have been submitted. Once Banner has processed the grades, the Banner Status and Banner Message will be updated for each grade.
1.	Log into Canvas and navigate to your course.
2.	In the course navigation, click RU Faculty Tools. If RU Faculty Tools is not listed, please enable it in the course navigation.
3.	Click Launch GradeSync. 
4.	GradeSync will open in a new tab. 
5.	Click Launch Banner Final GradeSync.
6.	Review the GradeSync Terms of Use and click I Agree.
7.	If you are enrolled in more than 1 section in the Canvas course site, select the section in the drop-down menu.
8.	Click View GradeSync Status to continue. You may also receive an error message for each individual record. Possible Banner Messages are:
•	
o	Submission successful:The grade was successfully transferred to Banner. Log into Banner to view the grade.
o	Student enrollment not valid: The student in the Canvas course is not on the official Banner roster. Contact your school registrar to resolve this issue. 
o	Submission skipped; existing grade present: An existing grade for the enrolled student exists in Banner. 
o	Submitted grade not allowed: The letter grade is not valid. Please check your grading scheme only includes allowed letter grades. 
o	Submission skipped; enrolled section is not valid: The Canvas course includes a section that is not an official Banner course. Contact your school registrar and the Rutgers Canvas Help Desk to resolve this issue. 
o	Submission skipped; enrolled section is not gradable: The section in Banner is not gradable. 
o	Submission skipped; submitter not instructor of record: Contact your school registrar to be listed as a course instructor or ask another course instructor to submit the grades.
o	Submission skipped; Banner enrollment not valid: The student in the Canvas course is not on the official Banner roster. Contact your school registrar to resolve this issue. 
o	Submission skipped; Banner enrollment not gradable: The enrolled student in Banner is not gradable. 
o	Submission skipped; final grade generated from component marks: The course final grade is automatically calculated from assessment grades submitted to Banner.

To be accepted as a valid grade in the Canvas gradebook, temporary grades must appear in the Canvas grading scheme. Ideally, you will set the temporary grades as the lowest possible points earned to avoid erroneously assigning them to other students. This grading scheme should be set after you have completed all your assignment grades at the end of the term.

This error commonly occurs when an instructor first accesses Rutgers Canvas with an email login, and then a NetID login is added to their Rutgers Canvas user account.

This error commonly occurs when an instructor first accesses Rutgers Canvas with an email login and then a NetID login is added to their Rutgers Canvas user account.
The email login must be removed from the user’s profile to use REGIS GradeSync. Please contact the Rutgers Canvas Helpdesk with the error message and ask that your email login be removed from your user account.

title: Tools Mirror Sites – Instructor Guide
body:
This page describes how an instructor will use Mirror Sites in Rutgers Canvas to create a new blank course site and mirror the student roster for active sections.
Table of Contents
•	Important Information before using Mirror Sites
•	Requesting a Mirror Site 
o	Part 1: Launch Mirror Sites in the RU Faculty Tools
o	Part 2: Select Sections to Request Mirror Sites
o	Part 3: Mirror Site Confirmation Page
o	Part 4: Review Mirror Site Course Settings
•	Frequently Asked Questions 
o	When do the students get updated in the Mirror Sites?
o	Why am I getting an error when opening Mirror Sites?
o	Why are only some of the sections listed on the Mirror Site request page?
o	How do I transfer the grades on my Mirror Site to Rutgers?
Important Information before using Mirror Sites
•	Mirror Sites are only available for active Rutgers Course offerings. This tool cannot be used with Rutgers Health BANNER courses or with any manually created sections.
•	Mirror Sites cannot use the Canvas GradeSync tool. Make sure to keep final grades in the original site if you plan to use Canvas REGIS Gradesync.
•	Mirror Sites cannot use First Day Course Materials. First Day content must be shared on the original course site to take advantage of the discount course materials program.
•	You must be enrolled in the section as a teacher, TA, Facilitator, Course Support, or other editing role. If you are a sub-account admin, you must first add your non-admin netid into the section with one of the specified roles; your netid-adm account will not work. 
•	Only one Mirror Site may be created per section. If another course instructor has already requested a Mirror Site for a section, their NetID and request date will be listed on the request page.
Requesting a Mirror Site
Part 1: Launch Mirror Sites in the RU Faculty Tools
You must have an active NetID and be enrolled in this course with an editing role to use the Mirror Site tool.
1.	In Course Navigation, click RU Faculty Tools. If RU Faculty Tools is not listed, please enable it in the course navigation.
2.	Click Launch Mirror Sites.
3.	The tool will open in a new tab.

Error! Filename not specified.
Part 2: Select Sections to Request Mirror Sites
On the Mirror Site landing page, there will be an overview of the tool and the list of active sections pulled from the course. If the course has multiple sections or is cross-listed, each section will be displayed in a separate row. 
1.	Check the box for each section where a Mirror Site is needed and click Create Mirror Sites to submit the request.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	If the Request Status says “In Use”, then the Mirror Site already exists. Additional information about the previous request will be displayed in the table. 

Error! Filename not specified.
Part 3: Mirror Site Confirmation Page
When the request is completed, a confirmation page will provide links to each Mirror Site. You can go to the site by clicking on the Mirror Course Title or by finding Mirror Sites listed on your Canvas Courses page. 
Each selected section will create a separate Mirror Site. If you need to merge multiple Mirror Sites into 1 course site, please use the Canvas Cross-Listing Feature.
Error! Filename not specified.
Part 4: Review Mirror Site Course Settings
Mirror Sites are created in the same term and Canvas sub-account as the original site. Edit additional course settings to improve the student experience.
1.	The Course Name is displayed on the Dashboard. It is recommended to change the name so users can differentiate the Mirror Site from the original site.
2.	The Course Code is displayed at the top of the page in the course as a breadcrumb. It is recommended to change the course code so users can identify that they are currently viewing the Mirror Site.
3.	The Start and End dates are set to the term dates as the original course. To allow early access or immediate access, these dates need to be updated. See additional instructions on how to set earlier access.
4.	All sites are unpublished by default. After reviewing the start/end dates, publish the site to allow student access.

Error! Filename not specified.
Frequently Asked Questions
When do the students get updated in the Mirror Sites?
After a Mirror Site is requested, the requester is added immediately. The student roster will be added in the next student enrollment update. Additional information about students updating in Canvas can be found on the Canvas Provisioning page.
Why am I getting an error when I click on Launch Mirror Sites?
There are user and course requirements for the Mirror Sites creation app to work properly. If any of these requirements are not met, it may return a specific error message to you.
User Requirements:
•	Currently an active faculty or staff member at Rutgers.
•	Logging into Canvas with a Rutgers NetID. Email accounts will not work.
•	Enrolled in the Canvas section as a teacher, TA, Facilitator, Course Support, or other editing role.
Course Requirements:
•	Requesting a current or future term. Past terms are disabled and will not update the roster.
•	The Canvas section is associated with an active REGIS registration index number. This tool cannot be used with a Rutgers Health BANNER course.
If you receive any error messages, please send your course information and the error to help@canvas.rutgers.edu.
Why are only some of the sections listed on the Mirror Site request page?
Mirror Sites are only available for active Rutgers course offerings. This tool cannot be used with Rutgers Health BANNER courses or with manually created sections. If you created your own section, it will not have the required unique ID to pull the roster from the Rutgers Course Scheduling System.
If you believe your sections should be listed, please send your course information to help@canvas.rutgers.edu.
How do I transfer the grades from my Mirror Site to Rutgers REGIS?
Mirror Sites cannot use the Canvas GradeSync. Grades will need to be submitted from the original course site after it is finalized.
To copy the grades from the Mirror Site, it is recommended to create assignment columns for non-submission assignments in the Gradebook as a placeholder in the original course site. If you need assistance with copying the grades, please email help@canvas.rutgers.edu.

title: Tools Post'em – Getting Started for Instructors
body:
Instructors can use Rutgers Post'em to privately present individual feedback and/or grades to students. Multiple files can be shared with course students; each file may have as many data columns as needed. This tool does not communicate with the Canvas gradebook.
Table of Contents
•	Requirements
•	Create your Spreadsheet 
o	Special Characters
o	Course Roster Sync and Rutgers Post'em
•	Upload your Spreadsheet
•	What do my Students See?
•	How do I manage my worksheets?
Requirements
To share files with students, instructors must have a teacher, teacher-based, TA, or TA-based course role. Custom roles based on teacher and TA roles will have editor access in Post'em. With these roles, users can upload, publish, unpublish, download, delete, and update files.
•	Designer and observer roles will have student access in Post'em and can only view data if their login ID is included in the worksheet.
•	The uploaded file must be a comma-separated value (.csv) file type.
•	The first column must include the students' login IDs in lowercase. This value may be in the form of a Rutgers NetID or an email address for users who are not affiliated with Rutgers.
•	The worksheet cannot include any blank rows between rows with data.
•	The first row must include a heading for every column that contains data in your worksheet.
•	The worksheet must contain at least two columns and two rows.
Create your Spreadsheet
Course instructors must create a spreadsheet using the students' login IDs. This is obtained from a Grades export.
1.	Log in to Canvas and navigate to your course.
2.	Click Grades.

     Error! Filename not specified.
3.	In the Actions menu, select Export Entire Gradebook. 
4.	Please note whether the Canvas Test Student is listed.
5.	Click the downloaded file, or navigate to your downloads to open it.
6.	Highlight and copy the values in the SIS Login ID column for all your students. Do not include the column heading.

     Error! Filename not specified.
7.	Do not select the SIS Login ID for the Canvas Test Student created by using Student View.
8.	In your spreadsheet program, create a new worksheet.

     Error! Filename not specified.
9.	In the first column, add the login id as a column heading.
10.	Paste your student SIS Login IDs in the row below the login ID column heading.
11.	Add column headings in the first row and corresponding student-specific information to your spreadsheet. You may copy the student names from the gradebook export for your clarity when you view the entire worksheet in Rutgers Post'em. Rutgers Post'em will display each student's name.
12.	Save your file as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
Special Characters
Post'em is compatible with alphanumeric characters, including 0-9 and a-z, and most punctuation, including ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + , - / : ; < = > ? @ [ ] ^ _ { | } ~. Post'em does not display the backslash "\" or other ASCII characters, such as Greek symbols and accented characters. In other words, Rutgers Post'em will display printable ASCII characters 1-126, except 92, and not display ASCII characters 127-255.
Course Roster Sync and Rutgers Post'em
Since worksheets are created manually, course instructors need to monitor course rosters to add newly enrolled students to the worksheets. If a student's login ID is not included in a worksheet, the worksheet will not be displayed to the student. If information is included for a student who has dropped the course, the following error message is displayed: "The following user(s) are not in this course: [login ID]. Data for these users will be discarded."
Upload your Spreadsheet
Before uploading a file to Rutgers Post’em, please close other Canvas browsers and tabs to ensure your file is uploaded to the correct course.
1.	Click Rutgers Post’em in your course navigation. If it is not listed, enable it by managing the course navigation links in course Settings.
2.	Click +CSV to add a new CSV file.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Enter a title for the file.
4.	Click Select a CSV file and browse to your file location.
5.	To save your file and advance to the Preview screen, click Submit. To cancel and return to the main Post’em screen, click Cancel.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	On the Preview screen, you will see a sample of how the file will appear to your students. The column headers, Item Name and Item Detail, are not editable. You may do one of the following:
1.	Save will save the file without publishing it, so it is available only to teachers and TAs. You will return to the main Post’em page that lists all worksheets. 
2.	Save & Publish saves the file and makes it available to students immediately. You will return to the main Post’em page that lists all worksheets.
3.	Back to Upload will remove the uploaded file and let you select a different one.
4.	Cancel will not save your work and return you to the main Post’em page.

Error! Filename not specified.
7.	From the main Post’em page that lists all worksheets, click to expand the Actions menu. The options are:
1.	Publish/Unpublish to change availability to students.
2.	Edit to change the entry title and to replace the existing worksheet.
3.	Delete to remove the worksheet entry. Once a worksheet is published to students, it cannot be deleted; it can only be unpublished, so it remains part of the course record.
4.	View Worksheet to view the worksheet as an individual student or in its entirety.
5.	Download Worksheet to download a copy of the existing worksheet.

What do my Students See?
When a student accesses Rutgers Post’em in your course navigation, they will see a list of worksheets you have published (1). They will not see the full list of worksheets, including published (2) and unpublished (3) worksheets available within the instructor view.

How do I manage my worksheets?
In Rutgers Post'em, instructors can use the following features to manage their list of worksheets:
1.	Hide Unpublished Worksheets: Worksheets with the Unpublished status may be hidden from view when this checkbox is enabled. 
2.	Show entries per page: Set the number of worksheets per page by selecting the desired value. When the number of worksheets exceeds the selected limit, pagination appears below the worksheet list.

title: Tools REGIS Warning GradeSync
body:
This page describes how an instructor will use REGIS Warning GradeSync to send warning grades and comments from Canvas to REGIS.
REGIS Warning GradeSync is not available for Camden, Newark, Rutgers Health, or Banner courses. Contact your department for information on how to submit Warning Grades.
Table of Contents
•	REGIS Warning GradeSync Requirements
•	Warning GradeSync

REGIS Warning GradeSync Requirements
•	The Warning Period is open in REGIS.
•	The Canvas course site contains at least one section tied to one REGINDEX in REGIS.
•	The Canvas instructor’s NetID is enrolled in the Canvas site as a Canvas Teacher, TA, Facilitator, or Course Support.
•	The Canvas instructor is assigned a role of Grader or higher in REGIS for that section.
•	The Canvas instructor has an active faculty or staff role for the current semester.
Note: Warning grades can be submitted and changed during the open warning period. If a different warning grade is resubmitted, it will overwrite the existing warning grade in REGIS.
REGIS Warning GradeSync is not available for Camden and Newark. If you have not used REGIS to submit warning grades in the past, please confirm with your department before using the Canvas Warning GradeSync tool.
Instructions for REGIS Warning GradeSync
1.	In the course navigation, click RU Faculty Tools. If RU Faculty Tools is not listed, please enable it in the course navigation.
2.	Click Launch GradeSync.
3.	Rutgers GradeSync will open in a new tab.

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.
6.	Enter the Warning Codes and Comments for your students.

Error! Filename not specified.
7.	Click Submit Warning Grades.
8.	On the submission page, you will see a message indicating that the Warning Grades were successfully submitted, along with the status of each student.

Error! Filename not specified.

If you do not meet the minimum user requirements to use GradeSync, you will receive an error message. 
o	[RESP CODE 401] You are not an assigned REGIS Grader for this section – You do not have REGIS access to post grades for this section. Ask your academic unit for access.
o	[RESP CODE 403] You must have a REGIS Grader role for this section – You do not have REGIS access to post grades for this section. Ask your academic unit for access.
o	[RESP CODE 409] No grades may be posted during a closed Warning or Grading Period – The grading period is not open. Refer to grading period dates in REGIS.
o	[RESP CODE 500] REGIS Internal server error for the section [{0}]’s grade submission – Retry your submission.
9.	During the open warning period, warning grades can be submitted multiple times. If a warning grade is changed and resubmitted, it will overwrite the existing warning grade in REGIS.
10.	You may Return to Warning Grades or log into REGIS directly to verify grade submissions, resolve any issues, and make changes.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Where can I find the Warning Grading Period Dates?
REGIS will accept Warning Grades only during active grading periods. Any submissions outside of these dates will not be accepted.
To find these dates, go to the Electronic Student Grading System website and select Rosters & Electronic Grading Information System (REGIS).
On your section's roster page, you will see the dates for both Warning and Grading periods.
Where can I find more information about Warning Grades?
Each campus may have its own policy and requirements. Review their documentation below before contacting your Registrar's office.
Camden: Office of Registrar – Grade Instruction
Newark: MyRUN – Warning Grades
New Brunswick: Registrar – Submission of Warnings and Grades

title: Tools Rutgers Crosslist Courses Tool

The Crosslist Courses tool in Canvas was added by Rutgers OIT to provide faculty and staff with an easier way to combine enrollments from multiple sections into a single course site.
Understanding the differences between Courses and Sections in Canvas will be helpful before using this tool.
Requirements for using the Crosslist Courses tool
•	The person cross-listing needs to be enrolled in each section as a teacher, TA, Facilitator, Course Support, or other editing role.
•	The course site is listed under an academic or non-credit term. Templates and other non-academic sites will not be available for selection.
Additional Use Guidelines
•	Always cross-list before students submit work. Assignment submissions are retained with the course, not with the section enrollments. If you cross-list after students have already submitted work, all cross-listed enrollments will lose any associated assignment submissions and grades.
•	Once a section is cross-listed, the original Canvas site associated with the section is no longer accessible. If the user would like to re-crosslist or de-crosslist, they will need to contact the Canvas Help Desk.
