title: Tools Rutgers NetID Lookup in Canvas for Admins
body:
Rutgers NetID Lookup, powered by Rutgers LDAP, is available only to Rutgers Canvas users with a Canvas Admin role and an active CAS session. Users who have been logged into Canvas for a long time may need to log out and log back in to refresh their NetID/CAS session.
Rutgers NetID Lookup allows Canvas admins to search for directory information for Rutgers NetID users. Rutgers Canvas Admins may search based on the following criteria:
•	Anywhere in Name: Matches any value that begins with the information you provide. You may use partial names, e.g., Quincy instead of John Quincy Adams
•	Last Name: Returns exact match, e.g., De Witt instead of Witt must be searched to return Simeon De Witt.
•	First Name: Returns exact match, e.g., Alexander instead of Alex must be searched to return Alexander Hamilton.
•	Email Address: Only default email addresses will be listed. A user may have multiple addresses so you may need to search by firstname.lastname@rutgers.edu, by netid@rutgers.edu, or by netid@domain.rutgers.edu
•	NetID: Returns an exact match.
•	Rutgers ID: Returns an exact match.
•	Banner A Number: Returns an exact match.
Search result limitations:
•	Search is not case-sensitive. Wildcards are not accepted, i.e., Jo* Smith.
•	Search results will only include Rutgers-affiliated faculty, staff, and students. Results will NOT include all Canvas users.
•	Search results will not include Rutgers-affiliated faculty, staff, and students who have opted out of directory searches or of displaying their email addresses.
•	Search results are limited to 100. If more than 100 results are returned, an error message will display.
How to access NetID Lookup in a course
Canvas admins may bookmark NetID Lookup. Rutgers NetID Lookup is not accessible to users without Canvas admin privileges. Note:
•	If you have recently logged in to Canvas and have an active CAS session, you will have immediate access to the NetID Lookup.
•	If your CAS session has expired when you access NetID Lookup, you will be prompted to log in with your NetID and password. Canvas admins should log in with their netid-adm account or the Canvas NetID account with admin privileges.

title: Connect to ResNet during summer conferences
body:
ResNet utilizes dynamically assigned IP addresses (DHCP) that make getting online easier than statically assigned IP addresses. During each academic term, our system gets daily updates from Housing for all regular students. However, if you live in a residence hall at Rutgers due to a summer conference, your conference coordinator provides this information.
If you are living in a residence hall as a summer student, you should be able to register using your NetID and password. If you are unable to register, contact the OIT Help Desk.
If you are a Rutgers student or staff member and are living in a residence hall as a conference attendee, you should be able to register using your NetID and password. If you cannot register, contact your conference coordinator to confirm that your housing information was submitted to ResNet.
If you are unaffiliated with Rutgers and live in a residence hall as a conference attendee, your conference coordinator will supply you with your username and password for registration. If you cannot register, contact your conference coordinator to confirm that your housing information was submitted to ResNet.

title: How do I connect to RUWireless Secure
body:
To ensure your security, the Rutgers University network utilizes a secure authentication mechanism known as WPA2-Enterprise and 802.1X. This security mechanism protects your username and password. In a wireless environment, your data is also protected by network encryption. To utilize this secure network, your network connection requires specific settings.
Go to wifi.rutgers.edu to automatically configure your device for RUWireless Secure. After you are configured for RUWireless Secure, any time you are in range of a RUWireless access point, you will automatically connect to RUWireless Secure.
RUWireless Secure Locations
RUWireless Secure is broadcast on all of the RUWireless access points on all four Rutgers campuses. RUWireless Secure is available in all student centers and dining halls, most libraries, dorms, and many academic and administrative buildings across the University.
Why use RUWireless Secure?
•	RUWireless Secure utilizes a secure authentication mechanism known as WPA2-Enterprise and 802.1X, which keeps your username and password safe when logging in.
•	RUWireless Secure protects your data that is sent over the wireless network. Even when using non-SSL or HTTPS connections.
•	The RUWireless Secure supplicant stores your username and password, so any time you are within range of a RUWireless access point, you will automatically connect to RUWireless Secure, bypassing the login page.*
How to Set Up RUWireless Secure
1.	Connect to RUWireless: Select the wireless network named RUWireless from the list of available networks on your device.
2.	Open a Browser: A login page should appear. If not, manually navigate to wifi.rutgers.edu.
3.	Log In: Click "I have a NetID and password" and follow the on-screen instructions.
4.	Automatic Configuration: Once setup is complete, your device will automatically connect to RUWireless Secure whenever you're in range.
Step-by-step instructions

•	RUWireless Secure Android setup
•	RUWireless Secure Windows setup

•	RUWireless Secure manual setup

body:
RUWireless is a wireless network available to Rutgers University visitors. The network provides campus guests and visitors with access to the wireless network while on campus for web, email, and other communication needs. This is an open wireless network with specific service restrictions that provide no data privacy.
Intended Use
This network does not require authentication and is not encrypted. The network is provided for visitors and short-term guests, offering limited Internet access. The RUWireless network is meant for normal web browsing, and some services are restricted. CAS is specifically restricted so that Rutgers students, faculty, and staff must use RUWireless Secure. For more information about RUWireless Secure, please visit the RUWireless Secure Setup page.
Why use RUWireless?
•	Guest access – visitors to the University receive access to an unencrypted wireless network, which does not require authentication.
•	Onboarding – affiliated students, faculty, and staff can use RUWireless to initially connect to the Internet and configure RUWireless Secure.
For a step-by-step guide, please follow the RUWireless Login Instructions.

title: policies
body:
Policies and guidelines
The Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy governs the use of RUWireless, policies specific to Office of Information Technology systems, and the RUWireless Virus and Bandwidth Guidelines. By using our networks, you agree to follow these policies and be responsible for any failure to do so. It is solely the user's responsibility to familiarize themselves with and adhere to the policy linked below.
Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Computing and Information Technology Resources 
By using the unsecured RUWireless network, you acknowledge that personal information can be compromised while being transmitted. Rutgers University cannot be held responsible for any resulting loss or damages, and as such, RUWireless encourages its users to utilize secure services when accessing network resources wirelessly.
If you wish to use RUWireless with encryption, please connect to RUWireless Secure.
Virus propagation guideline
RUWireless networks are automatically monitored for virus-like activity. Certain virus propagation techniques are scanned for and, if detected, are logged. The user of the offending host is then blocked from transmitting data until either the suspect activity can be explained or disinfection can be proven. Users are automatically notified when they attempt to log in to RUWireless of their "infected" status. It is the responsibility of the user to notify RUWireless administration when they are informed of their "infected" status, no attempt will be made to notify users by any other means.
It should be noted that certain seemingly harmless hacking attempts, such as port scanning or ping flooding a host, can be mistaken as virus propagation and will result in a loss of privileges on RUWireless.
Bandwidth utilization guideline
Bandwidth that passes through RUWireless and RUWireless Secure is dynamically allocated based on the combined usage of all clients. This approach generally results in higher network speeds than the previous limit of 3Mbps per host. The Internet bandwidth allocated to RUWireless is capped at 2Gbps; however, internal University traffic is not metered.
The system passively monitors network throughput when traffic is light. The system issues per-connection penalties as the overall usage approaches its limit based on the duration of each connection, a device's bandwidth consumption, and the number of active connections. In the long term, large consumers of data are more likely to be penalized when utilization is high, while burst traffic, such as voice, email, and web browsing, will be given priority. The system does not inspect the payload of the traffic that passes through it at any time in this process.
This is still a best-effort technology. Actual network speeds will vary based on several factors, including the model of the access point, client device, client load on the local access points, interference, overall network congestion, and remote server.
We are evaluating this approach on the New Brunswick/Piscataway campuses now and hope to employ it elsewhere in the future.

If you are in a RUWireless coverage area and connected to RUWireless, then you should get redirected when you attempt to load any Rutgers or external webpage.
If you do not get redirected, you should try to refresh your browser after 45 seconds. In some cases, when you first connect to a wireless network, multiple applications and/or browser extensions can try to update all at once, making our system think your computer is infected with a virus or spyware. This will cause you to be put in a penalty role for 30 seconds. After those 30 seconds, you will be released from this role. Restarting your browser will not help fix this problem and may cause all of your extensions to be reloaded and trigger the penalty role again.
In other cases, the webpage you are trying to reach might not be redirectable, including but not limited to SSL-encrypted HTTPS pages.
You may try to load another webpage, such as Google, to be redirected to the RUWireless Secure login page.
Optionally, you may navigate directly to the wifi.rutgers.edu to get started.

title: FAQ Why am I not able to send e-mail from RUWireless?
body:
Sending an email from RUWireless is possible, but it is restricted. Most email clients use the SMTP protocol to send emails.
Due to a large increase in the number of email viruses that spread using SMTP, RUWireless prevents email clients from connecting to non-Rutgers SMTP email servers (ports 25 and 465).
You can still send email through webmail services or trusted Rutgers SMTP servers using any authorized Rutgers-affiliated email address.

title: FAQ Why is the wireless connection slower than a wired connection?
body: There are several reasons why a wireless connection is slower than a wired connection. First, the technology itself is slower than most wired connections. Second, RUWireless uses a QoS bandwidth limitation to provide a fair level of service to all users. Without it, it would be possible for a single user to sit very close to an access point and “hog” all of the bandwidth. Third, the amount of bandwidth you get is partially determined by how strong your signal is, so even though the RUWireless team has made every effort to provide clear, strong signals in marked coverage areas, there still remains the possibility of outside interference such as microwaves and cordless phones which can drastically affect bandwidth.

title: FAQ Why is there a wireless access point in my room?
body:
What is a Wireless AP?
A wireless Access Point (AP) is a networking hardware device that allows Wi-Fi devices to connect to a network. They are used to provide network connectivity in large buildings and spaces. They make sure that everyone at Rutgers – students, teachers, and staff – can get a good wireless internet connection through the RUWireless network, wherever they are in the building.
Error! Filename not specified.
Why is it in my room?
The AP is in your room to ensure that the equipment is able to service full coverage and multiple devices, and some wireless access points are permanently installed within dorm rooms and apartments. These access points cannot be moved or removed as they are strategically placed to successfully service all residents.
If you have any questions or concerns about having the wireless devices in your room or apartment, you can contact Residence Life at (848) 445-0750 or oncampus@rutgers.edu for more information.
If you have any questions or concerns about wireless signal exposure, please see the FCC webpage for Wireless Safety information.

title: FAQ Are ScarletApps accounts required for all students?
body:

For this reason, Rutgers requires all Students to have a ScarletMail account to receive all official Rutgers emails. You may choose to forward your ScarletMail email to an external email account, but the ScarletMail account cannot be removed as a delivery address.

title: FAQ NotebookLM
body:
NotebookLM differs from traditional AI modules by allowing you to upload documents, webpages, videos, and audio files to a custom notebook. The tool then uses Google’s Gemini AI to analyze, digest, and make connections between the source material and transform the sources into study guides, mind maps, and even audio.
With the Rutgers license for NotebookLM, your data, including uploaded sources, queries related to the sources, and query responses, are not used to train Google’s AI models. 
What can I use NotebookLM for?
NotebookLM is useful for creating study guides, summarizing long documents, organizing research, creating outlines, and more. 
However, it should not be used to process any data that is considered PHI or used for University Business in accordance with University Policy 70.1.6. Review the ScarletApps section on the Data Classification Matrix for details on what can and cannot be used in NotebookLM. 
Who can use NotebookLM?
NotebookLM is part of the ScartMail/ScarletApps suite of tools and, therefore, is available at no cost to students, faculty, and staff who have a ScarletMail account.
When using NotebookLM with a ScarletMail account, you receive additional data privacy protections and ensure that materials, queries, and query responses are not used to train other AI models.
How is NotebookLM accessed? 
To access NotebookLM, you can visit the NotebookLM website and log in with your ScarletMail account. To utilize the data privacy protections, ensure you are logged in with your ScarletMail account, and not a personal Google account. 
Faculty and staff who do not have a ScarletMail account can activate their account to access the product.
Additional Information

title: Forwarding ScarletMail to Rutgers Connect
body:
Per University Policy 70.1.6, all email and calendaring used to conduct University Business must be created, stored, processed, and transmitted using the official University Email and Calendaring systems; where University Business is defined as "work performed as part of an employee’s job responsibilities, daily work, and duties performed on behalf of the University by faculty, staff, student workers, guests, and other persons."
If you are faculty or staff, all email activity related to University Business should be conducted by default on Rutgers Connect and not through ScarletMail. 
Turn on automatic forwarding
1.	On your computer, open Gmail and log in with your NetID@scarletmail.rutgers.edu address. 
2.	In the top right, click Settings and then See all settings.
3.	Click the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab.
4.	In the "Forwarding" section, click Add a forwarding address.
5.	Enter your Rutgers Connect email address in the format netid@domain.rutgers.edu.
6.	Click Next, then Proceed, and then OK.
7.	A verification message will be sent to that address. Click the verification link in that message.
8.	Go back to the settings page for the Gmail account you want to forward messages from, and refresh your browser.
9.	Click the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab.
10.	In the "Forwarding" section, select Forward a copy of incoming mail to. 
11.	Choose what you want to happen with the ScarletMail copy of your emails. It is recommended to keep a copy in your ScarletMail. 
12.	At the bottom of the page, click Save Changes. 
Turn off automatic forwarding
1.	On your computer, open Gmail and log in with your NetID@scarletmail.rutgers.edu address. 
2.	In the top right, click Settings and then See all settings.
3.	Click the Forwarding and POP/IMAP tab.
4.	In the "Forwarding" section, click Disable forwarding.
5.	At the bottom, click Save Changes.

title: Google Drive for Desktop
body:
Google offers a desktop application that lets you quickly access all your Google Drive files on demand, directly from your computer, without using up drive space. With Google Drive for desktop, your files are stored in the cloud instead of on your computer, and any changes you make are automatically synced to the cloud for quick, easy access anywhere you have an Internet connection.
Table of Contents
•	Installation 
o	System Requirements
•	Getting Started 
o	What are the features of Google Drive for Desktop?
o	How much storage do I have for my Drive files?
o	Making Files Available Offline
o	Where can I get more information?
Installation
1.	Download Google Drive for Mac or Windows. You must be logged into your Google account to see this page.
2.	Run the installation package.
3.	Log in to the portal with your ScarletMail email address and password.
4.	You'll then be prompted to enter your NetID and NetID Password.
5.	Follow the instructions and choose what you want to sync. 
On macOS, if you receive an error that says "Google Drive encountered a problem and has stopped," go to System Preferences > Security and Privacy > Allow Google Drive.
System Requirements
•	Windows: Windows 10 and up (64-bit only), Windows Server 2016 and up (64-bit only)
•	Mac: macOS Catalina 10.15.7 and up. For macOS 11 and lower, follow these steps.
Getting Started
Once Google Drive is installed, a folder called Google Drive will appear on the left in your Finder or File Explorer. This folder will contain both your personal Google Drive and any Team Drives you are part of. The only difference between these files and any other file on your computer is that they are not stored on your computer by default, and any changes you make to them will automatically sync with your cloud storage.
What are the features of Google Drive for Desktop?
With Drive, you can:
•	
o	Quickly see all your Google Drive files in Finder/Explorer (including Team Drives).
o	Browse and organize Google Drive files without downloading all of them to your computer.
o	Choose which files or folders you'd like to make available offline.
o	Open files in common apps like Microsoft Office and Adobe Photoshop.
How much storage do I have for my Drive files?
ScarletMail/ScarletApps accounts are limited to 30 gigabytes (GB).
Making Files Available Offline
By default, Google Drive does not store a copy of your files on your local computer. This means that if you do not have an Internet connection, you will not be able to access these files. In order to make your files accessible offline, right-click on a file or folder and select Available Offline under the Drive menu. Please note that doing so will store a copy on your computer, using up more of your hard drive space.
Where can I get more information?
To get started with Drive, visit the Drive Help Center. Please note that to see this page and install the new app, you must log in to Google with your ScarletMail email address and password.

title: Migrating ScarletMail/ScarletApps data to another account
body:
This procedure must be used exclusively on personally owned data. Data conducted as part of University business, or classified as Restricted or Critical ePHI under Rutgers Information Classification Policy 70.1.2 must not be transferred to any other non-Rutgers system. Doing so may represent a violation of the Federal HIPAA Privacy/Security rules, State Privacy Laws, and/or University policies. Please prepare your data accordingly prior to the migration procedure.
There are two different ways to migrate your ScarletMail information:
•	Google Transfer: Transfer your data from ScarletMail to a personal Gmail account.
•	Google Takeout: Download all your ScarletMail data to upload to another service.
Table of Contents
•	Google Transfer 
o	What can be transferred
o	How to transfer your data
•	Google Takeout 
o	How to download your data
•	Alternate download methods 
o	Files
o	Photos
o	Emails
o	Contacts
o	Calendars
•	Move files from your University Google Drive to another location 
o	Migrating to a drive on your computer
o	Migrate files to a different cloud service
Google Transfer
Let's you transfer your ScarletMail data listed below to a personal Gmail account. The original files stay in your school account. Any changes you make to the copied files do not affect the originals. 
What can be transferred
•	Emails (does not include contacts, chats, or tasks)
•	Documents that you own in Google Drive (except files in the "Google Photos" section of Drive)
•	Documents in My Drive (When the copy process is done, you'll be notified by email about any files in My Drive that weren't copied)
o	Note: A file in My Drive won't be copied if either of the following is true:
	You're a Viewer, not an Editor or Owner
	The owner has turned off download, print, and copy options for commenters and viewers
•	Photos, videos, and albums you own
How to transfer your data
1.	While logged into your ScarletMail account, go to Google's Transfer page.
2.	Enter the email address of the personal Google Account where you want to copy your content.
3.	Select Get code.
4.	On your personal Google Account, check your Gmail inbox for a confirmation email from Google.
5.	In the email, select Get confirmation code. A new tab will open with a code.
6.	On your ScarletMail account, go back to the "Transfer your content" page.
7.	Enter the code, then choose Verify.
8.	Select the content you'd like to copy, then select Start transfer.
9.	The copy process usually occurs within a few hours, but it can take up to a week. You'll receive an email once it is complete. 
10.	Verify that all data has been transferred correctly. 
11.	If the data is no longer needed in your ScarletMail account, delete it from there. 
12.	If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, empty the trash in the relevant services on your ScarletMail account (Drive, Photos, etc). 
Note:
•	The copy process usually occurs within a few hours, but it can take up to a week.
•	Extremely large amounts of data being transferred may run into issues. You'll receive an email should the transfer fail. If this happens, you can try transferring multiple small amounts of data instead of one large transfer. 
•	Copied files might appear in batches on your personal Google Account during the copy process.
•	Content will be copied to a folder labeled with the original account name and the date the process was initiated.
•	When your files are finished copying, you'll get an email at your Gmail address.
•	More details on the transfer process can be found on Google's Help Page.
To download data from your ScarletMail account that is not included in the list above (contacts, calendar, etc.), follow the directions below to download it via Google Takeout. You can then upload the files to the programs of your choosing.
Google Takeout
Allows you to download all your ScarletMail data (files, email, contacts, calendar, photos, etc.) by following the steps below.
How to download your data
1.	While logged into your ScarletMail account, go to the Download your data page. Google products that have your data are automatically selected.
2.	Go through all available data and uncheck any you do not wish to download. For some sections, you may be able to edit the options to select only some data for that section, as well as the file format it is exported to.
3.	Click Next Step.
4.	Choose your preferred Delivery Method, Frequency, File Type, and Size. 
5.	Click Create Export.
6.	Once the export is complete, you'll receive an email with a link to its location, depending on the Delivery Method chosen. 
7.	Verify that all data has been downloaded correctly. 
8.	If the data is no longer needed in your ScarletMail account, delete it from there. 
9.	If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, empty the trash in the relevant services on your ScarletMail account (Drive, Photos, etc). 
Note:
•	Depending on the amount of information in your account, the link to access your export may take a few minutes or several hours to be sent.
•	If you have a slow internet connection on your local device, you may try using the Computer Labs or the Virtual Labs, which may offer faster speeds. 
•	Extremely large amounts of data being downloaded may run into issues. If this happens, you can try downloading multiple small chunks of data instead of a single large download. 
•	Files will be downloaded in a variety of formats, e.g., DOC, PPTX, XLSX, JPG, PDF, MP4, JSON, or HTML formats.
•	More details on the download process can be found on Google's Help Page. 
Alternate download methods
Alternative methods to download the most common types of data from your ScarletMail account are listed below. 
Files
In order to migrate ScarletMail Docs to another service, you will need to download all of your docs to your local computer, then upload them to another service. Ensure you have a good internet speed on your local device. If you have a slow internet connection on your local device, you may try using the Computer Labs or the Virtual Labs as they may have a faster speed. 
To download your ScarletMail Docs, do the following:
1.	While logged into your ScarletMail account, go to Google Drive.
2.	Select all the files that you wish to download. You can hold the Ctrl key on your keyboard while clicking multiple files to select many files at once. Or after clicking a file, press Ctrl+A to select all files in your Drive. If you are using a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl.
3.	Click the Menu icon in the top-right corner of the window to access More Actions.
4.	Click Download.
5.	Verify that all files have been downloaded correctly. 
6.	If the files are no longer needed in your ScarletMail account, delete them from there. 
7.	If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, empty the trash in your Drive on your ScarletMail account.
This will download all of the files in your ScarletMail Drive to your local computer. From there, you can upload to another service like Dropbox. 
Photos
You can download photos or videos you select individually or in bulk to your local device, then upload them to another service. If you have a slow internet connection on your local device, you may try using the Computer Labs or the Virtual Labs, which may offer faster speeds. 
1.	On your computer, go to Google Photos.
2.	Select the check mark for the photos or videos you want to download.
3.	Click More Options (three dots) and then Download. 
4.	Verify that all photos have been downloaded correctly. 
5.	If the photos/videos are no longer needed in your ScarletMail account, delete them from there. 
6.	If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, empty the trash in Photos on your ScarletMail account.
You can also share your photos and videos with another Google account you own. When accepting the share on the other account, you can choose to save the photos there as well. 
1.	On your computer, go to Google Photos.
2.	Sign in with your Google Account.
3.	Click Settings > Partner sharing > Get started.
4.	Enter or select an email address for another Google Account you own.
5.	Select which photos to add to your shared account. 
o	All photos: You can share all photos.
o	Photos of specific people: You can select one or more face groups to share. Photos that match any of the selected face groups will be shared. Learn more about filtering by face groups.
o	Only show photos since this day: Any photos whose dates come after the selected date will be shared. Learn more about filtering by date.
6.	Click Next.
7.	Click Send invitation.
8.	On your computer, open Google Photos again.
9.	Sign in with the Google Account that you shared to.
10.	At the top left, click Sharing.
11.	Click the invitation you want to accept. Then, click Accept.
12.	At the top, click Settings > Partner sharing.
13.	Below Partner sharing, click on Save to Account to see options.
14.	Click Save. 
o	All photos: Any photos shared by partners will be saved.
o	Photos of selected people: Select from your face groups. When Google Photos recognizes any of those face groups from your partner’s photos, it’ll save the photos automatically.
15.	Click Done.
16.	Verify that all photos have been transferred correctly. 
17.	If the photos/videos are no longer needed in your ScarletMail account, delete them from there. 
18.	If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, empty the trash in Photos on your ScarletMail account.
It is important to remove the partner sharing once all photos have been transferred correctly.
1.	Click Settings > Partner Sharing.
2.	Click Remove Partner.
3.	Click Remove.
More information can be found on Google's Partner Sharing page. 
Emails
In order to migrate your ScarletMail email to another email service, you will need to configure an email program to access both your personal email account and your ScarletMail account.
For instructions on setting up an email program for your personal email account, please refer to your email provider's documentation.
After you have set up an email program for your personal email,l you will need to configure the program to connect to the ScarletMail account. The following documentation to help you with this procedure is listed below:
•	Setting up Outlook for ScarletMail
•	Setting up Thunderbird for ScarletMail
•	Setting up Windows Mail for ScarletMail
•	Setting up Mac Mail for ScarletMail
Now, you can start moving messages from your ScarletMail account to your personal email account. In many instances, you can simply click and drag messages from one account to another. You can also select multiple messages at once by holding the Control key and selecting individual messages or simply by holding down the Control and the A key (or the Command and the A key on Macintosh) to select all of the messages in the folder. 
If you want to free up more storage space on your ScarletMail account, delete the transferred emails and empty the trash in Gmail on your ScarletMail account.
Contacts
To migrate ScarletMail Contacts to another service, you will need to export your contacts to a CSV file. A CSV file is simply a text file with your contacts separated by commas. This type of file is very simple to import into another email reading program.
To export your contacts, do the following:
1.	While logged into your ScarletMail account, go to Google Contacts.
2.	Select one of the following:
o	A single contact: Check the box next to the contact name.
o	Multiple contacts: Check the boxes next to all the contacts you want to export.
o	All contacts: Check the box next to any contact, then in the top left, click Selection Actions, then All.
3.	In the top-left corner, click More actions, then Export.
4.	To back up your contacts, select CSV.
5.	To save your file, click Export.
This will create a file that can be imported into another email program or address book system.
Calendars
To migrate ScarletMail Calendars to another service, you will need to export your calendars in the ICS format. ICS is a standard format that most other calendar systems will understand.
To export your calendar,s do the following:
1.	While logged into your ScarletMail account, go to Google Calendar. Note: You can't export your calendar from the Google Calendar app.
2.	In the top right, click the Gear icon, then Settings.
3.	In the menu on the left, click Import & export.
4.	Under “Export," click Export.
5.	A ZIP file will download to your computer.
6.	If you open the ZIP file, you'll find individual ICS files for each of your calendars.
This will create a file that can be imported into another email program or address book system.
Move files from your University Google Drive to another location
Migrating to a drive on your computer
You can migrate your files to a drive attached to your computer by utilizing Google Takeout. 
Migrate files to a different cloud service
First, download the files using Google Takeout, then upload them to your storage option of choice. If you are uploading files to Box, you can find instructions in Box's Help Center. If you are uploading files to Microsoft OneDrive, instructions are available on Microsoft's Support Page. 
Information regarding storage options available to Rutgers Faculty, Staff, and Students is in Box and Microsoft OneDrive. Learn more about these on the Rutgers cloud storage website.

title: Reducing ScarletMail/ScarletApps storage
body:
What specific steps should I take to reduce my storage?
1.	Confirm how much storage you’re using on the Google storage overview page. 
2.	Clean up your ScarletApps account. 
o	Drive: Review your Drive storage and delete large or unnecessary files. After deleting, make sure to empty your trash folder since it still counts towards your storage until they are permanently deleted. 
o	Photos: Review your Photos Storage. 
	Delete large or unnecessary photos and videos. After deleting, make sure to empty your trash since it still counts towards your storage until they are permanently deleted. 
	You can also reduce the size of your photos and videos by storing them at a slightly reduced quality. To do this, go to the Photos Settings page and select Storage Saver. 
o	Mail: Review your Gmail and delete unnecessary emails. After deleting, make sure to empty your trash folder, since it still counts towards your storage until it is permanently deleted. 
3.	Transfer or download your data. 
o	Google Transfer lets you transfer your data from ScarletMail to a personal Gmail account.
o	Google Takeout lets you download your ScarletMail data to be uploaded to another service.
o	For more information and instructions on transferring or downloading your data, see the article on migrating ScarletMail data to another account.
4.	Review other storage solutions.
o	University data should be stored in accordance with Departmental IT guidance. Some options include Box for Rutgers or Microsoft Teams (part of Rutgers Connect, the university's implementation of Microsoft 365).
o	If you have extremely large storage needs due to research projects, videos, or other reasons, please contact the IT staff at the department sponsoring the research or the OIT Help Desk to explore other storage options.
o	Please review the Rutgers Acceptable Use Policy for Information Technology Resources and make sure you’re storing data in accordance with our policies.
For further assistance
If you have specific questions or need assistance, please contact your department’s IT staff, if applicable, or the OIT Help Desk.

title: account audits
body:
Who can have a ScarletMail account?
According to the Office of Information Technology guidelines, only the following classes of people are eligible to have ScarletMail accounts:
•	Current employees of Rutgers University
•	Current students 
•	Alumni
•	Retirees
•	Professor Emeritus
•	Guests: individuals who are conducting University business and are directly associated with the University, but are not officially on the University's payroll. Examples of guests include visiting professors/scholars, members of auxiliary groups, and others who are working on University business or affiliated with the University.
The following groups of people are not automatically eligible for ScarletMail accounts:
•	Prior students who have withdrawn from all courses
•	Employees of other organizations who are performing work at Rutgers
Any of the above may be eligible for a guest account if a Rutgers department or division is willing to sponsor them. Please see the Guest Account page for further information.
Recently re-hired employees who have not yet been added to the RIAS payroll system, and thereby given a Faculty or Staff role, may have their department's payroll person use the Early Employee NetID form to request an early role.
How can I keep my ScarletMail account?
We determine which accounts should be closed by comparing ScarletMail usernames with the active roles (e.g. Student or Alumni) of usernames listed in the University's Open Registry (OR) service, which is used as the basis for the Rutgers Online Directory. The OR may have some information that needs to be corrected.
If you have received an account closure notice and you believe that this is in error, please find the group you belong to in the appropriate subsection below (Current Employees, Guests, Students, Others) and follow the instructions there.
Current Employees
You may not be listed in OR as a current employee. To check this, go to the People Search tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, contact your department's Human Resources person.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, contact your department's Human Resources person.
If your information is correct, or when your department's Human Resources person has corrected your record, your department’s Rutgers Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Students
You may not be listed in the OR as a current student. To check this, go to the People Search tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
Guests
Guests will have to determine with their sponsor if Rutgers Connect, ScarletMail, or even no Rutgers email account (for example, using a home institution’s email service) is appropriate for their needs.
If you are affiliated with Rutgers but not employed full-time, you may request a guest account. Have a sponsor in the department you are working with, go to the Guest Account site and submit a request for you; it will be sent to our Accounts Office for processing. 
Every year, you must renew your guest account. You will be notified when it is time to renew your account (30 days prior to the account's expiration). 
Your Rutgers Delegated Administrator can assist your sponsor in submitting a Guest Account request and, if necessary, in creating your ScarletMail account.
Others
If you do not fit into any of the above categories, you may want to try contacting a department at Rutgers related to the work you do and ask if they would be willing to sponsor a Guest account for you.
We have no mechanism for people no longer associated with Rutgers to pay a fee and thus keep their accounts. These people should be able to pay for a full account on any number of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) or obtain a free e-mail account from various web services. Rutgers cannot recommend one such group over another.
What should I do before the account is closed?
If you will be losing access to your ScarletMail account, you may want to take the following steps.
•	Notify your regular correspondents, mailing lists, etc., about your change of address. We cannot forward mail from a deleted account to another address.
•	You will lose access to your data once your account is closed, so you will want to save your Google Drive files, emails, and contacts to another location. Review the information on how to migrate data from ScarletMail.
What happens after the account is closed?
After your account is closed, you will lose access to your ScarletMail account. When an account is closed, any e-mail addressed to such an account will be returned to the sender ("bounced") with an automatic message of the type "No such user at this site".
Approximately 4 weeks after your account is closed, your ScarletMail account will be deleted.
I need further assistance!
If you have questions about any of the above, you can email help@oit.rutgers.edu or contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: Setting up an iOS device for ScarletMail
body:

title: Spam and Virus Filtering at Rutgers
body:
Rutgers Connect
Rutgers Connect is a Microsoft product that provides its own spam filtering service.
Learn more about the Junk Email Filter (for the Microsoft Outlook application), or learn about Junk email and phishing (for Outlook on the web).
ScarletMail
ScarletMail is a Google Gmail system. Spam blocking and filtering is controlled by Google and not OIT.
For information about Spam Filtering with ScarletMail, please read Google's overview of Gmail's spam filter.
What should I do if legitimate emails are being blocked by the University's Spam or Antivirus Systems?
If you find that delivery of legitimate mail is being affected by the filters, please contact the OIT Help Desk.
When contacting the OIT Help Desk, please have as much information about the message being blocked as possible. Some information may include:
•	Address of the sender of the blocked email message
•	The time the message that was blocked was sent
•	The complete address to which the blocked message was sent
•	A copy of any error messages or notifications that the sender of the message received.
If you receive a phishing scam or other malicious email, please forward the full email to abuse@rutgers.edu.
Find more information about reporting abuse here.

title: FAQ Can an RBHS affiliate obtain a ScarletMail?
body:
If you are an affiliate of the Rutgers Biomedical and Health Sciences department your default email account will be Connect (Office 365). This is because those with an active RBHS role are typically flagged in our systems as having access to Protected Health Information (PHI). Connect is not open to third-party applications and is designed by Rutgers to keep protected health information secure.
RBHS affiliates can obtain a ScarletMail but are only allowed to set a delivery address that is an RBHS email account (Connect). They are only allowed to use their alias or RBHS email account as an official Rutgers email address and are not permitted to forward their RBHS email to another account (such as ScarletMail).
Both your Connect and ScarletMail can be setup during your NetID activation process or through Service Activation.

title: FAQ Can I change the display name on my ScarletMail?
body:
You can change your display name (your First and Last Name) that appears when you send from your ScarletMail. When it is first activated, ScarletMail will pull your First and Last name from what Rutgers has on file. However, it will not update your display name on ScarletMail if your name at Rutgers changes for any reason. You may also wish to add a distinguishing title, such as Dr., to your name, change your First name to a nickname, or your Last name if you are married. If you use Gmail's web interface, you may update your name by following the instructions below. If you use a different application or interface to send from your ScarletMail, you will have to review the documentation provided by that application's vendor. 
1.	Go to Gmail and enter your ScarletMail Email Address: netid@scarletmail.rutgers.edu. Click Next.
2.	Enter your Rutgers NetID and password. Click Login.
3.	In the top right, click the Gear Icon to get to Settings, and then click See all settings.
4.	Click the Accounts and Import or Accounts tab.
5.	Under Send mail as, click edit info.
6.	Under Name, enter the name you want to show when you send messages.
7.	At the bottom, click Save Changes.

title: FAQ Can I request my ScarletMail account be removed?
body:
While registered as a Student, you cannot request that your ScarletMail account be deleted. You must have a ScarletMail account as it is where official Rutgers emails are guaranteed to be received. 
If you are an Alumni or non-student Faculty/Staff, you may request that your account be deleted by submitting the ScarletMail self-deletion request form.

title: FAQ Can I sign into my ScarletMail and personal Gmail account at the same time?
body: Yes, multiple sign-ins with the same browser needs to be enabled though. This can be done using the multiple sign-in settings page.

title: FAQ
body:
Can my ScarletMail account use my name, not my NetID?" "
ScarletMail accounts are required to use the NetID as the account name, so it is not possible. However, you can set up a personalized email address, or mail alias, in the form of “firstname.lastname@rutgers.edu”, and set ScarletMail (or most preferred mail programs) to send using that address in the From line, rather than the netid@scarletmail.rutgers.edu address.
 Visit the article on setting up ScarletMail to use your official Rutgers email address for more details.

title: FAQ How can I forward my ScarletMail mail to my non-Rutgers email account?
body:
We do not recommend doing this. Fall and Spring Session Students are required to have ScarletMail accounts so that they can receive official messages from Rutgers. We cannot guarantee delivery of official Rutgers email to non-Rutgers accounts.
In addition per University Policy 70.1.6, all email and calendaring used to conduct University Business must be created, stored, processed, and transmitted using the official University Email and Calendaring systems; where University Business is defined as "work performed as part of an employee’s job responsibilities, daily work, and duties performed on behalf of the University by faculty, staff, student workers, guests, and other persons." Ensure that none of your ScarletMail emails fall within this definition if you set up forwarding. 
The recommended way of forwarding to an external account is using the auto-forward feature built into Gmail. Follow Google's guide on how to automatically forward Gmail messages to another account. It is highly recommended that during the setup process, you select to keep a copy of the email on ScarletMail. You may prefer to read the copies on the external account, but if a message fails to be delivered there, this will allow you to be able to find the copy on the ScarletMail account. 
Please make sure to log into your ScarletMail account every so often to delete any unneeded duplicate messages.

title: FAQ How long can I keep my ScarletMail account after I leave Rutgers?
body:
Only Alumni, Retirees, and Professor Emeritus are eligible to keep their ScarletMail/ScarletApps account after leaving the University. People who leave Rutgers without formally graduating, even if only for one semester, are subject to losing their accounts.
These accounts are subject to regular audits to check if it is still actively being used. If you are in one of these groups and your account is deemed inactive, you will be contacted to confirm that you are still using the account. It will remain active so long as you respond to these inquiries in a timely fashion. If there is no response, the account will be closed, and all data will be permanently deleted. 
Alumni who no longer want their ScarletMail accounts should complete the ScarletMail self-deletion request form. Closing a ScarletMail account will also remove access to other ScarletApps services. There is no way to remove a single ScarletApps service.
More information on who is eligible can be found on the ScarletMail account audit article.

title: FAQ I deleted my email on ScarletMail. Can it be retrieved?
body:
If you delete a message or document, it will be placed in your Trash folder for 30 days. After 30 days, it will be deleted permanently.
However, once you click Empty Trash now or Delete Forever the deleted message can no longer be retrieved. 
OIT does not have access to restore deleted data. 
Visit Google's site for more information on deleting messages.

title: FAQ Maximum Attachment Size in ScarletMail
body:
You can send up to 25 MB in attachments. If you have more than one attachment, they cannot add up to more than 25 MB. 
If your file is greater than 25 MB, Gmail automatically adds a Google Drive link in the email instead of including it as an attachment. 
For more detailed instructions, visit the Google Help article on how to send attachments with your Gmail message.
When you attach a Google Drive file to a message, Gmail checks to see if your recipients have access to the file. If they don't, you'll be prompted to change the sharing settings of the file before you send your message.
For more detailed instructions, refer to the Google Help article on sharing settings for Google Drive files.

title: FAQ ScarletMail/ScarletApps storage limits FAQ
body:
Table of Contents
•	Why is Rutgers instituting a 30GB limit for ScarletMail/ScarletApps?
•	When does the 30GB limit take effect?
•	What are the cloud storage options at Rutgers?
•	Where can I see how much storage I am using?
•	How can I reduce my ScarletMail/ScarletApps data?
•	How can I migrate my ScarletMail/ScarletApps information to another account?
•	What will happen if my storage amount still exceeds the 30GB limit on June 18, 2024?
•	What will happen when an account reaches the 30GB limit?
•	Will I be able to keep my ScarletMail/ScarletApps account after leaving the University?
•	What happens to ScarletMail/ScarletApps accounts that haven’t been actively used?
Why is Rutgers instituting a 30GB limit for ScarletMail/ScarletApps?
Google announced storage limits for Google Workspace for Education (known as ScarletMail/ScarletApps at Rutgers)—an end to unlimited storage for educational institutions. In response to this change, IT leaders and professionals from departments across Rutgers developed a plan to address the new Google limits. As part of this plan, Rutgers is seeking to ensure an equitable use of Google storage at Rutgers with the 30GB limit. Long-dormant ScarletApps/ScarletMail accounts are being closed, and individuals using in excess of the 30GB limit were contacted, and their storage under the limit was reduced. 
When does the 30GB limit take effect?
The new 30GB limit went into effect on June 18, 2024.
What are the cloud storage options at Rutgers?
Along with ScarletApps (Google Drive), the storage options available to Rutgers Faculty, Staff, and Students, are Box and Microsoft OneDrive. Learn more about these on the Rutgers cloud storage website.
Where can I see how much storage I am using?
Log into the Google storage overview page with your ScarletMail account to view your current storage amount. 
How can I reduce my ScarletMail/ScarletApps data?
Your storage can be reduced by deleting large and unnecessary emails, files and photos, You may also transfer or download your data to another location. More information can be found on the Reducing ScarletMail/ScarletApps storage article.
How can I migrate my ScarletMail/ScarletApps information to another account?
Data from your account can be transferred to a personal Gmail account or downloaded so that it can be uploaded to another service. Google provides two tools for this, Google Transfer and Google Takeout. More information and instructions can be found in the Migrating ScarletMail data to another account article. 
What will happen if my storage amount still exceeds the 30GB limit on June 18, 2024?
Accounts that have not reduced their storage under 30GB when the limit took effect on June 18, 2024, will have reduced functionality. You can still sign into and access your account, view and download your files, and send and receive emails. However, you will be unable to do the following:
•	Upload new files or images to Google Drive.
•	Create new files in collaborative content creation apps like Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drawings, Forms, and Jamboard. Until you reduce your storage usage, nobody can edit or copy your affected files or submit forms owned by you.
•	Back up any photos and videos to Google Photos.
•	Record new meetings in Google Meet.
If you are a teacher in a Google Classroom, you will be unable to:
•	Create assignments with new files that they haven't yet uploaded or been created.
•	Export grades to Google Sheets.
•	Have students submit assignments with file attachments.
If you are a student in a Google Classroom, you will be unable to:
•	Access files in Assignments that prompt you to make a copy.
What will happen when an account reaches the 30GB limit?
When your account reaches the 30GB limit after June 18, 2024, it will have reduced functionality. You can still sign into and access your account, view and download your files, and send and receive emails. However, you will be unable to do the following:
•	Upload new files or images to Google Drive.
•	Create new files in collaborative content creation apps like Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drawings, Forms, and Jamboard. Until you reduce your storage usage, nobody can edit or copy your affected files or submit forms owned by you.
•	Back up any photos and videos to Google Photos.
•	Record new meetings in Google Meet.
If you are a teacher in a Google Classroom, you will be unable to:
•	Create assignments with new files that they haven't yet uploaded or been created.
•	Export grades to Google Sheets.
•	Have students submit assignments with file attachments.
If you are a student in a Google Classroom, you will be unable to:
•	Access files in Assignments that prompt you to make a copy.
Will I be able to keep my ScarletMail/ScarletApps account after leaving the University?
Only Alumni, Retirees, and Professor Emeritus are eligible to keep their ScarletMail/ScarletApps account after leaving the University. These accounts are subject to regular audits to check if they are still being used. If you are in one of these groups and your account is deemed inactive, you will be contacted to confirm that you are still using the account. It will remain active as long as you respond to these inquiries promptly. If there is no response, the account will be closed, and all data will be permanently deleted. 
Current Faculty, Staff, Students, and select University Guests are eligible to have a ScarletMail/ScarletApps account only while at the University.
More information on who is eligible can be found on the ScarletMail account audit article. 
What happens to ScarletMail/ScarletApps accounts that haven’t been actively used?
While at the University, your account will remain even if it is not actively being used.
Only Alumni, Retirees, and Professor Emeritus are eligible to keep their ScarletMail/ScarletApps account after leaving the University. These accounts are subject to regular audits to check if they are still being used. If you are in one of these groups and your account is deemed inactive, you will be contacted to confirm that you are still using the account. It will remain active as long as you respond to these inquiries promptly. If there is no response, the account will be closed, and all data will be permanently deleted.

body:
Students can continue to use their personal Gmail account. A ScarletMail account is a separate account that does not affect existing Gmail accounts. The advantage of the Google Workspace for Education account is that each person has a Google account in an ad-free environment that maintains your Rutgers identity through your email address.
The difference is mostly on the look and feel of the applications. Behind the scenes, Google also delegates control of Rutgers Google Apps and user accounts to Rutgers system administrators.

title: ITSM Services ITSM Knowledge Base style guide
body:
The ITSM knowledge base content should provide clear, accessible advice for members of the Rutgers community. Follow these guidelines for formatting when developing knowledge base content.
Table of Contents
•	Guidelines
•	Font Formatting 
•	Titles
•	Commands, menus, and UI elements
•	Procedures and sequences
•	Lists
•	Error messages
•	Key names and keyboard sequences
•	Links
•	Placeholder text
•	Images/Screenshots 
o	Alt Text
•	Tables  
o	Header
o	Caption
Guidelines
Here are some key guidelines:
•	Write clear, accurate, and up-to-date content.
•	Know your audience. In particular, whether you’re writing for a general audience or an IT audience, adjust your use of technical terms appropriately. 
•	Employ a user-friendly tone.
•	Avoid jargon or acronyms that users would be unfamiliar with. 
•	Avoid using pronouns or the term "user(s)". Instead, use terms like you, your, or they. 
Within ServiceNow, knowledge base content can be created using various templates:
•	Standard: Provides one text box to describe information. This is the default template that should used. 
Font Formatting 
There should be a consistent look and feel throughout the knowledge base. Leave the default font settings when creating an article. 
•	Black font
•	Verdana
•	Paragraphs should be used for the main text.
•	Heading 2 should be used as the first heading used in the body of the article since the title of the article is considered Heading 1.
•	Use Heading 3, Heading 4, etc... under Heading 2, if you need to divide the section into smaller sub headings further. 
Titles
Titles of knowledge base articles should usually include the name of the relevant service. This is important for helping users to find relevant content when searching for it.
•	Recommended: Storage space limits for OneDrive
•	Not recommended: Storage Space Limits
Use sentence case (capitalize only the first word) for titles:
•	Recommended: Instructions for connecting to RUWireless
•	Not recommended: Instructions for Connecting to RUWireless
Commands, menus, and UI elements
Use bold text (not quotation marks) when referring to menus, menu options, dialog boxes, commands, buttons, and other user interface elements. Examples:
•	Recommended: To start your slide show choose Slide Show > Play from Current Slide.
•	Not recommended: To start your slide show choose “Slide Show,” and then “Play from Current Slide”.
In addition, try to avoid terms specific to one device or interface; also, avoid mentioning the specific UI element (i.e., that it’s a button). Instead, simply indicate what action a user needs to take. Examples:
•	Recommended: Select Save as and then…
•	Not recommended: Touch the Save as button.
Procedures and sequences
Use arrows for procedures. Bold the step, but not the arrow:
Example: Choose File > Share > Send PDF.
•	Recommended: Go to Tools > Spelling and Grammar > Hide Spelling Errors.
•	Not recommended: Go to the Tools menu, click Spelling and Grammar, and then select Hide Spelling Errors.
If including the purpose of an action, do so before the actions:
•	Reccomended: To share a document as a PDF, choose File > Share > Send PDF.
•	Not recommended: Choose File > Share > Send PDF to share a document as a PDF.
Lists
To enable screen readers to recognize this properly for accessibility standards, use the built-in numbered list and bullet point feature built into the toolbar of the editor. Avoid typing out numbers or bullet point manually. 
A sequence of steps should be formatted as a numbered list, to show there is an order of operations. 
A list of items should be in a bullet point list, typically these are informational and the order is not important. 
When a sequence of steps needs to be broken up into smaller subsections, you can create nested lists. Each nested list should be a different format, and in the following order: numbers, alphabetical, and then roman numerals. 
Example: 
1.	
1.	Go to File > Computer Configuration. 
1.	Check the box for Enabled. This will open a new dialog box.  
1.	Check the box for Authorized Users. 
2.	Click OK. 
2.	Click Save.
2.	Close the program window. 
For additional guidance, consult the Microsoft style guide for Lists. 
Error messages
Enclose examples in quotation marks.
Example: If you receive an error message saying, “Stop, you should wait to install Office 2016,” contact the Help Desk for assistance.
Key names and keyboard sequences
Capitalize key names and keyboard sequences such as:
•	Ctrl+Alt+Del
•	Shift
For additional guidance, consult the Microsoft style guide for keys and keyboard shortcuts.
Links
Use meaningful links and avoid “click here” as a link. Avoid displaying URLs unless necessary. 
•	Recommended: Contact the Help Desk for support.
•	Not recommended: To contact the Help Desk, click here.
•	Not recommended: Contact the Help Desk at https://it.rutgers.edu/help-support.
The link's text should clearly indicate what the link will redirect to.
•	Recommended: For more information, view the Microsoft Support page for Word. 
•	Not recommended: For more information, view the Microsoft Support page for Word. 
If the link is at the end of the sentence, avoid having the punctuation as part of the link. 
•	Recommended: For more information, view the Microsoft Support page for Word. 
•	Not recommended: For more information, view the Microsoft Support page for Word.
Placeholder text
Use italics for placeholder text. 
Example: Enter NetID username and password.
Images/Screenshots
Follow these general tips on inserting images. For more information, see ServiceNow's guide on inserting images. 
•	Avoid overusing screenshots unless they provide substantial value or clarification. For instance, do not use screenshots for obvious steps in a procedure, such as Next or OK.
•	If needed, add labels, arrows, or notes to clarify the content of screenshots.
•	Images should be added using the built-in Insert/edit image feature and not pasted into the article since a pasted image may not display correctly. 
•	Images should be resized so the text in the image is roughly the same size as the text of the article. Maximum width should be 840px to show correctly on the IT Help Self-Service Portal. 
•	All images should have Alt Text associated with them (added through the Insert/edit image feature) to allow the use of screen readers and to comply with accessibility standards. 
Alt Text
All images/media should have an alternative text associated with them so that screen readers can describe the context of the image. This aims to create a text alternative that serves the same purpose and presents the same information as the original non-text content. 
Example: A picture shows the login page for Rutgers Connect. Alt Text is "Login page for Rutgers Connect prompting for an email address"
General guidelines to follow for Alt Text:
•	You do not need to mention that it is a picture or screenshot of something, as that is implied. 
•	The Alt Text should adequately describe what is seen in the image, assuming no other context for the picture exists. 
•	If a particular button or icon is highlighted or pointed to, that should be mentioned in the Alt Text. 
•	If the image shows a series of steps, you do not need to mention the specific step numbers shown in the image since they will be in the numbered list of the knowledge article.
•	Similarly, the Alt Text should not say that it is "How to" do something, as that will be mentioned in the text of the knowledge article. 
•	Longer is not always better. Describing everything in extreme detail does not equate to good Alt Text.  
Tables 
Tables are not the most screen reader-friendly; as such, they should be used sparingly. Try reformatting to use a bulleted list whenever possible. To ensure digital accessibility, the table must have Headers and a Caption describing the table. 
Header
1.	Right-click on a cell in the row you want to make a Header. 
2.	Select Row > Row Properties. 
3.	Change Row Type to be Header. 
4.	Click Save. 
Caption
Every table should have a Caption at the top, so screen readers can access it first and describe the table, allowing the user to decide whether to go through the entire table or skip it completely. 
1.	Right-click on the table. 
2.	Click Table Properties. 
3.	Ensure Show Caption is checked. 
4.	Click Save.
5.	A new "cell" should appear at the top of the table with the word Caption in it. 
6.	Update the text as needed to describe the information the table presents. 
o	Similar to adding Alt Text to an image, it should allow the user to understand what the table is showing without being able to see the table itself.
o	Short and concise is preferred.  
o	You do not need to state that it is a table, or list every column header. Example for the table below:  
	Bad Example: "Table listing the available Headset item names, their description, and prices". 
	Good Example: "Available Headsets and their price".

title: ITSM Services Rutgers IT Help (ServiceNow) portal user guide
body:
"
Managed by the ServiceNow platform, the Rutgers IT Help portal is a self-service portal designed for faculty, staff, and students who require tech help and support for various IT services at Rutgers.
What can the Rutgers IT Help portal do for you?
