For more information, view the portal quick reference card (QRC) or micro-learning videos.

title: - Service Portal training materials
ITSM Services ServiceNow Knowledge Management Procedures
body:
Table of Contents • Knowledge Article Basics o Article States o Article Links o Can Read (User Criteria Groups) o Anchor Links o Images o General Article Tips o Fixing Formatting Issues o Formatting FAQs • Accessibility Standards o Text Alternative for Images/Media o Headings o Numbered or Bulleted Lists o Hyperlinks o Tables o Accessibility Checker tool • Creating Knowledge Articles o Default Settings o Knowledge Blocks • Editing Knowledge Articles o Checkout o Editing o Publishing o View Article o Recalling o Approving • Revert back to a previous version of a KA • Retiring Articles • Knowledge Feedback Tasks (KFTs) • Reviewing Expiring Knowledge Articles • Article Valid To Dates Knowledge Article Basics Article States Articles are categorized in one of the following States in the Workflow field. Draft Indicates it is in edit mode and the settings/article body can be changed. This occurs when you first create a new article or when you Checkout an existing article to make changes to it. The version number of the article will show with a decimal after it to indicate it is not published (ex: Version 0.01 for a new article) Review When a Draft is ready, clicking Publish puts the article in the Review state. The appropriate owners of the Knowledge Base the article is in would then need to approve it before it is visible to users. Scheduled for Publish For articles that have been approved after being reviewed but have a Scheduled Publish Date set for the article that has not passed yet. Published The article is visible to users based on it’s Can read and Cannot read settings. Published articles have version numbers that are whole digits (ex: 1.0). Pending Retirement An article was selected for retirement by clicking Retire. It is still visible and not actually retired until the appropriate owners of the Knowledge Base it is in, approves the retirement. Retired The retirement for the article was approved and it is no longer visible to users. Outdated Means that a newer version of this article is available. You can check the version number of the article to see which it is. (ex: viewing version 1.0 of an article will show workflow as Outdated, when there is an updated published version 2.0) How to view States • The Workflow column is visible in the back end view. Hovering over the icon displays which stage it is in. If you do not see this column you have to click on the gear icon on the top left of the list, and then add it to your Selected visible columns. Error! Filename not specified. • When viewing the article, the state is shown in the Workflow field. Error! Filename not specified. Article Links There are 4 different links that can take you to various versions of an article. Front End Permalink • This is the link that should always be used whenever referencing an article to a user. • It is the link on the self service Portal that takes the user to the most updated version of the article. • Navigate to the article on the Portal and click Copy Permalink located at the top or bottom of the article. • Example: https://ithelp.rutgers.edu/sp?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0012508 Front End sys_id link • When used, will take the user to this specific version of the article. If used it will not bring them to the most current version of the article if it has since been updated, which is why this one should not typically be used. • When viewing an article in the Portal, this is the link in the URL bar on the browser. • Example: https://ithelp.rutgers.edu/sp?id=kb_article_view&sys_kb_id=08138ef71bbe4110743c54a51a4bcbf0 Back End Permalink • It is the link in the back end of ServiceNow that takes the user to the most updated version of the article. This link can be used for internal documentation only for IT users with access to the backend of ServiceNow. • Navigate to the article in the back end and click the Copy Permalink button located at the bottom of the article. • Example: https://rutgers.service-now.com/kb_view.do?sysparm_article=KB0012508 Back End sys_id link • It is the link in the back end of ServiceNow that takes the user to a specific version of the article. This should not typically be used. • Navigate to the article in the back end, this is the link in the URL bar on the browser. • Example: https://rutgers.service-now.com/kb_knowledge.do?sys_id=08138ef71bbe4110743c54a51a4bcbf0&sysparm_referring_url=kb_view.do Permalinks will always have a URL that ends in the KB number. Can Read (User Criteria Groups) These are the groups used in the Can Read field to control who has access to the article. These groups are auto populated by the Assignment Groups (commonly used in Incidents) that are connected under the User Criteria Group. When adding one of these in the Can Read field on an article, you can select it to highlight it, then click the small information (i) icon to see what sources it pulls from to populate the membership for the group. Anchor Links These are bookmarks/direct links to a specific point in an article, which can be particularly useful if the article is long or has multiple sections you want to create a customized table of contents for at the top (there is a built in table of contents feature described below). To make an anchor link is a two step process. Making an anchor link Using the built in function 1. Click the spot in the text of the article you want to place the anchor point. 2. Click the Anchor button on the text editor toolbar which looks like a bookmark button. 3. Enter a short yet descriptive name for the anchor link, and do not include spaces. 4. Click OK and you should see the anchor icon appear in the article body. Manually 1. Click the spot in the text of the article you want to place the anchor point. 2. Click the Source Code button on the text editor toolbar which looks like <>. 3. Copy and paste the text below, replacing ANCHORNAME with a short yet descriptive text term for your anchor: Using an anchor link From a specific URL Take the PermaLink for the article then add /#ANCHORNAME at the end to create a URL link to take users directly to where you put in the anchor on the article. Replacing ANCHORNAME with the text term you used when creating the anchor. From within the article 1. If creating a table of contents for example, highlight the text you want users to click to take them to the anchor point. 2. Click the Insert/Modify Link button just as you would for creating an external link in the article. 3. In the URL field type #ANCHORNAME while replacing ANCHORNAME with the text term you used when creating the anchor. Table of Contents To easily create a table of contents you can use the built in button on the toolbar. Clicking it will automatically add it to the top of the article, utilizing all text formatted as Heading 1, 2 or 3 to create the clickable links in the table. Note that any text formatted as Heading 4 or lower will not be incorporated automatically into the table, you may manually insert it using an anchor link if desired. If any Headings are changed/deleted/added, you can click on the table itself and a refresh button will appear. Clicking on that will update the table to what the current Headings now are. Images To ensure consistent image formatting follow these guidelines. • Avoid copy/pasting images into articles. Depending on your browser's capabilities, device type, form view, and other factors, copy/pasting images into an article or form does not always work as expected. It can also not display the image properly on the Portal for users who are not logged in. The recommended way to get an image into your article is to use the Edit Image button on the article editor. Review ServiceNow’s guide on inserting images. • Screenshots/images should be indented over so they are not inline with text, therefore making it easier to scroll through the text. They should also have a blank line both above and under the image to provide a spacing buffer from any text in the article. • All images should have Alt Text. • Resize images, by dragging the corner of it, so the text in the image is roughly the same size or slightly bigger than the text of the article while viewing it in the html editor. • When inserting an image in a numbered or bullet sequence, press Shift+Enter to add a soft line break. This will tab down to the next line so the image can be inserted under the text, but does not continue the sequenced list for this line. After the image you can hit Enter to tab down to the next line and continue the numbered sequence. Image standards • 840px maximum width for it to be visible on the Portal. • .jpg, .gif, or .png format only. • Use file naming conventions that are logical and easy to remember. Include relevant keywords that are easy to search for, and have them numbered for a series of images of steps. • Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores in file names. Other characters (like question marks and ampersands) may upload incorrectly or cause unexpected behavior. How to Insert an Image 1. Within the Article Body, click the space where the image should appear. 2. On the text editor toolbar, click the Insert/Edit Image icon. The Insert/Modify Image pop-up displays. 3. Make sure the Type is set to Attachment. 4. Click the paperclip icon to browse for a new image (if no attachments are uploaded) or choose the image file name from the dropdown (when an article already has the image file uploaded). 5. Enter alternative text for the image in the Alt Text field. o Note: Alternative text (alt text) makes an image accessible to users who cannot see the image. Use Alt text for all images inserted into a KB article. Alt text should replicate in words what the image is communicating. 6. Click Save to close the window. 7. Ensure there is a blank line both above and below the image to provide a buffer from any surrounding text. Ensure it is indented over so it is not in line with the text above it. How to Edit an Image 1. Within the Article Body, click on the image to highlight it. 2. On the text editor toolbar, click the Insert/edit icon. The Insert/Modify Image pop-up displays. 3. Enter alternative text for the image in the Alt Text field if one is not present. o Note: Alternative text (alt text) makes an image accessible to users who cannot see the image. Use Alt text for all images inserted into a KB article. Alt text should replicate in words what the image is communicating. 4. Click Save to close the window. 5. Ensure there is a blank line both above and below the image to provide a buffer from any surrounding text. Ensure it is indented over so it is not in line with the text above it. General Article Tips • Review and follow the ITSM style guide as closely as possible! • Minimize references to specific individuals whenever possible to decrease the need to update the article more often as positions change and shift. • Avoid overusing acronyms. Acceptable on second and subsequent references; place the acronym in parentheses on the first reference. For example: “The Office of Information Technology (OIT) recently upgraded the service.” • Be attentive to language that has a specific meaning for IT people and an entirely different meaning for non-IT people, such as user, audit, client, domain, machine, package, tenant, and many others. Additionally, many technical terms, such as endpoints, SSID, and others, are not familiar to a non-technical audience; use other terms or define the terms you’re using, when applicable. • Be detailed / step-by-step instructions. • Avoid using gender specific pronouns (he/she) and instead use (they/them/you). • Reference and link to Vendor/Service documentation whenever possible to take the burden of keeping information up to date off of us. No need to duplicate the same information. • The editor can be a little weird and do strange things sometimes. When copying and pasting content into the HTML editor, press Ctrl+Shift+V to paste without any formatting. You can always click the Source Code button to see what the text and formatting is doing if it’s acting up at a particular spot in an article. Fixing Formatting Issues If when viewing an article any of the formatting looks off, such as a different font type, font size, or spacing issues this is typically caused by bad HTML code. More often than not it is from content that has been copied and pasted into an article without having the source formatting removed. Even if you highlight the text and manually change the font type and size to what it should be, it may still appear wrong if there is additional font styling in the code. You can see this by clicking the Source Code button ( <> ) in the KA editor toolbar and look for the word “style” in blue text as shown below. These inline style codes will override any other formatting for the specific text lines they are on. Example of bad inline style code: You can manually remove the entire style code, by deleting the word style and all the text formatting that appears in the reddish brown color, and leaving only the green code. For long articles with alot of customized inline style code this can be time consuming. To easily wipe out all style codes for an entire do the following, but note that this may cause issues if images have been pasted into an article and not inserted as an attachment: 1. Open the source code for the article giving you issues. 2. Press Ctrl + A to select all of the code. 3. Press Ctrl + C to copy all the code. 4. Go to this HTML Code Cleaner. 5. Paste the entire code in the empty box on the right side of the screen, the left side will show a preview of what the text currently looks like. 6. Click Clean HTML and this will remove all the inline style coding. 7. Click Ctrl + A to select all the freshly cleaned code from the right side, and then Ctrl + C to copy it. 8. Go back to the source code of the KA. 9. Delete all existing code. 10. Press Ctrl + V to paste in all the cleaned up code you copied from the website. 11. Click OK and confirm that everything looks correct and all the previous images are still there. Alternatively you can use the editor’s built in feature to clear some, but not all, formatting. 1. Highlight the text in the editor that you want to remove formatting from, or press Ctrl + A to select all the text. 2. Press the Clear formatting button on the toolbar, which looks like:Error! Filename not specified. 3. This should remove any style coding from the highlighted text. Viewing the article in the editor may not show all the formatting that may be hidden in the source code. This is why you should always view the article normally in the back end (by clicking View Article) or on the Portal, to see how it would truly appear. Especially before approving it to be published. Formatting FAQs Follow these general guidelines when handling a page that is entirely or partially a question and answer format (FAQs). For articles have more than 5 questions/answers: • o Format the questions as the appropriate level of Heading (2,3,4,etc..) with no other alterations to the text. o Format the answers as regular paragraph text but indented over. o Utilize the built in Table of Contents feature and place it at the beginning of the questions, ensuring that only the questions are show in the table and any other headings are removed. For articles with less than 5 questions/answers: • o Format the question as regular paragraph text, but bold it. o Format the answers as regular paragraph text but indented over. Accessibility Standards In order to adhere to Rutgers Digital Accessibility policies, all documentation should be in compliance with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. In particular the items below should be adhered to for all knowledge articles. Text Alternative for Images/Media General guidelines to follow for Alt Text: • You do not need to mention that it is a picture or screenshot of something, as that is implied. • The Alt Text should adequately describe what is seen in the image, assuming no other context for the picture exists. • If a particular button or icon is highlighted or pointed to, that should be mentioned in the Alt Text. • If the image shows a series of steps, you do not need to mention the specific step numbers shown in the image since they will be in the numbered list of the knowledge article. • Similarly, the Alt Text should not say that it is "How to" do something, as that will be mentioned in the text of the knowledge article. • Longer is not always better. Describing everything in extreme detail does not equate to good Alt Text. Examples • A picture shows the login page for Rutgers Connect. Alt Text is "Login page for Rutgers Connect prompting for an email address" • A picture shows how a knot is tied including arrows showing how the ropes go to make the knot. The text alternative describes how to tie the knot, not what the picture looks like. • A picture shows what a toy looks like from the front. The text alternative describes a front view of the toy. How to add/edit Alt Text For images already in an article: 1. Click on the image to highlight it. 2. On the toolbar, click the Insert/edit image icon. 3. In the Alt text field provide a short yet descriptive text alternative. 4. Click Save. Headings In order for screen readers to appropriately describe the text on the screen to users, headings should be formatted as such. This helps users “skim" the headings to locate the specific content they need, and is especially helpful when browsers or assistive technology allow navigation from heading to heading. These heading should be short yet descriptive ways to break up long articles into smaller sections. All headings should be set to use Heading 2 by default. Any further separation in each section should use Heading 3 then Heading 4 etc… but should always be in increasing sequential order. Example: An HTML page that describes the range of tasks for disaster preparation may have the following headings:

Disaster preparation

Flood preparation

Fire preparation

Note that the level 3 headings have the distinguishing information at the beginning (ie, instead of "Preparation for floods", "Preparation for fires", etc). Text should never be colored anything other than the default black. Colored text to denote importance does not adhere to the accessibility standards. Numbered or Bulleted Lists In order for screen readers to properly go through a series of steps or list of items it has to be formatted appropriately. A numbered or bulleted list should always be created using one of the list buttons in the editor toolbar. Simply typing numbers with parentheses or periods, such as "1), 2), 3)," or an asterisk in front of each item on a new line or paragraph will NOT create a numbered or bulleted list that is accessible by a screen reader. A good guide to follow can be found on Microsoft’s website on the proper procedure for lists. Inserting images into lists When inserting an image in a numbered or bullet sequence, press Shift+Enter to add a soft line break. This will tab down to the next line so the image can be inserted under the text, but does not continue the sequenced list for this line. After the image you can hit Enter to tab down to the next line and continue the numbered sequence. See the Images section of this article for more information on adding images. Hyperlinks Hyperlinks connect a hypertext file or document to another location or file. Linked information is typically presented in the form of text, websites, files, or video content. Embed a link within a concise string of text instead of using its URL as the link text. A screen reader user will more easily understand where an accessible link leads and will not have to listen while the reader pronounces every single character of a URL. Example: • o Accessible: OIT Help Desk o Not accessible: https://it.rutgers.edu/help-support/ Descriptive hyperlinks will more clearly explain what information they link to. Example: • o Descriptive: Benefits of Accessible Hyperlinks o Not descriptive: Benefits Use the full email address as the link text rather than embedding it in other link text. Example: • o Accessible: help@oit.rutgers.edu o Not accessible: OIT Help Desk Support *This example does not convey that it is an email address. Other Tips: • Choose hyperlink text that clearly identifies the content of the resource being linked to. • Hyperlink text should not consist of the URL unless it is likely to be printed; e.g., Word document. • If a hyperlink downloads a file, be sure to mention that. o Example: Campus Map (PDF, 5.62 MB) • Hyperlinks may fail to open when clicking on them in the backend of ServiceNow, as it tries to open the link within the ServiceNow window itself. If this happens, right click the link and choose to open it in a new tab which should open the link correctly. This only applies to the backend and not the user facing side of ServiceNow. Tables Tables are not the most screen reader-friendly, as such they should be use sparingly. Try reformatting to use a bulleted list whenever possible. To ensure digital accessibility, the table must have Headers and a Caption describing the table. Table Header Only available for a row or individual cells. You can not easily make a whole column a Header if that is what's needed. However, a table should be formatted so the top row is the header whenever possible. To make a row a Header (typically the top row): 1. Right-click on a cell in the row you want to make a Header. 2. Select Row > Row Properties. 3. Change Row Type to be Header. 4. Click Save. To make a cell a Header (if needed): 1. Right-click on a cell you want to make a Header. 2. Select Cell > Cell Properties. 3. Change Row Type to be Header. 4. Click Save. 5. Repeat for other cells as needed. Table Header Scope You must also define the scope to which the Header applies. Typically, this is the cell in the top row, and the scope would apply to the column beneath it. You must set the scope specifically for each cell. 1. Right-click on each cell. 2. Select Cell > Cell Properties. 3. Change Scope to be Column. 4. Click Save. Table Caption Every table should have a Caption at the top, so screen readers can access it first and describe the table, allowing the user to decide whether to go through the entire table or skip it completely. To add a caption to a table: 1. Right-click on the table. 2. Click Table Properties. 3. Ensure Show Caption is checked. 4. Click Save. 5. A new "cell" should appear at the top of the table with the word Caption in it. 6. Update the text as needed to describe the information the table presents. o Similar to adding Alt Text to an image, it should allow the user to understand what the table is showing without being able to see the table itself. o Short and concise is preferred. o You do not need to state that it is a table, or list every column header.  Bad Example: "Table listing the available Headset item names, their description, and prices".  Good Example: "Available Headsets and their price". Accessibility Checker tool The Accessibility Checker (person icon in the article editor toolbar) enables you to identify and resolve accessibility related issues in a Knowledge article. 1. Select it, and the Accessibility Checker window will display any issues it finds, along with suggestions for resolving them. 2. You can choose to Repair the issues automatically or Ignore them if they're not applicable. 3. If your article is already fully accessible, you'll see a success message. This tool may not catch all issues and adhere to all formatting standards described in this Knowledge article. Therefore, it's imperative to still conduct a manual review of all KAs and not ...

title: FAQ
body:
Table of Contents

•	How do I log in to Smartsheet?
What is Smartsheet Advanced Work Management (AWM)?
Starting in December 2025, Smartsheet will transition to the Advanced Work Management licensing mode. Visit the AWM Dashboard for information about each of the model’s components. While this update will result in increased costs and necessitate some adjustments to how user roles and access are managed, it will also introduce enhanced functionality and new user types.  
What will the new user roles be?? 
•	Member: Includes paid internal and external users. Grants full platform access. This cost is approximately $65/per month per member.? 
•	Provisional Member: A temporary seat type with full access, pending review and purchase of a member subscription. 
•	Viewer: For internal or external users with view-only access, no paid license required.? 
•	Guest: External users (non-Rutgers affiliated) with Commenter or Editor permissions, no paid license required.? 
Note that the "Free Unlicensed User/Collaborator" role will be discontinued. If you require more than Viewer access, you must purchase a Member subscription.? 
Will I lose access to Smartsheet on December 16th? 
No, you will not lose your Smartsheet access. 
•	Enterprise Licensed Smartsheet users will be assigned a Member role.
•	Enterprise Free Unlicensed Collaborators who have directly edited or commented on a sheet in the last 90 days will be temporarily assigned a Provisional Member role.
•	Enterprise Free Unlicensed Collaborators, who have not directly edited or commented on a sheet in the last 90 days, will be assigned a Viewer role.
Note: Work is underway to migrate the External Free Unlicensed Collaborators (trial accounts set up directly through Smartsheet) into the Enterprise account. 
•	If you have more the one Smartsheet account, they will be merged, and the Primary Email address will become your NetID@rutgers.edu address.
•	If you do not have your NetID@rutgers.edu email address on your account, it will be added and made the Primary Email Address.
How do I renew my subscription to ensure I don't lose access?? 
In November, all current licensed Smartsheet Enterprise users who have purchased a subscription within the past year will be sent an email. It will include a link to the new Smartsheet Enterprise Member Advanced Work Management product page. You must place your orders through the new product page.
•	Smartsheet Member Subscriptions can only be purchased via a monthly subscription using a payment account.
•	Orders placed in November will not be billed until January for the month of December.
•	If you do not renew your subscriptions prior to December 19th, your permission will be downgraded to Viewer.
I no longer want a paid subscription to Smartsheet. What do I need to do? 
No action is needed. If you do not renew your subscription prior to December 19th, your permission will be downgraded to Viewer.
What is a Provisional Member?
A Provisional Member is a temporary role with full access, pending review and purchase of a member subscription. If no Member subscription is purchased within the allotted time, the person's role will be downgraded to Viewer. 
What is the review process for Provisional Members?
1.	Enterprise Free Unlicensed Collaborators who have directly edited or commented on one sheet in the 90 days before 12/16/2025 will be temporarily assigned a Provisional Member role.
2.	The Provisional Members will receive an email that includes a link to the new Smartsheet Enterprise Member product page, along with the date (TBD) by which they must set up their monthly subscription.
3.	Those who do not purchase a subscription prior to that date will have their permission downgraded to Viewer on (TBD).
Can we get a list of licensed users in our department?
Yes, email software@rutgers.edu with the subject “Smartsheet licensed user list” and you will receive a link to a list of the licensed users, which includes User Name, Primary Email Address, Status, Sheets (Created), and Last Login.
Where can I find the links to the recordings for the Smartsheet Zoom meetings?
The Smartsheet team hosted a Zoom meeting on July 24, 2025, to provide details important to the upcoming licensing model changes scheduled for December 2025. The meeting included information on how to update existing processes to help make the transition smoother, as well as a discussion of some of the new features.  
July 24th Webinar recording
The Smartsheet team hosted a Zoom meeting on April 22, 2025, and provided details important to the upcoming licensing model changes scheduled for December 2025. The meeting included information on Data Shuttle and how to set up the Dynamic View feature.  
April 22nd Webinar recording

title: What Smartsheet help and training resources are there??
body:
The Smartsheet Support?team is standing by, ready to answer your questions and diagnose any issues you may be facing. 
Smartsheet Pro Desk - Pro Desk delivers practical one-on-one coaching sessions with a Smartsheet expert to help you optimize your projects, programs, and processes.?
Smartsheet University eLearning - This online, on-demand resource provides module-based Smartsheet training and offers "Smartsheet certification" so your users can certify their proficiency with the platform. It's a great place to go for a refresher on how to use Smartsheet or quick walkthroughs about using the latest features we release.? 
Smartsheet Community - Find peer-to-peer information about everything Smartsheet related – from project management best practices to invaluable how-to guidance from fellow users and Smartsheet experts.? 
Update Requests - Send update requests to get updated by any collaborator on key rows, regardless of whether they have a Smartsheet account or are shared to the sheet.? 
Forms - Forms make it easy to collect consistent, error-free data from all your stakeholders and save it directly into your sheet, where you can take action. Forms are ideal for field ticket collection, request management, event registration, collecting customer feedback, and more.? 
Approval Requests - Approval requests pause the workflow until the request is approved or declined. At each approval or rejection, the conditions and actions on the path determine what happens next.? (You do not need to be a member to approve requests.)? 
Alerts & Reminders - Both alerts and reminders can be set up individually or together as part of a larger workflow with multiple conditions. They can also be sent to various recipients regularly, even if the recipient is not shared in your sheet.? 
Dynamic View - Smartsheet Dynamic View enables business owners to share information with the right people at the right time for viewing or editing. Whether working with vendors, mixed internal and external teams, or across organizations, Dynamic View allows you to maintain process confidentiality by preventing users or vendors from accessing the whole sheet, all without hindering the collaboration required to execute work.? 
Data Shuttle - Data Shuttle by Smartsheet streamlines the process of transferring data between Smartsheet and other systems, making it easier for users to import and export data while maintaining accuracy and efficiency.? 
Calendar App - The Smartsheet Calendar App is a flexible, configurable calendar add-on that allows you to connect your Smartsheet data and forms to visualize your events in multiple views or by color-coded categories.?

title: FAQs How do I disable chat in my Webex meeting?
body:
The chat panel can be disabled during scheduling on the website and during an active meeting.
To disable the chat panel while scheduling from the website
1.	On the scheduling page, click on Show advanced options.
2.	Select the Scheduling options drop-down option.
3.	Navigate to Meeting options and select Edit meeting options.
4.	From the pop-up, uncheck the Chat box.
5.	Select OK.
To disable the chat panel within an active meeting
1.	Select the Meeting drop-down from the menu bar at the top.
2.	Select Options.
3.	In the Meeting Options window, uncheck the Chat box.
4.	Select OK.
To manage who participants can chat with in a meeting 
1.	Select the Participant drop-down from the menu bar at the top.
2.	Select Assign Privileges.
3.	Choose who participants can chat with.
4.	Select OK.

title: FAQs Why can no one hear me on Webex?
body:
If no one can hear you during your Webex session, there may be issues with your audio connection or microphone. Follow the troubleshooting steps below:
1.	Make sure that your device or microphone is not muted.
2.	Ensure you do not have other applications, such as Zoom or Skype, running in the background that may interfere with your mic. 
3.	Check your input microphone volume in Sound settings. 
4.	Make sure you have connected to the audio portion of the session either through your computer (Call Using Computer) or your telephone (Click More Options > I Will Call In).
5.	Ensure you have selected the proper Audio Source by navigating to Audio > Speaker, Microphone, and Camera. For the microphone, select the mic you want to use. If your mic isn't listed, it may not be plugged in properly.
For detailed instructions, visit the Webex Help Center page on choosing your audio and video settings before you join a meeting or webinar.

title: FAQs Why can no one see me on Webex?
body:
If no one can see you during your Webex session, there may be potential issues with your camera settings. Follow the troubleshooting steps below:
1.	Ensure your camera permissions are properly configured in Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera > Turn on Camera access. 
2.	Ensure you do not have other applications, such as Zoom or Skype, working in the background that may be accessing your camera.
3.	Ensure you have the proper Camera Input Source selected by navigating to the Stop video's drop-down menu. 
4.	If using a desktop camera, ensure your lens is not blocked, such as by a lens cover. If your camera is still off, click Start Video to show your video.
5.	If using a mobile camera, tap Turn on my video to show your video.
6.	If using a web browser, click Start Video to show your video. 
7.	Leave & Rejoin the Webex meeting. 
For detailed instructions, visit the Webex Help Center page on choosing your audio and video settings before you join a meeting or webinar.

You can transfer the license for most software you own to another person from the My Software page.
For certain products (such as BioRender, Graphpad, LucidSuite, Smartsheet, and Microsoft products), please refer to the instructions on how to transfer the subscription for these specific products.
For all other software, you can follow the instructions below:
1.	Visit the My Software page on the Software Portal to view all the software you currently own. This is also located under the My Account drop-down, then My Software.
2.	Click the three dots on the top right of the product you want to transfer. 
3.	Select Transfer License to Another User to give your license to someone else. 
o	We recommend searching using the person's NetID. Only people who currently have a profile with the Software Portal will show up in the search results (anyone with a valid NetID can create a profile simply by logging in to the portal for the first time).

title: Portal Help Monthly Subscriptions on the Software Portal
body:
Table of Contents
•	Payment method
•	How to subscribe
•	How to cancel your monthly subscriptions
•	FAQs 
o	When does the monthly subscription get billed?
o	If I cancel, when do I lose access?
o	Is there a prorated refund if I cancel mid-month?
o	How do I get access to a payment account to subscribe?
o	I'm the department's Director/Business Manager. How do I add an account for people to use?
o	Can we use a Project String?
Starting in July 2024, select products on the Software Portal are available to be subscribed to via an automatic recurring monthly subscription. This payment offering is in addition to the available term subscription (typically pro-rated yearly subscriptions), which must be renewed manually. 
Payment method
Monthly subscriptions can only be purchased if you have been given access to use a departmental payment account by the owner of that account. The payment accounts are tied directly to a General Ledger (GL) code for your department and must be set up by your department's Director/Business Manager. 
Credit Cards, Purchase Orders, or Project Strings are not acceptable forms of payment for monthly subscriptions. You may use these forms of payment for term subscriptions where available. Note: Some subscription based products are only available via monthly subscriptions. 
How to subscribe
If you have been given access to a departmental payment account to use for a monthly subscription, you may subscribe by doing the following.
1.	Log in to the Software Portal and find the software you want to subscribe to. 
2.	On the Software's Product Page, click on Get [Product Name]...
3.	Under Monthly Subscription, click Subscribe... 
o	If there is no Monthly Subscription option, then the software is not available for this payment option.
4.	In the drop-down menu under Payment Account, choose the account to be charged. You will only see accounts that you have been given access to. 
5.	Under Choose your recipients, enter the NetID of the individual(s) you want to subscribe to and select their name from the list. 
o	User accounts with (-adm) must not be used.
o	Your own user account will be pre-populated as a recipient of the subscription. However, if you only wish to subscribe for someone else, you will need to remove your own account by clicking the X.
6.	Confirm the information under Cost is correct, then click Subscribe. 
If you receive an error, email software@rutgers.edu with a screenshot.
How to cancel your monthly subscriptions
Only payment account owners or subscribed users can cancel user subscriptions.
Prior to cancellation, ensure that the user has downloaded and backed up any necessary data/files from the software since it will all be deleted when your subscription is canceled. 
1.	Log in to the Software Portal. 
2.	Under the My Account drop-down, select My Payment Accounts. 
3.	Go to the GL account and click Show Details. 
4.	Click on Subscriber Expenses. 
5.	Find the person/software you would like to cancel.
6.	Click Cancel and follow the prompts. 
FAQs
When does the monthly subscription get billed?
Monthly subscriptions are billed in arrears, meaning charges for subscriptions active in one month are billed the following month. For example, if a subscription starts in January, the billing entry will appear sometime in February.
If I cancel, when do I lose access?
When a monthly subscription is canceled, you retain access until the end of that calendar month.
Is there a prorated refund if I cancel mid-month?
There are no refunds for monthly subscriptions. If canceled in the middle of a month, you retain access until the end of that calendar month.
How do I get access to a payment account to subscribe?
Please reach out to your department's Director/Business Manager for further details. 
I'm the department's Director/Business Manager. How do I add an account for people to use?
See the Software Portal Account Manager knowledge article.
Can we use a Project String?
The use of Project Account Strings is not available. Some have chosen to set up the payment account using the department GL string. Then, depending on the cadence they choose (monthly, quarterly, biannually, or annually), they process a Journal Entry to the project.

body:

o	How do we transfer a subscription?
o	How do I transfer ownership of my Payment Account(s) to another person?
Starting in July 2024, select products on the Software Portal can be subscribed to via an automatic recurring monthly subscription. 
This article is intended for Directors/Business Managers to set up or manage a payment account for people in their department. The payment accounts are tied directly to a General Ledger (GL) or Project Strings for your department.  
Please contact your department's business manager to determine if a Payment Account Owner or a Delegated Payment Account Manager has been assigned to your area.
What roles are available? What are the access and responsibilities for each?
Payment Account Owner
The Payment Account Owner is the person responsible for billing against the Payment Account(s) they created in the Software Portal.
They can:
•	Add new Payment Accounts
•	Add Delegated Payment Account Manager(s)
•	Add Payment Account User(s)
•	Place orders for themselves and/or others
•	Cancel order for themselves and/or others
•	Run and review reports for users who are no longer with your department or the university.
Delegated Payment Account Manager
The Delegated Payment Account Manager is added to Payment Account(s) by the Payment Account Owner.
They can:
•	Add other Delegated Payment Account Manager(s)
•	Add Payment Account User(s)
•	Place orders for themselves and/or others
•	Cancel order for themselves and/or others
•	Run and review reports for users who are no longer with your department or the university.
Payment Account User
They can:
•	Can place orders for themselves. They will be able to place orders for any monthly subscription.
•	Cancel orders for themselves
How to become a Payment Account Owner
Confirm with your Director or Business Manager whether a Payment Account Owner or a Delegated Payment Account Manager has been assigned to your area.
If there is no Payment Account Owner assigned to your area, your department Director or Business Manager will need to email software@rutgers.edu with the subject line "Software Portal Payment Account Owner Access,” and include the Name, NetID, phone number, and email address in the body of the email. Each GL or Project String can only have one Payment Account Owner. 
Note: Payment Account Owners are responsible to:
•	Add new Payment Accounts
•	Add Delegated Payment Account Manager(s)
•	Add Payment Account User(s)
•	Place orders for themselves and/or others
•	Cancel order for themselves and/or others
•	Run and review reports for users who are no longer with your department or the university.
Once the Payment Account Owners' access has been updated in the Software Portal, they will be notified via the ServiceNow Incident that was created, and then they can proceed to add payment account(s).
Adding a payment account
1.	Log in to the Software Portal. 
2.	Under the My Account drop-down, select My Payment Accounts. 
3.	Click Add Account.  
o	The account code consists of 6 required parts, 1 fixed part, and 1 optional part. Specify all the parts of your account code, separating each part with a period(.).
4.	Enter the GL or Project string.  
o	GL String: 
	The account code consists of 6 required parts, 1 fixed part, and 1 optional part. Specify all the parts of your account code below, separating each part with a period (.). 
	The Unit.Division.Organization (UDO) combination is specified as the first 3 segments of the account code. The Chart of Accounts lists valid and invalid UDO combinations. These rules are enforced here during account code validation. 
	The next 3 segments specify Location.Fund Type.Business Line. Each segment corresponds to an existing element as defined in the Chart of Accounts. 
Expenditure type is a fixed code we automatically apply to your account code. You do not need to specify this segment, and you cannot override the fixed value. 
	Activity codes are now supported. Please specify your 4-character alphanumeric activity code as the last segment of your account code. The activity will default to "0000" if not specified. You must specify a known activity as defined in the Chart of Accounts COA Segment Listing. 
	Example values are:  
	Unit (100 – 900)
	Division (1000 – 6915)
	Organization (1005 – 9999)
	Location (0001 – 9020)
	Fund Type (100 – 999)
	Business Line (0500 – 9999)
	Account will default to 74103
	Activity Code, if left blank, will default to 0000
o	Project String 
	The project code consists of 8 required parts. Specify all the parts of your project account code below, separating each part with a period (.).
	The project code parts are: 
	Project.Task.Unit.Division.Organization.Location.FundType.BusinessLine
	The Unit.Division.Organization parts are sometimes concatenated into a single segment. Both forms are accepted here. 
5.	Click Create. 
Managing your payment account
1.	Log in to the Software Portal with your NetID and password. 
2.	Under the My Account drop-down, select My Payment Accounts. 
3.	Click Show Details next to the account you want to manage.
Payment Accounts may be disabled by unchecking the Enabled. This does not affect any active subscriptions on the account, but it prevents the account from incurring any new subscription charges. This allows you to design the account's access profile in a vacuum. Otherwise, a mistake in designing the access profile could result in unintended charges.
You'll have the following sections:
•	
o	Details: You can create a nickname for the account or update the account number.
o	Delegated Payment Managers: They have the same access as the Payment Account Owner, except they cannot create Payment Accounts.
o	Payment Account Users: Allows you to assign access to specific individuals, enabling them to use the account to subscribe to software, but only for their own use. They will be able to place orders for any monthly subscription.
o	Subscriber Expenses:  
	Displays a list of individuals with a monthly subscription using this payment account, along with the Product, Cost, Start Date, and OIT Order #. This is searchable by person's name/NetID and by product name.
	You can click on Export to download a .csv file of the current subscriptions being charged to the account.
	You can cancel individual subscriptions on this list by clicking Cancel on the appropriate line. The cancel button initiates the cancellation process. You must read and acknowledge the risk before submitting your cancellation request.
How to subscribe
You may order on behalf of someone else by doing the following:
1.	Log in to the Software Portal and find the software you want to subscribe someone to. 
2.	On the Software's Product Page, click on Get Product...
3.	Under Monthly Subscription, click Subscribe... 
o	If there is no Monthly Subscription option, then the software is unavailable for this payment option. 
4.	In the drop-down under Payment Account, choose the account to be charged. You will only see accounts that you have been given access to. 
5.	Under Choose your recipients, enter the NetID of the individual(s) you want to subscribe to and select their name from the list.  
o	User accounts with (-adm) must not be used.
6.	Confirm that the information under Cost is correct, then click Subscribe. 
If you receive an error, please email software@rutgers.edu with a screenshot.
How to transfer orders from one Payment Account to another
Important: All Payment Accounts must be created in the University Software Portal by a Payment Account Owner before requesting the transfer of existing orders.
Who Can Request a Transfer
Requests must be submitted by either:
•	The Payment Account Owner, or
•	A Delegated Payment Account Manager
How to Submit a Request
To transfer orders between Payment Accounts, submit a request via email to: software@rutgers.edu with the Subject line: Software Portal Payment Account Change for Existing Orders
The email request must include all of the following details:
•	Originating (current) Payment Account
•	Destination (new) Payment Account 
•	The destination Payment Account must already exist and be active in the Software Portal.
•	NetID(s) and the corresponding product(s) to be moved
Requests that are missing any required information noted above may be delayed.
How to cancel subscriptions from your payment account 
Before cancellation, ensure that the user has downloaded and backed up any necessary data/files from the software, as they will all be deleted when your subscription is canceled. 
1.	Log in to the Software Portal with your NetID and password. 
2.	Under the My Account drop-down, select My Payment Accounts. 
3.	Click Show Details next to the account you want to manage.
4.	Click on Subscriber Expenses.
5.	You'll see a list of who has a monthly subscription using this payment account, as well as the Product, Cost, Start, and OIT Order #. This is searchable by person's name/NetID and by product name.
6.	You can cancel individual subscriptions on this list by clicking Cancel on the appropriate line. 
FAQs
When does the monthly subscription get billed?  
Monthly subscriptions are billed in arrears, meaning charges for subscriptions active in one month are billed the following month. For example, if a subscription starts in January, the billing entry will appear sometime in February.
If I cancel, when do I lose access?
When a monthly subscription is canceled, you retain access until the end of that calendar month. 
Is there a prorated refund if I cancel mid-month?
There are no refunds for monthly subscriptions. If canceled mid-month, you retain access until the end of that calendar month. 
If a person's subscription is canceled and resubscribed in the same month, is the GL or Project String charged twice? 
Yes
Can I get a report of active subscriptions?
Yes. You can view the current list of subscriptions on the Software Portal under 'My Payment Accounts'. Here you can cancel user subscriptions or export a CSV file of all current ones. Account managers will also receive an alert when someone starts or cancels a monthly subscription using one of your accounts.
Can we use a Project String?
Yes, as of April 2026.
Are subscriptions canceled automatically if the user is no longer in my department or at the university?
No, subscriptions will be billed until canceled by the Payment Account Owner, Delegated Payment Account Manager, or the Payment Account User.  Reports should be run and reviewed for users who are no longer with your department or the university.
How do we transfer a subscription?
There is no need to transfer the monthly subscription; simply cancel and place a new order for the user.
How do I transfer ownership of my Payment Account(s) to another person?
Email software@rutgers.edu with the subject line "Software Portal Payment Account ownership transfer” and include the GL or Project string(s), your name and NetID, also the name and NetID of the new owner.

title: Certificates Current SSL Certificates
body:
Table of Contents
•	Certificates 
o	Types of Certificates Available
o	Generating a Certificate Request using OpenSSL
•	Requesting a non-Rutgers domain
•	Requesting Code Signing Certificates 
o	Important Changes to code-signing
o	Key Attestation
o	Details to provide
•	Domain Control Validation 
o	Email DCV
o	DNS DCV
o	File-based DCV
o	Wildcard domains
•	Automation with ACME 
o	Reasons to Automate
o	Automation Resources
o	How to get integrated with InCommon
 
Certificates
Types of Certificates Available
•	SSL/TLS Certificates
•	Extended Validation (EV) and Anchor Certificates
•	Client (Personal) Certificates
•	Code Signing Certificates
•	IGTF Server Certificates (Interoperable Global Trust Federation)
•	ECC (Elliptical Curve Cryptography) Certificates
More information can be found on the InCommon Certificate Service Home page.
Generating a Certificate Request using OpenSSL
Consult with the documentation for your web server to determine the preferred procedure for generating a certificate signing request (CSR).
To use OpenSSL to generate a CSR, first ensure it is installed: Get OpenSSL
Using RSA 2048 bit
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout myhost_private.key -out myhost_request.csr

Using ECDSA
openssl ecparam -name secp384r1 -genkey -out myhost_private.key
openssl req -new -key myhost_private.key -out myhost_request.csr

Comparing Algorithms
Compare ECDSA vs RSA
Details to include in the CSR
Please note that some of these details must be specified exactly as-is to meet the security requirements of the certificate issuing authority.
•	Country Name 
o	You must specify “US”
•	State or Province Name 
o	You must specify “New Jersey”
•	Locality Name 
o	Specify the city, e.g. “New Brunswick”
•	Organization Name 
o	You must specify “Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey”
•	Organization Unit Name 
o	Specify your department e.g. “Office of Information Technology”
•	Common Name 
o	This is the host domain that will be identified/secured by the certificate e.g. “myhost.rutgers.edu”
•	Email Address 
o	This is the contact email address e.g. “serveradmin@myhost.rutgers.edu“
Requesting a non-Rutgers domain
To request a non-Rutgers.edu domain be added (e.g., “scarletknights.com” or “orbit-lab.org”), contact ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu with the following information.
This request can take up to 4 business days.
The Whois records MUST reference “Rutgers” or it will not be able to be added to our agreement.
•	Domain name
•	Requester
•	Department
•	Department Organization ID
Once the domain is approved, we will initiate the Domain Control Validation (DCV). Please see the Domain Control Validation section below for more information.
Requesting Code Signing Certificates
To request a Code Signing Cert, contact ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu with the information below.
This request can take up to 2 business days.
You will receive an invitation via email.
Important Changes to code-signing
As of June 1, 2023, a hardware security module that supports key attestation is required for code-signing.
Sectigo recommends a Yubikey 5 FIPS series.
Key Attestation
You must provide a key attestation when making a new code-signing certificate request. 
Details to provide
Note: The email address defaults to the domain being requested and cannot be changed.
•	Organization
•	Department
•	Domain
•	Email Address
•	Term
•	Full Name
•	Contact Email
•	InCommon Certificates
Domain Control Validation
Domain Control Validation (DCV) is a way to verify that the person requesting a certificate actually has control of the domain in the request. This protects against malicious action against a domain.
Sectigo provides 3 DCV methods: Email, DNS, and file-based. Read the fully detailed explanation on the InCommon Certificate Service Home page.
Email DCV
Requires you to have access to one of a set of pre-defined email addresses associated with your domain. e.g. admin@mydomain.org
DNS DCV
Requires you to have access to the DNS record for your domain. You will need to enter a TXT record with a specific hash value that is generated by Sectigo.
File-based DCV
Requires your HTTP/S server to make a specifically named file available with a specific hash value within the file.
Wildcard domains
To request a wildcard certificate (e.g. *.mydomain.com), you must use the Email or DNS based DCV methods.
DCV is required annually for each domain, including rutgers.edu. However, if you are requesting a rutgers.edu certificate (e.g. myorg.rutgers.edu), you will be able to take advantage of DCV having already been completed for rutgers.edu.
If you are requesting a non-rutgers.edu certificate (e.g., mydomain.org), you will need to complete DCV annually alongside your certificate request.
Please consider which method you want to undertake when requesting DCV for your domain. This helps with turnaround time.
DCV remains a very hands-on way to validate control, and you will be required to be in active communication with a Rutgers OIT member for the entire process to complete it in a timely manner.
Automation with ACME
The Automated Certificate Management Environment is a protocol for software agents such as certbot to use to request, receive, revoke, and install certificates in your server environment.
Reasons to Automate
•	“Set it and forget it” 
o	Well, you should still check on it, but it’s easy to ask certbot what’s going on.
•	No more expired certificates 
o	Avoid the drama of browser certificate errors on your web site
•	Future proof 
o	You may think it’s okay to manually renew certs annually, but what happens when the industry moves to shorter expirations of 3 months?
•	Automate the entire process 
o	If you have a non-Rutgers domain, you’ll need to complete Domain Control Validation annually as well. ACME allows you to validate domain control at the time of request if you use a supported DNS provider.
Automation Resources
•	What is Acme?
•	certbot docs
•	Certify Certificate Manager
•	ACME clients on Github
How to get integrated with InCommon
•	Request an ACME account from OIT via ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu 
o	This will create a tracking incident
o	The account will be given permission to manage certificates for a specific set of domains. For direct subdomains of rutgers.edu, each domain must be specified individually
•	You will receive your account credentials to integrate with your chosen ACME client.
•	Simply contact ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu to whitelist additional domains if needed.

title: Certificates InCommon Certificate Service Transition FAQ
body:
Table of Contents
•	Why is the platform provider changing?
•	What is changing?
•	Who is InCommon?
•	What will happen to my certificates?
•	What will happen to my ACME clients?
•	What do I need to do right now?
•	What do I need to do later?
•	What is ACME?
•	Why ACME?
•	How do I get enrolled with ACME?
•	What is Domain Control Validation (DCV)?
•	How can I automate DCV?
•	What is the current certificate lifetime?
•	What is happening to certificate lifetimes?
•	Where can I get the CA root and intermediate certificates?
•	What resources are available to help with this transition?
Why is the platform provider changing?
After careful evaluation, InCommon has decided to transition from our current platform provider, Sectigo, to CertiNext for our certificate authority (CA) services. This transition will be better positioned in InCommon to address broader changes in the certificate industry and will be completed by July 17, 2026.
What is changing?
•	InCommon has ended its partnership with Sectigo and formed a partnership with CertiNext to provide SSL Certificates
•	Access to the Sectigo Certificate Manager (SCM) portal will end on July 17, 2026
•	All certificate requests will need to be processed through the CertiNext platform
•	Code-signing certificates are no longer included for free
Who is InCommon?
InCommon is an organization that bridges peer Universities and Colleges for Identity Management. 
What will happen to my certificates?
The expiration dates for certificates signed by Sectigo will be honored. However, certificates will no longer auto-renew.
What will happen to my ACME clients?
You will need to reconfigure your ACME clients using new EAB credentials issued from the CertiNext platform.
What do I need to do right now?
1.	Review the Sectigo/InCommon certificates you have deployed and renew them as soon as possible if their expiration date is within the next 6 months.
2.	Extend your certificates to the maximum lifetime 
o	If you have a cert expiring before Dec 1, 2026, you should renew now to maximize the amount of time you have available to transition to ACME.
o	Follow existing procedures to renew your certificates.
o	Existing ACME clients currently deployed should be engaged to force renewal of transaction certificates in their managed environment.
What do I need to do later?
Existing ACME clients currently deployed will need to be re-registered with new EAB credentials issued from the new CertiNext platform.
Hosts with certificates not currently managed should be transitioned to ACME on the new platform. i.e., automate your certificate management.
What is ACME?
Automated Certificate Management Environment, or ACME, is a protocol for requesting, renewing, and revoking SSL certificates (i.e., certificate management) through a Certificate Authority (e.g., CertiNext).
Why ACME?
In short, because the CA/Browser Forum that drives internet security policy has deemed automation of certificates and domain validation to be the most secure and reliable path forward
How do I get enrolled with ACME?
Email ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu to request an ACME account. You will be provided with "External Account Binding" credentials.
Choose an ACME client that is appropriate for your hosting environment. We recommend:
•	Linux 
o	certbot (github)
o	acme.sh
o	lego
•	Windows 
o	simple-acme
o	Certify the Web (paid license)
What is Domain Control Validation (DCV)?
DCV is a way for a Certificate Authority to verify that you own the domain associated with the certificate you're requesting.
How can I automate DCV?
•	DCV can be completed using a file on the host if that file can be accessed on the public internet. 
o	This is the most common way to automate and is supported by many ACME clients.
o	Configure your ACME client to manage your web server, and it can retrieve a token from the Certificate Authority and automatically place it at the correct location hosted by your web server.
•	DNS-based validation is also supported.
What is the current certificate lifetime?
199 days or ~6 months
What is happening to certificate lifetimes?
Certificate lifetimes and Domain Control Validation lifetimes are shortening annually until 2029, when they will be 45 days and 10 days, respectively.
This is unrelated to the InCommon partnership agreement.
The industry wants automation, and you are encouraged to automate.
Where can I get the CA root and intermediate certificates?
InCommon CAs (Confluence)
You will need the new Certinext InCommon intermediate CA and the emSign intermediates in your systems, but all TLS certs are trusted by browsers and OS vendors.
What resources are available to help with this transition?
InCommon Certificate Services Home (Confluence)
CertiNext REST API v2 Swagger UI documentation
Refer to the InCommon Transition FAQ for the latest information and resources.

title: Certificates Review and Renew SSL Certificates
body:
Learn how to review the details and submit renewal requests for InCommon SSL certificates in your hosted environment.
Please note that the information herein is intended as a general guideline, and it cannot account for variations across hosted environments where certificates may reside.
View Certificate Details of a (public) website
Using a web browser
1.	Access a website via HTTPS. 
o	e.g. https://www.rutgers.edu
2.	Click the shield/lock/menu icon next to the URL in the address bar. 
o	Firefox: Click Connection secure > More Site Information > Security > View Certificate
o	Chrome: Click Connection is secure > Certificate is valid
o	Edge: Click Connection is secure > Certificate icon
o	Other: Follow a similar procedure as above
3.	Examine the Validity Period and Issuer in the Certificate Viewer window to identify the certificate's expiration date and issuer.
Using openssl
See the OpenSSL s_client reference for detailed info.
Example:
HOST=www.rutgers.edu

openssl s_client -connect "$HOST:443" -servername "$HOST" </dev/null 2>/dev/null  | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -enddate
Expected response, showing the issuer and the expiration date (as notAfter).
issuer=C = US, O = Internet2, CN = InCommon RSA Server CA 2
notAfter=Jan 26 23:59:59 2027 GMT
Renew your Certificate
If your issuer is Internet2 or InCommon, renew your certificate to extend the maximum lifetime to 199 days.
via self-service
Please follow the current documentation for renewing via self-service.
via ACME
Follow the instructions for force-renewing certificates managed by the ACME clients in your environment. Here's a sample for some popular clients:
•	certbot 
o	Follow certbot documentation on renewals, with special attention toward re-creating and updating existing certificates
•	simple-acme (backward compatible with win-acme) 
o	Follow instructions on renewal management with special attention toward the --force switch documented under automatic renewals
Troubleshooting
•	AI tools can be very useful for quickly identifying configuration options that align with intricacies in your environment. It is encouraged to use these tools by providing full context when troubleshooting.
•	Email ssl_support@oit.rutgers.edu for additional assistance.

Troubleshooting tips
Cursor blink issue
When you are logged into a session (either QWS3270 Secure or RUID test) and change the cursor to Solid instead of blinking, it reverts to a blinking cursor in subsequent sessions. Use this procedure to set the cursor permanently to Solid:
1.	Click on the QWS3270 Secure icon on your desktop.
2.	When the session opens, DO NOT select a session from the drop-down menu. Click the Cancel button instead.
3.	Click Options on the menu bar at the top, then select Session.
4.	Under Display on the Options List, click Cursor on the left-hand side.
5.	In the two Cursor Style boxes, click the Solid radio buttons under Normal Mode and Insert Mode at the top.
6.	Click the Apply button on the lower right-hand side.

Correcting the faded print issue
Please note: Color will be spelled colour (Canadian spelling) throughout the program options

4.	Go to the Colour Options box at the bottom of the screen, in the middle.
5.	Select Black & white.
6.	Click the Apply button in the bottom right-hand corner.
7.	Click the OK button.

title: Meeting BigBlueButton – Troubleshooting Audio/Video Issues
body:
BigBlueButton by Blindside Networks is a web conferencing system designed for online learning. BigBlueButton enables the sharing of audio, slides, chat, video, and desktop applications between instructors,  students, and invited guests.
Audio/Video Issues
Audio
For a more detailed tutorial, see the BigBlueButton setting up audio tutorial video.
•	Verify you are using the correct equipment, it is plugged in, and selected as the channel to use.
•	Toggle sharing off and on using the headphone icon in the upper left, and go through the audio wizard again.
•	Review the BigBlueButton help article on how to join audio, including the troubleshooting tips at the end.
•	If you continue to have audio issues, connect to audio by dialing the phone number.
Video
To record a conference, the box for Enable recording for this conference must be checked when creating the conference. This only makes it possible to record, and does not actually start the recording.
Error! Filename not specified.
•	If the "Enable recordings" option was not checked when creating a conference, you can click the gear icon to the right of the conference and select Edit to enable recordings.
o	This can only be done before a conference has started. Once a conference has begun, changing this setting will not take effect.
•	The recording of the conference can be started and stopped by clicking the "Record button" icon at the top bar of the conference.

Error! Filename not specified.
•	Recordings will be available after the conference has concluded and the recording is processed. Processing time varies based on the length of the recording and server load.
•	Recordings can be accessed by clicking the name of the conference under "Concluded Conferences," which will display the length of the recording in hh: mm format, and the view button on the right to open the recording in another browser tab.
•	Once opened, the recording can be downloaded by right-clicking on the recording and selecting Save video as.
•	Since the recording is hosted on blindsidenetworks.com and not Canvas, you can also share the URL with anyone to view the recording. No login is required.

To use the Webex Integration, Rutgers NetID users will need an existing Rutgers Webex account. Please enable Webex via the Service Activation Portal.

Webex Setup
1.	Click on Cisco Webex in the course navigation. If it is not listed, enable it by managing the course navigation links in course Settings.
2.	In the Setup tab, check the box next to the options you plan to use in your course. You will need to choose your features for every new course site. 
3.	Select your time zone in the drop-down menu and choose Save.

Error! Filename not specified.
Virtual Meetings
Schedule a Meeting
1.	Click Cisco Webex on the course navigation menu.

Error! Filename not specified.
2.	Click the Meetings tab, if not enabled, go to the Setup tab to enable.
3.	Click the Schedule meeting button.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Enter a name for the meeting.
5.	Set the meeting date and time. 
o	Optionally, the Recurrence setting can be enabled if the meeting time is to be repeated.
o	Recurrence pattern (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly). 
	Daily – Meetings occur at the same time every day.
	Weekly – Choose the day(s) of the week and the meeting cadence.
	Monthly – Choose the date of the month or the day preference.
	Yearly - Choose the date of the month or the day preference.
o	Ends can be set either to a specific date or after a number of meetings. 
6.	Set the Join rules for guests who have not been invited to attend the meeting. It is recommended to check "They wait in the lobby until they're admitted."
7.	Set Audio connection options.
8.	Automatic recording can be enabled when the meeting starts. To ensure the meeting recording is associated with the meeting host, set join rules to "They wait in the lobby until they're admitted.
9.	Click Schedule.
After a meeting is created, it will be listed in your Upcoming tab. You can Start (host), Edit, or Delete a meeting from this tab.
When a Webex session is complete, it will be listed in the Completed tab, and any recordings will be viewable here. Meeting participants will be listed when you click on the meeting name in Completed Meetings.
Office Hours
Office hours are instructor-specific, with the meeting links tied to an instructor’s Webex account. Webex Office hours are not course-specific, so the office hours you set in one course populate all your courses in Canvas. Multiple instructors inside a Canvas course may claim the same time period.
1.	Click Cisco Webex on the course navigation menu.

Error! Filename not specified.

Error! Filename not specified.

9.	Scroll down and click Save.

1.	Click Cisco Webex on the course navigation menu.

Error! Filename not specified.

Please caution your students against sharing Webex links. Webex links are unique to the participant (student) and the meeting. The Webex link will also include the meeting password. What is Zoom?
Zoom is a cloud-based web conferencing service that supports video, voice, content sharing, and chat on any device. Zoom is available to all Rutgers faculty, staff, and students on the left-hand navigation of Canvas courses or through the Rutgers Zoom Web portal at rutgers.zoom.us

Best Practices for Zoom Meetings in your Canvas Course

title: Meeting Zoom – Alternate Hosts and your Canvas Course
body:
This article explains how the Zoom LTI in Canvas adds and manages alternate hosts when scheduling Zoom meetings within Canvas.
When a meeting is scheduled in the Zoom integration in Canvas, the following users are automatically added to Zoom meetings as alternate hosts when the meetings are created in the LTI:
•	Teachers, TAs, and teacher-based roles who have visited the Zoom page in the Canvas course previously 
o	The alt-hosts may not be displayed immediately when scheduling the meeting; however, teachers and teacher-based roles (Facilitator, course support, and other school-created course roles) will be granted access to host course meetings once they access the Zoom tool in their course. See Course Roles and Permissions. 
•	Canvas administrators  
o	Canvas admins are considered instructors by Zoom. When a Canvas admin visits the Zoom LTI in a course, they will be added as an alternative host to the meetings on the course schedule.
Automating the addition of alternative hosts reduces the work for course instructors who schedule course meetings.
Who can serve as alternative hosts?
For Zoom meetings created in Canvas, anyone associated with the Rutgers Zoom license may serve as an alternative host. They do not have to be enrolled in the Canvas course.
How can I edit or change alternative hosts?
Alternate hosts must have an active Rutgers Zoom account and be added using the email address associated with that account. They may be added via the meeting details through the Zoom integration in Canvas or through the Zoom Web Portal.
To add the alternative host, add the user with their netid@rutgers.edu email address. Other Rutgers email address forms will not work; firstname.lastname@rutgers.edu and netid@domain.rutgers.edu are not associated with a Rutgers Zoom account. Your alternative host will receive an email notification that they are an alternative host. This email is the only link to access the Zoom meeting, as the meeting will not appear in the Zoom integration in Canvas or in the Zoom Web Portal.

title: Services Rutgers Live TV Activation and Installation
body:
Rutgers live TV is delivered over an IPTV app via an Android TV device. It is available in public spaces, offices, residence hall lounges, athletic buildings, and other campus areas. Using a Google Chromecast or similar Android TV (OS) device, you can stream content on devices connected to the non-residential wireless network (RUIOT). This service is not available for student use in dorms; students should explore available streaming plans and discounts for use in residence halls. 
You must contact your local IT support for assistance to watch TV content in a non-residential campus location. Your IT department will need to:
1.	Obtain a compatible streaming device.
2.	Get the device's wireless MAC address.
3.	Complete an initial setup and activation.
4.	Request service activation from OIT.
For more information about the service, you can view the channel lineup or visit the Rutgers Television Content Services website. 
IT Admin Activation and Setup Instructions
Departmental IT Staff can obtain and set up Live TV in two ways. 
•	Contact OIT - Enterprise Infrastructure to obtain a pre-configured streaming device and receive assistance with setup. This service comes at a cost. 
•	Obtain and configure your own departmental device. 
Configure your own departmental device
1.	Obtain a Google Chromecast device or similar Android TV (OS) device.  
2.	You'll need to get the device's MAC address before proceeding. Follow the instructions on how to locate your Chromecast MAC address.  
o	For Chromecast with Google TV devices, you must first connect to an alternate WiFi network, such as a phone hotspot, and complete the device setup process to reach the MAC address.
3.	Follow the guide on how to set up your Chromecast.  
o	Rutgers Scarletmail accounts are not able to download the required app from the Google Play store to access IPTV. You will need to have an alternate Google account. 
o	Google accounts do not need to be associated with a Gmail email address; instead, you can create an account using a Rutgers Email address. It is recommended that you create one using a departmental email address or distribution list to centralize the management of multiple devices. You can follow the instructions on how to create a Google account with a non-Gmail email address. 
o	During setup, custom room names are recommended to identify the building and room number in which the device will be located. 
4.	Submit a request for service activation from OIT with the Device's MAC address. 
5.	Once OIT activates your service, you will receive a password to connect the device to the RUIOT wireless network. 
o	The device must be on the RUIOT wireless network to access the IPTV service. 
o	Remember to go back and forget the network that you originally used to obtain the MAC address.
6.	After connecting to RUIOT, download the iMPlayer TV IPTV app on the Chromecast device. 
o	This app is not available for download if logged in using a ScarletMail account. 
7.	Open the app and select Management Code, then enter the code provided to you by OIT.  
o	After entering the code, please wait about 30 seconds for the channels and guide to fully load. After they load the first channel in the list (CBS) will start playing. If they do not play, be sure you are connected to RUIOT, or restart the device. 
8.	Updating the following settings for unattended locations, such as public spaces that display constant Live TV content, is recommended.  
o	Change the power settings so it never turns off. Located in Settings > System > Power & Energy > Never.
o	Turn on Profile Lock to keep anyone from accessing your profile or changing certain settings. 
For instructions on how to use the application, refer to the Rutgers Live TV User Guide.

title: login FAQ Do I need to use two-step login every time I use my software?
body:
On some applications or services, you will only need to authenticate with two-step verification when you first set up or log in to the application.
The first time you approve the Duo authentication request, you'll see the option to confirm the device is yours. This creates a trusted browser session for 30 days that will let you skip Duo two-factor authentication when you log in again with the same browser and device until that trust session expires. You are still required to authenticate with your NetID and Password each time, and your remembered device confirms your identity. Note that this feature is browser-specific and not shared between different browsers. For example, logging in with Chrome today and using Firefox later will ask you to authenticate again.
Do not select that this is your device when using a public or shared computer! This could leave your Duo session available to other users. Trust the browser only when you access applications from your own computer. Clicking on No, other people use this device will not create a trust session. You won't be asked to trust that device again for 14 days.
     Error! Filename not specified.
When your trusted browser session expires, you must use two-factor authentication again. Duo Push, phone call, text message, and passcode authentication methods will show the option to Remember Me already checked for you. Leaving the option enabled creates a new trusted browser session. If you don't want to trust that browser again, uncheck the Remember Me box before you approve the Duo Push or phone call request or enter a passcode.

title: login FAQ Do other universities use two-step login with Duo Security?
body: Duo Security is the leading providing of two-step login in higher education. Duo Two-step login is a requirement for accessing university resources at Harvard, Indiana, MIT, Penn State, University of South Carolina, University of Rochester, University of Michigan, and many other institutions.

title: login FAQ
body:
Does opting to select "Yes, this is my device" for Duo reduce my authentication security?" "
No. Selecting "Yes, this is my device" will not reduce your authentication security. With the "Yes, this is my device" feature enabled, your device becomes your two-step authentication method and is fully logged for auditing. Having this feature will prevent a new Duo authentication prompt from being asked every time you log in to a Rutgers University service or tool. Some may find this convenient instead of approving the Duo prompt frequently. However, if you log in from a new browser or device, the Duo prompt will reappear. 
There is a minimal chance that your authentication security will be reduced. Someone would need to obtain your NetID & NetID Password AND access to your device to compromise your credentials. 
Note that you must have Cookies enabled on your browser for the "Yes, this is my device" feature to work properly.

1.	Log in to the NetID Application Management Tool.
