title: login FAQ Is Duo blocked in some countries due to U.S. sanctions?
body:
To comply with U.S. regulations, two-step login with Duo is blocked for users in countries or regions subject to economic and trade sanctions enforced by the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
“Users attempting to authenticate to a Duo-protected application from an access device with an IP address originating in an OFAC-regulated country or region will be blocked from completing their login and receive an error message,” according to Duo Support. 
You may receive the following error message in the Duo Prompt: "Access denied. Duo Security does not provide services in your current location." 
Blocked authentications will appear in the Authentication Log as “Restricted OFAC location.”
For additional details, including an updated list of countries and regions blocked as part of these OFAC sanctions, see this knowledge base article posted by Duo.

title: login FAQ Verified Duo Push FAQs
body:
What is changing? 
Currently, when logging in to Rutgers systems, you accept a push notification from the Duo Mobile app. Once the change occurs, the device being used for access will display a three-digit verification code. You will then be asked to open the Duo Mobile app and enter the three-digit verification code that’s displayed. This new Duo method is known as Verified Duo Push (VDP). View the Verified Duo Push instructions to learn how to log in.  
What is not changing?
This change does not impact other methods of Duo two-factor authentication, which will remain available. This includes SMS passcodes, Touch ID, Hardware Tokens, Duo Mobile Generated Passcodes, and Security Keys. 
When will this change take place? 
Verified Duo Push will be introduced on October 7, 2025. However, not everyone will notice or see the change immediately. If you have clicked on "Yes, this is my device" during a previous Duo verification, you created a trusted browser session that is typically “saved” for up to 30 days. You will see the new Verified Duo Push after your trusted session has expired. Alternatively, you can use an Incognito or Private tab on your browser to see the new experience before then. 
Why is this changing? 
When someone tries to log in using a stolen account, it can trigger a series of push notifications to the account owner. These repeated alerts may become confusing or frustrating, leading the individual to accidentally approve a login request that isn't legitimate. Authentication via number matching takes a few seconds longer than typical push notifications but dramatically increases account security. It also works with the existing Duo app—no need to download new apps or tools.
Where will I have to use the new Verified Duo Push? 
Verified Duo Push is designed to work with web-based login prompts, so only those services will support this new function. Non-web browser applications, such as the Rutgers VPN, will continue to see the standard Duo push that does not require the 3-digit verification code. 
What are the minimum Duo Mobile app requirements? 
To use Verified Duo Push, a supported version of the Duo Mobile app must be installed and activated on your mobile device.
Effective February 2, 2026, the requirements for each operating system are: 
•	Android: Duo Mobile app version 4.85.0
•	iOS: Duo Mobile version 4.85.0
Note that the Duo app can only be installed on supported versions of iOS or Android that are noted in the article Update iOS and Android Software Versions to Use Two-Step Login with Duo. 
If you have an older version of Duo Mobile, you will receive a Duo Push request without the code entry field. When you try to approve, the login will fail, and you will see a message instructing you to update your software.

title: login FAQ What are the different Duo authentication passcodes available?
body:
Duo Mobile passcodes
These are one-time-use passcodes generated by the Duo Mobile application. You can use this code as your two-step login with Duo on all services. 
SMS passcodes
These are sent to your device via an SMS text message. When requested, you will receive one code in a text message. SMS codes are single-use; if you send multiple codes to your phone, only the most recent code is valid. 
Bypass codes
These are generated from the Duo Administration Service. The Rutgers OIT Help Desk can provide these codes based on user needs. Each bypass code is good for 2 uses for two hours after the code is generated. You can use these codes to authenticate your two-step login with Duo for all services. To avoid needing a bypass code, having a second device on one's Duo account is encouraged. 
Duo Hardware Tokens
These are thumb-sized plastic devices that generate codes you enter after your NetID password to access Rutgers services. For more information, visit Duo hardware token information.

By using two-step login, you’re protecting yourself and the university from hacking, phishing, and other cyber-attacks.

title: login FAQ What should I do when I receive an unexpected Duo prompt?
body:
Two-step login with Duo is an additional security measure to protect your account and information in case your password is compromised. You should NEVER approve a two-step login request from Duo if you did not prompt for it and are not expecting it.
If you get an unexpected Duo prompt, follow the instructions provided to report a fraudulent attempt to gain access to your account:
1.	Deny the Duo request prompt.
o	For push notifications: click Deny on the notification you receive, or I'm not logging in on the Duo app. If you open the Duo app to deny the request, it will then ask if this was a suspicious login: 
	Press Yes if you were not expecting the push. This will be reported to the Rutgers Information Security Office, and you will receive an email with further instructions.
	Press No if this was a mistake, and it will not be reported.
2.	To ensure your account is secure, immediately go to the NetID Management page, click on Manage NetID Password, and log in to reset your password.
3.	If you use this same password for any other personal accounts (which is not recommended), make sure you change those passwords as well in case the attacker tries to use it to access your other accounts.
When receiving push notifications, the Duo app will also show the approximate location of where the request originated. This can further help identify if it is a fraudulent attempt to gain access to your account from a location you are not currently near.
Be aware that if someone is trying to access your account, they may send repeated Duo prompts to annoy you into approving it. This is a sign of an active attack; you should deny every request and change your NetID password as soon as possible, which should also stop all fraudulent Duo prompts.
Should you have any further questions about an unexpected Duo prompt, contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: login FAQ When should I use push vs. passcode for Duo authentication?
body:
It is your choice! Note that the Verified Duo Push approval method requires an active internet connection on your enrolled device. This may require Wi-Fi or a valid Data Plan for the Push method to work properly.
If you do not have an active internet connection, it's recommended to utilize the DUO Mobile Generated Passcodes method to authenticate. 
Verified Duo Push 
Benefits
This is the best primary device for most people. Enter a verification code on your smartphone or tablet when you log in via the Duo Mobile App. 
Disadvantages
This requires using your personal device and an active internet connection. You will need to download the Duo Mobile App on your enrolled device. This may not be viable if you work at a place that does not allow personal devices, such as a testing center or a corrections facility.
Duo Mobile Generated Passcodes
Benefits
This is a great secondary method if you do not have an internet connection on your device. It allows you to generate a code to log in to the Duo Mobile App.
Disadvantages
This requires you to use your personal device. This may not be viable if you work at a place that does not allow personal devices, such as a testing center or a corrections facility.
Additional Inofrmation
To view other available authentication methods, view the list of Two-step Login with Duo Authentication Methods.

title: login FAQ Who will use two-step login with Duo?
body:
Starting in April 2022, the university requires all Rutgers students, faculty, staff, student workers, and others to use two-step login with Duo to access most services and tools requiring a NetID login. 
For more information, visit the Rutgers Information Technology Newsroom article regarding Students: Protecting your info with Duo.

title: login FAQ Will I be notified if someone else attempts to access my online resources?
body:
Using two-step authentication with Duo, you will be notified via one of the authentication methods provided by Duo Security. With Duo, you can either approve the login requests or report them as fraud with a click of a button.
If you believe someone else is attempting to access your online resources, you should report it as fraud with Duo. Follow the guide on what to do when you receive an unexpected Duo prompt.

title: login FAQ Will I need to authenticate with Duo when using Rutgers services on campus?
body:
If you are connected to RUWireless Secure or with an Ethernet cable on campus, you will still need to authenticate with Duo to access Rutgers services.
If you are connected at home, on a mobile hotspot, or via a non-secure wireless network on campus, you will need to authenticate with Duo to access Rutgers services. If you use the Rutgers VPN while connected this way, you will not be prompted for Duo when signing in to Rutgers services.
Further information regarding the Rutgers VPN can be found on the Rutgers VPN site.

title: Login with Duo Can I opt-out of two-step login with Duo?

title: Login with Duo Duo Quick Resources for OIT Staff
body:
Response to general concern about using Duo
Rutgers requires all users to use two-step login with Duo. You will need to use your NetID password and another method—typically a smartphone with the Duo app—to verify your identity when logging in to Canvas, myRutgers, Microsoft Office, OneDrive, ScarletMail, Zoom, and most other services that require a NetID. This reduces the risk that anyone but you will access your account, even if your password has been compromised. By using two-step login, you’re helping to protect yourself and the university from hacking, phishing, and other cyberattacks.
Accessibility concerns
Those who are requesting an exemption should be directed to https://ods.rutgers.edu/. Please note that, for privacy and legal reasons, you cannot request additional information about a user's disability or accessibility needs. 
Security concerns 
Security concerns or any escalated request for an exemption should result in the incident being created and assigned to the ISO – Information Security Office triage group. Please do not create an incident task.
Parents concerned about losing access to student information
Should set up a CommunityID, and the student can provide them access following the directions here. 
Frequent Resources
•	Enrollment guide for two-step login with Duo
•	How is Duo used in places such as exam rooms that forbid mobile phones?
•	Hardware token information
•	Getting Help article, which includes token resync directions
•	All public Duo articles
Common problems and solutions
•	Duo window does not pop up when they are trying to activate
o	Make sure that they temporarily enable pop-ups
•	Scanning the QR code does not work
o	Make sure they are scanning their own specific barcode generated by the Duo process and not the one in the knowledge article
•	Does not have the device on them (lost or another reason)
o	OIT Help Desk can generate a bypass code.
•	Got a new phone/changing phones
o	If the same number, they can use the code option (when they select enter passcode, it will show the option to send codes as SMS)
o	If it is a new number, the OIT Help Desk can generate a bypass code to set up a new device
•	Unable to use Duo app on a device with a language other than English
o	Duo Mobile will localize to English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, or Portuguese (Brazilian) on iOS and Android based on the user's device language (Japanese and Spanish support added in Duo Mobile version 3.48.0 and newer; Brazilian Portuguese added in version 4.8.0 or newer).
Bypass notes
•	Before doing a bypass code, always verify that the user has no access to any device that could be used to authenticate.
•	If they get a new phone but keep the same number, they can still authenticate and receive codes by text.
•	If they have a new number but the same device and it has not been reset, they can use push or the code from the app to set up the device.
•	If they have a new number and a new device, but the device has been restored, they may be able to use push if the app data was restored from a previous device.
•	If none of these are available, proceed to request a bypass from the OIT Help Desk Full-Time staff.

title: Login with Duo Duo request failure due to outdated TLS
body:
Beginning June 30, 2023, Duo requires that all authentication requests come via TLS 1.2. The following connection requests will receive an error response from Duo, resulting in blocked MFA and end-users unable to log in to protected applications:
•	TLS 1.0/1.1 connection requests
•	TLS connection requests negotiated by unsupported cipher suites
This can affect connection requests from:
•	Duo Windows applications
•	Duo Unix on a Unix/Linux system with OpenSSL version 1.0.0 or earlier
•	Duo SDKs used by custom applications
•	Third-party SDKs that connect to Duo APIs
•	Duo LDAPS application for SSL VPN
•	Duo Mobile is still in use on older versions of Android
•	Any device used to access a Duo-protected application using an embedded browser, operating system, or web browser that is no longer supported by Duo
Duo recommends using updated software. All versions of macOS, Android, and iOS supported by Duo will be unaffected because their default configuration uses TLS 1.2 and secure cipher suites.
For more information, please refer to Duo's guide on support after TLS 1.0/1.1 end of life.

body:
Rutgers requires two-step login with Duo for all Rutgers students, faculty, staff, and guests. Visit the Rutgers Two-Step login with Duo page to learn more about Duo.
Two-step login helps protect your account by adding an extra layer of security beyond your password. With two-step login, you will need to provide additional identity verification to access many university online resources.
Duo Mobile is an app for your smartphone that helps you authenticate quickly and easily. Without it, you'll still be able to log in via text message, hardware token, or security key, but for the best experience, we recommend using Duo Mobile. After installing the app, you will receive a notification on your phone to approve your login.
Note: If you are required to obtain and enroll with a hardware token, please follow the directions on the hardware token information page.

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	When you receive confirmation that the new mobile phone number has been added for texts, click Continue to log in to the application with the passcode sent via text message from Duo.
Logging in with Duo for the first time
The first time you log in with Duo, it automatically selects one of your configured login options from a sequenced list of available options. If you don't want to use the method Duo automatically suggests for that application, cancel the Duo authentication in progress and click Other options. Then, select the method you want from the list.
Completing a Duo login sets the authentication method you used as the first choice. Future Duo logins from the same device and browser will automatically use that same method. If you cancel the authentication in process and choose a different device, then the device you use becomes the first choice. There is no way to turn off automatic device selection or to explicitly configure a default authentication device.
This is the sequence of authentication methods Duo uses when you first log in. If you don't have a specific authentication method set up, Duo automatically selects the next available option.
1.	Touch ID
2.	Security keys
3.	Verified Duo Push
4.	Duo Mobile generated passcodes
5.	Hardware token passcodes
6.	SMS passcodes
Remembered Devices
The first time you approve the Duo authentication request, you'll see the option to confirm the device is yours. This creates a trusted browser session that lets you skip Duo two-factor authentication when you log in again with the same browser and device, until that trust session expires. You are still required to authenticate with your NetID and Password each time, and your remembered device acts as a confirmation of your identity. Please note that this feature is browser-specific and not shared between different browsers. For example, if you log in with Chrome today and use Firefox later, it will ask you to authenticate again.
Do not select that this is your device when using a public or shared computer! This could leave your Duo session available to other users. Trust the browser only when you access applications from your own computer. Clicking on No, other people use this device will not create a trust session. You won't be asked to trust that device again for 14 days.
When your trusted browser session expires, you will need to use two-factor authentication again. The Duo Push, phone call, text message, and passcode authentication methods will already show the option to Remember Me checked for you. Leaving the option enabled creates a new trusted browser session. If you don't want to trust that browser again, uncheck the "Remember Me" box before proceeding with verification.

title: Login with Duo Setting up a security key for two-step login with Duo
body:
A security key is an external device that, when tapped or when the button is pressed, sends a signed response back to Duo to validate your login. Duo uses the WebAuthn authentication standard to interact with your security keys. You may also see WebAuthn referred to as "FIDO2".
To use a security key with Duo, make sure you have the following:
•	A supported security key. WebAuthn/FIDO2 security keys from Yubico or Feitian are good options. U2F-only security keys (like the Yubikey NEO-n) can't be used with the Universal Prompt.
•	A supported browser: Chrome, Safari, Firefox, or Edge. Refer to the Duo browser support table for minimum browser versions with security key support in Duo.

Remember Me issues
The first time you approve the Duo authentication request, you'll see the option to confirm the device is yours. This creates a trusted browser session that will let you skip Duo two-factor authentication when you log in again with the same browser and device until that trust session expires. You are still required to authenticate with your NetID and Password each time, and your remembered device acts as a confirmation of your identity. Note that this feature is browser-specific and not shared between different browsers. For example, if you log in with Chrome today and use Firefox later, it will ask you to authenticate again.
Do not select that this is your device when using a public or shared computer! This could leave your Duo session available to other users. Trust the browser only when you access applications from your own computer. Clicking on No, other people use this device will not create a trust session. You won't be asked to trust that device again for 14 days.
The Remember Me feature relies on cookies, and when enabled correctly, you will not be prompted to complete two-factor authentication the next time you use the same browser. Be aware of the following restrictions that can impact the Remember Me feature and adjust your settings as necessary:
•	
o	Chrome Incognito and other private browsers do not provide support for Remember Me, as cookies are cleared at the end of the session.
o	Microsoft Edge has a “Delete browsing history on exit” in its General settings. If this is enabled, the Remember Me feature will not work.
o	Some browsers may have security settings that restrict cookies to only authorized sites. If so, add “duosecurity.com” as a trusted site.

title: Login with Duo Update iOS and Android Software Versions to Use Two-Step Login with Duo
body:
Which versions of iOS does Duo Mobile support?
The current version of Duo Mobile supports iOS 17.0 and greater, but cannot guarantee Duo Mobile's functionality on preview/beta software provided by Apple. Duo recommends upgrading your device to the most recent version of iOS. 
For more detailed information, visit the Duo Support page regarding compatible iOS versions with Duo Mobile. 
Which versions of Android does Duo Mobile support? 
The current version of Duo Mobile supports Android 12.0 and greater and Android Go 12.0 and greater. Duo recommends upgrading your device to the most recent version of Android. We cannot guarantee Duo Mobile's compatibility with custom variants or Android distributions. Duo Mobile is not supported on Chrome OS or Huawei devices. Duo does not provide official support for non-standard custom Android distributions like OnePlus, LineageOS, or ColorOS.
For more detailed information, visit the Duo Support page regarding compatible Android versions with Duo Mobile. 
How do I update my device?
The Office of Information Technology strongly recommends that you follow these instructions from Apple and Google Android Help, respectively, to update your device(s):
•	Updating iOS
•	Updating Android
Which authentication methods are affected?
Verified Duo Push and Duo Mobile passcodes will continue to work on devices running iOS 16 or Android 11 that already have Duo Mobile installed. However, you will not be able to upgrade your Duo app version.
If a new Duo mobile app version install is attempted on a device with an older operating system, the following authentication methods will not work:
•	Verified Duo Push
•	Duo Mobile Generated Passcodes
Which authentication methods are NOT affected?
The following methods are not affected in any way by incompatible software versions:
•	Touch ID
•	Security Keys (U2F)
•	Hardware Token Passcodes
•	SMS Passcodes
These authentication methods do not rely on Duo Mobile.
For further assistance, please contact your Department's IT Staff or the OIT Help Desk.

title: Login with Duo What is two-step login with Duo?
body:
What is Two-Step Login with Duo?
Two-Step Login with Duo is a service that provides additional security, enabling university systems to verify someone's identity with greater confidence. This is especially important for protected and sensitive systems.
Two-factor authentication adds a second layer of security to your online accounts. Verifying your identity with a second factor (such as your phone or another mobile device) prevents anyone but you from logging in, even if they know your password.

2.	Use your phone to verify your identity

Security Benefits
•	Adding a second layer of protection to your digital identity.
•	Further protects sensitive data you access, even if a NetID/password is compromised.
•	Helps mitigate phishing attacks by preventing access to sensitive information.
•	Meets new industry security regulations and compliance.
•	Conveniently functions on- and off-campus.
•	Enterprise License is centrally funded.
“Over 95% of attacks involve harvesting credentials from customer devices, then logging into web applications with them.” — Verizon 2015 Data Breach Investigations Report
Required for
•	All Active Rutgers University Employees (Faculty, Staff, Student Workers)
•	Active Guests (Visiting scholars, Contractors, etc.)
•	Active Students
•	Retirees
Enrollment
Follow the instructions on how to enroll in Two-Step Login with Duo. 
Note: It is best to enroll more than one device, such as a smartphone or tablet, to avoid difficulties authenticating when your primary device is unavailable. Smartphone authentication via Verified Duo Push and DUO Mobile passcodes is recommended.
How Does Two-Step Login with Duo Authentication Work?
After you enroll for Two-Step Login with Duo, when you access any University central authentication service (CAS) protected web application, you will complete the first authentication step by entering your Rutgers NetID and password in the CAS login page. You will then be prompted to complete the second step using any of the available DUO Security authentication methods you have set up.
International Traveler Information
Two-Step Login with Duo can be used while traveling abroad. All available authentication methods should work. When cellular service and internet access are unavailable, push notifications and SMS passcodes will not be available on your device. In this case, you can still use the Duo Mobile Passcodes or hardware token if you have one.

title: & Multimedia Kaltura - Capture Desktop App
body:
Kaltura Capture, also known as the Kaltura Capture desktop recorder, is an application that enables anyone to create videos anywhere.
Kaltura Capture has a simple user interface that requires only one click to record, with no complex setup or lengthy learning curve. Kaltura capture is supported on both Windows and Mac. You can record: two camera inputs at once, two screens, or a camera and a screen. Kaltura Capture uploads new videos to the Kaltura Mediaspace video portal and to the My Kaltura Media integration in Canvas. There is a 2-hour limit to capture recordings.
Kaltura Capture includes:
•	Screen and webcam capture in one click
•	Automatic slide detection and creation of searchable chapters
•	Support for software management installation
•	Seamless uploading to Learning and Content Management Systems and Kaltura MediaSpace
•	Intuitive user interface
Table of Contents
•	Installation
•	Getting Started
•	Recording Options
•	Capturing your recording
•	Uploading your recording
•	Additional Resources
Installation
1.	Log in to your Rutgers MediaSpace account or go to the My Kaltura Media tool in your Canvas Account.
2.	Click the + Create button and select Capture from the dropdown menu.

Error! Filename not specified.
3.	Click the appropriate download link for your operating system. 

Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Launch the installer and follow the instructions to install Kaltura Capture. 
o	Windows: Double-click the downloaded .msi file to launch the installer (you may need administrative permissions).
o	Mac OS: Double-click the .dmg to mount its contents, then drag the application from the .dmg window into the Applications folder to install. You may need an administrator password. 
Getting Started
Initially, Kaltura Capture must be launched from the Kaltura Mediaspace video portal or from the My Kaltura Media integration within Canvas. After the desktop application has been paired with the online service, you can launch it directly from the desktop.
After installing the desktop application, go to your account in Rutgers MediaSpace or to My Kaltura Media in your Canvas Account, click + Create, and select Capture as was done to install the app. When the app is already installed, this option opens a prompt asking whether you would like to launch the program. Depending on the browser, checking the box to Remember my choice or Always use this app will launch the app without prompting on future attempts.
Once you have paired your desktop application to the web service, you may click the icon on your computer to launch the app directly.
Recording Options
In Kaltura Capture, the default selection is to use the screen as the primary input and the camera as the secondary input. To record only one input, select the input and disable the other. Once launched, the Kaltura Capture Recorder is displayed.
1.	The Record button will start a recording.
2.	The up and down arrows to the right of the computer and camcorder icons will toggle the preview window for their respective recording sources.
3.	Clicking the computer, camcorder, or microphone icons toggles their respective recording options on or off. When the option is enabled, the icon has a blue outline. When disabled, the icon will be gray with a line through it.
4.	The ^ or ? next to the microphone icon lets you select your audio source.
5.	The Preview Window displays an image of what will be recorded from that source. It also has options to select the source from a drop-down menu and to record full screen or a specific area.
6.	Clicking the Manage link opens your recording Library and provides access to the Settings and Information about the Recorder.

Error! Filename not specified.
Additional information on specific recording scenarios, including presentations, is available at Kaltura Capture – Recording Options.
Capturing your recording
Once the record button is clicked, a 5-second countdown will appear before the recording begins, and the recording controls will appear in the lower-right corner of your screen. These controls are visible by default during recording, but they can be hidden.
1.	The Stop button stops your recording. Once clicked, you will get a pop-up asking you to confirm that you wish to conclude your recording. Once concluded, your Library will open.
2.	The Pause / Play button lets you pause your recording. Clicking it again will resume the recording.
3.	The Cancel button will cancel your recording, and nothing will be saved.
4.	The Timer indicates the length of your current recording.
5.	The Microphone icon can be toggled to enable or disable audio recording.
6.	The Screen Drawing toggle will toggle the screen drawing panel on or off.
7.	The Screen Drawing Panel provides tools for drawing on your screen while recording.
8.	The Minimize icon will minimize the recording controls to the taskbar in Windows or the dock in macOS, effectively hiding them during the recording. There are Keyboard Shortcuts you can use while the controls are minimized.

Error! Filename not specified.
Uploading your recording
After you end your recording, you will be directed to the entry page. If you click Stop by mistake, you can always click Cancel to return your recording to a paused state. If you want to complete the recording, enter the following information:

2.	Description
3.	Tags
4.	Click Save and Upload or Save to save your recording.

When you save a recording without uploading it, the Management window opens with the Edit tab, displaying options to Upload or Delete your media. You may select Delete all uploaded files to delete all uploaded media files from your local storage to save disk space.
When uploading, follow the onscreen prompts, and the upload must be completed before exiting the program. 
The Management Window opens to your Library by default, which contains your recordings and the following controls:
1.	The Library button can be used to access your video library

title: & Multimedia Kaltura - How do I use the Kaltura media player?
body:
Course instructors may share instructor-generated videos in a Canvas course or through links or embeds from Rutgers MediaSpace. The videos may be available in the Kaltura Course Gallery or embedded on a Canvas page, assignment, discussion, announcement, or Canvas quiz question. The video player is powered by the Kaltura V7 media player. Some media player features will depend on how the course instructor shared the video. 
When you visit web content that displays the V7 player, viewers will not see any player controls until you click Play. After you press play, the controls and menus appear. 
Kaltura V7 Media Player in Canvas
Kaltura V7 media players available in Rutgers Canvas are listed below. All video players using the Kaltura integration in Canvas display the transcript during playback. Depending on the selected video's size, the transcript may completely cover the video.  Viewers should view the video in full screen or close the transcript. Video and audio players do not have a share button because users must be logged in to Canvas to play the media.
•	Main Player: supports dual-screen video, playlists, documents, images, live streams, and 360 ° & VR media. The transcript will open upon play.
•	Video & Transcript Download Player: includes all the same features as the Main player and allows course participants to download the transcript, captions, attachments, and video.
•	Playback-only Player: includes all the same features as the Main player. The viewer will not be able to skip ahead in the video timeline. Viewers may skip back to a point in the timeline that they have already viewed.
•	Audio Player: supports audio-only media in a player with a smaller size. The transcript does not automatically display upon play.
•	Loop Player: is the Transcript Closed player, but replays the video continuously until it is stopped. Viewers can click Show Transcript to view the transcript.
•	Transcript Closed: is the main Kaltura player, but the transcript is closed by default. Viewers can click Show Transcript to view the transcript.
•	Transcript Download: is the main Kaltura player and allows downloading the transcript file.
Kaltura V7 Media Player from MediaSpace Links or Embeds
Kalura V7 media players available in Rutgers MediaSpace are listed below. All media players and embed codes from Rutgers MediaSpace include a share button and the option to view transcripts. Share links and embed codes distributed via Canvas do not automatically display the transcript when the video is played, and video analytics do not capture viewer information.
•	Main Player: supports dual-screen video, playlists, documents, images, live streams, and 360 ° & VR media. The transcript does not appear when play is started.
•	Transcript Player: includes all the same features as the Main player, with the transcript appearing upon play.
•	Download Player: includes all the same features as the Main player and allows any viewer to download the transcript, captions, attachments, and video.
•	Audio Player: supports audio-only media in a player with a smaller size.
•	Transcript Open: supports dual-screen video, playlists, documents, images, livestream, and 360 & VR media. The transcript will open upon play.
•	Loop Player: replays the video continuously until stopped. Viewers can click Show Transcript to view the transcript.
•	No Sharing: based on the Main Player, but does not include the information icon, sharing option, or transcript.
•	No Sharing with Transcript Download: based on the Main Player, but does not include the information icon or sharing option. Viewers can download the video transcript.
Kaltura V7 Media Player Features

The features of the Kaltura V7 media player are:
1.	Play/pause
2.	Seek forward or backward 10 seconds

title: & Multimedia Kaltura - How to View Videos Using the Media Player in Canvas
body:
This document describes how to use the controls on the Kaltura video player to personalize the playback experience. Kaltura in Rutgers Canvas and MediaSpace uses the Kaltura version 7 (v7) media player. Viewers may see the Kaltura media player on Rutgers websites and in Rutgers Canvas course sites. 
Table of Contents

Kaltura V7 Media Player Features
•	Faster load times – Course content with multiple videos on a page loads faster.
•	Enhanced security and performance.
•	Multiple means of representation – With advice from Rutgers instructional designers and accessibility experts, the new V7 player displays a transcript by default in Rutgers Canvas. The searchable transcript may be opened in a pop-up window or closed if unnecessary.
•	Responsive design and modern look – The player works seamlessly across different screen sizes and supports multiple-stream recordings (main video and picture-in-picture), improving performance on mobile devices.
•	Extended audio descriptions – The V7 player supports extended audio description (EAD) if requested for the video.
•	A customizable caption display allows users to choose font size and color based on their needs and preferences.
Sample Content
The sample video below includes many features that may be available when viewing a video or playlist in Rutgers Canvas. To improve performance and reduce the risk that legacy embed codes will stop working, it is recommended that course instructors and website content creators update their existing embeds over the next 6 months.

title: & Multimedia VoiceThread – Audio/video recording issues
body:
VoiceThread allows you to create multimedia discussions and projects for your course that students can interact with. 
However, when issues arise, it is best for you to try a series of troubleshooting steps. VoiceThread has additional troubleshooting articles.
Check your web browser’s settings
•	Make sure that you are using either Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, or Safari.
•	Make sure your web browser is fully up to date.
•	Check the browser’s microphone and webcam settings to ensure the correct input is selected and that VoiceThread is not blocked.
•	Clear your browser’s cache.
•	Make sure your browser allows third-party cookies.
•	If using Safari, you may need to adjust privacy settings to allow external tools to work correctly.
Restart your computer
A simple computer restart can help with some issues, especially if it has been a while since your last restart or if you have many other applications running.
Settings for your computer
Make sure that the correct microphone and/or webcam is selected in your computer’s sound input settings. If you can successfully record audio or video in other applications, you can skip this step.
Check your network settings
VoiceThread requires certain URLs and ports to be open on your network or allowed in your browser. If one is blocked, this may prevent successful recording. Click here if you are working on a local area network.
Try another internet connection and computer
Trying another location and/or computer will at least narrow down where the issue is occurring. It will also allow you to complete your VoiceThread work in the short term while you continue troubleshooting your own computer or network.

What is One Button to Push?
One Button to Push (OBTP) is a feature on the Cisco conference room systems that allows you to join a scheduled meeting with a single tap. Instead of dialing a meeting ID or passcode, a green "Join" button will appear on the room’s Touch Controller before your meeting begins.
How it works
When you invite a conference room to your calendar event, the Cisco system reads the meeting link (Teams, Zoom, or Webex) from the invitation. It then automatically configures the "Join" button to dial into that specific meeting at the scheduled time.
How to enable OBTP
Before you can use OBTP for the first time, you must contact your Departmental IT. They will need to create a Resource account for you in Rutgers Connect and enable the required platform (Teams/Webex/Zoom) for that account. They must then contact EITC and provide them with the following: 
•	UPN for the Resource account.
•	Name of the Teleconferencing System, building number, and the room it is located in.
•	Whether the Meeting title should appear on the room system. 
How to Schedule a Room
After your Departmental IT has confirmed OBTP has been set up, follow these steps to ensure the "Join" button appears correctly based on your preferred platform.
Your departmental IT will determine if the meeting title will appear on the Cisco controller. Please note that the meeting title may contain personal or sensitive information. 
Microsoft Teams 
1.	Create a new meeting in Outlook or Teams.
2.	Add the Conference Room Name (Resource Account) in the Required Attendees field.
3.	Ensure the Teams Meeting toggle is turned ON.
4.	Save the meeting.

On the room system, the host's name, meeting name, and meeting time are displayed. You can join the meeting by pressing Join without needing to enter a passcode separately.

2.	Add the Conference Room Name (Resource Account) in the Required Attendees field.
3.	Important: Ensure the Teams Meeting toggle is turned OFF before adding the Zoom meeting. 
4.	Add a Zoom meeting.
5.	Save the meeting.

On the room system, the host's name, meeting name, and meeting time are displayed. You can join the meeting by pressing Join without needing to enter a passcode separately.

o	Alternatively, start the meeting from your laptop or phone, and the room system will be automatically admitted.
•	If the Zoom Meeting does not have a waiting room enabled, you will automatically join.

Best Practices
Avoid Meeting Overlap
If your Outlook settings automatically add a Teams link to every meeting, but you also manually add a Zoom or Webex link, the Cisco system may experience issues with the multiple links.
•	The Hierarchy: If multiple links are present in a single calendar event, the Cisco system prioritizes them in the following order: Webex, Zoom, and then Teams.
•	Clean Invites: To ensure the room joins the correct platform, delete any unused meeting links or passcodes from the body of the calendar invite before sending.
Do not modify the meeting numbers and passcodes of meetings’ invites added via Teams, Webex, or Zoom add-ins. The Cisco devices read this information and pass it to the meeting. 
Room Conflicts
If you receive a "Declined" email from the room, it means the room is already booked. However, the Cisco controller may still show both meetings if they overlap. To avoid confusion for others, choose a different room or time if your request is declined.
Known Issues
Search Limits 
As of December 2025, when using the Cisco Webex webpage scheduling portal, note that MTR (Microsoft Teams Room) units are currently not visible in the "Invitees" search field. This is a known limitation currently being addressed by Cisco.

title: Best practices for secure Webex meetings
body:
Webex is an important tool for the Rutgers community to meet and collaborate in real time. While Webex provides a secure environment, it is also an open place to share information. This makes it extremely important to know the best practices of Webex security. Below are a few general rules to follow and six useful tips.
•	Do not share your Audio PIN or Host key with anyone.
•	Provide meeting passwords only to users who need them.
•	Never share sensitive information in your meeting until you know who is in attendance.
Use scheduled meetings instead of your personal room
Webex has two different modes – scheduled meetings and personal rooms. Scheduled meetings are designed for higher security, while personal rooms are aimed at ease of use. A scheduled meeting is like booking a conference room with a keycard entry for all attendees, whereas a personal room leaves your office open all the time, waiting for someone to show up to start the meeting. You should only use scheduled meetings for class meetings and other large gatherings. You should NOT use your personal room. For more information on scheduling a meeting, visit Scheduling a meeting with your personal account page. Please note there are other web conferencing tools available for class meetings and lectures in the university’s learning management systems. See the information on the Technology Resources for Remote Instruction webpage at the university-wide information technology guide.
Thoughtfully distribute your meeting invitation
Please ensure that all of the invitees are appropriate for the meeting and discourage invitees from forwarding the meeting invite.
Restrict access to the meeting
Lock the meeting once all attendees have joined the meeting. This practice prevents more attendees from joining. Hosts can lock or unlock the meeting at any time while the session progresses. To lock a meeting that you’re currently hosting, select Meeting > Lock Meeting.
For personal rooms, this option will allow anyone joining the meeting, including participants invited to the meeting, to enter the meeting lobby to await admission by the host and/or moderators of the meeting.
Participants cannot join most scheduled meetings even if they have been invited.
To unlock a meeting that you’re currently hosting, select Meeting > Unlock Meeting.
Validate identity of all users in a call
Accounting for every attendee by using a roll call is a secure practice. Ask users to turn on their video or state their names to confirm their identity.
Remove a participant from the meeting
Participants can be expelled at any time during a meeting. Select the participant's name whom you want to remove, then select Participant > Expel. If it is necessary to expel disruptive participants, it is best to lock the meeting as described above. Doing so will prevent expelled attendees from attempting to rejoin and cause further disruptions.
Share application, not screen
Use Share > Application > instead of Share > My Screen to share specific applications and prevent accidental exposure of sensitive information on your screen.
For more Webex security best practices, please visit Cisco Webex Best Practices for Secure Meetings: Hosts resource at the Cisco Webex Help Center.

title: How do Webex recordings work?
body:
Only the host or an alternate host can record a meeting. You cannot record if the recording option is not available.
If an alternate host records the meeting, the meeting host still receives and owns the recording after the meeting ends.
If you record on your computer in MP4 format, the panels, such as the Chat panel, and any files you share using Share File are not included in the recording. Recordings in the cloud are saved in MP4 format. Computer recordings are saved in MP4 format or Webex Recording Format (WRF).
After recording, you must log in to Webex and download the recording to view it. Otherwise, you can delete it and purge it from your account.
For more information, please consult our knowledge article on recording a Webex meeting. 
Please note that the cloud storage for recordings is 25GB.

title: Preventing uninvited guests from joining your Webex meeting
body:
Locking Webex Meetings
To prevent uninvited guests from joining your Webex meeting, lock it. 
1.	From the meeting window, select the ellipses (...).
2.	Select Lock Meeting.
3.	A small key should appear in the upper-right corner, indicating that the meeting is locked.
4.	When someone attempts to join, they will be placed in a holding state until you allow them into the room.
You can also expel uninvited participants at any time during the meeting:
1.	Select the name of the participant whom you want to remove
2.	Click Participant > Expel.
Preventing Guests from Joining Scheduled Meetings
As a meeting host, you can also require that attendees sign in to the Webex site before joining a scheduled meeting.
1.	Sign in to your Webex account.
2.	Go to Meetings > Schedule
3.	Enter the details of your meeting.
4.	Select Show advanced options > Scheduling Options > Unlocked meetings section, check Guests can't join the meeting. 
5.	Select Schedule or Start.

title: Providing IT support for Webex Meetings
body:
Individual Account Provisioning
Users can self-provision a Webex account via the Service Activation page. Users can also enable this service when activating their NetID for the first time. See the Personal Account Requirements section below for more information on creating individual accounts. 
Shared Account Provisioning
Shared accounts must be created by a Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator. All shared Webex accounts must be associated with a service account in Rutgers Connect. 
You can ask your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator to activate a shared Webex account for an existing service account or make you a new service account. 
Account Types and Features
Webex supports several account types. Most users will only utilize Host accounts.
You do not need an account to attend a Webex meeting and should not get a Webex account unless you intend to host meetings or manage a shared account.
Host Account – Webex Native
•	
o	
	A host account is a licensed account capable of hosting meetings.
	All host accounts must be licensed.
	Host accounts that have not hosted meetings recently enough will be deactivated to manage license costs.
	Faculty and Staff will be licensed in a manner that provides PSTN phone bridge capabilities.
	Students will be licensed in a manner that does not provide PSTN features. They will have VOIP capability only for audio participation.
Shared Account –RU specific configuration of a host account.
•	
o	
	Shared accounts are normal host accounts except those not mapped to an individual's NetID.
	Shared account meetings can be hosted by logging into the service account, or by someone designated as a co-host on a meeting. 
	As currently implemented, shared accounts will not support standing phone bridges for personal meeting rooms.
Personal Account Requirements
Users must hold an active faculty, staff, or student role to self-provision a person's Webex account. Guests must contact their Rutgers Connect Domain Administrator to have a Webex account activated. See the following page regarding creating a personal Webex account for information on creating a Webex account. 
Shared Account Requirements
A shared Webex account allows multiple users to access and manage the account. To access information on the shared Webex account, you need to be a delegated user for that account. Your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator can provision and manage access to your shared Webex account.

title: Recording a Webex meeting
body:
Currently, the storage space for recordings in the cloud is 25GB. You can record as many meetings or classes as needed within this capacity limit; however, all recordings have a 3-year retention before automatically deleting them.
1.	While in the meeting, select Record.
2.	If using a Windows device, a dialog box will appear and ask if you want to save the recording in the cloud on on your computer. 
o	If you choose to record on your computer, select Accept if prompted to agree to your organization’s privacy and security guidelines. Then choose a location to save the recording, and click Save.
o	NOTE: You can only record audio on your computer using the Call Using Computer option.
3.	While recording, you can press Record to do one of the following:
o	Select Pause and Resume to maintain a single recording, but to stop and resume the recording as necessary. 
o	Select Stop to end your current recording.
4.	If you recorded in the cloud, you receive an email with the recording link when the meeting or event ends. Depending on file size and bandwidth, it can take up to 24 hours to receive your recording.
5.	To view/access your recordings, log on to Webex and select Recordings on the left-hand side menu.
6.	After making a recording, you can disable the ability to download it by navigating to Webex > Recordings > My Recordings. Select the recording to edit, then press Edit Recording > check off Prevent downloading.

title: account audits
body:
Who can have a Webex account?
According to the Office of Information Technology guidelines, only the following classes of people are eligible to have Webex accounts:
•	Current employees of Rutgers University
•	Current students
•	Professor Emeritus
•	Guests: individuals who are conducting University business and are directly associated with the University but are not officially on the University's payroll. For example, visiting professors/scholars, members of auxiliary groups, and others working on University business or affiliated with the University.
The following groups of people are not automatically eligible to Webex accounts:
•	Former employees (including teaching/graduate assistants who may still be students but are not actively working for Rutgers)
•	Employees of other organizations who are performing work at Rutgers
•	Alumni
•	Retirees
Any of the above may be eligible for a guest account if a department or division of Rutgers is willing to sponsor them. Please see the Guest Account page for further information.
Recently re-hired employees who have not yet been added to the RIAS payroll system and thereby given a Faculty or Staff role may have their department's payroll person use the Early Employee NetID form to request an early role.
How can I keep my Webex account?
We determine which accounts should be closed by comparing Webex usernames with the active roles (e.g., Faculty, or Staff) of usernames listed in the University's Open Registry (OR) service, which is used as the basis for the Rutgers Online Directory. The OR may have some information that needs to be corrected.
If you have received an account closure notice, and believe this is in error ,please find the group you belong to in the appropriate subsection below (Current Employees, Guests, Students, Others) and follow the instructions there.
Current Employees
You may not be listed in the OR as a current employee. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. Contact your department’s Human Resources person if your name does not appear.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, contact your department's Human Resources person.
If your information is correct, or when your department's Human Resources person has corrected your record, your department’s Rutgers Delegated Administrator can verify that your account is no longer subject to closure.
Students
You may not be listed in the OR as a current student. To check this, go to the Search for People tool and search for your name. Review each result if you get more than one. If your name does not appear, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
When your entry appears, review the information there. If it is incorrect, please inquire about your registration via One Stop.
Guests
If you are affiliated with Rutgers but not actually employed full-time by Rutgers, you may request a guest account. Have a sponsor at the department you are working with go to the Guest Account site, and submit a request for you, which will be sent to our Accounts Office for processing.
Every year, you must renew your guest account. You will be notified when the time to renew your account arrives (30 days prior to the expiration of the account).
Your Rutgers Delegated Administrator can assist your sponsor with submitting a Guest Account request and creating your Webex account, if necessary.
Others
If you do not fit into any of the above categories, you may want to try contacting a department at Rutgers related to your work and ask if they would be willing to sponsor a Guest account for you.
We have no mechanism for people no longer associated with Rutgers to pay a fee and thus keep their accounts. These people should be able to pay for a full account on various video conference providers from various web services. Rutgers cannot recommend one such group over another.
What is the typical account audit timeline?
Once an account is found to be ineligible for Webex:
•	On day one, i.e., same day found to be ineligible: The account is sent an email notification.
•	On day seven, i.e., approximately one week later: The account is locked out of Webex.
•	On day thirty-five, i.e., approximately 5 weeks later: The account is deleted from Webex.
Note: If the account is found to be eligible for Webex at any time prior to deletion, the account will exit the audit.
What should I do before the account is closed?
If you will be losing your Webex account, you may want to take some of the following steps.
•	Contact the IT staff in your department to determine the correct protocol for the data (recordings, upcoming meetings) in your account. Departments that handle PHI or other sensitive data may have procedures put in place for security.
•	You will lose access to your Webex recordings once your account is deleted, so you want to save them to another location. Please contact your local IT staff to assist with this process.
What happens after the account is closed?
After your account is closed, you will lose access to your Webex account.
Approximately 4 weeks after your account is closed, your Webex account will be deleted.
When an account is deleted, you will no longer be able to access Webex service.s
For further assistance
If you have questions about any of the above, you can send e-mail to help@oit.rutgers.edu or contact the OIT Help Desk.

title: Calling
body:
Webex Calling replaces Jabber as the University's softphone system. It allows you to use the Webex app on your desktop or mobile device like your office phone. 
Requirements
You must have a Cisco desk phone to utilize Webex Calling since it will use your office phone number.
You will also need to have a Rutgers Webex account. You can confirm your account is active on the Service Activation page under the Webex section. 
To utilize Webex Calling on a mobile device, download the Webex app from the Intune Company Portal app, not from your phone's default app store. Using it on your desktop requires the installation of the Webex App. 
To set up for Webex Calling, submit a Voice Services Ticket and include the MAC address of your office phone. The MAC address can be found listed on the back of your phone. After Voice Services has enabled the feature on your account, you will be provided instructions on completing the setup in the Webex App. 
Additional Information
For more information, view Webex's article on the supporting calling options and instructions on how to call anyone with a phone number.

General Information
Rutgers University provides Webex Meeting access to all current faculty, staff, and students. This video conferencing solution allows you to communicate and collaborate with others using audio, video, chat, file sharing, whiteboard, and other tools. It can be used for:
•	Scheduled or “on the fly” meetings
•	Office hours
•	Hybrid and online courses
•	Group work
•	Study sessions
•	Support
•	And more
Webex is easy to use and can be used on any computer with an internet connection. It will install on your computer the first time that you use it. It’s also accessible through most smartphone and other mobile devices.
Video conferencing units can also be used with Webex Meetings but may not have access to all functionality (e.g. file sharing, polling). If you are in a room with video conferencing equipment, you may want one of the in-person attendees to log in using a laptop.
Before your meeting
•	Use Outlook to schedule meetings using the Webex meetings desktop app. This makes it easy to invite others, send updates and reminders, and stay organized.
•	Log in and test Webex Meetings before your session to ensure you have installed the software and it’s working as expected.
•	Close all programs, particularly those that might use audio/video before starting Webex. Email and chat alerts can be very distracting for both you and your attendees. Quitting other programs will ensure that Webex has full access to your audio and/or video.
•	Start your meeting early. Most meetings can’t start without you (the host) so make sure that you’re online ahead of time to allow attendees to enter and check audio and/or video before the meeting begins.
•	Wired connections are best. Although wireless access is available in many locations, the meeting quality may be worse.
•	Use a phone or wired headset if possible, as they will provide the best audio. Ensure you check for any potential audio errors on your device's settings.
Reduce distractions
If you have many attendees (participants), you may want to adjust your participant settings for the meeting. These can be changed throughout the meeting if needed.
•	Enable/Check: Mute on Entry
•	Disable/Uncheck: Entry and Exit Tone
•	Disable/Uncheck: Anyone Can Share
Error! Filename not specified.
Can you hear me now?
Webex will prompt you to select your audio options once you start your meeting. You can use your computer or video conferencing unit audio or a phone. If you’re using your computer, the default microphone and speakers will be selected. You can change your settings from the pop-up menu next to your Mute button or from the Audio button in the top menu bar.
Error! Filename not specified.
You can switch connections between your system audio and telephone by selecting Switch audio at the bottom of this same menu.
Error! Filename not specified.
If you’re using your computer audio, you may want to switch between a headset, webcam, speakers, and/or built-in microphone by first clicking Change Settings and then using the pull-down menus.
If you are in a room with a Telepresence system, you may want to use the Connect to a Video System option found underneath the Ellipses (...) menu.
 
Error! Filename not specified.
They still can’t hear me!
Look at the microphone button at the bottom of your Webex window. If there is a slash through the microphone and it reads Unmute, that means you’ve muted yourself. The microphone button is a toggle, so simply click it. Your audio will turn on, and the slash will be removed from the microphone.
Additionally, if the intended microphone isn't appearing - please check the device's settings to troubleshoot and configure any errors with the microphone's connection to the device.
Note: You can see which of your attendees are muted in the Participants list as indicated by the red microphone icon to the right of their names. The default position for the Participants panel is on the top right, but you may have moved it or hidden it (see below to restore it).
Error! Filename not specified.
I lost my: Participants, Chats, Video Control!
Sometimes, you collapse a panel to get more room on your screen, and then can’t figure out where it went. You can go to the View menu to Restore Layout, Show Panels, Show Participant Video, or Show or Hide Meeting Controls.
If that doesn’t help, check if it’s on a second monitor or behind another window if you were screen sharing.
Error! Filename not specified.
Sharing Content
Webex allows you to share content and annotate that content!
•	Screen Sharing is easy and gives you flexibility, especially if you need to switch between applications.
•	File Sharing is an excellent option for static content (e.g. an agenda or a copy of the presentation) and can be helpful because participants can save the files. Please note that recordings won’t contain files, and Telepresence, Video conferencing units, and non-Webex video conferencing applications cannot access shared files. Multiple files can be shared.
•	Application Sharing allows you to share a single application on your computers, such as PowerPoint or Excel, without sharing your entire desktop, so there’s less chance of accidentally displaying the content you may not want to share. Everything except the explicitly shared application will be grayed out for the participants when sharing an application. Placing another window over the shared application window results in the overlapped section being grayed out. If you’ve moved the shared application window to another screen, it will still be visible to the participants until you stop sharing.
•	Whiteboard Sharing Only works for the Webex software application and does not deliver a consistent experience across all platforms, so it is not recommended for use now.
You can select the type of content by going to the Share menu or clicking the Share button at the bottom of the screen.
Error! Filename not specified.
    
I can’t stop sharing!
At the top of your screen, you should see an orange tab, which will expand when you place your mouse over the area. The Stop Sharing button is on the right.
Note: There’s also a Pause sharing option in case you want to suspend sharing while arranging windows or opening files.
Error! Filename not specified.
Annotations
Annotations allow you to draw over any shared content. You’ll see an orange tab at the top of your screen when sharing content. When you place your mouse over the tab, it will expand to allow you access to the annotation tool. To get out of that mode, click the Annotate option again. All annotations will be cleared, so save them first if you want to save them.

title: Polling
body:
Webex Polls
Hosts or cohosts in meetings/webinars can create polls to use and share questionnaires.
To use polls in a meeting, turn polling on by going to Advanced Options > Scheduling Options > Meeting Options or Advanced Options > Scheduling Options > Webinar Options.
How to create polls
Select View > Panels > Manage Panels during your meeting, then select Polling > Add > OK.
From there, you can select the ellipsis and select Polling. Select the question type from the drop-down list in the Question section (Short Answer, Multiple Choice - Multiple Answer, Multiple Choice - Single Answer).  
Click New to create a new question - and fill in the appropriate questions and answer sections! From there, you select your poll and click Open Poll to present to your attendees.
To end the poll, click Close Poll and view Quick reference tasks to view options on how to save, share, and view poll results.
For further information, visit the Webex Support page for starting a poll in meetings or webinars.

title: Shared Account Basics
body:
What is a shared Webex account?
A shared Webex account allows multiple people to access and manage an account. These accounts are not associated with an individual's NetID; however, multiple delegates can be set up. Delegates can schedule, host, and record meetings using a shared account. Please note that shared accounts cannot attend a meeting as an attendee. 
How can I get a shared Webex account?
All shared Webex accounts must be associated with a service account in Rutgers Connect. 
You can ask your Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator to activate a shared Webex account for an existing service account or they can make you a new one with a shared Webex account attached. 
What does it mean to be a delegate on a shared Webex account?
If you are not a Rutgers Connect Delegated Administrator, you can still access the information for the shared Webex account by becoming a delegate. A delegate for a Webex account can host and schedule meetings for the shared account. You can schedule meetings by logging into the service account's Webex and scheduling a meeting as the account. 
How can I access recordings on a shared account?
Log into the shared Webex service account to act as the account and access the recordings. Please note that it may take up to 24 hours before new recordings are available from Webex.

title: Key tips to avoid Zoombombing and unwanted meeting guests
body:
Table of Contents
•	Before the Meeting 
o	Passcodes
o	CAPTCHA verification
o	Use a Waiting Room
o	Only allow Rutgers users to join
o	Do not share your Meeting link in public forums
o	Keep Zoom updated
o	Don’t select “Allow participants to join anytime”
o	Don’t use your personal Zoom meeting ID
•	During the Meeting 
o	Manage the meeting with Host Security Controls
o	Lock your session
o	Remove unwanted participants
o	Pause the meeting temporarily to remove a disruptive participant
o	Limit screen sharing
Are you using Zoom for large meetings or classroom instruction? If you are, be sure you’re taking proactive steps to ensure a safe environment for you and your students or other attendees.
Zoom has implemented several security enhancements to ensure safe meetings and prevent instances of Zoombombing — a term referring to intruders disrupting online meetings. Nevertheless, anyone running a meeting has a key role in ensuring the safety and security of their meetings.
Note that Zoom continues to enhance security. Visit the Zoom Privacy and Security webpage for the latest details, and also consider reading Zoom’s blog post on keeping uninvited guests from your Zoom meeting.
Follow these steps to ensure your meetings are secure:
Before the Meeting
Passcodes
Passcodes are automatically enabled and required for any newly scheduled meetings. They are unique to each scheduled meeting and are meant to be shared with your invited meeting participants, along with the meeting ID, so they can gain access. You should not share passcodes publicly by posting them on a public website or by sharing via social media. Zoom offers more guidance on the use of passcodes.
CAPTCHA verification
A brief check (such as selecting images or entering characters) is used to confirm that a participant is a real person. This applies only to a participant who does not join using their Rutgers credentials and whose behavior indicates a potential security risk, as detected by Zoom. This addresses attempts by hackers, bots, and automated tools to access, record, or share online meetings without permission. 
Use a Waiting Room
Enable the Waiting Room feature in your Zoom account. This virtual staging area prevents people from joining a meeting until the host is ready to begin. You can customize the settings to control which participants can join your meeting and when they can join. Learn more about the Waiting Room feature in Zoom.
Only allow Rutgers users to join
When you schedule a meeting through your Zoom account, you can check the Require authentication to join option in the meeting's Security section. If you check this box, only users with a Rutgers Zoom account will be able to join your meeting. Ensure that all participants have a Rutgers account prior to the event. Get more info on how to select this security feature.
Do not share your Meeting link in public forums
Don’t share meeting information on social media accounts, chat rooms, direct messaging platforms, or other public places. Only use an official, secure method of communication to share a meeting link with your invited guests. By publicly sharing your meeting links, you can expose it to intruders. Learn more about how to share your Zoom meetings and webinars securely.
Keep Zoom updated
Don’t assume Zoom will automatically update your desktop or mobile application. Always ensure you are using the latest version of Zoom, which includes security enhancements. Learn how to update Zoom.
Don’t select “Allow participants to join anytime”
In your meeting settings, under Options, ensure that Allow participants to join anytime is unchecked to prevent disruptive visitors from joining before you do.
Don’t use your personal Zoom meeting ID
Zoom’s default choice is to generate a unique Meeting ID when you schedule a meeting. Make sure to choose that setting. If you use your personal meeting room ID instead and share it with others, anyone who knows it can join your personal meeting by adding that ID to the meeting link. If a meeting ID is automatically generated each time, unwanted users won’t have access to it.
During the Meeting
Manage the meeting with Host Security Controls
The host or co-host can quickly enable or disable certain settings from the meeting controls toolbar to secure the meeting and minimize disruption, including locking the meeting, enabling waiting room, and suspending participant activities. To access them, in the meeting controls toolbar, click Host tools. Learn more about how to enable or disable all the available in-meeting security controls.
Lock your session
Sometimes you’ll want to lock your meeting after it’s gotten underway to prevent unexpected visitors. When you do this, participants won’t be able to join, even if they have the password. To lock your meeting while it's in progress, click Security at the bottom of your Zoom window. In the pop-up, click Lock Meeting.
Remove unwanted participants
Hosts are given the ability to remove participants once a meeting is underway. Zoom advises: “From that Participants menu, you can mouse over a participant’s name, and several options will appear, including Remove. Click that to kick someone out of the meeting.” Learn more about managing participants.
Pause the meeting temporarily to remove a disruptive participant
Hosts and co-hosts can temporarily pause their meetings and remove a disruptive participant. Under the Security icon on your Zoom meeting screen, you can click “Suspend Participant Activities.” By doing this, all video, audio, in-meeting chat, annotation, screen sharing, and recording during that time will stop, and Breakout Rooms will end.
Limit screen sharing
Prevent other participants from sharing their screens without individual authorization. Turning this feature off will eliminate unwanted distractions, as the meeting host controls what’s shared. To limit screen sharing, click the ^ arrow next to Share Screen while in the meeting, click Advanced Sharing Options, then under Who can share? choose Host Only. Get more info on these features and others for managing participants.

title: Sharing your Zoom meeting or webinar securely
body:
To avoid unwanted guests, it is essential to share your meeting information securely. It's recommended that you configure your meeting or webinar with the settings options below to minimize disruptions.
To help ensure security and prevent unwanted guests from attending your meetings or webinars, it is recommended that you avoid sharing meeting links (which contain your passcodes) on social media, websites, or other public forums. By sharing your meeting links publicly, you are increasing the risk of Zoombombing.
Meetings
1.	To begin, navigate to Rutgers Zoom and select Sign in.
2.	Then sign in with your NetID and password, and select the blue Schedule a meeting link on the right side of the screen.
3.	When scheduling the meeting here, select the box labeled Required next to Registration.

      Error! Filename not specified.
o	If you want to edit an existing meeting, after logging in to Rutgers Zoom, you can select Meetings on the left side of your screen and then Edit to access these settings.

      Error! Filename not specified.
4.	Once you save the meeting, you will see a panel at the bottom of the page that displays settings, with the first tab labeled Registration.

     Error! Filename not specified.
5.	There are two options available for you to select from by choosing Edit, depending on your preferred level of security. 
o	Automatically Approved (Not Recommended) means that anyone can register using the registration link, and their registration will be automatically approved. At this point, they will receive the actual link to join the meeting. This can be helpful in that only users who take the time to register and fill out the requested information can obtain the join link. However, as registration is not restricted, it could still allow malicious individuals to access the meeting link.
o	Manually Approve means that the meeting host will need to manually approve each person who registers before they are provided with the link to join the meeting. This requires more energy on the part of the host, as they will need to review each applicant. However, it is the most secure option as all users will be vetted by the host.
o	You can view additional information about protecting your meetings on Zoom's best practices webpage.

     Error! Filename not specified.
o	With either of these settings, instead of the join link, you will now see a registration link that you can copy and share to promote your meeting. This link only goes to the registration page for your event and as such is safer to share than the actual meeting link that allows someone to join.
Webinars (Recommended for public-facing events)
Webinars can be set up with the same configuration as described above, with the option to enable and edit registration settings in the same locations. Learn more about Zoom Webinars.
By default, Zoom webinars have all attendees muted unless they are added as panelists for the webinar.
You can enable registration for your Webinar to enhance its security. To help ensure the webinar is not shared or redistributed, you can add a custom question to the registration page that all attendees must accept.
