title: Help Desk - Application Support IT Application Support - After Hours - Environment Power Outage Checklist
body:
Environment - Power Outage Checklist for After Hours
Please read thoroughly and ask/call a supervisor at any time if you have any questions on what to do.
•	This form must be submitted to a manager after the outage is resolved via print out or email. Whichever is quicker at the time.
•	This form can be printed using the printer in the old apps office. The computers in the NOC have access to the Color LaserJet Pro MFP M281fdw.
•	All calls and texts should be made from the AH iPhone, unless there is an issue reported with the phone.
There are three scenarios that may happen with a power outage. Your first indication of an outage is that the lights will flicker. This could lead to the following scenarios: 
1.	Generator turns on: The UPS (uninterruptible power supply) carries the data center load to give time for the generator to turn on. Once the generator turns on you will receive an automated email from omx@omnimetrix.net that the generator is running. The majority of the building is now powered by the generator, though wall outlets in offices and some lights will be not work when on generator power, for example the bathrooms by the old apps office.
2.	Generator does NOT turn on: The UPS switches to battery power, but the generator does not turn on. We will not get an email from omx@omnimetrix.net, but we will get emails "On Battery" from the UPS, and a variety of alerts from the data center monitoring software. 
1.	The UPS batteries will carry the data center load for ~20 minutes and the UPS will send email indicating how much battery life remains. Once the batteries are exhausted everything will go dark because we will have lost all power. It's important to know that the data center air conditioners will only run under generator power, so the room will begin to get very hot. Also, the hallway lights and elevators will not function.
3.	Glitch: The lights flicker, but the generator does not turn on. We do not get an email from omx@omnimetrix.net and we do not lose power after 1 minute. This means there was only a glitch and we have returned to normal power. You can also check if all the lights are on in the basement of Hill Center. 
Each scenario has its own steps to complete. Contact information is at the end of this document.
Scenario 1: Generator turns on 
The UPS (uninterruptible power supply) turns on to give time for the generator to turn on. Once the generator turns on you will receive an automated email from omx@omnimetrix.net that the generator is running. 
1.	The top priority is to start contacting people in the following order and let them know of the current situation: 
1.	RUPD: Inform them of your name and department and that the Hill Center data center is now running on generator power. Inquire of a cause and an ETA on power restoration. 
1.	Notes:_________________________________________________________________________________________
2.	Email ei_dcts@email.rutgers.edu and cc operator@oit.rutgers.edu and noc@rutgers.edu to report the outage. Include any information you received from RUPD. 
1.	Notes:_________________________________________________________________________________________
3.	Call Caryn. If Caryn is not available, start calling the following people in this order until you reach someone: Tina, Ana, Liz, then the HD Managers on-call list. 
1.	Names of who you called: ______________________________________________________________________
2.	Names of who you spoke to: ___________________________________________________________________
3.	Any instructions given: _________________________________________________________________________
4.	Post to the following Slack channels of the outage and any details you have gathered: 
1.	esd_outage_degradation
2.	esd_nb_hd_apps_dc_coord
3.	esd_nb_hd_apps_td_coord
4.	esd_nb_hd_afterhours
5.	Call John Wieczorek, John Lyons, Dave Salvaryn, and the NOC On-Call list. 
1.	Names of who you called: _______________________________________________________________________
2.	Names of who you spoke to: ____________________________________________________________________
3.	Names of who would like to be called back with updates: ___________________________________________
4.	Names of who would like to be called back when power is restored: _________________________________
6.	Create an incident in ServiceNow.
7.	Update the visual task board with the outage. The data center's temperature will increase.
8.	The wall outlets in the center will power fans, the doors should be open, and the fans deployed to exhaust hot air from the data center.
2.	If power is restored at this point (within 30 minutes) skip to step 4. You will know power is restored when you receive an email from omx@omnimetrix.net that the generator is off.
3.	If power is NOT restored within 30 minutes, continuing contacting people in the following order: 
1.	Call RUPD to follow-up. 
1.	Notes: _________________________________________________________________________________________
2.	Call whoever stated they would like updates to inform them that the generator has been running for 30+ minutes.
2.	Send a follow-up email to ei_dcts@email.rutgers.edu and cc operator@oit.rutgers.edu and hd_mgr@oit.rutgers.edu with current status.
3.	Update previously mentioned Slack channels with current status.
4.	Update the visual task board with current status.
4.	If power is restored within your shift note the time (meaning you received an email that the generator is off from omx@omnimetrix.net):_________ 
1.	Call back whoever stated they would like to know when power is restored.
2.	Send email to noc@rutgers.edu, ei_dcts@email.rutgers.edu, and cc operator@oit.rutgers.edu and hd_mgr@oit.rutgers.edu with a summary of the timeline of events and who was contacted.
3.	Escalate any issues still on Grafana 10 minutes after the outage is over which have not already been reported.
5.	If power is not restored within your shift: 
1.	Be sure to communicate everything that was done and still must be done with your relief.
2.	If no one is coming to relieve you, update the previous Slack channels so that everyone is aware.
Scenario 2: Hill Center loses all power 
The UPS turns on, but the generator does not turn on. We will not get an email from omx@omnimetrix.net and after 20 minutes Hill Center will go dark. 
1.	This is the most critical form of power emergency. Call RUPD to inquire about the power outage and notify them of the loss of power in the data center as an FYI. 
1.	Notes:_________________________________________________________________________________________________
2.	Call Caryn. If Caryn cannot be reached, follow instructions in step 1.3 from Section1.
1.	Notes:_________________________________________________________________________________________________
3.	Call John Wieczorek, John Lyons, Dave Salvaryn, and the NOC On-Call list. 
1.	Notes:_________________________________________________________________________________________________
Scenario 3: It was only a glitch 
The lights flicker, but the generator does not turn on. We do not get an email from omx@omnimetrix.net and we do not lose power after 1 minute. 
1.	Send an email to operator@oit.rugers.edu ei_dcts@email.rutgers.edu and noc@rutgers.edu to inform the recipients of the glitch.
2.	Check Grafana to follow up on any issues.

title: Help Desk - Application Support ScarletMail Programmable Search Engine Request
body:
In the Slack channel #scarlet-support-staff, or your SCTASKs, you may see a RITM from ScarletMail Support requesting that the Help Desk confirm specific information regarding a ScarletMail Programmable Search Engine request.
Google Programmable Search Engine (PSE), formerly known as Google Custom Search Engine (CSE), lets web developers add a customizable search box to their web pages. The search uses the base Google search engine; however, it can be customized, for example, to only search specific sites. This product is popular for compliance with Rutgers website policy 80.1.7 "Search Function" requirements. A ScarletMail PSE, which may be requested via this form, offers benefits such as OIT-administered ownership that survives unit-level personnel changes and excludes advertising.
To handle the request:
1.	When you open the RITM, scroll down to the SCTASKs and open the one assigned to OIT-HD - ScarletMail Support Staff.
2.	Assign the task to yourself. If you cannot assign the task to yourself, please inform a manager.
3.	The SCTASK will ask you to confirm the following information: 
o	Confirm the status/authority of the listed DDDC. DDDC refers to the Requestor Dean/Director/Chair. Job titles can be checked in CAT or IDCheck.
o	Verify University business affiliation. Is the requester a Rutgers University department member?
o	Verify 18+ status (whether through self-affirmation and/or IdM records). Verify that the requester is 18 or older.
4.	Once all this information is confirmed, state this in a work note and change the state of the SCTASK to "Closed Complete".
5.	If this request came through Slack or email, respond when the task is set as Closed Complete.
See RITM0064214 as an example of the request and process.
Link to the original request form.

title: - Handling Generic Requests
body:
One of the General Request forms on the self-service portal creates a Request Item (RITM) and a corresponding Service Catalog Task (SCTASK), instead of an Incident. As part of your shift, please also check the filter below and follow the procedure on how to handle them.
Review the Filter for Service Catalog Tasks.
1.	Open the SCTASK and review the request.
2.	If the request can be reassigned to another group, change the Assignment Group and click Save. No further action is needed.
o	Not all Assignment Groups that are available in an Incident will also be available in a Task, if the group does not appear, move to the next step.
3.	If the request is something the HD handles or the Assignment Group is not available in the Catalog Task, create a new Incident for the user.
4.	Copy over all pertinent information. (Including SCTASK and RITM numbers into the Incident Work Notes).
5.	There may also be attachments associated with the SCTASK located on the Requested Item Attachments tab on the bottom. Please make sure to add these to the incident.
6.	On the SCTASK:
1.	Add the Incident number as a Work Note.
2.	Assign it to yourself.
3.	Set the Assignment Group to: NB-HD - Level 1.
4.	Select the appropriate Configuration Item if applicable.
5.	Save and then mark it as Closed Complete.
	SCTASKs are linked under their corresponding RITM. Closing a SCTASK will also automatically close the RITM. 
7.	Finish helping the user as normal through the Incident.

title: - Knowledge Management Policies and Procedures
body:
Table of Contents • Knowledge Article Basics o Article States o Article Links o Can Read (User Criteria Groups) o Anchor Links o Images o General Article Tips o Fixing Formatting Issues o Formatting FAQs • Accessibility Standards o Text Alternative for Images/Media o Headings o Numbered or Bulleted Lists o Hyperlinks o Tables o Accessibility Checker tool • Creating Knowledge Articles o Public Knowledge o Internal articles (HDIs) o Knowledge Blocks • Editing Knowledge Articles o Checkout o Editing o Publishing o View Article o Recalling o Approving • Revert back to a previous version of a KA • Archiving Articles • Retiring Articles • Knowledge Feedback Tasks (KFTs) • Reviewing Expiring Knowledge Articles o Service Owner Review of Expiring Articles o KM Process to Review Expiring Articles • Article Expiration Calendar o Breakdown o Calendar Knowledge Article Basics Article States Articles are categorized in one of the following States in the Workflow field. Draft Indicates it is in edit mode and the settings/article body can be changed. This occurs when you first create a new article or when you Checkout an existing article to make changes to it. The version number of the article will show with a decimal after it to indicate it is not published (ex: Version 0.01 for a new article) Review When a Draft is ready, clicking Publish puts the article in the Review state. The appropriate owners of the Knowledge Base the article is in would then need to approve it before it is visible to users. Scheduled for Publish For articles that have been approved after being reviewed but have a Scheduled Publish Date set for the article that has not passed yet. Published The article is visible to users based on it’s Can read and Cannot read settings. Published articles have version numbers that are whole digits (ex: 1.0). Pending Retirement An article was selected for retirement by clicking Retire. It is still visible and not actually retired until the appropriate owners of the Knowledge Base it is in, approves the retirement. Retired The retirement for the article was approved and it is no longer visible to users. Outdated Means that a newer version of this article is available. You can check the version number of the article to see which it is. (ex: viewing version 1.0 of an article will show workflow as Outdated, when there is an updated published version 2.0) How to view States • The Workflow column is visible in the back end view. Hovering over the icon displays which stage it is in. If you do not see this column you have to click on the gear icon on the top left of the list, and then add it to your Selected visible columns. Error! Filename not specified. • When viewing the article, the state is shown in the Workflow field. Error! Filename not specified. Article Links There are 4 different links that can take you to various versions of an article. Front End Permalink • This is the link that should always be used whenever referencing an article to a user. • It is the link on the self service Portal that takes the user to the most updated version of the article. • Navigate to the article on the Portal and click Copy Permalink located at the top or bottom of the article. • Example: https://ithelp.rutgers.edu/sp?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0012508 Front End sys_id link • When used, will take the user to this specific version of the article. If used it will not bring them to the most current version of the article if it has since been updated, which is why this one should not typically be used. • When viewing an article in the Portal, this is the link in the URL bar on the browser. • Example: https://ithelp.rutgers.edu/sp?id=kb_article_view&sys_kb_id=08138ef71bbe4110743c54a51a4bcbf0 Back End Permalink • It is the link in the back end of ServiceNow that takes the user to the most updated version of the article. This link can be used for internal documentation only for IT users with access to the backend of ServiceNow. • Navigate to the article in the back end and click the Copy Permalink button located at the bottom of the article. • Example: https://rutgers.service-now.com/kb_view.do?sysparm_article=KB0012508 Back End sys_id link • It is the link in the back end of ServiceNow that takes the user to a specific version of the article. This should not typically be used. • Navigate to the article in the back end, this is the link in the URL bar on the browser. • Example: https://rutgers.service-now.com/kb_knowledge.do?sys_id=08138ef71bbe4110743c54a51a4bcbf0&sysparm_referring_url=kb_view.do Permalinks will always have a URL that ends in the KB number. Can Read (User Criteria Groups) These are the groups used in the Can Read field to control who has access to the article. These groups are auto populated by the Assignment Groups (commonly used in Incidents) that are connected under the User Criteria Group. When adding one of these in the Can Read field on an article, you can select it to highlight it, then click the small information (i) icon to see what sources it pulls from to populate the membership for the group. Common groups for public knowledge articles: • Blank: If the Can Read is left blank, the article is visible to anyone inside and outside the University. • Any User: Visible to anyone with a NetID, only after they log into the self service Portal. This only works with PermaLinks and not when searching for an article, therefore it should not be used. The workaround for this is to set the Cannot Read field to Unauthenticated Users. • Rutgers IT Professionals: Any one with an ITIL role at the University. • Rutgers OIT Staff: Those with a Staff role in OIT. • Faculty: Any one with a Faculty Role. • Staff: Any one with a Staff Role. • Student: Any one with a Student role. Common groups for internal HDI articles: • NB Help Desk (NB, F/S, LMS): Any staff at the New Brunswick Student, Fac/Staff, and LMS help desks. • NB-HD User Criteria Group: Any staff assigned to the Student help desk as a CIT or higher. • NB-HD - Level 1 User Criteria Group: Any staff at the Student help desk as a Level 1 or higher. • NB-HD - Level 2 User Criteria Group: Any staff at the Student help desk as a Level 2 or higher. • NB-HD - Level 3 User Criteria Group: Any staff at the Student help desk as a Level 3 or higher. • NB-HD - Level 2: Any staff at the Student help desk as a Level 2 or higher. • NB-HD - FT User Criteria Group: Any Full Time staff at the Student help desk. • ESD - NB HD Full Time Staff: Any Full Time staff at Student, Fac/Staff and LMS help desk. • NB-HD - Application Support & FT staff: Any Application Support or Full Time staff at the Student help desk. • NB-Labs - Busch: Any labs consultants at Busch and NB-Labs - Managers. • NB-Labs - College Ave: Any labs consultants at College Ave and NB-Labs - Managers. • NB-Labs - Cook/Douglass: Any labs consultants at C/D and NB-Labs - Managers. • NB-Labs - Livingston: Any labs consultants at Livingston and NB-Labs - Managers. • OIT Lab Employees: All Staff and Student Worker roles in org codes for: OIT-Camden Computing Services, OIT-Newark Computing Services, OIT-NB Computing Services • CMD Help Desk Staff: Camden Help Desk Full Time only. • CMD Student Workers: Camden Help Desk Student Consultants. • RUN - IT Staff: Active Staff or Student Worker roles in departments: OIT-Newark Computing Services, OIT-Enterprise IT Client Services Note for internal articles: Only 1 group should be selected for the Can Read field. Higher groups inherit the permissions from lower groups. Example: you only need to set the Can Read to NB-HD - Level 2 User Criteria Group for all Level 2s, Level 3s, and FT to view the article. Anchor Links These are bookmarks/direct links to a specific point in an article, which can be particularly useful if the article is long or has multiple sections you want to create a customized table of contents for at the top (there is a built in table of contents feature described below). To make an anchor link is a two step process. Making an anchor link Using the built in function 1. Click the spot in the text of the article you want to place the anchor point. 2. Click the Anchor button on the text editor toolbar which looks like a bookmark button. 3. Enter a short yet descriptive name for the anchor link, and do not include spaces. 4. Click OK and you should see the anchor icon appear in the article body. Manually 1. Click the spot in the text of the article you want to place the anchor point. 2. Click the Source Code button on the text editor toolbar which looks like <>. 3. Copy and paste the text below, replacing ANCHORNAME with a short yet descriptive text term for your anchor: Using an anchor link From a specific URL Take the PermaLink for the article then add #ANCHORNAME at the end to create a URL link to take users directly to where you put in the anchor on the article. Replacing ANCHORNAME with the text term you used when creating the anchor. From within the article 1. If creating a table of contents for example, highlight the text you want users to click to take them to the anchor point. 2. Click the Insert/Modify Link button just as you would for creating an external link in the article. 3. In the URL field type #ANCHORNAME while replacing ANCHORNAME with the text term you used when creating the anchor. Table of Contents To easily create a table of contents you can use the built in button on the toolbar. Clicking it will automatically add it to the top of the article, utilizing all text formatted as Heading 1, 2 or 3 to create the clickable links in the table. Note that any text formatted as Heading 4 or lower will not be incorporated automatically into the table, you may manually insert it using an anchor link if desired. If any Headings are changed/deleted/added, you can click on the table itself and a refresh button will appear. Clicking on that will update the table to what the current Headings now are. Images To ensure consistent image formatting follow these guidelines. • Avoid copy/pasting images into articles. Depending on your browser's capabilities, device type, form view, and other factors, copy/pasting images into an article or form does not always work as expected. It can also not display the image properly on the Portal for users who are not logged in. The recommended way to get an image into your article is to use the Edit Image button on the article editor. Review ServiceNow’s guide on inserting images. • Screenshots/images should be indented over so they are not inline with text, therefore making it easier to scroll through the text. They should also have a blank line both above and under the image to provide a spacing buffer from any text in the article. • All images should have Alt Text. • Resize images, by dragging the corner of it, so the text in the image is roughly the same size or slightly bigger than the text of the article while viewing it in the html editor. • When inserting an image in a numbered or bullet sequence, press Shift+Enter to add a soft line break. This will tab down to the next line so the image can be inserted under the text, but does not continue the sequenced list for this line. After the image you can hit Enter to tab down to the next line and continue the numbered sequence. Image standards • 840px maximum width for it to be visible on the Portal. • .jpg, .gif, or .png format only. • Use file naming conventions that are logical and easy to remember. Include relevant keywords that are easy to search for, and have them numbered for a series of images of steps. • Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores in file names. Other characters (like question marks and ampersands) may upload incorrectly or cause unexpected behavior. How to Insert an Image 1. Within the Article Body, click the space where the image should appear. 2. On the text editor toolbar, click the Insert/Edit Image icon. The Insert/Modify Image pop-up displays. 3. Make sure the Type is set to Attachment. 4. Click the paperclip icon to browse for a new image (if no attachments are uploaded) or choose the image file name from the dropdown (when an article already has the image file uploaded). 5. Enter alternative text for the image in the Alt Text field. o Note: Alternative text (alt text) makes an image accessible to users who cannot see the image. Use Alt text for all images inserted into a KB article. Alt text should replicate in words what the image is communicating. 6. Click Save to close the window. 7. Ensure there is a blank line both above and below the image to provide a buffer from any surrounding text. Ensure it is indented over so it is not in line with the text above it. How to Edit an Image 1. Within the Article Body, click on the image to highlight it. 2. On the text editor toolbar, click the Insert/edit icon. The Insert/Modify Image pop-up displays. 3. Enter alternative text for the image in the Alt Text field if one is not present. o Note: Alternative text (alt text) makes an image accessible to users who cannot see the image. Use Alt text for all images inserted into a KB article. Alt text should replicate in words what the image is communicating. 4. Click Save to close the window. 5. Ensure there is a blank line both above and below the image to provide a buffer from any surrounding text. Ensure it is indented over so it is not in line with the text above it. General Article Tips • Review and follow the ITSM style guide as closely as possible! • Minimize references to specific individuals whenever possible to decrease the need to update the article more often as positions change and shift. • Avoid overusing acronyms. Acceptable on second and subsequent references; place the acronym in parentheses on the first reference. For example: “The Office of Information Technology (OIT) recently upgraded the service.” • Be attentive to language that has a specific meaning for IT people and an entirely different meaning for non-IT people, such as user, audit, client, domain, machine, package, tenant, and many others. Additionally, many technical terms, such as endpoints, SSID, and others, are not familiar to a non-technical audience; use other terms or define the terms you’re using, when applicable. • Be detailed / step-by-step instructions. • Avoid using gender specific pronouns (he/she) and instead use (they/them/you). • Reference and link to Vendor/Service documentation whenever possible to take the burden of keeping information up to date off of us. No need to duplicate the same information. • The editor can be a little weird and do strange things sometimes. When copying and pasting content into the HTML editor, press Ctrl+Shift+V to paste without any formatting. You can always click the Source Code button to see what the text and formatting is doing if it’s acting up at a particular spot in an article. Fixing Formatting Issues If when viewing an article any of the formatting looks off, such as a different font type, font size, or spacing issues this is typically caused by bad HTML code. More often than not it is from content that has been copied and pasted into an article without having the source formatting removed. Even if you highlight the text and manually change the font type and size to what it should be, it may still appear wrong if there is additional font styling in the code. You can see this by clicking the Source Code button ( <> ) in the KA editor toolbar and look for the word “style” in blue text as shown below. These inline style codes will override any other formatting for the specific text lines they are on. Example of bad inline style code: You can manually remove the entire style code, by deleting the word style and all the text formatting that appears in the reddish brown color, and leaving only the green code. For long articles with a lot of customized inline style codes, this can be time-consuming. To easily wipe out all style codes for an entire do the following, but note that this may cause issues if images have been pasted into an article and not inserted as an attachment. If a list is also formatted as lower-alphabetical, Roman numerals, discs, or dashes, it will remove that specific style formatting, which will need to be adjusted back after the cleaned-up code is back in ServiceNow. 1. Open the source code for the article giving you issues. 2. Press Ctrl + A to select all of the code. 3. Press Ctrl + C to copy all the code. 4. Go to this HTML Code Cleaner. 5. Paste the entire code in the empty box on the right side of the screen, the left side will show a preview of what the text currently looks like. 6. Click Clean HTML and this will remove all the inline style coding. 7. Click Ctrl + A to select all the freshly cleaned code from the right side, and then Ctrl + C to copy it. 8. Go back to the source code of the KA. 9. Delete all existing code. 10. Press Ctrl + V to paste in all the cleaned up code you copied from the website. 11. Click OK and confirm that everything looks correct and all the previous images are still there. Alternatively you can use the editor’s built in feature to clear some, but not all, formatting. 1. Highlight the text in the editor that you want to remove formatting from, or press Ctrl + A to select all the text. 2. Press the Clear formatting button on the toolbar, which looks like:Error! Filename not specified. 3. This should remove any style coding from the highlighted text. Viewing the article in the editor may not show all the formatting that may be hidden in the source code. This is why you should always view the article normally in the back end (by clicking View Article) or on the Portal, to see how it would truly appear. Especially before approving it to be published. Formatting FAQs Follow these general guidelines when handling a page that is entirely or partially a question and answer format (FAQs). For articles have more than 5 questions/answers: • Format the questions as the appropriate level of Heading (2,3,4,etc..) with no other alterations to the text. • Format the answers as regular paragraph text but indented over. • Utilize the built in Table of Contents feature and place it at the beginning of the questions, ensuring that only the questions are show in the table and any other headings are removed. For articles with less than 5 questions/answers: • Format the question as regular paragraph text, but bold it. • Format the answers as regular paragraph text but indented over. Accessibility Standards In order to adhere to Rutgers Digital Accessibility policies, all documentation should be in compliance with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. In particular, the items below should be adhered to for all knowledge articles. Text Alternative for Images/Media All images/media should have an alternative text associated with them so that screen readers can describe the context of the media. The objective of this is to create a text alternative that serves the same purpose and presents the same information as the original non-text content. General guidelines to follow for Alt Text: • You do not need to mention that it is a picture or screenshot of something, as that is implied. • The Alt Text should adequately describe what is seen in the image, assuming no other context for the picture exists. • If a particular button or icon is highlighted or pointed to, that should be mentioned in the Alt Text. • If the image shows a series of steps, you do not need to mention the specific step numbers shown in the image since they will be in the numbered list of the knowledge article. • Similarly, the Alt Text should not say that it is "How to" do something, as that will be mentioned in the text of the knowledge article. • Longer is not always better. Describing everything in extreme detail does not equate to good Alt Text. Examples • A picture shows the login page for Rutgers Connect. Alt Text is "Login page for Rutgers Connect prompting for an email address" • A picture shows how a knot is tied including arrows showing how the ropes go to make the knot. The text alternative describes how to tie the knot, not what the picture looks like. • A picture shows what a toy looks like from the front. The text alternative describes a front view of the toy. How to add/edit Alt Text For images already in an article: 1. Click on the image to highlight it. 2. On the toolbar, click the Insert/edit image icon. 3. In the Alt text field provide a short yet descriptive text alternative. 4. Click Save. Headings In order for screen readers to appropriately describe the text on the screen to users, headings should be formatted as such. This helps users “skim" the headings to locate the specific content they need, and is especially helpful when browsers or assistive technology allow navigation from heading to heading. These heading should be short yet descriptive ways to break up long articles into smaller sections. All headings should be set to use Heading 2 by default. Any further separation in each section should use Heading 3 then Heading 4 etc… but should always be in increasing sequential order. Example: An HTML page that describes the range of tasks for disaster preparation may have the following headings:

Disaster preparation

Flood preparation

Fire preparation

Note that the level 3 headings have the distinguishing information at the beginning (ie, instead of "Preparation for floods", "Preparation for fires", etc). Text should never be colored anything other than the default black. Colored text to denote importance does not adhere to the accessibility standards. Numbered or Bulleted Lists In order for screen readers to properly go through a series of steps or list of items it has to be formatted appropriately. A numbered or bulleted list should always be created using one of the list buttons in the editor toolbar. Simply typing numbers with parentheses or periods, such as "1), 2), 3)," or an asterisk in front of each item on a new line or paragraph will NOT create a numbered or bulleted list that is accessible by a screen reader. A good guide to follow can be found on Microsoft’s website on the proper procedure for lists. Inserting images into lists When inserting an image in a numbered or bullet sequence, press Shift+Enter to add a soft line break. This will tab down to the next line so the image can be inserted under the text, but does not continue the sequenced list for this line. After the image you can hit Enter to tab down to the next line and continue the numbered sequence. See the Images section of this article for more information on adding images. Hyperlinks Hyperlinks connect a hypertext file or document to another location or file. Linked information is typically presented in the form of text, websites, files, or video content. Embed a link within a concise string of text instead of using its URL as the link text. A screen reader user will more easily understand where an accessible link leads and will not have to listen while the reader pronounces every single character of a URL. Example: • Accessible: OIT Help Desk • Not accessible: https://it.rutgers.edu/help-support/ Descriptive hyperlinks will more clearly explain what information they link to. Example: • Descriptive: Benefits of Accessible Hyperlinks • Not descriptive: Benefits Use the full email address as the link text rather than embedding it in other link text. Example: • Accessible: help@oit.rutgers.edu • Not accessible: OIT Help Desk Support *This example does not convey that it is an email address. Other Tips: • Choose hyperlink text that clearly identifies the content of the resource being linked to. • Hyperlink text should not consist of the URL unless it is likely to be printed; e.g., Word document. • If a hyperlink downloads a file, be sure to mention that. o Example: Campus Map (PDF, 5.62 MB) • Hyperlinks may fail to open when clicking on them in the backend of ServiceNow, as it tries to open the link within the ServiceNow window itself. If this...

title: - Connect - PowerShell Cmdlets
body:
To connect to PowerShell, follow the documentation provided by Connect Support. This page also contains the full list of available cmdlets which can be used, with some contained below for reference which can be used on our internal groups to adjust permissions as indicated by ACE.
Group Commands
Get-DistributionGroupMember -identity <GroupName> gives all members of a distribution group.
Add-DistributionGroupMember -identity <GroupName> -member <Member> adds the member to the group.
Remove-DistributionGroupMember -identity <GroupName> -member <Member> removes the member from the group.
Get-UnifiedGroupLinks -identity <GroupName> gives all members of a unified group.
Add-UnifiedGroupLinks -identity <GroupName> -Link Type <Owner/Member> -Links <Member,Member> adds the member(s) to the group.
Remove-UnifiedGroupLinks -identity <GroupName> -Link Type <Owner/Member> -Links <Member,Member> removes the member(s) to the group.
SendAS
Get-RecipientPermission -identity <Group> -AccessRights SendAS lists all with sendas permissions on a desired group.
Add-RecipientPermission -identity <Group> -AccessRights SendAS -Trustee <Member> adds sendas permissions for the desired member on a group.
Remove-RecipientPermission -identity <Group> -AccessRights SendAS -Trustee <Member> removes sendas permissions for the desired member on a group.

title: - IDM - Shibboleth Services and Required Attributes
body:
Shibboleth is an open software system implemented based on a federated identity solution, which shares people s electronic identities and attributes securely among multiple organizations and applications. Service Providers that are typically hosted externally are not required to handle Single Sign On (SSO); instead, this is delegated to the Shibboleth Identity Provider which interacts with the authentication services and retrieves the necessary attributes, passing them electronically to the service providers. More information can be found on KB0017446.

title: - Notifying Phished Users
body:
Connect Support may email requesting that we contact a list of users who may have had their passwords compromised by a phishing link. These emails will be sent to hd_ft@oit and help@oit. To handle these emails:
1. Ensure a sample message is provided and formatted.
2. If the list is greater than 500 addresses follow the procedure below (if not it can be sent directly through Connect, skip to step 3) 
o Take the list of emails and add them to the do_not_reply Mailman list. 
1. To populate the list, log in, then go to Membership Management and ensure no one is currently subscribed.
2. Go to Mass Subscription and paste the list (ensure one address per line) and ensure the following settings are set as follows: 
* Subscribe these users now or invite them? Subscribe
* Send welcome messages to new subscribers? No
* Send notifications of new subscriptions to the list owner? No
3. Create an email with the settings as indicated below, depending on the method of notification: 
o Mailman 
* From: help@oit
* To: do_not_reply@email.rutgers.edu
* Cc: help@oit
* Subject (if not provided): Notice Regarding Phishing Scam <TODAY'S DATE>
o Connect 
* From: help@oit
* To: -
* Bcc: addresses of affected users
* Subject (if not provided): Notice Regarding Phishing Scam <TODAY'S DATE>
4. Post the list of users, message sent, and a brief notification to the oit_allcampus_hdft channel within the RutgersIT slack instance
5. Post the message sent and notification, we may receive emails to the esd_nb_hd_email and esd_nb_hd_all channels within the OIT/ESD slack instance
6. Have a supervisor create a tag for calls/emails related to this issue (i.e., [Phishing MM/DD])

title: - Using REGIS for the Help Desk
body:
Accessing REGIS
1. Go to https://sims.rutgers.edu/rosters/ .
2. Click the Rosters & Electronic Grading Information System (REGIS) link.
3. Log in through Central Authentication (CAS).
Navigating REGIS
There are 4 tabs available.
View Rosters
There are two tabs available: Quick Search and Drill-down Search.
Quick Search
1. Quick Search requires that you know the full course number. Everything but the section number is required.
2. Then click the Retrieve Roster button.
3. The class roster will be displayed. See the FERPA warning below regarding the proper use of this information.
4. We have access to see all courses. Faculty members will be restricted to those courses for which they have been given permission by the department chair or his/her designee.
5. Click the View Rosters tab to return to the main View Rosters page.
Drill-down Search
1. Drill-down Search allows you to search for course information.
2. Use pulldown menus to select criteria.
3. Click Retrieve Roster
View Roster Status
1. Enter course number and click View Status button.
2. Roster status and the assigned professor is displayed.
View & Grant/Revoke Privileges
1. The View & Grant/Revoke Privileges page shows a person's current privileges. It shows your own privileges by default, and only for the current and previous years.
2. Older sets of privileges are found through the Display Complete List ... link.
3. Searches for others can be done by name or NetID.
4. Click on a name to see its privs.
5. Help Desk staff cannot change privs. We can only see the current ones. There are four main types of privs, each with its own set of abilities. 
o Someone who is unable to do something in REGIS may not have been granted the privs for that access. Refer the person to either the person who granted the existing or previous privs (shown in the "Granted By" column) or to the departmental administrator (if no privs have been granted, or the previous granter is not available).
6. We have also found undefined DEAN and GC_GUEST roles/privs.
Main Menu
Returns you to the page with the Rosters & Electronic Grading Information System (REGIS) link.
How to use REGIS access
1. For people with existing access, see who granted the access and send the inquirer to that person.
2. For people who never had access before, or in cases where the original granter is no longer around, refer the inquirer to the department chair or administrator.
3. We cannot search to see who has access to a given class roster. We can only search for access via a given name or a NetID that has access.
4. Dos/Don'ts 
o This tool is intended for use in specific cases to research someone's reported REGIS problem. Abuse of this access will result in immediate termination. Examples of abuse might be a parent searching for a child's roster or an idle examination of a colleague's roster.
o Pay attention to the FERPA restrictions. They are briefly described in every displayed roster.
o Rosters and privileges may also be viewed for REGIS training purposes.
o Do not look up info on behalf of one of our employees. Refer the person to his/her professor.
o Every time you use it, please make sure you are making a comment in the relevant ServiceNow incident. Document what you did and why you did it. Avoid including specific people's info in the ticket.
o Log out of the REGIS tool when done; do not leave REGIS windows active. Delete any downloaded data when done.
o When someone asks about a REGIS problem, you may tell them, "I need to verify your identity to make sure you have the right to this information." Do not show REGIS information to anyone other than the person whose access you are checking. (For example, do not tell a TA what sort of access the professor has.)
o Refer all access/priv problems to the granter or department. You may explain that we cannot make changes in REGIS.

title: - Switches
body:
When using switches, you must copy the statuses of all ports involved in the changes into the ticket before making changes. Have a supervisor verify what you are doing and post approval for what you do in SN. Copy all switch work into the ticket and briefly describe what you did. One of the primary Office resources for switches is the Switchlist. This list contains information about the switches, including IP addresses, hostnames, and the rooms they serve.

Errors on the Switches

Two errors that may come up on the switches are runts and giants. Runts are discarded packets that are smaller than the average packet size. A giant is the opposite; it is a packet that exceeds the maximum packet size and is discarded. Several factors can cause runts and giants, but collisions are often the cause. If the error counters on the switch occur frequently within a short period, this could affect user connectivity and is something you should speak to a Network Support Supervisor about. 

Sometimes, a port's status may switch to "err-disabled," indicating that an error caused it to shut down. To check the cause, on an IOS switch, you can use the "show interface status err-disabled" command or "show log" to view the system log and see when it occurred and what the cause was. 

There are also occasionally issues with certain devices failing to pass their MAC addresses. This can be seen in the log, where the device shows UNKNOWN_MAC instead of its MAC address. While this can often be resolved by connecting a second device, it will resolve itself in roughly 10-20 minutes.

Switches used in the dorms

We use two switch types in ResNet Office; they are differentiated by the operating system they run. CatOS (Catalyst Operating System) is the discontinued operating system used by the older switches in the dorms. More current switches use the Cisco IOS operating system.

CatOS shows confirmation for command input and does not have a # at the end of every input line. Cisco IOS switches use different commands and do not show confirmation for command input. They are indicated by the # at the end of each input line.

Logging into the switches

Using PuTTY or Terminal (Mac), ssh to nbcs.rutgers.edu. You can then log in to the switch you want using the "telnet (switch IP)" command. Log in to the switch using your NetID and Enigma card.

Trunk ports

The trunk port of a switch receives all traffic from outside the switch and redirects traffic to the port that requested it. The trunk ports are often the first or last two ports on a blade. The port description will often list it as the trunk port. Unlike other ports, the trunk uses a gigabit fiber connection (1000Base-SX) rather than a Cat5/CAT6 connection. The VLAN can also identify it for the port, which will list "trunk".

If the trunk port is disabled, it will shut down connectivity for the entire switch and any other connected switches. If this occurs, the switch can only be returned online by NOC during regular business hours (M-F 9-5). NEVER SHUTDOWN THE TRUNK PORT.

Port security

The Port Security feature on a switch remembers the MAC address associated with the switch’s port and allows only that MAC address to communicate on that port. If any other MAC address tries to communicate through the port, port security will disable the port. ResNet uses this feature when we restrict the ports a specific user can connect to. In these cases, we will shut down the offending user's port (CIRT or rogue DHCP) and enable port security on their roommate’s port(s). This means an offender cannot access the internet from anywhere in their room. When a port security violation occurs (for example, you set port security on a port and a different MAC address tries to use that port), the port's status can revert to either "err-disabled" or "shutdown".

title: - Switches - Frozen VLANs
body:
What is a frozen VLAN?

A frozen Vlan occurs when a VLAN is not included in the spanning tree of the switch. Spanning trees are based on the spanning tree protocol, which is a link layer network protocol that creates a spanning tree within a mesh network of connected switches. Links not part of the spanning tree, which leaves a single path between two network nodes, are disabled. If a VLAN does not fall in the spanning tree, the users will not receive connectivity beyond their switch.

Symptoms

Users experiencing the frozen VLAN issue cannot pull an IP address and will receive a 169.254.x.x address. However, they will show as connected on the switch and won’t be able to access websites if they are set statically. Since this issue is on our end, the user’s computer will not be the issue.

The only indication of a user experiencing a frozen VLAN is that they will show on the switch as connected but not receive Internet access. This is a good time to identify whether it is a frozen VLAN.

Identifying a frozen VLAN
Run the command: show vlan
Check the output and record the VLAN in which the problem ports are.
Run the command: show trunk ("show interfaces trunk" for IOS based switches)

If the show int trunk command does not work, see the subsection labeled "Identifying frozen VLANs on the Catalyst 3500" below.
In the output, check the section labeled "VLAN in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned".

If the VLAN is in the list then the VLAN is not frozen. Continue troubleshooting and dispatch if necessary.
Here is an example using a switch in Nichols

Note how all residential ports on this switch are located on VLAN 234.

Notice that VLAN 234 is included in the "Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned" list. This means that the VLAN is not frozen.

body:

Table of Contents

Help Desk

ACE Users

RP (Responsible Party) Groups
Adding someone to a RP
Removing someone from a RP
Creating a RP
Home 
Processing your Privs

On the home screen you will see a list of all privs that you are listed as a RP for. Alternatively you can click all tasks to see a list of all outstanding privs for all RPs. You can sort any of the columns alphabetically by clicking on the column name. 

Green privs are ones that need to be granted. Red privs are ones that need to be revoked. 

Processing individual privs

Click on the priv to see the grant/revoke instructions. Click Confirm to mark the priv as completed. You can change the date the priv was granted/revoked if it is different, or add a comment if needed. 

Bulk processing privs

To check off multiple privs at a time you can press CTRL and select individual rows. You may also click one row, hold down shift to click on a second row, which will select everything between those two. Hit Enter to process all selected privs at once. 

Employees
Individually add a new employee

This can be done to add new employees or add new positions to existing employees. 

Click Employees tab on the top.
Click Add Employee(s) at the top or bottom of the page. 
Enter their NetID. 
Choose the site they will work at. 
Choose the position they start in. 
Click Confirm. 
Bulk add new employees

This can be done to add new employees or add new positions to existing employees. 

Download the Ace Bulk Upload Employees spreadsheet. 
Enter their NetIDs and Save. 
Go to ACE. 
Click Employees tab on the top.
Click Add Employee(s) at the top or bottom of the page. 
Choose Add Multiple. 
Drag and Drop or select the file from your computer.
Choose the Site and Position (will be applied to all NetIDs on the spreadsheet, you must do multiple sheets if adding for multiple positions). 
Click Confirm. 
Viewing an Employee's page and info
Go to the Manage Employee tab. 
Enter their NetID and hit Enter to be brought to the employee's page. 
Positions

This section lists all current and past Positions the employee has held. 

Hovering over the start or end date will show the NetID of the person who assigned/removed the position for the employee. 

You can add or remove a position from this page by clicking Add Position or hitting the red X next to the position you want to remove. 

Missing Privs

This section lists all pending privs for the employee that still need to be completed by the RP. An RP can not complete a grant action for a priv on this page, they will need to do so from the Home tab. 

Hovering over the Position will also show which Site the Position is in. Hovering over the Required days remaining will show the date that the priv was marked as needed for the employee. 

Current Privs

Lists all the privs currently assigned to the Employee. Any priv in Red are ones that are pending removal by the RP. An RP can mark the priv as removed from this page by clicking the Red X next to the priv, instead of completing this action from the Home tab. 

Hovering over the Position will also show which Site the Position is in. Hovering over the Granted date will show the NetID of the person who completed the grant action for the priv for this employee. 

Past Privs

Shows a historical record of any priv that has both been granted and revoked for the employee, in addition to the NetID of the person who completed each action. 

Privs that have a strike through the name are privs that have also been deleted from ACE, but are still kept here for record-keeping purposes. 

adm

On the user's Employee page in ACE, there is a section that indicates whether they have their -adm account yet (including a timestamp for when it was last checked), as well as indicating if any pending privs need an -adm account. You can also click Refresh -adm to manually run a check for their -adm account. Their adm status is updated every 10 minutes. 

Privileges
Creating a Priv

When creating a priv, look for existing ones that may be similar to determine which Category to create the priv in. 

Click on the Privileges tab.
Find the Category the new priv should be in. Look for similar privs to help determine which one to go in if you're unsure. 
Click Add Priv at the bottom of the Category it should be in. 
Enter the name for the priv. See the Naming section below for more details. 
Click Confirm. 
You'll be taken to a new page to finish creating the priv. See the sections below for more details. 
Naming

If similar privs exist, copy and paste that priv name into the new one and then alter only the parts you need to change. This ensures consistent naming and helps when sorting lists alphabetically. 

For Bomgar and RAD group privs, ACER looks at the priv name, so it must be formatted exactly as the others in order for ACER to work.

VCC privs are just for record keeping, as VCC pulls from the RAD group when granting/revoking privs.  

Actions

Add detailed instructions on the steps needed for the Responsible Party (RP) to Grant or Revoke the priv from the employee. Click in each section to add text. Copy and paste the action from another priv if it's similar, to ensure the same language and formatting. 

Responsible Party (RP)

The RP can be set separately for each individual site, and for each action (grant or revoke). Privs are assigned to a position, and then the positions are in each of the different sites.

Example: if the priv is assigned to a Consultant Position at the Busch site, and a Consultant Position in the Livi site, you can set a separate RP for each. So that Busch FT are responsible for granting the priv for the Busch Consultant, and Livi FT are responsible for granting the priv for the Livi Consultant. 

Typically, it is easiest to just select all Labs/HD sites (except for Newark and Camden) and have the RP be assigned for all, even if the priv is just meant for a single site. This is done because when viewing the Privileges tab, the RP column shows you any RP assigned to that priv, and not what site each of those RPs are responsible for. Which can be confusing, and the only way to check is to go into the RP for the priv and check each individual site. This also prevents the priv from being missed in the future if the priv is assigned to a new position that is in a site that doesn't have an RP set for it (it will go unnoticed and not show up on anyone's home page to process). 

Only set the RP for a singular site if you truly want to set a specific different RP per site. 

Click the RP field for the Grant or Revoke section of the priv. 
Choose which site you want to assign a RP. You can click and drag to select multiple sites to set the RP for at one time. 
Choose what Group or User should be the RP for the selected site(s). 
Avoid selecting individual Users, as it is more cumbersome to go priv by priv and update the RP if that user leaves OIT. Instead, make an RP group, even if just for one person, and assign that group as the RP for the priv. That way if that user leaves you only have to update the Group in one spot vs having to go into each priv. 
Click Confirm when done.
You must click Confirm before you can update the RP for a different site, this requires you to repeat theses steps from the beginning for the next site you want to update. 
Inherit

Positions can be set to inherit privs from other positions. This is beneficial for a similar position, at different sites, to inherit privs from one "Master" position. Or for positions to inherit privs from lower positions as a consultant is promoted up the ladder. If there are several Positions that inherit sequentially from each other, the priv only has to be assigned to the lowest most position and it will inherit upward through all the sequential positions. 

Checking off Inherit allows the priv to be assigned to any position that inherits a position with the priv already assigned. 

If left unchecked, the priv will have to be assigned to each position that needs it individually. 

adm

If ADM is checked off, then the person's -adm account will be listed in any tasks to complete or used in any automatic priv RAD group. If they do not have an -adm account yet, ACE will recheck every 10 minutes to try to add them to the RAD Group. On the user's Employee page in ACE, there is a section that indicates whether they have their -adm account yet (including a timestamp for when it was last checked), as well as indicating if any pending privs need an -adm account. You can also click Refresh -adm to manually run a check for their -adm account. Their adm status is updated every 10 minutes. 

Automatic Priv

These will create RAD groups that contain the NetIDs (or NetID-adm if the adm box is checked off). The name of the RAD group is listed on the Priv in the Privileges tab in ACE. The number after the "P" in the priv name is the ID number for that priv. 

Users are automatically added to the RAD group listed by ACE as soon as they are assigned a position with that privilege associated with it. They are also automatically removed from the RAD Group when they are unassigned that priv. 

Automatic privs will not have a NetID listed under "Granted by" or "Revoked By" since it was not done by an individual. 

To make a priv automatic, you must contact Anton (NetID: antsar).

Deleting a Priv

You should first check to see who the priv is still assigned to before deleting by clicking Show in the Empl. column on the Privileges tab.

A priv can be deleted by clicking the X in the Del column. It will then ask you to Confirm. If the priv is still assigned to anyone, you will get two options after clicking Confirm:

Revoke the privs right now, all at once. - This should be used if the priv does not need to still be removed from those it is assigned to. Typically, this is for a service that no longer exists and no one has access to anymore. 
Do not touch them, the privs will have to be removed one-by-one manually. - This should be used if access still needs to be removed for anyone who still has the priv assigned. A revoke action will show up on the Home page for the RP of the priv. 
Check who has a specific Priv

To see who currently has a priv, navigate to the Privileges tab and click Show in the Empl. column next to the priv you want to check. This will show you anyone who has the priv assigned (but not those who are still pending and are still on the Home list for the RP to process). 

Positions

Positions are located within a specific Site (Busch, Livingston, Newark, etc). Positions can not be moved between or copied from Site to Site. 

Adding a Position to an employee

Student Employees should only have 1 Position per Site, since each Position inherits the one below it. This also helps keep an accurate count of employees in each Position when looking at the Positions tab. 

During promotions, you should add the employee's new Position before removing their old one. 

Individually
Go to the Manage Employee tab. 
Enter their NetID and hit Enter to be brought to the employee's page. 
Click Add Position. 
Select the Site the position is in. 
Then choose the new Position to add. 
Change the start date if necessary. 
Click Confirm. 
Bulk

Follow the process for Bulk uploading new employees to add the same position to multiple employees at once. 

Removing a Position from an employee
Individually
Go to the Manage Employee tab. 
Enter their NetID and hit Enter to be brought to the employee's page. 
If they are being promoted or changing to a new Position, add that one first before removing their current one. 
Click the X next to the Position you want to remove. 
Choose the reason why and change the date if necessary.
Click Confirm. 
Bulk

No option currently exists to bulk remove positions. 

Check who is currently assigned to a specific Position

You can view a list of all employees assigned to a particular Position. 

Go to the Positions tab. 
Click on the Position you want to check. 
Click List Employees. 
Check what other Positions inherit privs from a specific Position

You can check to see what other positions may inherit privs from a specific position. This will show only the positions that are set to directly inherit the privs from the position you are viewing (the next step up in a sequential ladder). This does not show any subsequent positions higher up the ladder (3rd, 4th, 5th, etc.. rungs of the ladder). 

Go to the Positions tab. 
Click on the Position you want to check. 
Click List Positions. 
Creating a new Position

Any priv that would be specific to only select individuals, and not to an entire position, should be listed as it's own position in the Help Desk Access site. Examples of this are for individual FT that might be Admins for a service that not all FT have access to. 

Go to the Positions tab. 
Click Add Position in the appropriate Site. 
Name the Position. See the naming section below for more details. 
Click Confirm. 
You'll then be taken to the Position's page where you can assign privs and inherit positions. See sections below for more details. 
Naming

Ensure consistent name formatting with similar or sequential Positions. Copy and paste the name from similar Positions to ensure consistency. 

Inheriting privs from other Positions

You can choose if the position will inherit privs from a "Master" position or from a lower-level position. 

In the Other Positions To Inherit Privileges From box, find the position (s) you want to inherit privileges from. 
The list will show all positions on the same site first, then all other positions in alphabetical order based on the site. 
To select multiple positions, you must press CTRL when clicking on multiple positions. Clicking on just 1 position without holding CTRL will unselect any other already selected positions, and only select the one you just clicked. 
Inheriting from another position will not inherit all privs from that position. It will only inherit the privs on that position that have the Inherit checkbox marked on the priv itself in the Privileges tab. 
Click Save Changes in the Other Positions To Inherit Privileges From box when done. 
Clicking Save Changes under the Positions Info box is not the same. 
Adding Privs to a Position

If you have also just chosen to inherit privs from another Position, make sure you clicked Save Changes in the Other Positions To Inherit Privileges From box. This is so that the inherited privs are checked off accordingly (grey check marks) before you now go to check off new privs individually to the position. 

Go to the Position you want to change.
Click the heading name of each priv section to expand it. Alternatively, click Expand all sections at the top of the priv list to automatically expand all of them. 
Find the priv you want to add. 
Click the check box on the priv. If the box is already checked off and grey, that means it is already inheriting the priv from another position. 
Click Save Changes in the Position Info box to save. 
Removing Privs from a Position

This is the same as adding, but uncheck the box next to the appropriate priv. 

Note that if a priv that is not inherited is added to a position, and then the priv is changed at a later date to actually be inherited, the check box will remain blue. If you uncheck the priv box and click Save Changes, the box will now turn grey to show that it is inherited.

ACE Users

Users are Full-Time or Student Supervisor Employees who can access and update things in ACE. 

Adding User
Go to the Settings tab. 
Click Add User. 
Enter their NetID. 
Click Confirm. 
By default, they are added as a Supervisor. change their access level if needed. 
Removing User
Go to the Settings tab. 
Click the X next to the NetID to be removed. 
Click Confirm. 
Access Levels

Each of the 3 different access levels have the following permissions

Supervisor
View an employee's page including current positions and privs
Add/remove positions to employees
Full-Time
View an employee's page including current positions and privs
Add/remove positions to employees
Add/remove employees
Process privs assigned to them as an RP
Admin
View an employee's page including current positions and privs
Add/remove positions to employees
Add/remove employees
Process privs assigned to them as an RP
Add/remove/update privs and Positions
Add/remove/update Users
Add/remove/update RP Groups
RP (Responsible Party) Groups

RPs are the ones responsible for granting/revoking privs. RPs will only see privs on their Home tab to process for the Groups they are in. They must also be on the Users list in order to access ACE. 

Adding someone to a RP
Go to the Settings tab. 
Find the RP to update. 
Enter the User's NetID to the list, leaving a space between each NetID. 
Hit Enter on your keyboard to save. If you do not hit Enter it will not update. 
Removing someone from a RP
Go to the Settings tab. 
Find the RP to update. 
Delete the User's NetID from the list, leaving a space between each NetID. 
Hit Enter on your keyboard to save. If you do not hit Enter it will not update. 
Creating a RP
Go to the Settings tab.
Click Add Group. 
Enter a name for the group. Follow similar group name formatting if applicable. 
Click Confirm. 
Add Users to the Group as noted above.
